  13 function print_head(bool $simple=false) : void
  14 {
  15   global $refresh_rate;
  16 
  17   echo "<head>\n";
  18 
  19   echo "<meta charset=\"" . get_charset() . "\">\n";
  20 
  21   // Set IE=edge so that IE10 will display MRBS properly, even if compatibility mode is used
  22   // on the browser.  If we don't do this then MRBS will treat IE10 as an unsupported browser
  23   // when compatibility mode is turned on, potentially confusing users who may have forgotten
  24   // that they are using compatibility mode.   Unfortunately we can't set IE=edge in the header,
  25   // which is where we would normally do it, because then we won't be able to detect IE9 using
  26   // conditional comments.  So we have to do it in a <meta> tag, after the conditional comments
  27   // around the <html> tags.
  28   echo "<meta http-equiv=\"X-UA-Compatible\" content=\"IE=edge\">\n";
  29 
  30   // Improve scaling on mobile devices
  31   echo "<meta name=\"viewport\" content=\"width=device-width, initial-scale=1\">\n";
  32 
  33   if (!$simple)
  34   {
  35     // Add the CSRF token so that JavaScript can use it
  36     echo "<meta name=\"csrf_token\" content=\"" . escape_html(Form::getToken()) . "\">\n";
  37   }
  38 
  39   echo "<meta name=\"robots\" content=\"noindex, nofollow, noarchive\">\n";
  40 
  41   if (($refresh_rate != 0) && (this_page(false, '.php') == 'index'))
  42   {
  43     // If we're using JavaScript we'll do the refresh by getting a new
  44     // table using Ajax requests, which means we only have to download
  45     // the table not the whole page each time
  46     echo "<noscript>\n";
  47     echo "<meta http-equiv=\"Refresh\" content=\"$refresh_rate\">\n";
  48     echo "</noscript>\n";
  49   }
  50 
  51   echo "<title>" . get_vocab("mrbs") . "</title>\n";
  52 
  53   require_once MRBS_ROOT . "/style.inc";
  54 
  55   if (!$simple)
  56   {
  57     require_once MRBS_ROOT . "/js.inc";
  58   }
  59 
  60   echo "</head>\n";
  61 }

  86     $logo_size = @getimagesize($mrbs_company_logo);

  92     }

  94 
  95     if (!empty($mrbs_company_url))
  96     {
  97       echo "</a>\n";
  98     }
  99     echo "</div>\n";

 105   {
 106     echo '<a href="' . escape_html($mrbs_company_url) . '">';

 111     echo "</a>\n";

 118   }
 119   echo '<a href="' . escape_html(multisite('index.php')) . '">' . get_vocab('mrbs') . "</a>\n";
 120   echo "</div>\n";

 124 function print_goto_date(array $context) : void
 125 {
 126   global $multisite, $site;
 127 
 128   if (!checkAuthorised('index.php', true))
 129   {
 130     // Don't show the goto box if the user isn't allowed to view the calendar
 131     return;
 132   }
 133 
 134   $form = new Form();
 135 
 136   $form_id = 'form_nav';
 137 
 138   $form->setAttributes(array('id'     => $form_id,
 139                              'class'  => 'js_hidden',
 140                              'action' => multisite('index.php')))
 141        ->addHiddenInput('view', $context['view']);
 142 
 143   if (isset($context['area']))
 144   {
 145     $form->addHiddenInput('area', $context['area']);
 146   }
 147 
 148   if (isset($room))
 149   {
 150     $form->addHiddenInput('room', $context['room']);
 151   }
 152 
 153   if ($multisite && isset($site) && ($site !== ''))
 154   {
 155     $form->addHiddenInput('site', $site);
 156   }
 157 
 158   $input = new ElementInputDate();
 159   // Add the 'navigation' class so that the JavaScript knows it can use hidden days
 160   $input->setAttributes(array(
 161     'name'        => 'page_date',
 162     'value'       => format_iso_date($context['year'], $context['month'], $context['day']),
 163     'class'       => 'navigation',
 164     'aria-label'  => get_vocab('goto'),
 165     'required'    => true,
 166     'data-submit' => $form_id)
 167   );
 168 
 169   $form->addElement($input);
 170 
 171   $submit = new ElementInputSubmit();
 172   $submit->setAttribute('value', get_vocab('goto'));
 173   $form->addElement($submit);
 174 
 175   $form->render();
 176 }

 179 function print_outstanding(string $query) : void
 180 {
 181   $mrbs_user = session()->getCurrentUser();
 182 
 183   if (!isset($mrbs_user))
 184   {
 185     return;
 186   }
 187 
 188   // Provide a link to the list of bookings awaiting approval
 189   // (if there are any enabled areas where we require bookings to be approved)
 190   $approval_somewhere = some_area('approval_enabled', TRUE);
 191   if ($approval_somewhere && ($mrbs_user->level > 0))
 192   {
 193     $n_outstanding = get_entries_n_outstanding($mrbs_user);
 194 
 195     $class = 'notification';
 196 
 197     if ($n_outstanding > 0)
 198     {
 199       $class .= ' attention';
 200     }
 201 
 202     $url = 'pending.php';
 203     if ($query !== '')
 204     {
 205       $url .= "?$query";
 206     }
 207     echo '<a href="' . escape_html(multisite($url)) . '"' .
 208          " class=\"$class\"" .
 209          ' title="' . get_vocab('outstanding', $n_outstanding) .
 210          "\">$n_outstanding</a>\n";
 211   }
 212 }

 307 // Generate the username link, which gives a report on the user's upcoming bookings.
 308 function print_report_link(User $user) : void
 309 {
 310   // If possible, provide a link to the Report page, otherwise the Search page
 311   // and if that's not possible just print the username with no link.  (Note that
 312   // the Search page isn't the perfect solution because it searches for any bookings
 313   // containing the search string, not just those created by the user.)
 314   if (checkAuthorised('report.php', true))
 315   {
 316     $attributes = array('action' => multisite('report.php'));
 317     $hidden_inputs = array('phase'        => '2',
 318                            'creatormatch' => $user->username);
 319   }
 320   elseif (checkAuthorised('search.php', true))
 321   {
 322     $attributes = array('action' => multisite('search.php'));
 323     $date_now = new DateTime();
 324     $hidden_inputs = array(
 325       'search_str' => $user->username,
 326       'from_date'  => $date_now->getISODate()
 327     );
 328   }
 329   else
 330   {
 331     echo '<span>' . escape_html($user->display_name) . '</span>';
 332     return;
 333   }
 334 
 335   // We're authorised for either Report or Search so print the form.
 336   $form = new Form(Form::METHOD_POST);
 337 
 338   $attributes['id'] = 'show_my_entries';
 339   $form->setAttributes($attributes)
 340        ->addHiddenInputs($hidden_inputs);
 341 
 342   $submit = new ElementInputSubmit();
 343   $submit->setAttributes(array('title' => get_vocab('show_my_entries'),
 344                                'value' => $user->display_name));
 345   $form->addElement($submit);
 346 
 347   $form->render();
 348 }

 351 function print_logonoff_button(array $params, string $value) : void
 352 {
 353   $form = new Form($params['method']);
 354   $form->setAttributes(array('action' => $params['action']));
 355 
 356   // A Get method will replace the query string in the action URL with a query
 357   // string made up of the hidden inputs.  So put any parameters in the action
 358   // query string into hidden inputs.
 359   if ($params['method'] == Form::METHOD_GET)
 360   {
 361     $query_string = parse_url($params['action'], PHP_URL_QUERY);
 362     if (isset($query_string))
 363     {
 364       parse_str($query_string, $query_parameters);
 365       $form->addHiddenInputs($query_parameters);
 366     }
 367   }
 368 
 369   // Add the hidden fields
 370   if (isset($params['hidden_inputs']))
 371   {
 372     $form->addHiddenInputs($params['hidden_inputs']);
 373   }
 374 
 375   // The submit button
 376   $element = new ElementInputSubmit();
 377   $element->setAttribute('value', $value);
 378   $form->addElement($element);
 379 
 380   $form->render();
 381 }

 409 // $context is an associative array indexed by 'view', 'view_all', 'year', 'month', 'day', 'area' and 'room'.
 410 // When $omit_login is true the Login link is omitted.
 411 function print_banner(?array $context, $simple=false, $omit_login=false) : void
 412 {
 413   global $kiosk_QR_code, $auth;
 414 
 415   echo '<header class="banner' . (($simple) ? ' simple' : '') . "\">\n";
 416 
 417   $vars = array();
 418 
 419   if (isset($context['view']))
 420   {
 421     $vars['view'] = $context['view'];
 422   }
 423   if (isset($context['year']) && isset($context['month']) && isset($context['day']))
 424   {
 425     $vars['page_date'] = format_iso_date($context['year'], $context['month'], $context['day']);
 426   }
 427   if (isset($context['area']))
 428   {
 429     $vars['area'] = $context['area'];
 430   }
 431   if (isset($context['room']))
 432   {
 433     $vars['room'] = $context['room'];
 434   }
 435 
 436   $query = http_build_query($vars, '', '&');
 437 
 438   print_header_site_info();
 439 
 440   if (!$simple)
 441   {
 442     echo "<nav class=\"container\">\n";
 443 
 444     echo "<nav>\n";
 445 
 446     echo "<nav class=\"menu\">\n";
 447     print_menu_items($query);
 448     echo "</nav>\n";
 449 
 450     echo "<nav class=\"logon\">\n";
 451     print_outstanding($query);
 452 
 453     $mrbs_user = session()->getCurrentUser();
 454 
 455     // The empty string username is a special case when using anonymous booking
 456     if (isset($mrbs_user) && (!$auth['allow_anonymous_booking'] || ($mrbs_user->username !== '')))
 457     {
 458       print_report_link($mrbs_user);
 459       print_logoff();
 460     }
 461     elseif (!$omit_login)
 462     {
 463       print_logon();
 464     }
 465 
 466     echo "</nav>\n";
 467 
 468     echo "</nav>\n";
 469 
 470     echo "<nav>\n";
 471     print_goto_date($context);
 472     print_search($context);
 473     echo "</nav>\n";
 474 
 475     echo "</nav>\n";
 476 
 477     // Add in a QR code for kiosk mode
 478     // (The QR code library requires PHP 7.4 or greater and the mbstring extension)
 479     if (isset($context['kiosk']) &&
 480         $kiosk_QR_code &&
 481         (version_compare(PHP_VERSION, '7.4') >= 0) &&
 482         //Check for a Mbstring constant rather than using extension_loaded, which is sometimes disabled
 483         defined('MB_CASE_UPPER'))
 484     {
 485       $url = multisite(url_base() . "/index.php?$query");
 486       echo '<nav class="qr" title="' . escape_html($url) . "\">\n";
 487       $options = new QROptions([
 488         'outputType'  => QRCode::OUTPUT_MARKUP_SVG,
 489         'imageBase64' => false,
 490       ]);
 491       $qrcode = new QRCode($options);
 492       echo $qrcode->render($url);
 493       echo "</nav>\n";
 494     }
 495   }
 496 
 497   echo "</header>\n";
 498 }
 499 
 500 
 501 
 502 // Print a message which will only be displayed (thanks to CSS) if the user is
 503 // using an unsupported browser.
 504 function print_unsupported_message(?array $context) : void
 505 {
 506   echo "<div class=\"unsupported_message\">\n";
 507   print_banner($context, true);
 508   echo "<div class=\"contents\">\n";
 509   echo "<p>" . get_vocab('browser_not_supported', get_vocab('mrbs_abbr')) . "</p>\n";
 510   echo "</div>\n";
 511   echo "</div>\n";
 512 }
 513 
 514 
 515 // Print the page header
 516 // $context is an associative array indexed by 'view', 'view_all', 'year', 'month', 'day', 'area' and 'room',
 517 // any of which can be NULL.
 518 // If $simple is true, then just print a simple header that doesn't require any database
 519 // access or JavaScript (useful for fatal errors and database upgrades).
 520 // When $omit_login is true the Login link is omitted.
 521 function print_theme_header(?array $context=null, bool $simple=false, bool $omit_login=false) : void
 522 {
 523   global $multisite, $site, $default_view, $default_view_all, $view_week_number, $style_weekends;
 524 
 525   if ($simple)
 526   {
 527     $data = array();
 528     $classes = array();
 529   }
 530   else
 531   {
 532     // Set the context values if they haven't been given
 533     if (!isset($context))
 534     {
 535       $context = array();
 536     }
 537 
 538     if (empty($context['area']))
 539     {
 540       $context['area'] = get_default_area();
 541     }
 542 
 543     if (empty($context['room']))
 544     {
 545       $context['room'] = get_default_room($context['area']);
 546     }
 547 
 548     if (!isset($context['view']))
 549     {
 550       $context['view'] = (isset($default_view)) ? $default_view : 'day';
 551     }
 552 
 553     if (!isset($context['view_all']))
 554     {
 555       $context['view_all'] = (isset($default_view_all)) ? $default_view_all : true;
 556     }
 557 
 558     // Need to set the timezone before we can use date()
 559     // This will set the correct timezone for the area
 560     get_area_settings($context['area']);
 561 
 562     // If we don't know the right date then use today's
 563     if (!isset($context['year']))
 564     {
 565       $context['year'] = (int) date('Y');
 566     }
 567 
 568     if (!isset($context['month']))
 569     {
 570       $context['month'] = (int) date('m');
 571     }
 572 
 573     if (!isset($context['day']))
 574     {
 575       $context['day'] = (int) date('d');
 576     }
 577 
 578     // Get the form token now, before any headers are sent, in case we are using the 'cookie'
 579     // session scheme.  Otherwise we won't be able to store the Form token.
 580     Form::getToken();
 581 
 582     $page = this_page(false, '.php');
 583 
 584     // Put some data attributes in the body element for the benefit of JavaScript.  Note that we
 585     // cannot use these PHP variables directly in the JavaScript files as those files are cached.
 586     $data = array(
 587       'view'          => $context['view'],
 588       'view_all'      => $context['view_all'],
 589       'area'          => $context['area'],
 590       'room'          => $context['room'],
 591       'page'          => $page,
 592       'page-date'     => format_iso_date($context['year'], $context['month'], $context['day']),
 593       'is-admin'      => (is_admin()) ? 'true' : 'false',
 594       'is-book-admin' => (is_book_admin()) ? 'true' : 'false',
 595       'lang-prefs'    => json_encode(get_lang_preferences())
 596     );
 597 
 598     if ($multisite && isset($site) && ($site !== ''))
 599     {
 600       $data['site'] = $site;
 601     }
 602 
 603     if (isset($context['kiosk']))
 604     {
 605       $data['kiosk'] = $context['kiosk'];
 606     }
 607 
 608     $mrbs_user = session()->getCurrentUser();
 609     if (isset($mrbs_user))
 610     {
 611       $data['username'] = $mrbs_user->username;
 612     }
 613 
 614     // We need $timetohighlight for the day and week views
 615     $timetohighlight = get_form_var('timetohighlight', 'int');
 616     if (isset($timetohighlight))
 617     {
 618       $data['timetohighlight'] = $timetohighlight;
 619     }
 620 
 621     // Put the filename in as a class to aid styling.
 622     $classes[] = $page;
 623     // And if the user is logged in, add another class to aid styling
 624     if (isset($mrbs_user))
 625     {
 626       $classes[] = 'logged_in';
 627     }
 628 
 629     // To help styling
 630     if ($view_week_number)
 631     {
 632       $classes[] = 'view_week_number';
 633     }
 634     if ($style_weekends)
 635     {
 636       $classes[] = 'style_weekends';
 637     }
 638 
 639   }
 640 
 641   $headers = array("Content-Type: text/html; charset=" . get_charset());
 642   http_headers($headers);
 643 
 644   echo DOCTYPE . "\n";
 645 
 646   // We produce two <html> tags: one for versions of IE that we don't support and one for all
 647   // other browsers.  This enables us to use CSS to hide and show the appropriate text.
 648   echo "<!--[if lte IE 9]>\n";
 649   echo "<html lang=\"" . escape_html(get_mrbs_lang()) . "\" class=\"unsupported_browser\">\n";
 650   echo "<![endif]-->\n";
 651   echo "<!--[if (!IE)|(gt IE 9)]><!-->\n";
 652   echo "<html lang=\"" . escape_html(get_mrbs_lang()) . "\">\n";
 653   echo "<!--<![endif]-->\n";
 654 
 655   print_head($simple);
 656 
 657   echo '<body class="' . escape_html(implode(' ', $classes)) . '"';
 658   foreach ($data as $key => $value)
 659   {
 660     if (isset($value))
 661     {
 662       // Convert booleans to 0 or 1
 663       if (is_bool($value))
 664       {
 665         $value = (int)$value;
 666       }
 667       echo " data-$key=\"" . escape_html($value) . '"';
 668     }
 669   }
 670   echo ">\n";
 671 
 672   print_unsupported_message($context);
 673 
 674   print_banner($context, $simple, $omit_login);
 675 
 676   // This <div> should really be moved out of here so that we can always see
 677   // the matching closing </div>
 678   echo "<div class=\"contents\">\n";
 679 
 680 
 681 } // end of print_theme_header()
 682

/areadefaults.inc.php

   1 <?php
   2 declare(strict_types=1);
   3 namespace MRBS;
   4 
   5 /**************************************************************************
   6  *   MRBS area defaults file (default settings for NEW areas)
   7  *
   8  * DO _NOT_ MODIFY THIS FILE YOURSELF. IT IS FOR _INTERNAL_ USE ONLY.
   9  *
  10  * TO CONFIGURE MRBS FOR YOUR SYSTEM ADD CONFIGURATION PARAMETERS FROM
  11  * THIS FILE INTO config.inc.php, DO _NOT_ EDIT THIS FILE.
  12  *
  13  * This file contains the default settings for configuration parameters that
  14  * can be set on a per-area basis by using a web browser and following the
  15  * "Rooms" link in MRBS.    The settings in this file just determine the
  16  * default values that are used when new areas are created.   They are kept
  17  * in a separate file to system defaults to draw attention to the fact that
  18  * they are merely the default settings for new areas:  it can be a little
  19  * frustrating sometimes to edit these values and find they have no effect
  20  * on existing areas
  21  **************************************************************************/
  22 
  23 
  24 
  25 /*******************
  26  * Calendar settings
  27  *******************/
  28 
  29 // This setting controls whether to use "clock" or "times" based intervals
  30 // (FALSE and the default) or user defined periods (TRUE).
  31 
  32 // $enable_periods is settable on a per-area basis.
  33 
  34 $enable_periods = FALSE;  // Default value for new areas
  35 
  36 
  37 // TIMES SETTINGS
  38 // --------------
  39 
  40 // These settings are all set per area through MRBS.   These are the default
  41 // settings that are used when a new area is created.
  42 
  43 // The "Times" settings are ignored if $enable_periods is TRUE.
  44 
  45 // Note: Be careful to avoid specifying options that display blocks overlapping
  46 // the next day, since it is not properly handled.
  47 
  48 // Resolution - what blocks can be booked, in seconds.
  49 // Default is half an hour: 1800 seconds.
  50 $resolution = (30 * 60);  // DEFAULT VALUE FOR NEW AREAS
  51 
  52 // If the following variable is set to TRUE, the resolution of bookings
  53 // is forced to be the value of $resolution, rather than the resolution set
  54 // for the area in the database.
  55 $force_resolution = FALSE;
  56 
  57 // Default duration - default length (in seconds) of a booking.
  58 // Defaults to (60 * 60) seconds, i.e. an hour
  59 $default_duration = (60 * 60);  // DEFAULT VALUE FOR NEW AREAS
  60 // Whether the "All Day" checkbox should be checked by default.  (Note
  61 // that even if this is set to true, $default_duration should still
  62 // be set as that is the duration that will be used when the All Day
  63 // checkbox is unchecked)
  64 $default_duration_all_day = FALSE;  // DEFAULT VALUE FOR NEW AREAS
  65 
  66 // Start and end of day.
  67 // NOTE:  The time between the beginning of the last and first
  68 // slots of the day must be an integral multiple of the resolution.
  69 // If the last slot is before the first slot, then the booking day is
  70 // assumed to span midnight and the last slot is on the day after the
  71 // first slot.
  72 
  73 
  74 // The default settings below (along with the 30 minute resolution above)
  75 // give you 24 half-hourly slots starting at 07:00, with the last slot
  76 // being 18:30 -> 19:00
  77 
  78 // The beginning of the first slot of the day (DEFAULT VALUES FOR NEW AREAS)
  79 $morningstarts         = 7;   // must be integer in range 0-23
  80 $morningstarts_minutes = 0;   // must be integer in range 0-59
  81 
  82 // The beginning of the last slot of the day (DEFAULT VALUES FOR NEW AREAS)
  83 $eveningends           = 18;  // must be integer in range 0-23
  84 $eveningends_minutes   = 30;   // must be integer in range 0-59
  85 
  86 // Example 1.
  87 // If resolution=3600 (1 hour), morningstarts = 8 and morningstarts_minutes = 30
  88 // then for the last period to start at say 4:30pm you would need to set eveningends = 16
  89 // and eveningends_minutes = 30
  90 
  91 // Example 2.
  92 // To get a full 24-hour display with 15-minute steps, set morningstarts=0; eveningends=23;
  93 // eveningends_minutes=45; and resolution=900.
  94 //
  95 // Example 3.
  96 // To get a booking day running from 6.00 pm to 2.00 am with 30 minute steps, set
  97 // morningstarts=18, morningstarts_minutes = 0, eveningends = 1, eveningends_minutes = 30
  98 // and resolution = 1800.
  99 
 100 
 101 // PERIODS SETTINGS
 102 // ----------------
 103 
 104 // The "Periods" settings are used only in areas where the mode has
 105 // been set to "Periods".
 106 
 107 // Define the name or description for your periods in chronological order
 108 // For example:
 109 // $periods[] = "Period 1"
 110 // $periods[] = "Period 2"
 111 // ...
 112 // or
 113 // $periods[] = "09:15 - 09:50"
 114 // $periods[] = "09:55 - 10:35"
 115 // ...
 116 
 117 // Period names are encoded in UTF-8
 118 
 119 // NOTE:  The maximum number of periods is 60.   Do not define more than this.
 120 unset($periods);    // Include this line when copying to config.inc.php
 121 $periods[] = "Period 1";
 122 $periods[] = "Period 2";
 123 // NOTE:  The maximum number of periods is 60.   Do not define more than this.
 124 
 125 // NOTE:  See INSTALL for information on how to add or remove periods in an
 126 // existing database.
 127 
 128 
 129 /******************
 130  * Booking policies
 131  ******************/
 132 
 133 // It is possible to set policies that restrict how far in advance ordinary users can make
 134 // bookings.   Both minimum and maximum values can be set.  It is also possible to distinguish
 135 // between creating new bookings and deleting existing bookings.  Editing an existing booking
 136 // involves deleting the existing booking and creating a new booking at the (possibly) new time.
 137 // So if for example you want to stop people editing existing bookings, but allow the creation
 138 // of new bookings, then you will need to prevent deletion but allow creation.
 139 
 140 // If the variables below are set to TRUE, MRBS will force a minimum and/or maximum advance
 141 // booking time on ordinary users (admins can make bookings for whenever they like).   The
 142 // minimum advance booking time allows you to set a policy saying that users must book
 143 // at least so far in advance.  The maximum allows you to set a policy saying that they cannot
 144 // book more than so far in advance.  How the times are determined depends on whether Periods
 145 // or Times are being used.
 146 
 147 // DEFAULT VALUES FOR NEW AREAS
 148 
 149 // Creating new bookings
 150 $min_create_ahead_enabled = FALSE;    // set to TRUE to enforce a minimum advance booking time
 151 $max_create_ahead_enabled = FALSE;    // set to TRUE to enforce a maximum advance booking time
 152 
 153 // Deleting existing bookings
 154 $min_delete_ahead_enabled = FALSE;    // set to TRUE to enforce a minimum advance booking time
 155 $max_delete_ahead_enabled = FALSE;    // set to TRUE to enforce a maximum advance booking time
 156 
 157 // The advance booking limits are measured in seconds and are set by the two variables below.
 158 // The relevant time for determining whether a booking is allowed is the start time of the
 159 // booking.  Values may be negative: for example setting $min_delete_ahead_secs = -300 means
 160 // that users cannot delete (and this will include editing) a booking more than 5 minutes in
 161 // the past.
 162 
 163 
 164 // DEFAULT VALUES FOR NEW AREAS
 165 
 166 // Creating new bookings
 167 $min_create_ahead_secs = 0;           // (seconds) cannot book in the past
 168 $max_create_ahead_secs = 60*60*24*7;  // (seconds) no more than one week ahead
 169 
 170 // Deleting existing bookings
 171 $min_delete_ahead_secs = 0;           // (seconds) cannot book in the past
 172 $max_delete_ahead_secs = 60*60*24*7;  // (seconds) no more than one week ahead
 173 
 174 // NOTE:  If you are using periods, MRBS has no notion of when the periods occur during the
 175 // day, and so cannot impose policies of the kind "users must book at least one period
 176 // in advance".    However it can impose policies such as "users must book at least
 177 // one day in advance".   The two values above are rounded down to the nearest whole
 178 // number of days when using periods.   For example 86401 will be rounded down to 86400
 179 // (one day) and 1 will be rounded down to 0.
 180 //
 181 // As MRBS does not know when the periods occur in the day, there is no way of specifying, for example,
 182 // that bookings must be made at least 24 hours in advance.    Setting $min_create_ahead_secs=86400
 183 // will allow somebody to make a booking at 11:59 pm for the first period the next day, which
 184 // may occur at 8.00 am.
 185 
 186 
 187 // Set a maximum duration for bookings
 188 $max_duration_enabled = FALSE; // Set to TRUE if you want to enforce a maximum duration
 189 $max_duration_secs = 60*60*2;  // (seconds) - when using "times"
 190 $max_duration_periods = 2;     // (periods) - when using "periods"
 191 
 192 
 193 
 194 // DEFAULT VALUES FOR NEW AREAS
 195 // Set the maximum number of bookings that can be made in an area by any one user, in an
 196 // interval, which can be a day, week, month or year, or else in the future.  (A week is
 197 // defined by the $weekstarts setting).   These are per-area settings but you can use them
 198 // in conjunction with the global settings.   This would allow you to set policies such as
 199 // allowing a maximum of 10 bookings per month in total with a maximum of 1 per day in Area A.
 200 $max_per_interval_area_enabled['day']    = FALSE;
 201 $max_per_interval_area['day'] = 1;      // max 1 bookings per day in an area
 202 
 203 $max_per_interval_area_enabled['week']   = FALSE;
 204 $max_per_interval_area['week'] = 5;     // max 5 bookings per week in an area
 205 
 206 $max_per_interval_area_enabled['month']  = FALSE;
 207 $max_per_interval_area['month'] = 10;   // max 10 bookings per month in an area
 208 
 209 $max_per_interval_area_enabled['year']   = FALSE;
 210 $max_per_interval_area['year'] = 50;    // max 50 bookings per year in an area
 211 
 212 $max_per_interval_area_enabled['future'] = FALSE;
 213 $max_per_interval_area['future'] = 100; // max 100 bookings in the future in an area
 214 
 215 // Set the maximum total *length* of bookings that can be made by any one user, in an interval,
 216 // which can be a day, week, month or year, or else in the future.  (A week is defined
 217 // by the $weekstarts setting).   These are per-area settings but you can use them
 218 // in conjunction with the global settings.   This would allow you to set policies such as
 219 // allowing a maximum of 10 hours per week in total with a maximum of 1 hour per day in Area A.
 220 // These settings only apply to areas in "times" mode.
 221 
 222 $max_secs_per_interval_area_enabled['day']    = false;
 223 $max_secs_per_interval_area['day'] = 60*60*2;      // max 2 hours per day in total
 224 
 225 $max_secs_per_interval_area_enabled['week']   = false;
 226 $max_secs_per_interval_area['week'] = 60*60*10;    // max 10 hours per week in total
 227 
 228 $max_secs_per_interval_area_enabled['month']  = false;
 229 $max_secs_per_interval_area['month'] = 60*60*25;   // max 25 hours per month in total
 230 
 231 $max_secs_per_interval_area_enabled['year']   = false;
 232 $max_secs_per_interval_area['year'] = 60*60*100;   // max 100 hours per year in total
 233 
 234 $max_secs_per_interval_area_enabled['future'] = false;
 235 $max_secs_per_interval_area['future'] = 60*60*100; // max 100 hours in the future in total
 236

 239  * Display settings
 240  ******************/
 241 
 242 // In the day view, to display times on the x-axis (along the top) and rooms on the y-axis (down
 243 // the side set to true; the default/traditional version of MRBS has rooms along the top and
 244 // times down the side.    Transposing the table can be useful if you have a large number of
 245 // rooms and not many time slots.
 246 $times_along_top = false;
 247 
 248 
 249 /************************
 250  * Miscellaneous settings
 251  ************************/
 252 
 253 // PRIVATE BOOKINGS SETTINGS
 254 
 255 // These settings are all set per area through MRBS.   These are the default
 256 // settings that are used when a new area is created.
 257 
 258 // Only administrators or the person who booked a private event can see
 259 // details of the event.  Everyone else just sees that the time/period
 260 // is booked on the schedule.
 261 
 262 $private_enabled = FALSE;  // DEFAULT VALUE FOR NEW AREAS
 263            // Display checkbox in entry page to make
 264            // the booking private.
 265 
 266 $private_mandatory = FALSE;  // DEFAULT VALUE FOR NEW AREAS
 267            // If TRUE all new/edited entries will
 268            // use the value from $private_default when saved.
 269            // If checkbox is displayed it will be disabled.
 270 
 271 $private_default = FALSE;  // DEFAULT VALUE FOR NEW AREAS
 272            // Set default value for "Private" flag on new/edited entries.
 273            // Used if the $private_enabled checkbox is displayed
 274            // or if $private_mandatory is set.
 275 
 276 $private_override = "none";  // DEFAULT VALUE FOR NEW AREAS
 277            // Override default privacy behavior.
 278            // "none" - Private flag on entry is used
 279            // "private" - ALL entries are treated as private regardless
 280            //             of private flag on the entry.
 281            // "public" - NO entry is treated as private, regardless of
 282            //            private flag on the entry.
 283            // Overrides $private_default and $private_mandatory
 284            // Consider your users' expectations of privacy before
 285            // changing to "public" or from "private" to "none"
 286 
 287 
 288 // SETTINGS FOR APPROVING BOOKINGS - PER-AREA
 289 
 290 // These settings control whether bookings made by ordinary users need to be
 291 // approved by an admin.   The settings here are the default settings for new
 292 // areas.  The settings for individual areas can be changed from within MRBS.
 293 
 294 $approval_enabled = FALSE;  // Set to TRUE to enable booking approval
 295 
 296 // Set to FALSE if you don't want users to be able to send reminders
 297 // to admins when bookings are still awaiting approval.
 298 $reminders_enabled = TRUE;
 299 
 300 
 301 // SETTINGS FOR BOOKING CONFIRMATION
 302 
 303 // Allows bookings to be marked as "tentative", ie not yet 100% certain,
 304 // and confirmed later.   Useful if you want to reserve a slot but at the same
 305 // time let other people know that there's a possibility it may not be needed.
 306 $confirmation_enabled = TRUE;
 307 
 308 // The default confirmation status for new bookings.  (TRUE: confirmed, FALSE: tentative)
 309 // Only used if $confirmation_enabled is TRUE.   If $confirmation_enabled is
 310 // FALSE, then all new bookings are confirmed automatically.
 311 $confirmed_default = TRUE;

 320 $default_type = "I";

/dbsys.inc

   1 <?php
   2 declare(strict_types=1);
   3 namespace MRBS;
   4 
   5 // Returns the full table name including schema and prefix for a given table.
   6 // Needs to be dynamic rather than static in case we are running a multisite
   7 // installation and want to switch sites, eg during a database upgrade.
   8 
   9 use MRBS\DB\DB;
  10 use MRBS\DB\DBFactory;
  11 use MRBS\Errors\Errors;
  12 use PDO;
  13 
  14 function _tbl(string $short_name, bool $include_schema=true) : string
  15 {
  16   global $dbsys, $db_tbl_prefix, $db_schema;
  17 
  18   // Do some sanity checking
  19   if (!isset($short_name))
  20   {
  21     throw new \Exception('$short_name not set.');
  22   }
  23 
  24   $result = $db_tbl_prefix . $short_name;
  25 
  26   // Prepend the schema name if set and form a qualified name for all databases
  27   // other than MySQL, which is one of the few that doesn't support schemas.
  28   // (Although in practice this means PostgreSQL at the moment, it's possible that
  29   // in the future support for more databases may be added)
  30   if ($include_schema && (mb_strpos($dbsys, 'mysql') === false) && isset($db_schema))
  31   {
  32     $result = $db_schema . '.' . $result;
  33   }
  34 
  35   return $result;
  36 }
  37 
  38 
  39 function get_table_short_name(string $table) : string
  40 {
  41   global $db_tbl_prefix;
  42 
  43   // Get everything after the last '.', ie strip off any database
  44   // and schema names
  45   if (false !== ($pos = mb_strrpos($table, '.')))
  46   {
  47     $result = mb_substr($table, $pos + 1);
  48   }
  49   else
  50   {
  51     $result = $table;
  52   }
  53 
  54   // Strip the prefix off the table name
  55   return mb_substr($result, mb_strlen($db_tbl_prefix));
  56 }
  57 
  58 
  59 // Convenience wrapper function to provide access to a DB object for
  60 // default MRBS database
  61 function db() : DB
  62 {
  63   global $db_persist, $db_host, $db_login, $db_password,
  64          $db_database, $db_port, $dbsys, $db_options;
  65 
  66   static $db_obj = null;
  67 
  68   try
  69   {
  70     if (is_null($db_obj))
  71     {
  72       throw new \Exception("DB object not yet created");
  73     }
  74     // Check to see if the connection is still there.  If it isn't - perhaps because it
  75     // has been timed out, eg by MySQL's wait_timeout - then we throw an exception which
  76     // will cause us to re-create a connection.
  77     // (Note that we cannot try a "SELECT 1" query or something similar to check if the
  78     // connection is still there, because if it is then the query will cause the last insert
  79     // id to be lost.)
  80     // TODO: sometimes the symptom of a lost connection is a warning of the form "Packets
  81     // TODO: out of order. Expected 1 received 0. Packet size=145".  Need to work out why
  82     // TODO: this happens and do something about it.
  83     if ($db_obj->getAttribute(PDO::ATTR_SERVER_INFO) == 'MySQL server has gone away')
  84     {
  85       // On most recent versions of PHP the call to getAttribute() on a lost connection will
  86       // throw an exception anyway, but just in case it doesn't we'll throw one. See
  87       // https://stackoverflow.com/questions/21595402/php-pdo-how-to-get-the-current-connection-status
  88       throw new \Exception('MySQL server has gone away');
  89     }
  90   }
  91   catch (\Exception $e)
  92   {
  93     try
  94     {
  95       $db_obj = DBFactory::create(
  96         $dbsys,
  97         $db_host,
  98         $db_login,
  99         $db_password,
 100         $db_database,
 101         (bool)$db_persist,
 102         $db_port,
 103         $db_options
 104       );
 105     }
 106     catch (\Exception $e)
 107     {
 108       trigger_error($e->getMessage(), E_USER_WARNING);
 109       Errors::fatalError(get_vocab('fatal_db_error'));
 110     }
 111   }
 112 
 113   return $db_obj;
 114 }
 115 
 116 
 117 // Returns the db schema version as recorded in the database.   If there is no version
 118 // recorded then returns 0.  If $local is true then the local db schema version is returned.
 119 function db_schema_version(DB $handle, bool $local=false) : int
 120 {
 121   if ($handle->table_exists(_tbl('variables')))
 122   {
 123     $sql_params = [':variable_name' => ($local) ? 'local_db_version' : 'db_version'];
 124     $sql = "SELECT variable_content
 125               FROM " . _tbl('variables') . "
 126              WHERE variable_name=:variable_name";
 127     $result = $handle->query1($sql, $sql_params);
 128   }
 129   else
 130   {
 131     // Default version is 0, before we had schema versions
 132     $result = 0;
 133   }
 134 
 135   return max($result, 0);
 136 }

   1 <?php

   3 namespace MRBS;
   4 
   5 use MRBS\Errors\Errors;

   7 use MRBS\Form\ElementInputSubmit;
   8 use MRBS\Form\ElementP;

  10 use MRBS\Form\FieldInputPassword;
  11 use MRBS\Form\FieldInputSubmit;
  12 use MRBS\Form\FieldInputText;
  13 use MRBS\Form\FieldSelect;
  14 use MRBS\Form\Form;
  15 
  16 /*****************************************************************************\
  17 *                                                                            *
  18 *   File name     edit_users.php                                             *
  19 *                                                                            *
  20 *   Description   Edit the user database                                     *
  21 *                                                                            *
  22 *   Notes         Designed to be easily extensible:                          *
  23 *                 Adding more fields for each user does not require          *
  24 *                 modifying the editor code. Only to add the fields in       *
  25 *                 the database creation code.                                *
  26 *                                                                            *
  27 *                 An admin rights model is used where the level (an          *
  28 *                 integer between 0 and $max_level) denotes rights:          *
  29 *                      0:  no rights                                         *
  30 *                      1:  an ordinary user                                  *
  31 *                      2+: admins, with increasing rights.   Designed to     *
  32 *                          allow more granularity of admin rights, for       *
  33 *                          example by having booking admins, user admins     *
  34 *                          snd system admins.  (System admins might be       *
  35 *                          necessary in the future if, for example, some     *
  36 *                          parameters currently in the config file are      *
  37 *                          made editable from MRBS)                          *
  38 *                                                                            *
  39 *                 Only admins with at least user editing rights (level >=    *
  40 *                 $min_user_editing_level) can edit other users, and they    *
  41 *                 cannot edit users with a higher level than themselves      *
  42 *                                                                            *
  43 *                                                                            *
  44 \*****************************************************************************/
  45 
  46 require "defaultincludes.inc";
  47 
  48 if (!auth()->canCreateUsers())
  49 {
  50   // You shouldn't be here unless you can create users
  51   location_header('index.php');
  52 }
  53 
  54 // Get non-standard form variables
  55 $action = get_form_var('action', 'string');
  56 $id = get_form_var('id', 'int');
  57 $password0 = get_form_var('password0', 'string', null, INPUT_POST);
  58 $password1 = get_form_var('password1', 'string', null, INPUT_POST);
  59 $invalid_email = get_form_var('invalid_email', 'int');
  60 $name_empty = get_form_var('name_empty', 'int');
  61 $name_not_unique = get_form_var('name_not_unique', 'int');
  62 $taken_name = get_form_var('taken_name', 'string');
  63 $pwd_not_match = get_form_var('pwd_not_match', 'string');
  64 $pwd_invalid = get_form_var('pwd_invalid', 'string');
  65 $invalid_dates = get_form_var('invalid_dates', 'array');
  66 $datatable = get_form_var('datatable', 'int');  // Will only be set if we're using DataTables
  67 $back_button = get_form_var('back_button', 'string');
  68 $delete_button = get_form_var('delete_button', 'string');
  69 $edit_button = get_form_var('edit_button', 'string');
  70 $update_button = get_form_var('update_button', 'string');
  71 
  72 if (isset($back_button))
  73 {
  74   unset($action);
  75 }
  76 elseif (isset($delete_button))
  77 {
  78   $action = 'delete';
  79 }
  80 elseif (isset($edit_button))
  81 {
  82   $action = 'edit';
  83 }
  84 elseif (isset($update_button))
  85 {
  86   $action = 'update';
  87 }
  88 
  89 $is_ajax = is_ajax();
  90 
  91 // Checks whether the current user can view the target user
  92 function can_view_user($target)
  93 {
  94   global $auth, $min_user_viewing_level;
  95 
  96   $mrbs_user = session()->getCurrentUser();
  97 
  98   // You can only see this user if you are logged in and (a) we allow everybody to see all
  99   // users or (b) you are an admin or (c) you are this user
 100   if (!isset($mrbs_user))
 101   {
 102     return false;
 103   }
 104 
 105   return (!$auth['only_admin_can_see_other_users']  ||
 106           ($mrbs_user->level >= $min_user_viewing_level) ||
 107           (strcasecmp_locale($mrbs_user->username, $target) === 0));
 108 }
 109 
 110 
 111 // Checks whether the current user can edit the target user
 112 function can_edit_user($target)
 113 {
 114   $mrbs_user = session()->getCurrentUser();
 115 
 116   return (is_user_admin() || (isset($mrbs_user) && strcasecmp_locale($mrbs_user->username, $target) === 0));
 117 }
 118 
 119 
 120 function output_row($row)
 121 {
 122   global $is_ajax, $json_data;
 123   global $fields, $ignore_columns, $select_options;
 124 
 125   $values = array();
 126 
 127   // First column, which is the display name
 128   // Make sure we've got a display name.  If not, use the username.
 129   if (!isset($row['display_name']) || (trim($row['display_name']) === ''))
 130   {
 131     $row['display_name'] = $row['name'];
 132   }
 133   // You can only edit a user if you have sufficient admin rights, or else if that user is yourself
 134   if (can_edit_user($row['name']))
 135   {
 136     $form = new Form(Form::METHOD_POST);
 137     $form->setAttributes(array('action' => multisite(this_page())));
 138     $form->addHiddenInput('id', $row['id']);
 139     $submit = new ElementInputSubmit();
 140     $submit->setAttributes(array('class' => 'link',
 141                                  'name'  => 'edit_button',
 142                                  'value' => $row['display_name']));
 143     $form->addElement($submit);
 144     $display_name_value = $form->toHTML();
 145   }
 146   else
 147   {
 148     $display_name_value = "<span class=\"normal\">" . escape_html($row['display_name']) . "</span>";
 149   }
 150 
 151   $sortname = get_sortable_name($row['display_name']);
 152   // TODO: move the data-order attribute up into the <td> and get rid of the <span>
 153   $values[] = '<span data-order="' . escape_html($sortname) . '"></span>' . $display_name_value;
 154 
 155   // Then the username
 156   $values[] = '<span class="normal">' . escape_html($row['name']) . '</span>';
 157 
 158   // Other columns
 159   foreach ($fields as $field)
 160   {
 161     $key = $field['name'];
 162     if (!in_array($key, $ignore_columns))
 163     {
 164       $col_value = $row[$key];
 165 
 166       // If you are not a user admin then you are only allowed to see the last_updated
 167       // and last_login times for yourself.
 168       if (in_array($key, array('timestamp', 'last_login')) &&
 169           !can_edit_user($row['name']))
 170       {
 171         $col_value = null;
 172       }
 173 
 174       switch($key)
 175       {
 176         // special treatment for some fields
 177         case 'level':
 178           // the level field contains a code and we want to display a string
 179           // (but we put the code in a span for sorting)
 180           $values[] = '<span title="' . escape_html($col_value) . '"></span>' .
 181                       "<div class=\"string\">" . get_vocab("level_$col_value") . "</div>";
 182           break;
 183         case 'email':
 184           // we don't want to truncate the email address
 185           if (isset($col_value) && ($col_value !== ''))
 186           {
 187             $escaped_email = escape_html($col_value);
 188             $values[] = "<div class=\"string\">\n" .
 189                         "<a href=\"mailto:$escaped_email\">$escaped_email</a>\n" .
 190                         "</div>\n";
 191           }
 192           else
 193           {
 194             $values[] = '';
 195           }
 196           break;
 197         case 'timestamp':
 198           // Use the 'last_updated' value because it will have been converted
 199           // from 'timestamp' using the correct timezone, ie the timezone of
 200           // the database server.
 201           $col_value = $row['last_updated'];
 202           // Fall through
 203         case 'last_login':
 204           // Put the UNIX timestamp in a span so that the JavaScript can sort it properly.
 205           // If there isn't a date then put '0' in the title, otherwise DataTables throws
 206           // a TypeError if you try and sort the column.
 207           $values[] = '<span title="' . (($col_value) ? escape_html($col_value) : '0') . '"></span>' .
 208                       (($col_value) ? escape_html(time_date_string($col_value)) : '');
 209           break;
 210         default:
 211           // Where there's an associative array of options, display
 212           // the value rather than the key
 213           if (isset($select_options["users.$key"]) &&
 214               is_assoc($select_options["users.$key"]))
 215           {
 216             if (isset($row[$key]) && isset($select_options["users.$key"][$row[$key]]))
 217             {
 218               $col_value = $select_options["users.$key"][$row[$key]];
 219             }
 220             else
 221             {
 222               $col_value = '';
 223             }
 224             $values[] = "<div class=\"string\">" . escape_html($col_value) . "</div>";
 225           }
 226           elseif (($field['nature'] == 'boolean') ||
 227               (($field['nature'] == 'integer') && isset($field['length']) && ($field['length'] <= 2)) )
 228           {
 229             // booleans: represent by a checkmark
 230             $values[] = (!empty($col_value)) ? "&check;" : '';
 231           }
 232           elseif (($field['nature'] == 'integer') && isset($field['length']) && ($field['length'] > 2))
 233           {
 234             // integer values
 235             $values[] = $col_value;
 236           }
 237           else
 238           {
 239              // strings
 240             if (!isset($col_value))
 241             {
 242               $col_value = '';
 243             }
 244             $values[] = "<div class=\"string\" title=\"" . escape_html($col_value) . "\">" .
 245                         escape_html($col_value) . "</div>";
 246           }
 247           break;
 248       }  // end switch
 249     }
 250   }  // end foreach
 251 
 252   if ($is_ajax)
 253   {
 254     $json_data['aaData'][] = $values;
 255   }
 256   else
 257   {
 258     echo "<tr>\n<td>\n";
 259     echo implode("</td>\n<td>", $values);
 260     echo "</td>\n</tr>\n";
 261   }
 262 }

 265 function get_field_level($params, $disabled=false)
 266 {
 267   global $level;
 268 
 269   // Only display options up to and including one's own level (you can't upgrade yourself).
 270   // If you're not some kind of admin then the select will also be disabled.
 271   // (Note - disabling individual options doesn't work in older browsers, eg IE6)
 272   $options = array();
 273 
 274   for ($i=0; $i<=$level; $i++)
 275   {
 276     $options[$i] = get_vocab("level_$i");
 277   }
 278 
 279   $field = new FieldSelect();
 280   $field->setLabel($params['label'])
 281         ->setControlAttributes(array('name' => $params['name'],
 282                                      'disabled' => $disabled))
 283         ->addSelectOptions($options, $params['value'], true);
 284 
 285   return $field;
 286 }

 289 function get_field_name($params, $disabled=false)
 290 {
 291   $field = new FieldInputText();
 292 
 293   $field->setLabel($params['label'])
 294         ->setControlAttributes(array('name'     => $params['name'],
 295                                      'value'    => $params['value'],
 296                                      'disabled' => $disabled,
 297                                      'required' => true,
 298                                      'pattern'  => REGEX_TEXT_POS));
 299 
 300   if (null !== ($maxlength = maxlength('users.name')))
 301   {
 302     $field->setControlAttribute('maxlength', $maxlength);
 303   }
 304 
 305   // If the name field is disabled we need to add a hidden input, because
 306   // otherwise it won't be posted.
 307   if ($disabled)
 308   {
 309     $field->addHiddenInput($params['name'], $params['value']);
 310   }
 311 
 312   return $field;
 313 }

 315 
 316 function get_field_display_name($params, $disabled=false)
 317 {
 318   $field = new FieldInputText();
 319 
 320   $field->setLabel($params['label'])
 321     ->setControlAttributes(array('name'     => $params['name'],
 322                                  'value'    => $params['value'],
 323                                  'disabled' => $disabled,
 324                                  'required' => true,
 325                                  'pattern'  => REGEX_TEXT_POS));
 326 
 327   if (null !== ($maxlength = maxlength('users.display_name')))
 328   {
 329     $field->setControlAttribute('maxlength', $maxlength);
 330   }
 331 
 332   // If the name field is disabled we need to add a hidden input, because
 333   // otherwise it won't be posted.
 334   if ($disabled)
 335   {
 336     $field->addHiddenInput($params['name'], $params['value']);
 337   }
 338 
 339   return $field;
 340 }

 360 
 361 function get_field_custom($custom_field, $params, $disabled=false)
 362 {
 363   global $select_options, $datalist_options, $is_mandatory_field, $pattern;
 364   global $text_input_max;
 365 
 366   // TODO: have a common way of generating custom fields for all tables
 367 
 368   // Output a checkbox if it's a boolean or integer <= 2 bytes (which we will
 369   // assume are intended to be booleans)
 370   if (($custom_field['nature'] == 'boolean') ||
 371       (($custom_field['nature'] == 'integer') && isset($custom_field['length']) && ($custom_field['length'] <= 2)) )
 372   {
 373     $class = 'FieldInputCheckbox';
 374   }
 375   // Otherwise check if it's an integer field
 376   elseif ((($custom_field['nature'] == 'integer') && ($custom_field['length'] > 2)) ||
 377           ($custom_field['nature'] == 'decimal'))
 378   {
 379     $class = 'FieldInputNumber';
 380   }
 381   elseif (!empty($select_options[$params['field']]))
 382   {
 383     $class = 'FieldSelect';
 384   }
 385   elseif (!empty($datalist_options[$params['field']]))
 386   {
 387     $class = 'FieldInputDatalist';
 388   }
 389   // Output a textarea if it's a character string longer than the limit for a
 390   // text input
 391   elseif (($custom_field['nature'] == 'character') && isset($custom_field['length']) && ($custom_field['length'] > $text_input_max))
 392   {
 393     $class = 'FieldTextarea';
 394   }
 395   elseif ($custom_field['type'] == 'date')
 396   {
 397     $class = 'FieldInputDate';
 398   }
 399   else
 400   {
 401     $class = 'FieldInputText';
 402   }
 403 
 404   $full_class = __NAMESPACE__ . "\\Form\\$class";
 405   $field = new $full_class();
 406   $field->setLabel($params['label'])
 407         ->setControlAttribute('name', $params['name']);
 408 
 409   if ($custom_field['nature'] == 'decimal')
 410   {
 411     list( , $decimal_places) = explode(',', $custom_field['length']);
 412     $decimal_places = intval($decimal_places);
 413     $step = pow(10, -$decimal_places);
 414     $step = number_format($step, $decimal_places);
 415     $field->setControlAttribute('step', $step);
 416   }
 417 
 418   if (!empty($is_mandatory_field[$params['field']]))
 419   {
 420     $field->setControlAttribute('required', true);
 421   }
 422 
 423   if ($disabled)
 424   {
 425     $field->setControlAttribute('disabled', true);
 426     $field->addHiddenInput($params['name'], $params['value']);
 427   }
 428 
 429   // Pattern attribute, if any
 430   if (!empty($pattern[$params['field']]))
 431   {
 432     $field->setControlAttribute('pattern', $pattern[$params['field']]);
 433     // And any custom error messages
 434     $tag = $params['field'] . '.oninvalid';
 435     $oninvalid_text = get_vocab($tag);
 436     if (isset($oninvalid_text) && ($oninvalid_text !== $tag))
 437     {
 438       $field->setControlAttribute('oninvalid', "this.setCustomValidity('". escape_js($oninvalid_text) . "')");
 439       // Need to clear the invalid message
 440       $field->setControlAttribute('onchange', "this.setCustomValidity('')");
 441     }
 442   }
 443 
 444   switch ($class)
 445   {
 446     case 'FieldInputCheckbox':
 447       $field->setChecked($params['value']);
 448       break;
 449 
 450     case 'FieldSelect':
 451       $options = $select_options[$params['field']];
 452       $field->addSelectOptions($options, $params['value']);
 453       break;
 454 
 455     case 'FieldInputDate':
 456     case 'FieldInputNumber':
 457       $field->setControlAttribute('value', $params['value']);
 458       break;
 459 
 460     case 'FieldInputDatalist':
 461       $options = $datalist_options[$params['field']];
 462       $field->addDatalistOptions($options);
 463       // Drop through
 464 
 465     case 'FieldInputText':
 466       if (!empty($is_mandatory_field[$params['field']]))
 467       {
 468         // Set a pattern as well as required to prevent a string of whitespace
 469         $field->setControlAttribute('pattern', REGEX_TEXT_POS);
 470       }
 471       // Drop through
 472 
 473     case 'FieldTextarea':
 474       if ($class == 'FieldTextarea')
 475       {
 476         $field->setControlText($params['value'] ?? '');
 477       }
 478       else
 479       {
 480         $field->setControlAttribute('value', $params['value']);
 481       }
 482       if (null !== ($maxlength = maxlength($params['field'])))
 483       {
 484         $field->setControlAttribute('maxlength', $maxlength);
 485       }
 486       break;
 487 
 488     default:
 489       throw new \Exception("Unknown class '$class'");
 490       break;
 491   }
 492 
 493   return $field;
 494 }

 497 function get_fieldset_password($id=null, $disabled=false)
 498 {
 499   $fieldset = new ElementFieldset();

 501   // If this is an existing user then give them the message about optionally
 502   // changing their password.

 527 // Adds the submit buttons.
 528 //    $delete               If true, make the second button a Delete button instead of a Back button
 529 //    $disabled             If true, disable the Delete button
 530 //    $last_admin_warning   If true, add a warning about editing the last admin
 531 function get_fieldset_submit_buttons(?int $user_id, $delete=false, $disabled=false, $last_admin_warning=false)
 532 {
 533   global $auth;
 534 
 535   // Check whether the user can be deleted and if so what message to use
 536   if ($delete && isset($user_id))
 537   {
 538     $user = auth()->getUserByUserId($user_id);
 539     // If the user has bookings of some form in the system, then either
 540     // disallow the deletion, depending on the config setting, or provide
 541     // a different warning message.
 542     if (isset($user) && $user->isInBookings())
 543     {
 544       if ($auth['db']['prevent_deletion_of_users_in_bookings'])
 545       {
 546         $delete = false;
 547       }
 548       else
 549       {
 550         $message = get_vocab("confirm_delete_user_plus");
 551       }
 552     }
 553     else
 554     {
 555       $message = get_vocab("confirm_delete_user");
 556     }
 557   }
 558 
 559   $fieldset = new ElementFieldset();
 560 
 561   if ($last_admin_warning)
 562   {
 563     $p = new ElementP();
 564     $p->setText(get_vocab('warning_last_admin'));
 565     $fieldset->addElement($p);
 566   }
 567 
 568   $field = new FieldInputSubmit();
 569 
 570   $button = new ElementInputSubmit();
 571 
 572   if ($delete)
 573   {
 574     $name = 'delete_button';
 575     $value = get_vocab('delete_user');
 576   }
 577   else
 578   {
 579     $name = 'back_button';
 580     $value = get_vocab('back');
 581   }
 582   $button->setAttributes(array('name'           => $name,
 583                                'value'          => $value,
 584                                'disabled'       => $disabled,
 585                                'formnovalidate' => true));
 586 
 587   if ($delete)
 588   {
 589     $button->setAttribute('onclick', "return confirm('" . escape_js($message) . "');");
 590   }
 591 
 592   $field->setAttribute('class', 'submit_buttons')
 593         ->setLabelAttribute('class', 'no_suffix')
 594         ->addLabelElement($button)
 595         ->setControlAttributes(array('class' => 'default_action',
 596                                      'name'  => 'update_button',
 597                                      'value' => get_vocab('save')));
 598 
 599   // Remove the 'for' attribute which will automatically have been set by
 600   // setControlAttributes().  It is unnecessary and leaving it in results in
 601   // an HTML5 validation error.
 602   $field->removeLabelAttribute('for');
 603 
 604   $fieldset->addElement($field);
 605 
 606   return $fieldset;
 607 }
