 609 
 610 // Set up for Ajax.   We need to know whether we're capable of dealing with Ajax
 611 // requests, which will only be if the browser is using DataTables.    We also need
 612 // to initialise the JSON data array.
 613 $ajax_capable = $datatable;
 614 
 615 if ($is_ajax)
 616 {
 617   $json_data['aaData'] = array();
 618 }
 619 
 620 // Get the information about the fields in the users table
 621 $fields = db()->field_info(_tbl('users'));
 622 
 623 $users = auth()->getUsers();
 624 
 625 
 626 /*---------------------------------------------------------------------------*\
 627 |                         Authenticate the current user                         |
 628 \*---------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
 629 
 630 // Check the CSRF token if we're going to be altering the database
 631 if (isset($action) && in_array($action, array('delete', 'update')))
 632 {
 633   Form::checkToken();
 634 }
 635 
 636 $initial_user_creation = false;
 637 
 638 if (count($users) > 0)
 639 {
 640   $mrbs_user = session()->getCurrentUser();
 641   $level = (isset($mrbs_user)) ? $mrbs_user->level : 0;
 642   // Check the user is authorised for this page
 643   checkAuthorised(this_page());
 644 }
 645 else
 646 // We've just created the table.   Assume the person doing this IS an administrator
 647 // and then send them through to the screen to add the first user (which we'll force
 648 // to be an admin)
 649 {
 650   $initial_user_creation = true;
 651   if (!isset($action))   // second time through it will be set to "update"
 652   {
 653     $action = "add";
 654     $id = null;
 655   }
 656   $level = $max_level;
 657 }
 658 
 659 
 660 /*---------------------------------------------------------------------------*\
 661 |             Edit a given entry - 1st phase: Get the user input.             |
 662 \*---------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
 663 
 664 if (isset($action) && ( ($action == "edit") or ($action == "add") ))
 665 {
 666 
 667   if (isset($id))
 668   {
 669     // If it's an existing user then get the data from the database
 670     $sql = "SELECT *
 671               FROM " . _tbl('users') . "
 672              WHERE id=?";
 673     $result = db()->query($sql, array($id));
 674     $data = $result->next_row_keyed();
 675     unset($result);
 676     // Check that we've got a valid result.   We should do normally, but if somebody alters
 677     // the id parameter in the query string then we won't.   If the result is invalid, go somewhere
 678     // safe.
 679     if (!$data)
 680     {
 681       trigger_error("Invalid user id $id", E_USER_NOTICE);
 682       location_header(this_page());
 683     }
 684   }
 685   if (!isset($id) || (!$data))
 686   {
 687     // Otherwise try and get the data from the query string, and if it's
 688     // not there set the default to be blank.  (The data will be in the
 689     // query string if there was an error on validating the data after it
 690     // had been submitted.   We want to preserve the user's original values
 691     // so that they don't have to re-type them).
 692     foreach ($fields as $field)
 693     {
 694       $type = get_form_var_type($field);
 695       $value = get_form_var($field['name'], $type);
 696       $data[$field['name']] = (isset($value)) ? $value : "";
 697     }
 698   }
 699 
 700   // First make sure the user is authorized
 701   if (!$initial_user_creation && !can_edit_user($data['name']))
 702   {
 703     showAccessDenied();
 704     exit();
 705   }
 706 
 707   $context = array(
 708       'view'      => $view,
 709       'view_all'  => $view_all,
 710       'year'      => $year,
 711       'month'     => $month,
 712       'day'       => $day,
 713       'area'      => isset($area) ? $area : null,
 714       'room'      => isset($room) ? $room : null
 715     );
 716 
 717   print_header($context);
 718 
 719   echo "<h2>";
 720   if ($initial_user_creation)
 721   {
 722     echo get_vocab('no_users_initial');
 723   }
 724   else
 725   {
 726     echo ($action == 'edit') ? get_vocab('edit_user') : get_vocab('add_new_user');
 727   }
 728   echo "</h2>\n";
 729 
 730   if ($initial_user_creation)
 731   {
 732     echo "<p>" . get_vocab('no_users_create_first_admin') . "</p>\n";
 733   }
 734 
 735   // Find out how many admins are left in the table - it's disastrous if the last one is deleted,
 736   // or admin rights are removed!
 737   if ($action == "edit")
 738   {
 739     $sql = "SELECT COUNT(*)
 740               FROM " . _tbl('users') . "
 741              WHERE level=?";
 742     $n_admins = db()->query1($sql, array($max_level));
 743     $editing_last_admin = ($n_admins <= 1) && ($data['level'] == $max_level);
 744   }
 745   else
 746   {
 747     $editing_last_admin = false;
 748   }
 749 
 750   // Error messages
 751   if (!empty($invalid_email))
 752   {
 753     echo "<p class=\"error\">" . get_vocab('invalid_email') . "</p>\n";
 754   }
 755   if (!empty($name_not_unique))
 756   {
 757     echo "<p class=\"error\">'" . escape_html($taken_name) . "' " . get_vocab('name_not_unique') . "<p>\n";
 758   }
 759   if (!empty($name_empty))
 760   {
 761     echo "<p class=\"error\">" . get_vocab('name_empty') . "<p>\n";
 762   }
 763   if (!empty($invalid_dates))
 764   {
 765     foreach ($invalid_dates as $field)
 766     {
 767       echo "<p class=\"error\">" . get_vocab('invalid_date', get_loc_field_name(_tbl('users'), $field)) . "<p>\n";
 768     }
 769   }
 770 
 771   // Now do any password error messages
 772   if (!empty($pwd_not_match))
 773   {
 774     echo "<p class=\"error\">" . get_vocab("passwords_not_eq") . "</p>\n";
 775   }
 776   if (!empty($pwd_invalid))
 777   {
 778     echo "<p class=\"error\">" . get_vocab("password_invalid") . "</p>\n";
 779     if (isset($pwd_policy))
 780     {
 781       echo "<ul class=\"error\">\n";
 782       foreach ($pwd_policy as $rule => $value)
 783       {
 784         if ($value != 0)
 785         {
 786           echo "<li>" . get_vocab('policy_' . $rule, $value) . "</li>\n";
 787         }
 788       }
 789       echo "</ul>\n";
 790     }
 791   }
 792 
 793   $form = new Form(Form::METHOD_POST);
 794 
 795   $form->setAttributes(array('id'     => 'form_edit_users',
 796                              'class'  => 'standard',
 797                              'action' => multisite(this_page())));
 798 
 799   if (isset($id))
 800   {
 801     $form->addHiddenInput('id', $id);
 802   }
 803 
 804   $fieldset = new ElementFieldset();
 805 
 806   foreach ($fields as $field)
 807   {
 808     $key = $field['name'];
 809 
 810     $params = array('label' => get_loc_field_name(_tbl('users'), $key),
 811                     'name'  => VAR_PREFIX . $key,
 812                     'value' => $data[$key]);
 813 
 814     $disabled = !$initial_user_creation &&
 815                 !is_user_admin() &&
 816                 in_array($key, $auth['db']['protected_fields']);
 817 
 818     switch ($key)
 819     {
 820       case 'id':            // We've already got this in a hidden input
 821       case 'password_hash': // We don't want to do anything with this
 822       case 'timestamp':     // Nor this
 823       case 'last_login':
 824       case 'reset_key_hash':
 825       case 'reset_key_expiry':
 826         break;
 827 
 828       case 'level':
 829         if ($action == 'add')
 830         {
 831           // If we're creating a new user and it's the very first user, then they
 832           // should have maximum rights.  Otherwise make them an ordinary user.
 833           $params['value'] = ($initial_user_creation) ? $max_level : 1;
 834         }
 835         // Work out whether the level select input should be disabled (NB you can't make a <select> readonly)
 836         // We don't want the user to be able to change the level if (a) it's the first user being created or
 837         // (b) it's the last admin left or (c) they don't have admin rights
 838         $level_disabled = $initial_user_creation || $editing_last_admin || $disabled;
 839         $fieldset->addElement(get_field_level($params, $level_disabled));
 840         // Add a hidden input if the field is disabled
 841         if ($level_disabled)
 842         {
 843           $form->addHiddenInput($params['name'], $params['value']);
 844         }
 845         break;
 846 
 847       case 'name':
 848         $fieldset->addElement(get_field_name($params, $disabled));
 849         break;
 850 
 851       case 'display_name':
 852         $fieldset->addElement(get_field_display_name($params, $disabled));
 853         break;
 854 
 855       case 'email':
 856         $fieldset->addElement(get_field_email($params, $disabled));
 857         break;
 858 
 859       default:
 860         $params['field'] = "users.$key";
 861         $fieldset->addElement(get_field_custom($field, $params, $disabled));
 862         break;
 863 
 864     }
 865   }
 866 
 867   // Now the password fields
 868   $disabled = !$initial_user_creation &&
 869               !is_user_admin() &&
 870               in_array('password_hash', $auth['db']['protected_fields']);
 871 
 872   $form->addElement($fieldset)
 873        ->addElement(get_fieldset_password($id, $disabled));
 874 
 875   // Administrators get the right to delete users, but only those at the
 876   // the same level as them or lower.  Otherwise present a Back button.
 877   $delete = isset($id) &&
 878             is_user_admin() &&
 879             ($level >= $data['level']);
 880 
 881   // Don't let the last admin be deleted, otherwise you'll be locked out.
 882   $button_disabled = $delete && $editing_last_admin;
 883 
 884   $form->addElement(get_fieldset_submit_buttons($id, $delete, $button_disabled, $editing_last_admin));
 885 
 886   $form->render();
 887 
 888   // Print footer and exit
 889   print_footer();
 890   exit;
 891 }
 892 
 893 /*---------------------------------------------------------------------------*\
 894 |             Edit a given entry - 2nd phase: Update the database.            |
 895 \*---------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
 896 
 897 if (isset($action) && ($action == "update"))
 898 {
 899   // If you haven't got the rights to do this, then exit
 900   if (isset($mrbs_user))
 901   {
 902     $sql = "SELECT id
 903               FROM " . _tbl('users') . "
 904              WHERE name=?
 905              LIMIT 1";
 906     $my_id = db()->query1($sql, array(mb_strtolower($mrbs_user->username)));
 907   }
 908   else
 909   {
 910     $my_id = null;
 911   }
 912 
 913   // You are only allowed to do this if (a) you're creating the first user or
 914   // (b) you are a user admin or (c) you are editing your own details
 915   if (!$initial_user_creation &&
 916       !is_user_admin() &&
 917       (!isset($my_id) || ($id != $my_id )))
 918   {
 919     // It shouldn't normally be possible to get here.
 920     trigger_error("Attempt made to update a user without sufficient rights.", E_USER_NOTICE);
 921     location_header('edit_users.php');
 922   }
 923 
 924   // otherwise go ahead and update the database
 925   $values = array();
 926   $q_string = (isset($id)) ? "action=edit" : "action=add";
 927   foreach ($fields as $index => $field)
 928   {
 929     $fieldname = $field['name'];
 930     $type = get_form_var_type($field);
 931 
 932     if ($fieldname == 'id')
 933     {
 934       // id: don't need to do anything except add the id to the query string;
 935       // the field itself is auto-incremented
 936       if (isset($id))
 937       {
 938         $q_string .= "&id=$id";
 939       }
 940       continue;
 941     }
 942 
 943     // first, get all the other form variables, except for password_hash which is
 944     // a special case,and put them into an array, $values, which  we will use
 945     // for entering into the database assuming we pass validation
 946     if ($fieldname !== 'password_hash')
 947     {
 948       $values[$fieldname] = get_form_var(VAR_PREFIX. $fieldname, $type);
 949       // Turn checkboxes into booleans
 950       if (($fieldname !== 'level') &&
 951           ($field['nature'] == 'integer') &&
 952           isset($field['length']) &&
 953           ($field['length'] <= 2))
 954       {
 955         $values[$fieldname] = (empty($values[$fieldname])) ? 0 : 1;
 956       }
 957 
 958       if (is_string($values[$fieldname]))
 959       {
 960         // Trim the field to remove accidental whitespace
 961         $values[$fieldname] = trim($values[$fieldname]);
 962         // Truncate the field to the maximum length as a precaution.
 963         if (null !== ($maxlength = maxlength("users.$fieldname")))
 964         {
 965           $values[$fieldname] = mb_substr($values[$fieldname], 0, $maxlength);
 966         }
 967       }
 968     }
 969 
 970     // Remove any extra whitespace that may have accidentally been inserted in the display name
 971     if ($fieldname == 'display_name')
 972     {
 973       $values[$fieldname] = remove_extra_whitespace($values[$fieldname]);
 974     }
 975 
 976     // we will also put the data into a query string which we will use for passing
 977     // back to this page if we fail validation.   This will enable us to reload the
 978     // form with the original data so that the user doesn't have to
 979     // re-enter it.  (Instead of passing the data in a query string we
 980     // could pass them as session variables, but at the moment MRBS does
 981     // not rely on PHP sessions).
 982     switch ($fieldname)
 983     {
 984       // some of the fields get special treatment
 985       case 'name':
 986         // name: convert it to lower case
 987         $q_string .= "&$fieldname=" . $values[$fieldname];
 988         $values[$fieldname] = mb_strtolower($values[$fieldname]);
 989         break;
 990       case 'password_hash':
 991         // password: if the password field is blank it means
 992         // that the user doesn't want to change the password
 993         // so don't do anything; otherwise calculate the hash.
 994         // Note: we don't put the password in the query string
 995         // for security reasons.
 996         if ($password0 !== '')
 997         {
 998           $values[$fieldname] = password_hash($password0, PASSWORD_DEFAULT);
 999         }
1000         break;
1001       case 'level':
1002         // level:  set a safe default (lowest level of access)
1003         // if there is no value set
1004         $q_string .= "&$fieldname=" . $values[$fieldname];
1005         if (!isset($values[$fieldname]))
1006         {
1007           $values[$fieldname] = 0;
1008         }
1009         // Check that we are not trying to upgrade our level.    This shouldn't be possible
1010         // but someone might have spoofed the input in the edit form
1011         if ($values[$fieldname] > $level)
1012         {
1013           location_header('edit_users.php');
1014         }
1015         break;
1016       case 'timestamp':
1017       case 'last_login':
1018         // Don't update this field ourselves at all
1019         unset($fields[$index]);
1020         unset($values[$fieldname]);
1021         break;
1022       default:
1023         $q_string .= "&$fieldname=" . $values[$fieldname];
1024         break;
1025     }
1026   }
1027 
1028   // Now do some form validation
1029   $valid_data = true;
1030   foreach ($values as $fieldname => $value)
1031   {
1032     switch ($fieldname)
1033     {
1034       case 'name':
1035         // check that the name is not empty
1036         if ($value === '')
1037         {
1038           $valid_data = false;
1039           $q_string .= "&name_empty=1";
1040         }
1041 
1042         $sql_params = array();
1043 
1044         // Check that the name is unique.
1045         // If it's a new user, then to check to see if there are any rows with that name.
1046         // If it's an update, then check to see if there are any rows with that name, except
1047         // for that user.
1048         $query = "SELECT id
1049                     FROM " . _tbl('users') . "
1050                    WHERE name=?";
1051         $sql_params[] = $value;
1052         if (isset($id))
1053         {
1054           $query .= " AND id != ?";
1055           $sql_params[] = $id;
1056         }
1057         $query .= " LIMIT 1";  // we only want to know if there is at least one instance of the name
1058         $result = db()->query($query, $sql_params);
1059         if ($result->count() > 0)
1060         {
1061           $valid_data = false;
1062           $q_string .= "&name_not_unique=1";
1063           $q_string .= "&taken_name=$value";
1064         }
1065         break;
1066       case 'password_hash':
1067         // check that the two passwords match
1068         if ($password0 != $password1)
1069         {
1070           $valid_data = false;
1071           $q_string .= "&pwd_not_match=1";
1072         }
1073         // check that the password conforms to the password policy
1074         // if it's a new user, or else if it's an existing user
1075         // trying to change their password
1076         if (!isset($id) || (isset($password0) && ($password0 !== '')))
1077         {
1078           if (!auth()->validatePassword($password0))
1079           {
1080             $valid_data = false;
1081             $q_string .= "&pwd_invalid=1";
1082           }
1083         }
1084         break;
1085       case 'email':
1086         // check that the email address is valid
1087         if (isset($value) && ($value !== '') && !validate_email_list($value))
1088         {
1089           $valid_data = false;
1090           $q_string .= "&invalid_email=1";
1091         }
1092         break;
1093     }
1094   }
1095 
1096   // Now check some specific data types
1097   foreach ($fields as $field)
1098   {
1099     // If this a Date type check that we've got a valid date format before
1100     // we get an SQL error.  If the field is nullable and the string is empty
1101     // we assume that the user is trying to nullify the value.
1102     if ($field['type'] == 'date')
1103     {
1104       if ($field['is_nullable'] && (!isset($values[$field['name']]) || ($values[$field['name']] === '')))
1105       {
1106         $values[$field['name']] = null;
1107       }
1108       elseif (!validate_iso_date($values[$field['name']]))
1109       {
1110         $valid_data = false;
1111         $q_string .= "&invalid_dates[]=" . urlencode($field['name']);
1112       }
1113     }
1114   }
1115 
1116 
1117   // if validation failed, go back to this page with the query
1118   // string, which by now has both the error codes and the original
1119   // form values
1120   if (!$valid_data)
1121   {
1122     location_header("edit_users.php?$q_string");
1123   }
1124 
1125 
1126   // If we got here, then we've passed validation and we need to
1127   // enter the data into the database
1128 
1129   $sql_params = array();
1130   $sql_fields = array();
1131 
1132   // For each db column get the value ready for the database
1133   foreach ($fields as $field)
1134   {
1135     $fieldname = $field['name'];
1136 
1137     // Stop ordinary users trying to change fields they are not allowed to
1138     if (!$initial_user_creation &&
1139         !is_user_admin() &&
1140         in_array($fieldname, $auth['db']['protected_fields']))
1141     {
1142       continue;
1143     }
1144 
1145     // If the password field is blank then we are not changing it
1146     if (($fieldname == 'password_hash') && (!isset($values[$fieldname])))
1147     {
1148       continue;
1149     }
1150 
1151     if ($fieldname != 'id')
1152     {
1153       $value = $values[$fieldname];
1154 
1155       // pre-process the field value for SQL
1156       switch ($field['nature'])
1157       {
1158         case 'decimal':
1159         case 'integer':
1160           if (!isset($value) || ($value === ''))
1161           {
1162             // Try and set it to NULL when we can because there will be cases when we
1163             // want to distinguish between NULL and 0 - especially when the field
1164             // is a genuine integer.
1165             $value = ($field['is_nullable']) ? null : 0;
1166           }
1167           break;
1168         default:
1169           // No special handling
1170           break;
1171       }
1172 
1173       /* If we got here, we have a valid, sql-ified value for this field,
1174        * so save it for later */
1175       $sql_fields[$fieldname] = $value;
1176     }
1177   } /* end for each column of user database */
1178 
1179   /* Now generate the SQL operation based on the given array of fields */
1180   if (isset($id))
1181   {
1182     /* if the id exists - then we are editing an existing user, rather than
1183      * creating a new one */
1184 
1185     $assign_array = array();
1186     $operation = "UPDATE " . _tbl('users') . " SET ";
1187 
1188     foreach ($sql_fields as $fieldname => $value)
1189     {
1190       array_push($assign_array, db()->quote($fieldname) . "=?");
1191       $sql_params[] = $value;
1192     }
1193     $operation .= implode(",", $assign_array) . " WHERE id=?";
1194     $sql_params[] = $id;
1195   }
1196   else
1197   {
1198     /* The id field doesn't exist, so we're adding a new user */
1199 
1200     $fields_list = array();
1201     $values_list = array();
1202 
1203     foreach ($sql_fields as $fieldname => $value)
1204     {
1205       array_push($fields_list,$fieldname);
1206       array_push($values_list,'?');
1207       $sql_params[] = $value;
1208     }
1209 
1210     foreach ($fields_list as &$field)
1211     {
1212       $field = db()->quote($field);
1213     }
1214     $operation = "INSERT INTO " . _tbl('users') . " " .
1215       "(". implode(",", $fields_list) . ")" .
1216       " VALUES " . "(" . implode(",", $values_list) . ")";
1217   }
1218 
1219   /* DEBUG lines - check the actual sql statement going into the db */
1220   //echo "Final SQL string: <code>" . escape_html($operation) . "</code>";
1221   //exit;
1222   db()->command($operation, $sql_params);
1223 
1224   /* Success. Redirect to the user list, to remove the form args */
1225   location_header('edit_users.php');
1226 }
1227 
1228 /*---------------------------------------------------------------------------*\
1229 |                                Delete a user                                |
1230 \*---------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
1231 
1232 if (isset($action) && ($action == "delete"))
1233 {
1234   $user = auth()->getUserByUserId($id);
1235 
1236   if (!isset($user))
1237   {
1238     Errors::fatalError("Fatal error while deleting a user");
1239   }
1240 
1241   // You can't delete a user if you're not some kind of admin, and then you can't
1242   // delete someone higher than you.
1243   // You also can't delete a user if MRBS has been configured not to allow the
1244   // deletion of users that appear in bookings in some form.
1245   if (!is_user_admin() || ($level < $user->level) ||
1246       ($auth['db']['prevent_deletion_of_users_in_bookings']) && $user->isInBookings())
1247   {
1248     showAccessDenied();
1249     exit();
1250   }
1251 
1252   $sql = "DELETE FROM " . _tbl('users') . "
1253            WHERE id=?";
1254   db()->command($sql, array($id));
1255 
1256   /* Success. Do not display a message. Simply fall through into the list display. */
1257 }

1263 /* Print the standard MRBS header */
1264 
1265 if (!$is_ajax)

1268     'view'      => $view,

1298 if ($initial_user_creation != 1)   // don't print the user table if there are no users
1299 {
1300   // Display the user data in a table
1301 
1302   // We don't display these columns or they get special treatment
1303   $ignore_columns = array(
1304       'id',
1305       'password_hash',
1306       'name',

1313   if (!is_user_admin())

1316     {
1317       if ($is_private)
1318       {
1319         list($table, $column) = explode('.', $fieldname, 2);
1320         if ($table == 'users')
1321         {
1322           $ignore_columns[] = $column;
1323         }
1324       }
1325     }
1326   }
1327 
1328   if (!$is_ajax)
1329   {
1330     echo "<div id=\"user_list\" class=\"datatable_container\">\n";
1331     echo "<table class=\"admin_table display\" id=\"users_table\">\n";
1332 
1333     // The table header

1335     echo "<tr>";
1336 
1337     // First two columns which are the name and display name
1338     echo '<th><span class="normal" data-type="string">' . get_vocab("users.display_name") . "</span></th>\n";
1339     echo '<th><span class="normal" data-type="string">' . get_vocab("users.name") . "</span></th>\n";
1340 
1341     // Other column headers
1342     foreach ($fields as $field)
1343     {
1344       $fieldname = $field['name'];
1345 
1346       if (!in_array($fieldname, $ignore_columns))
1347       {
1348         $heading = get_loc_field_name(_tbl('users'), $fieldname);
1349         // We give some columns a type data value so that the JavaScript knows how to sort them
1350         switch ($fieldname)
1351         {
1352           case 'level':
1353           case 'timestamp':
1354           case 'last_login':
1355             // TODO: Switch from using title-numeric to just numeric(?)
1356             $heading = '<span class="normal" data-type="title-numeric">' . $heading . '</span>';
1357             break;
1358           default:
1359             if ($field['nature'] == 'character')
1360             {

1362             }
1363             break;

1365         echo '<th id="col_' . escape_html($fieldname) . "\">$heading</th>";
1366       }
1367     }
1368 
1369     echo "</tr>\n";
1370     echo "</thead>\n";
1371 
1372     // The table body
1373     echo "<tbody>\n";
1374   }
1375 
1376   // If we're Ajax capable and this is not an Ajax request then don't output
1377   // the table body, because that's going to be sent later in response to
1378   // an Ajax request
1379   if (!$ajax_capable || $is_ajax)

  17 // Strips out extra whitespace from a string.  Useful for sanitizing
  18 // user input before it is inserted into the database, eg when the
  19 // user has accidentally typed "Joe  Smith" instead of "Joe Smith".
  20 function remove_extra_whitespace(string $string) : string
  21 {
  22   return preg_replace('/\s+/', ' ', $string);
  23 }

  25 
  26 // Constrain an integer to fit a certain type.  Useful for making sure
  27 // that integers will fit within the range for a database type.
  28 // Only 4 byte unsigned integers supported at the moment.
  29 function constrain_int(int $n, int $bytes, bool $unsigned=false) : int
  30 {
  31   if (!$unsigned && ($bytes == 4))
  32   {
  33     $max_limit = 0x7fffffff;
  34     $min_limit = -$max_limit;
  35   }
  36   else
  37   {
  38     throw new \Exception("Other combinations not yet supported");
  39   }
  40 
  41   return max(min($n, $max_limit), $min_limit);
  42 }

  45 // Case-insensitive in_array
  46 // See https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.in-array.php#Hcom89256
  47 function in_arrayi($needle, array $haystack, bool $strict=false) : bool
  48 {
  49   return in_array(mb_strtolower($needle),
  50                   array_map('mb_strtolower', $haystack),
  51                   $strict);
  52 }

  56 // Checks if a string ends with one of an array of given substrings
  57 function str_ends_with_array(string $haystack, array $needles) : bool
  58 {
  59   foreach ($needles as $needle)
  60   {
  61     if (str_ends_with($haystack, $needle))
  62     {
  63       return true;
  64     }
  65   }
  66 
  67   return false;

  71 function generate_token(int $length) : string
  72 {
  73   if (function_exists('random_bytes'))
  74   {
  75     try
  76     {
  77       return bin2hex(random_bytes($length));  // PHP 7 and above
  78     }
  79     catch (\Exception $e)
  80     {
  81       // random_bytes() will throw an Exception if an appropriate source of randomness cannot be found.
  82       // If that happens, just fall through and use one of the other methods.
  83     }
  84   }
  85 
  86   if (function_exists('openssl_random_pseudo_bytes'))
  87   {
  88     return bin2hex(openssl_random_pseudo_bytes($length));
  89   }
  90 
  91   return md5(uniqid((string)rand(), true));
  92 }

  95 // A locale aware version of strcasecmp()
  96 function strcasecmp_locale(string $string1, string $string2) : int
  97 {
  98   // Trivial case
  99   if ($string1 === $string2)
 100   {
 101     return 0;
 102   }
 103 
 104   // Sort the array.  If the order is reversed then $string1 > $string2
 105   // (When this function is being used as a callback for usort, and if the original array
 106   // is sorted in ascending order, which it well might be if it's the result of
 107   // an SQL query with an ORDER BY, then it's fastest to test for $string1 > $string2
 108   // first, as below.)
 109   $original_array = array($string1, $string2);
 110   $array = $original_array;
 111   asort($array,SORT_LOCALE_STRING | SORT_FLAG_CASE);
 112   if ($array !== $original_array)
 113   {
 114     return 1;
 115   }
 116   // Otherwise, flip the array and try again.  If the order is reversed then $string2 > $string1
 117   $original_array = array($string2, $string1);
 118   $array = $original_array;
 119   asort($array,SORT_LOCALE_STRING | SORT_FLAG_CASE);
 120   if ($array !== $original_array)
 121   {
 122     return -1;
 123   }
 124   // Otherwise they must be equal
 125   return 0;
 126 }

 129 // Returns a name in the format last_name first_name for sorting
 130 function get_sortable_name(?string $name) : ?string
 131 {
 132   global $sort_users_by_last_name;
 133 
 134   if (!isset($name))
 135   {
 136     return null;
 137   }
 138 
 139   if (empty($sort_users_by_last_name))
 140   {
 141     return $name;
 142   }
 143 
 144   // Look for anything in brackets (ordinary or square) at the
 145   // end of the name and treat it as a suffix.  For example if
 146   // the display name is "Joe Bloggs (visitor)" then the last name
 147   // is really "Bloggs".
 148   $pattern = '/\s*\(.*\)$|[.*]$/';
 149   if (preg_match($pattern, $name, $matches))
 150   {
 151     $suffix = $matches[0];
 152     $name = preg_replace($pattern, '', $name);
 153   }
 154 
 155 
 156   $tokens = explode(' ', $name);
 157 
 158   // Get rid of other whitespace (eg tabs)
 159   $tokens = array_map('trim', $tokens);
 160 
 161   // Get the last name
 162   $result = array_pop($tokens);
 163 
 164   // Add back in the first names
 165   while (null !== ($token = array_shift($tokens)))
 166   {
 167     if ($token !== '') // weeds out multiple spaces in a name
 168     {
 169       $result .= ' ' . $token;
 170     }
 171   }
 172 
 173   // Add back in any suffix
 174   if (isset($suffix))
 175   {
 176     $result .= $suffix;
 177   }
 178 
 179   return $result;
 180 }

 183 function compare_display_names(string $name1, string $name2) : int

 242 // Returns the maximum length, in characters, of a column, or NULL if the maximum
 243 // length is not known.   Should only be called after any database upgrades have been
 244 // performed as the results are stored in a static variable and so the maximum lengths
 245 // may change after an upgrade.  $column is of the form, <table_short_name.column_name>,
 246 // for example, 'area.area_name'.
 247 function maxlength(string $column) : ?int
 248 {
 249   static $maxlengths = array();
 250 
 251   list($table_short_name, $column_name) = explode('.', $column);
 252 
 253   if (!isset($maxlengths[$table_short_name]))
 254   {
 255     $maxlengths[$table_short_name] = array();
 256 
 257     // Check to see if the table exists, as it won't yet if it's about
 258     // to be created as part of an upgrade
 259     if (db()->table_exists(_tbl($table_short_name)))
 260     {
 261       // Find the maximum length of the CHAR and VARCHAR fields (we won't
 262       // worry about TEXT fields)
 263       $field_info = db()->field_info(_tbl($table_short_name));
 264 
 265       foreach ($field_info as $field)
 266       {
 267         if (($field['nature'] == 'character') &&
 268             isset($field['length']) &&
 269             ($field['length'] < 256))
 270         {
 271           $maxlengths[$table_short_name][$field['name']] = (int) $field['length'];
 272         }
 273       }
 274     }
 275   }
 276 
 277   return (isset($maxlengths[$table_short_name][$column_name])) ? $maxlengths[$table_short_name][$column_name] : null;
 278 }
 279 
 280 
 281 // Truncate any fields that have a maximum length as a precaution.
 282 // Although the MAXLENGTH attribute is used in the <input> tag, this can
 283 // sometimes be ignored by the browser, for example by Firefox when
 284 // autocompletion is used.  The user could also edit the HTML and remove
 285 // the MAXLENGTH attribute.    Another problem is that the <datalist> tag
 286 // does not accept a maxlength attribute.  Passing an oversize string to some
 287 // databases (eg some versions of PostgreSQL) results in an SQL error,
 288 // rather than silent truncation of the string.
 289 //
 290 // We truncate to a maximum number of UTF8 characters rather than bytes.
 291 // This is OK in current versions of MySQL and PostgreSQL, though in earler
 292 // versions of MySQL (I haven't checked PostgreSQL) this could cause problems
 293 // as a VARCHAR(n) was n bytes long rather than n characters.
 294 function truncate(string $value, string $column) : string
 295 {
 296   if (null !== ($maxlength = maxlength($column)))
 297   {
 298     return mb_substr($value, 0, $maxlength);
 299   }
 300 
 301   return $value;
 302 }

 305 // Formats a number taking into account the current locale.  (Could use
 306 // the NumberFormatter class, but the intl extension isn't always installed.)
 307 function number_format_locale($number, int $decimals=0) : string
 308 {
 309   $locale_info = localeconv();
 310   return number_format($number, $decimals, $locale_info['decimal_point'], $locale_info['thousands_sep']);

 314 function get_microtime()
 315 {

 341 // Set the default timezone.   If $tz is not set, then the default MRBS

 343 function mrbs_default_timezone_set(?string $tz=null) : void
 344 {
 345   global $area_defaults;
 346 
 347   if (!isset($tz))
 348   {
 349     if (isset($area_defaults['timezone']))
 350     {
 351       $tz = $area_defaults['timezone'];

 353     else
 354     {
 355       // This should have been picked up before now, but just in case ...
 356 
 357       // We don't just use a default default timezone such as UTC because then
 358       // people would start running into DST problems with their bookings.
 359       $message = 'MRBS configuration error: $timezone has not been set.';
 360       // Use die() rather than Errors::fatalError() because unless we have set the timezone
 361       // PHP starts complaining bitterly if we try and do anything remotely complicated.
 362       die($message);
 363     }
 364   }
 365 
 366   if (!date_default_timezone_set($tz))
 367   {
 368     $message = "MRBS configuration error: invalid timezone '$tz'";
 369     die($message);  // See comment above about use of die()
 370   }
 371 
 372 }

 406 function get_cookie_path()
 407 {
 408   global $cookie_path_override, $server;
 409 
 410   if (isset($cookie_path_override))
 411   {
 412     $cookie_path = $cookie_path_override;
 413   }
 414   else
 415   {
 416     // REQUEST_URI isn't set on all PHP systems, so fall back to PHP_SELF
 417     $cookie_path = $server['REQUEST_URI'] ?? $server['PHP_SELF'];
 418     // Strip off everything after the last '/'
 419     $cookie_path = preg_replace('/[^\/]*$/', '', $cookie_path);
 420     // Some cases have been observed of the cookie path being set to, for example,
 421     // '/mrbs/ajax/' or '/mrbs/js/'.  It's not clear how this can happen (possibly
 422     // some kind of timing issue when an Ajax request arrives before the main page??)
 423     // but in case it does, strip off any trailing 'ajax/' or 'js/' string.
 424     $cookie_path = preg_replace('/(ajax|js)\/$/', '', $cookie_path);
 425   }
 426 
 427   return $cookie_path;
 428 }

 431 // Gets the url path from either $_SERVER['PHP_SELF'] or $_SERVER['REQUEST_URI'], whichever
 432 // happens to be non-empty.  (Some systems will not have one or the other variable set).
 433 function url_path()
 434 {
 435   global $server;
 436 
 437   if (isset($server['PHP_SELF']) && ($server['PHP_SELF'] !== ''))
 438   {
 439     $result = $server['PHP_SELF'];
 440   }
 441   elseif (isset($server['REQUEST_URI']) && ($server['REQUEST_URI'] !== ''))
 442   {
 443     // The REQUEST_URI includes the query string, so we need to strip it off
 444     $result = parse_url($server['REQUEST_URI'], PHP_URL_PATH);
 445     if ($result === false)
 446     {
 447       trigger_error('Cannot parse $_SERVER["REQUEST_URI"] of "' . $server['REQUEST_URI'] . '"', E_USER_NOTICE);
 448       $result = '';
 449     }
 450   }
 451   else
 452   {
 453     if (!is_cli())
 454     {
 455       trigger_error('$_SERVER["PHP_SELF"] and $_SERVER["REQUEST_URI"] are both empty.  Check your server configuration.', E_USER_NOTICE);
 456     }
 457     $result = '';
 458   }
 459 
 460   return $result;
 461 }

 463 
 464 // Returns the base URL for MRBS.  If the config variable $url_base is set then that
 465 // overrides the automatic calculation.  A '/' will be appended to the end of the string,
 466 // unless it is empty or already ends in a '/'.
 467 function url_base() : string
 468 {
 469   global $url_base, $server;
 470 
 471   if (isset($url_base))
 472   {
 473     $result = $url_base;
 474   }
 475   elseif (isset($server['HTTP_HOST']))
 476   {
 477     $result = $server['HTTP_HOST'] . dirname(url_path());
 478   }
 479   else
 480   {
 481     $result = '';
 482   }
 483 
 484   // Add a scheme if we haven't got one
 485   if (null === parse_url($result, PHP_URL_SCHEME))
 486   {
 487     $result = ((is_https()) ? 'https' : 'http') . '://' . $result;
 488   }
 489 
 490   // Add a trailing '/' if there isn't one
 491   if (($result !== '') && (substr($result, -1) !== '/'))
 492   {
 493     $result .= '/';
 494   }
 495 
 496   return $result;
 497 }

 500 
 501 function is_https() : bool
 502 {
 503   global $server;
 504 
 505   if (!empty($server['HTTP_X_FORWARDED_PROTO']))
 506   {
 507     return ($server['HTTP_X_FORWARDED_PROTO'] === 'https');
 508   }
 509   elseif (!empty($server['HTTP_X_FORWARDED_PROTOCOL']))
 510   {
 511     return ($server['HTTP_X_FORWARDED_PROTOCOL'] === 'https');
 512   }
 513   elseif (!empty($server['HTTP_X_FORWARDED_SSL']))
 514   {
 515     return (strcasecmp($server['HTTP_X_FORWARDED_SSL'], 'on') === 0);
 516   }
 517 
 518   return (isset($server['HTTPS']) &&
 519           !empty($server['HTTPS']) &&
 520           (strcasecmp($server['HTTPS'], 'off') !== 0));
 521 }

 524 // Returns the current page.   If the page ends in $suffix this will be cut off.
 525 // The existing query string is optionally added.
 526 function this_page(bool $with_query_string=false, string $suffix='') : string
 527 {
 528   global $server;
 529 
 530   if ((!isset($server['SCRIPT_NAME']) || ($server['SCRIPT_NAME'] === '') && !is_cli()))
 531   {
 532     trigger_error('$_SERVER["SCRIPT_NAME"] is empty.  Check your server configuration.', E_USER_NOTICE);
 533   }
 534 
 535   // We use basename() because the full name causes problems when reverse proxies are being used.
 536   $result = basename($server['SCRIPT_NAME'], $suffix);
 537 
 538   // Get the query string if required
 539   if ($with_query_string &&
 540       isset($server['QUERY_STRING']) &&
 541      ($server['QUERY_STRING'] !== ''))
 542   {
 543     $query_string = $server['QUERY_STRING'];
 544   }
 545   else
 546   {
 547     $query_string = '';
 548   }
 549 
 550   parse_str($query_string, $query_string_parts);
 551 
 552   // Add the query string back in
 553   if (!empty($query_string_parts))
 554   {
 555     $result .= '?' . http_build_query($query_string_parts, '', '&');
 556   }
 557 
 558   return $result;
 559 }

 562 // Format a timestamp in RFC 1123 format, for HTTP headers
 563 //
 564 // e.g. Wed, 28 Jul 2010 12:43:58 GMT
 565 function rfc1123_date(int $timestamp) : string
 566 {
 567   return gmdate("D, d M Y G:i:s \\G\\M\\T", $timestamp);
 568 }

 571 // Rebuilds a url that has been decompomosed into parts by parse_url().
 572 // See https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.parse-url.php#106731
 573 function build_url(array $parts) : string
 574 {
 575     return (isset($parts['scheme']) ? "{$parts['scheme']}:" : '') .
 576           ((isset($parts['user']) || isset($parts['host'])) ? '//' : '') .
 577           (isset($parts['user']) ? "{$parts['user']}" : '') .
 578           (isset($parts['pass']) ? ":{$parts['pass']}" : '') .
 579           (isset($parts['user']) ? '@' : '') .
 580           (isset($parts['host']) ? "{$parts['host']}" : '') .
 581           (isset($parts['port']) ? ":{$parts['port']}" : '') .
 582           (isset($parts['path']) ? "{$parts['path']}" : '') .
 583           (isset($parts['query']) ? "?{$parts['query']}" : '') .
 584           (isset($parts['fragment']) ? "#{$parts['fragment']}" : '');
 585 }

 588 // A wrapper for sending a Location header.  This function will urlencode and add
 589 // the site parameter as necessary
 590 function location_header(string $location) : void
 591 {
 592   global $debug;
 593 
 594   if ($debug && (version_compare(MRBS_MIN_PHP_VERSION, '8.1') >= 0))
 595   {
 596     trigger_error("The return type can be changed to 'never'.", E_USER_NOTICE);
 597   }
 598 
 599   // Add the site parameter if necessary
 600   $location = multisite($location);
 601 
 602   // Encode the query string if there is one
 603   $parts = parse_url($location);
 604 
 605   if (isset($parts['query']))
 606   {
 607     parse_str($parts['query'], $result);
 608     $parts['query'] = http_build_query($result, '', '&');
 609   }
 610 
 611   header('Location: ' . build_url($parts));
 612   exit;
 613 }

 615 
 616 function add_query_parameter(string $location, string $name, $value) : string
 617 {
 618   $parts = parse_url($location);
 619 
 620   if ($parts === false)
 621   {
 622     throw new \Exception("Could not parse the URL '$location'");
 623   }
 624 
 625   if (!isset($parts['query']))
 626   {
 627     $parts['query'] = '';
 628   }
 629 
 630   parse_str($parts['query'], $result);
 631   $result[$name] = $value;
 632   $parts['query'] = http_build_query($result, '', '&');
 633   return build_url($parts);
 634 }
 635 
 636 
 637 function remove_query_parameter(string $location, string $name) : string
 638 {
 639   $parts = parse_url($location);
 640 
 641   if ($parts === false)
 642   {
 643     throw new \Exception("Could not parse the URL '$location'");
 644   }
 645 
 646   if (!isset($parts['query']))
 647   {
 648     $parts['query'] = '';
 649   }
 650 
 651   parse_str($parts['query'], $result);
 652   unset($result[$name]);
 653   $parts['query'] = http_build_query($result, '', '&');
 654   return build_url($parts);
 655 }

 658 // Adds the site parameter in the query string if necessary
 659 function multisite(string $location) : string
 660 {
 661   global $multisite, $site;
 662 
 663   // Add the site, if there is one, to the query string
 664   if ($multisite && isset($site) && ($site !== ''))
 665   {
 666     return add_query_parameter($location, 'site', $site);
 667   }
 668 
 669   return $location;

 673 // Add a version parameter to a filename in order to force the use of the new
 674 // file instead of the cached version
 675 function add_version(string $filename) : string
 676 {
 677   $url_path = parse_url($filename, PHP_URL_PATH);
 678 
 679   if (is_readable($url_path))
 680   {
 681     $mtime = filemtime($url_path);
 682     if ($mtime !== false)
 683     {
 684       return add_query_parameter($filename, 'v', $mtime);
 685     }
 686   }
 687 
 688   return $filename;
 689 }

 692 // A little helper function to send an "Expires" header. Just one
 693 // parameter, the number of seconds in the future to set the expiry.
 694 // If $seconds is <= 0, then caching is disabled.
 695 function expires_header(int $seconds) : void
 696 {
 697   global $debug;
 698 
 699   if (!$debug && ($seconds > 0))
 700   {
 701     // We also send a couple of extra headers as the "Expires" header alone
 702     // does not always result in caching.
 703     header("Expires: " . rfc1123_date(time() + $seconds));
 704     header("Pragma: cache");
 705     header("Cache-Control: max-age=$seconds");
 706   }
 707   else
 708   {
 709     // Make sure that caching is disabled.   Setting the "Expires" header
 710     // alone doesn't always turn off caching.
 711     header("Pragma: no-cache");                          // HTTP 1.0
 712     header("Expires: Mon, 26 Jul 1997 05:00:00 GMT");    // Date in the past
 713   }
 714 }
 715 
 716 
 717 // Outputs the HTTP headers, passed in the array $headers, followed by
 718 // a set of headers to set the cache expiry date.  If $expiry_seconds <= 0
 719 // then caching is disabled.
 720 function http_headers(array $headers, int $expiry_seconds=0) : void
 721 {
 722   foreach ($headers as $header)
 723   {
 724     header($header);
 725   }
 726 
 727   expires_header($expiry_seconds);
 728 }

 799 // Converts a duration of $dur seconds into a duration of
 800 // $dur $units
 801 // $max_unit can be set to 'seconds', 'minutes', 'hours', etc. and
 802 // is used to specify a maximum size of unit to use.  For example if
 803 // it is set to 'minutes', 3600 seconds will give 60 minutes rather
 804 // than 1 hour.
 805 function toTimeString(int &$dur, &$units, bool $translate=true, ?string $max_unit=null)
 806 {
 807   if (!isset($max_unit))
 808   {
 809     $max_unit = 'years';
 810   }
 811 
 812   if (($max_unit != 'seconds') && (abs($dur) >= 60) && ($dur % 60 == 0))
 813   {
 814     $dur /= 60;
 815 
 816     if (($max_unit != 'minutes') && (abs($dur) >= 60) && ($dur % 60 == 0))
 817     {
 818       $dur /= 60;
 819 
 820       if(($max_unit != 'hours') && ((abs($dur) >= 24) && ($dur % 24 == 0)))
 821       {
 822         $dur /= 24;
 823 
 824         if(($max_unit != 'days') && ((abs($dur) >= DAYS_PER_WEEK) && ($dur % DAYS_PER_WEEK == 0)))
 825         {
 826           $dur /= DAYS_PER_WEEK;
 827 
 828           if (($max_unit != 'weeks') && ((abs($dur) >= 52) && ($dur % 52 == 0)))
 829           {
 830             $dur  /= 52;
 831             $units = 'years';
 832           }
 833           else
 834           {
 835             $units = 'weeks';
 836           }
 837         }
 838         else
 839         {
 840           $units = 'days';
 841         }
 842       }
 843       else
 844       {
 845         $units = 'hours';
 846       }
 847     }
 848     else
 849     {
 850       $units = 'minutes';
 851     }
 852   }
 853   else
 854   {
 855     $units = 'seconds';
 856   }
 857 
 858   // Limit any floating point values to three decimal places
 859   if (is_float($dur))
 860   {
 861     $dur = sprintf('%.3f', $dur);
 862     $dur = rtrim($dur, '0');  // removes trailing zeros
 863   }
 864 
 865   // Translate into local language if required
 866   if ($translate)
 867   {
 868     $units = get_vocab($units);
 869   }
 870 }
 871 
 872 
 873 // Converts a time period of $units into seconds, when it is originally
 874 // expressed in $dur_units.   (Almost the inverse of toTimeString(),
 875 // but note that toTimeString() can do language translation)
 876 function fromTimeString(&$units, $dur_units)
 877 {
 878   if (!isset($units) || !isset($dur_units))
 879   {
 880     return;
 881   }
 882 
 883   switch($dur_units)
 884   {
 885     case "years":
 886       $units *= 52;
 887     case "weeks":
 888       $units *= DAYS_PER_WEEK;
 889     case "days":
 890       $units *= 24;
 891     case "hours":
 892       $units *= 60;
 893     case "periods":
 894     case "minutes":
 895       $units *= 60;
 896     case "seconds":
 897       break;
 898   }
 899   $units = (int) $units;
 900 }
 901 
 902 
 903 // Gets the interval in periods for a booking with $start_time and $end_time
 904 // Takes account of DST
 905 function get_period_interval(int $start_time, int $end_time, int $area_id) : int
 906 {
 907   static $area_details = [];
 908 
 909   if (!isset($area_details[$area_id]))
 910   {
 911     $area_details[$area_id] = get_area_details($area_id);
 912   }
 913 
 914   $periods_per_day = count(json_decode($area_details[$area_id]['periods']));
 915   $date_time_zone = new DateTimeZone($area_details[$area_id]['timezone']);
 916 
 917   // Create start and end dates and set both dates to noon so that we can compare them
 918   // and get an integral number of days difference.  Noon also happens to be when
 919   // periods start, so will be useful in a moment.
 920   $startDate = new DateTime();
 921   $startDate
 922     ->setTimezone($date_time_zone)
 923     ->setTimestamp($start_time)
 924     ->modify('12:00');
 925 
 926   $endDate = new DateTime();
 927   $endDate
 928     ->setTimezone($date_time_zone)
 929     ->setTimestamp($end_time)
 930     ->modify('12:00');
 931 
 932   // Calculate the difference in days
 933   $interval = $startDate->diff($endDate);
 934   $interval_days = intval($interval->format('%a'));
 935 
 936   if ($interval_days === 0)
 937   {
 938     // If the interval starts and ends on the same day, then we just calculate the number
 939     // of periods by calculating the number of minutes between the start and end times.
 940     $result = ($end_time - $start_time)/60;
 941   }
 942   else
 943   {
 944     // Otherwise we calculate the number of periods on the first day
 945     $startDate->add(new DateInterval('PT' . $periods_per_day . 'M'));
 946     $result = get_period_interval($start_time, $startDate->getTimestamp(), $area_id);
 947     // Add in the number of whole days worth of periods in between
 948     $result += ($interval_days - 1) * $periods_per_day;
 949     // And add in the number of periods on the last day
 950     $result += get_period_interval($endDate->getTimestamp(), $end_time, $area_id);
 951   }
 952 
 953   return (int) $result;
 954 }
 955 
 956 
 957 function toPeriodString($start_period, &$dur, &$units, $translate=true)
 958 {
 959   global $periods;
 960 
 961   $max_periods = count($periods);
 962   $dur /= 60;  // duration now in minutes
 963   $days = $dur / MINUTES_PER_DAY;
 964   $remainder = $dur % MINUTES_PER_DAY;
 965   // strip out any gap between the end of the last period on one day
 966   // and the beginning of the first on the next
 967   if ($remainder > $max_periods)
 968   {
 969     $remainder += $max_periods - MINUTES_PER_DAY;
 970   }
 971 
 972   // We'll express the duration as an integer, in days if possible, otherwise periods
 973   if (($remainder == 0) || (($start_period == 0) && ($remainder == $max_periods)))
 974   {
 975     $dur = (int) $days;
 976     if ($remainder == $max_periods)
 977     {
 978       $dur++;
 979     }
 980     $units = $translate ? get_vocab("days") : "days";
 981   }
 982   else
 983   {
 984     $dur = (intval($days) * $max_periods) + $remainder;
 985     $units = $translate ? get_vocab("periods") : "periods";
 986   }
 987 }
 988 
 989 // Converts a period of $units starting at $start_period into seconds, when it is
 990 // originally expressed in $dur_units (periods or days).   (Almost the inverse of
 991 // toPeriodString(), but note that toPeriodString() can do language translation)
 992 function fromPeriodString($start_period, &$units, $dur_units)
 993 {
 994   global $periods;
 995 
 996   if (!isset($units) || !isset($dur_units))
 997   {
 998     return;
 999   }
1000 
1001   // First get the duration in minutes
1002   $max_periods = count($periods);
1003   if ($dur_units == "periods")
1004   {
1005     $end_period = $start_period + $units;
1006     if ($end_period > $max_periods)
1007     {
1008       $units = (MINUTES_PER_DAY * floor($end_period/$max_periods)) + ($end_period%$max_periods) - $start_period;
1009     }
1010   }
1011   if ($dur_units == "days")
1012   {
1013     if ($start_period == 0)
1014     {
1015       $units = $max_periods + ($units-1)*MINUTES_PER_DAY;
1016     }
1017     else
1018     {
1019       $units = $units * MINUTES_PER_DAY;
1020     }
1021   }
1022 
1023   // Then convert into seconds
1024   $units = (int) $units;
1025   $units = 60 * $units;
1026 }
1027 
1028 
1029 // Returns the BYDAY value for a given timestamp, eg 4SU for fourth Sunday in
1030 // the month, or -1MO for the last Monday.
1031 function date_byday(int $timestamp) : string
1032 {
1033   $dow = RFC5545::DAYS[date('w', $timestamp)];
1034   $dom = date('j', $timestamp);
1035   $ord = intval(($dom - 1)/DAYS_PER_WEEK) + 1;
1036   if ($ord == 5)
1037   {
1038     $ord = -1;
1039   }
1040   return $ord . $dow;
1041 }

1044 // Returns TRUE if the time $hm1 is before $hm2
1045 // $hm1 and $hm2 are associative arrays indexed by 'hours' and 'minutes'.
1046 // The indices are chosen to allow the result of the PHP getdate() function
1047 // to be passed as parameters
1048 function hm_before(array $hm1, array $hm2) : bool
1049 {
1050   return ($hm1['hours'] < $hm2['hours']) ||
1051          (($hm1['hours'] == $hm2['hours']) && ($hm1['minutes'] < $hm2['minutes']));
1052 }
1053 
1054 
1055 // Returns TRUE if the end of the last slot is on the day after the beginning
1056 // of the first slot
1057 function day_past_midnight() : bool
1058 {
1059   global $morningstarts, $morningstarts_minutes, $eveningends, $eveningends_minutes, $resolution;
1060 
1061   $start_first_slot = (($morningstarts * 60) + $morningstarts_minutes) * 60;
1062   $end_last_slot = ((($eveningends * 60) + $eveningends_minutes) * 60) + $resolution;
1063   $end_last_slot = $end_last_slot % SECONDS_PER_DAY;
1064 
1065   return ($end_last_slot <= $start_first_slot);
1066 }
1067 
1068 
1069 // Gets the UNIX timestamp for the start of the first slot on the given day
1070 function get_start_first_slot(int $month, int $day, int $year) : int
1071 {
1072   global $morningstarts, $morningstarts_minutes, $enable_periods;
1073 
1074   if ($enable_periods)
1075   {
1076     $result = mktime(12, 0, 0, $month, $day, $year);
1077   }
1078   else
1079   {
1080     $result = mktime($morningstarts, $morningstarts_minutes, 0,
1081                      $month, $day, $year);
1082   }
1083 
1084   if ($result === false)
1085   {
1086     throw new \Exception("Invalid arguments to mktime()");
1087   }
1088 
1089   return $result;
1090 }
1091 
1092 
1093 // Gets the UNIX timestamp for the start of the last slot on the given day
1094 function get_start_last_slot(int $month, int $day, int $year) : int
1095 {
1096   global $morningstarts, $morningstarts_minutes, $eveningends, $eveningends_minutes, $enable_periods, $periods;
1097 
1098   if ($enable_periods)
1099   {
1100     $result = mktime(12, count($periods) -1, 0, $month, $day, $year);
1101   }
1102   else
1103   {
1104     // Work out if $evening_ends is really on the next day
1105     if (hm_before(array('hours' => $eveningends, 'minutes' => $eveningends_minutes),
1106         array('hours' => $morningstarts, 'minutes' => $morningstarts_minutes)))
1107     {
1108       $day++;
1109     }
1110 
1111     $result = mktime($eveningends, $eveningends_minutes, 0,
1112                      $month, $day, $year);
1113   }
1114 
1115   if ($result === false)
1116   {
1117     throw new \Exception("Invalid arguments to mktime()");
1118   }
1119 
1120   return $result;
1121 }
1122 
1123 
1124 function get_end_last_slot(int $month, int $day, int $year) : int
1125 {
1126   global $resolution;
1127 
1128   return intval(get_start_last_slot($month, $day, $year) + $resolution);
1129 }
1130 
1131 
1132 // Determines with a given timestamp is within a booking day, ie between the start of
1133 // the first slot and end of the last slot.   Returns a boolean.
1134 function is_in_booking_day(int $t) : bool
1135 {
1136   global $morningstarts, $morningstarts_minutes,
1137          $eveningends, $eveningends_minutes,
1138          $resolution, $enable_periods;
1139 
1140   if ($enable_periods)
1141   {
1142     return true;
1143   }
1144 
1145   $start_day_secs = (($morningstarts * 60) + $morningstarts_minutes) * 60;
1146   $end_day_secs = (((($eveningends * 60) + $eveningends_minutes) * 60) + $resolution) % SECONDS_PER_DAY;
1147 
1148   $date = getdate($t);
1149   $t_secs = (($date['hours'] * 60) + $date['minutes']) * 60;
1150 
1151   if ($start_day_secs == $end_day_secs)
1152   {
1153     return true;
1154   }
1155   elseif (day_past_midnight())
1156   {
1157     return (($t_secs >= $start_day_secs) || ($t_secs <= $end_day_secs));
1158   }
1159   else
1160   {
1161     return (($t_secs >= $start_day_secs) && ($t_secs <= $end_day_secs));
1162   }
1163 }
1164 
1165 
1166 // Takes a Unix timestamp and sets the time, while keeping the day the same.
1167 // $time is a string in hh:mm format (24 hour clock)
1168 function timestamp_set_time(int $timestamp, string $time) : int
1169 {
1170   list($hour, $minute) = explode(':', $time);
1171   $hour = intval($hour);
1172   $minute = intval($minute);
1173   $date = new DateTime();
1174   $date->setTimestamp($timestamp);
1175   $date->setTime($hour, $minute);
1176   return $date->getTimestamp();
1177 }
1178 
1179 
1180 // Force a timestamp $t to be on a booking day, either by moving it back to the end
1181 // of the previous booking day, or forward to the start of the next.
1182 function fit_to_booking_day(int $t, bool $back=true) : int
1183 {
1184   if (is_in_booking_day($t))
1185   {
1186     return $t;
1187   }
1188 
1189   $date = getdate($t);
1190   // Remember that we need to cater for days that stretch beyond midnight.
1191   if ($back)
1192   {
1193     $new_t = get_end_last_slot($date['mon'], $date['mday'], $date['year']);
1194     if ($new_t > $t)
1195     {
1196       $new_t = get_end_last_slot($date['mon'], $date['mday'] - 1, $date['year']);
1197     }
1198   }
1199   else
1200   {
1201     $new_t = get_start_first_slot($date['mon'], $date['mday'], $date['year']);
1202     if ($new_t < $t)
1203     {
1204       $new_t = get_start_first_slot($date['mon'], $date['mday'] + 1, $date['year']);
1205     }
1206   }
1207 
1208   return $new_t;
1209 }
1210 
1211 
1212 /**
1213  * Get the duration of an interval given a start time and end time.
1214  *
1215  * Corrects for DST changes so that the duration is what the user would expect to see.
1216  * For example, 12 noon to 12 noon crossing a DST boundary is 24 hours.
1217  *
1218  * @param int $start_time Unix timestamp
1219  * @param int $end_time Unix timestamp
1220  * @param bool $enable_periods Whether periods are being used
1221  * @param bool $translate Whether to translate into the browser language
1222  * @return array{duration: int, dur_units: string}
1223  */
1224 function get_duration(int $start_time, int $end_time, bool $enable_periods, int $area_id, bool $translate=true) : array
1225 {
1226   $result = array();
1227 
1228   $period_names = get_period_names();
1229 
1230   if ($enable_periods)
1231   {
1232     $periods_per_day = count($period_names[$area_id]);
1233     $n_periods = get_period_interval($start_time, $end_time, $area_id);  // this handles DST
1234     if (($n_periods % $periods_per_day) == 0)
1235     {
1236       $result['duration'] =  intval($n_periods/$periods_per_day);
1237       $result['dur_units'] = ($translate) ? get_vocab('days') : 'days';
1238     }
1239     else
1240     {
1241       $result['duration'] = $n_periods;
1242       $result['dur_units'] = ($translate) ? get_vocab('periods') : 'periods';
1243     }
1244   }
1245   else
1246   {
1247     $result['duration'] = $end_time - $start_time;
1248     // Need to make DST correct in opposite direction to entry creation
1249     // so that user see what he expects to see
1250     $result['duration'] -= cross_dst($start_time, $end_time);
1251     toTimeString($result['duration'], $result['dur_units'], $translate);
1252   }
1253   return $result;
1254 }

1256 
1257 // Escape a PHP variable for use in HTML
1258 function escape_html($value)
1259 {
1260   switch ($type = gettype($value))
1261   {
1262     case 'double':
1263     case 'integer':
1264       return $value;
1265       break;
1266     case 'string':
1267       return htmlspecialchars($value);
1268       break;
1269     default:
1270       throw new TypeError("Type '$type' not supported as an argument.");
1271       break;
1272   }
1273 }
1274 
1275 
1276 // Escape a PHP string for use in JavaScript
1277 //
1278 // Based on a function contributed by kongaspar at gmail dot com at
1279 // http://www.php.net/manual/function.addcslashes.php
1280 function escape_js(string $str) : string
1281 {
1282   return addcslashes($str, "\\\'\"&\n\r<>/");
1283 }

1286 // Return a default area; used if no area is already known. This returns the
1287 // area that contains the default room (if it is set, valid and enabled) otherwise the
1288 // first area in alphabetical order in the database (no guarantee there is an area 1).
1289 // The area must be enabled for it to be considered.
1290 // This could be changed to implement something like per-user defaults.
1291 function get_default_area() : int
1292 {
1293   global $default_room;
1294 
1295   // It's possible that this function is being called during an upgrade
1296   // process before the disabled column existed.
1297   $disabled_field_exists = db()->field_exists(_tbl('room'), 'disabled');
1298 
1299   // If the $default_room is set and exists and is enabled and is visible to
1300   // the current user, then return the corresponding area
1301   if (isset($default_room) && is_visible($default_room))
1302   {
1303     $sql = "SELECT area_id
1304               FROM " . _tbl('room') . " R, " . _tbl('area') . " A
1305              WHERE R.id=:id
1306                AND R.area_id = A.id";
1307 
1308     if ($disabled_field_exists)
1309     {
1310       $sql .= " AND R.disabled = 0 AND A.disabled = 0";
1311     }
1312 
1313     $sql .= " LIMIT 1";
1314     $area = db()->query1($sql, array(':id' => $default_room));
1315 
1316     if ($area >= 0)
1317     {
1318       return (int) $area;
1319     }
1320   }
1321 
1322   // Otherwise return the first enabled area in the database that has an
1323   // enabled and visible room
1324   $sql = "SELECT R.id, R.area_id
1325             FROM " . _tbl('room') . " R, " . _tbl('area') . " A
1326            WHERE R.area_id = A.id";
1327 
1328   if ($disabled_field_exists)
1329   {
1330     $sql .= " AND R.disabled = 0 AND A.disabled = 0";
1331   }
1332 
1333   $order_by_column = (db()->field_exists(_tbl('area'), 'sort_key')) ? 'sort_key' : 'area_name';
1334   $sql .= " ORDER BY A.$order_by_column";
1335 
1336   $res = db()->query($sql);
1337 
1338   while (false !== ($row = $res->next_row_keyed()))
1339   {
1340     if (is_visible($row['id']))
1341     {
1342       return (int) $row['area_id'];
1343     }
1344   }
1345 
1346   return 0;
1347 }
1348 
1349 // Return a default room given a valid area; used if no room is already known.
1350 // If the area contains $default_room and $default_room is visible to the current
1351 // user, then it returns $default_room. Otherwise it returns the first visible room
1352 // in sort_key order in the database.
1353 // This could be changed to implement something like per-user defaults.
1354 function get_default_room(int $area) : int
1355 {
1356   global $default_room;
1357 
1358   // It's possible that this function is being called during
1359   // an upgrade process before the disabled columns existed.
1360   $disabled_field_exists = db()->field_exists(_tbl('room'), 'disabled');
1361 
1362   // Check to see whether this area contains $default_room
1363   if (isset($default_room))
1364   {
1365     $sql = "SELECT id
1366               FROM " . _tbl('room') . "
1367              WHERE id=:id AND area_id=:area_id";
1368 
1369     if ($disabled_field_exists)
1370     {
1371       $sql .= " AND disabled=0";
1372     }
1373 
1374     $sql .= " LIMIT 1";
1375     $sql_params = array(':id' => $default_room, ':area_id' => $area);
1376     $room = db()->query1($sql, $sql_params);
1377 
1378     if (($room >= 0) && is_visible($room))
1379     {
1380       return (int) $room;
1381     }
1382   }
1383 
1384   // Otherwise just return the first visible room in the area
1385   $rooms = get_rooms($area, !$disabled_field_exists);
1386 
1387   return (count($rooms) > 0) ? (int) $rooms[0]['id'] : 0;
1388 }

1390 
1391 // Return an area id for a given room
1392 function get_area(int $room) : int
1393 {
1394   $sql = "SELECT area_id
1395             FROM " . _tbl('room') . "
1396            WHERE id=?
1397            LIMIT 1";
1398 
1399   $area = db()->query1($sql, array($room));
1400 
1401   return ($area < 0 ? 0 : (int) $area);
1402 }

1404 
1405 // Clean up a row from the area table, making sure there are no nulls, casting
1406 // boolean fields into bools and doing some sanity checking
1407 function clean_area_row(array $row) : array
1408 {
1409   global $force_resolution, $area_defaults, $private_override_options;
1410 
1411   // This code can get called during the upgrade process and so must
1412   // not make any assumptions about the existence of extra columns in
1413   // the area table.
1414 
1415   // Cast the columns to their intended types (the pseudo-booleans will
1416   // be picked up later)
1417   row_cast_columns($row, 'area');
1418 
1419   // Get the default settings if necessary
1420   $columns = Columns::getInstance(_tbl('area'));
1421 
1422   foreach ($columns as $column)
1423   {
1424     // Cast the pseudo-booleans to bools
1425     if (isset($row[$column->name]) && ($column->getNature() == Column::NATURE_INTEGER) && ($column->getLength() <=2))
1426     {
1427       $row[$column->name] = (bool)$row[$column->name];
1428     }
1429 
1430     if (array_key_exists($column->name, $area_defaults))
1431     {
1432       // If the "per area" setting is in the database, then use that.  Otherwise
1433       // just stick with the default setting from the config file.
1434       // (don't use the database setting if $force_resolution is TRUE
1435       // and we're looking at the resolution field)
1436       if (!isset($row[$column->name]) ||
1437           (($column->name == 'resolution') && !empty($force_resolution) && empty($row['enable_periods'])) )
1438       {
1439         $row[$column->name] = $area_defaults[$column->name];
1440       }
1441     }
1442   }
1443 
1444   // Do some sanity checking in case the area table is somehow messed up
1445   // (1) 'private_override' must be a valid value
1446   if (array_key_exists('private_override', $row) &&
1447       !in_array($row['private_override'], $private_override_options))
1448   {
1449     $row['private_override'] = 'private';  // the safest default
1450     $message = "Invalid value for 'private_override' in the area table.  Using '{$row['private_override']}'.";
1451     trigger_error($message, E_USER_WARNING);
1452   }
1453   // (2) 'resolution' must be positive
1454   if (array_key_exists('resolution', $row) &&
1455       (empty($row['resolution']) || ($row['resolution'] < 0)))
1456   {
1457     $row['resolution'] = 30*60;  // 30 minutes, a reasonable fallback
1458     $message = "Invalid value for 'resolution' in the area table.   Using {$row['resolution']} seconds.";
1459     trigger_error($message, E_USER_WARNING);
1460   }
1461 
1462   return $row;
1463 }
1464 
1465 
1466 // Update the default area settings with the ones specific to this area.
1467 // If no value is set in the database, use the value from the config file.
1468 // If $area is empty, use the default area
1469 function get_area_settings(int $area) : void
1470 {
1471   global $auth;
1472   global $resolution, $default_duration, $default_duration_all_day;
1473   global $morningstarts, $morningstarts_minutes, $eveningends, $eveningends_minutes;
1474   global $private_enabled, $private_default, $private_mandatory, $private_override;
1475   global $min_create_ahead_enabled, $max_create_ahead_enabled, $min_create_ahead_secs, $max_create_ahead_secs;
1476   global $min_delete_ahead_enabled, $max_delete_ahead_enabled, $min_delete_ahead_secs, $max_delete_ahead_secs;
1477   global $max_duration_enabled, $max_duration_secs, $max_duration_periods;
1478   global $approval_enabled, $reminders_enabled, $enable_periods, $periods;
1479   global $confirmation_enabled, $confirmed_default, $timezone;
1480   global $max_per_interval_area_enabled, $max_per_interval_area;
1481   global $max_secs_per_interval_area_enabled, $max_secs_per_interval_area;
1482   global $interval_types;
1483   global $times_along_top, $default_type;
1484 
1485   // This code can get called during the upgrade process and so must
1486   // not make any assumptions about the existence of extra columns in
1487   // the area table.
1488   if (empty($area))
1489   {
1490     $area = get_default_area();
1491   }
1492 
1493   // Get all the "per area" config settings
1494   $columns = array('timezone', 'resolution', 'default_duration', 'default_duration_all_day',
1495                    'morningstarts', 'morningstarts_minutes',
1496                    'eveningends', 'eveningends_minutes',
1497                    'private_enabled', 'private_default', 'private_mandatory', 'private_override',
1498                    'min_create_ahead_enabled', 'max_create_ahead_enabled',
1499                    'min_create_ahead_secs', 'max_create_ahead_secs',
1500                    'min_delete_ahead_enabled', 'max_delete_ahead_enabled',
1501                    'min_delete_ahead_secs', 'max_delete_ahead_secs',
1502                    'max_duration_enabled', 'max_duration_secs', 'max_duration_periods',
1503                    'max_per_day_enabled', 'max_per_day',
1504                    'max_per_week_enabled', 'max_per_week',
1505                    'max_per_month_enabled', 'max_per_month',
1506                    'max_per_year_enabled', 'max_per_year',
1507                    'max_per_future_enabled', 'max_per_future',
1508                    'max_secs_per_day_enabled', 'max_secs_per_day',
1509                    'max_secs_per_week_enabled', 'max_secs_per_week',
1510                    'max_secs_per_month_enabled', 'max_secs_per_month',
1511                    'max_secs_per_year_enabled', 'max_secs_per_year',
1512                    'max_secs_per_future_enabled', 'max_secs_per_future',
1513                    'approval_enabled', 'reminders_enabled', 'enable_periods', 'periods',
1514                    'confirmation_enabled', 'confirmed_default',
1515                    'times_along_top', 'default_type');
1516 
1517   $sql = "SELECT *
1518             FROM " . _tbl('area') . "
1519            WHERE id=?
1520            LIMIT 1";
1521 
1522   $res = db()->query($sql, array($area));
1523   if ($res->count() == 0)
1524   {
1525     // We still need to set the timezone even if the query didn't
1526     // return any results
1527     mrbs_default_timezone_set($timezone);
1528     return;
1529   }
1530   else
1531   {
1532     $row = $res->next_row_keyed();
1533 
1534     // Periods are stored as a JSON encoded string in the database
1535     if (isset($row['periods']))
1536     {
1537       $row['periods'] = json_decode($row['periods']);
1538     }
1539 
1540     $row = clean_area_row($row);
1541     foreach ($columns as $column)
1542     {
1543       if (array_key_exists($column, $row))
1544       {
1545         $$column = $row[$column];
1546       }
1547     }
1548   }
1549   // Set the timezone
1550   mrbs_default_timezone_set($timezone);
1551 
1552   // Set the $max_per_interval_area_enabled, $max_per_interval_area,
1553   // $max_secs_per_interval_area_enabled and $max_secs_per_interval_area
1554   // arrays, which are handled slightly differently
1555   foreach ($interval_types as $interval_type)
1556   {
1557     $var = "max_per_{$interval_type}_enabled";
1558     if (isset($$var))
1559     {
1560       $max_per_interval_area_enabled[$interval_type] = $$var;
1561     }
1562 
1563     $var = "max_per_$interval_type";
1564     if (isset($$var))
1565     {
1566       $max_per_interval_area[$interval_type] = $$var;
1567     }
1568 
1569     $var = "max_secs_per_{$interval_type}_enabled";
1570     if (isset($$var))
1571     {
1572       $max_secs_per_interval_area_enabled[$interval_type] = $$var;
1573     }
1574 
1575     $var = "max_secs_per_$interval_type";
1576     if (isset($$var))
1577     {
1578       $max_secs_per_interval_area[$interval_type] = $$var;
1579     }
1580   }
1581 
1582   // Sanitise the settings
1583   if ($enable_periods)
1584   {
1585     $resolution = 60;
1586     $morningstarts = 12;
1587     $morningstarts_minutes = 0;
1588     $eveningends = 12;
1589     $eveningends_minutes = count($periods) - 1;
1590   }
1591   elseif (!isset($morningstarts_minutes))
1592   {
1593     // ensure that $morningstarts_minutes defaults to zero if not set
1594     $morningstarts_minutes = 0;
1595   }
1596 
1597   // If it's been set in the config settings then force all bookings to be shown
1598   // as private for users who haven't logged in.
1599   if ($auth['force_private_for_guests'] && (null === session()->getCurrentUser()))
1600   {
1601     $private_override = 'private';
1602   }
1603 }

1609 {

1639 //

1641 function some_area(string $field, bool $only_enabled=false, bool $not=false) : bool

1644   $sql = "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM " . _tbl('area') . " WHERE $predicate";

1676 
1677 // Splits a date in ISO 8601 format ('yyyy-mm-dd') and returns an
1678 // array of year, month, day with leading zeros removed, or FALSE
1679 // on failure.
1680 function split_iso_date(string $iso_date)
1681 {
1682   if (false === ($date = DateTime::createFromFormat(DateTime::ISO8601_DATE, $iso_date)))
1683   {
1684     return false;
1685   }
1686 
1687   return array(
1688     (int) $date->format('Y'),
1689     (int) $date->format('n'),
1690     (int) $date->format('j')
1691   );
1692 }
1693 
1694 
1695 // Validates that a string is a valid ISO date in yyyy-mm-dd format
1696 function validate_iso_date(string $date) : bool
1697 {
1698   // Try creating a DateTime object.  If that is successful and
1699   // the inverse operation gives the original string then it is
1700   // valid.  (This is to check that, for example, 2021-09-31 hasn't
1701   // been converted into 2021-10-01).
1702   $format = DateTime::ISO8601_DATE;
1703   $datetime = DateTime::createFromFormat($format, $date);
1704 
1705   return ($datetime && ($datetime->format($format) === $date));
1706 }

1709 // Get the local day name based on language.

1713 
1714   if (!isset($format))
1715   {
1716     $format = $datetime_formats['day_name'];
1717   }
1718 
1719   // Note 2000-01-02 is a Sunday.
1720   return datetime_format($format, mktime(0,0,0,1,2+$day_number,2000), $locale);
1721 }

1724 // Gets the monthly repeat day for an entry, for example "20" or "second Wednesday"
1725 function get_monthly_repeat_day(array $data) : string
1726 {
1727   // Fix up the keys while we're still transitioning to the RepeatRule
1728   if (isset($data['repeat_rule']))
1729   {
1730     $repeat_rule = $data['repeat_rule'];
1731     if ($repeat_rule->getMonthlyType() == RepeatRule::MONTHLY_ABSOLUTE)
1732     {
1733       $data['month_absolute'] = $repeat_rule->getMonthlyAbsolute();
1734     }
1735     else
1736     {
1737       $data['month_relative'] = $repeat_rule->getMonthlyRelative();
1738     }
1739   }
1740 
1741   if (isset($data['month_absolute']))
1742   {
1743     $result = (string) $data['month_absolute'];
1744   }
1745   elseif (isset($data['month_relative']))
1746   {
1747     // Note: this does not internationalise very well and could do with revisiting.
1748     // It follows the select box order in edit_entry, which is the more difficult one
1749     // to sort out.  It assumes all languages have the same order as English
1750     // eg "the second Wednesday" which is probably not true.
1751     list('ordinal' => $ord, 'day' => $dow) = RFC5545::parseByday($data['month_relative']);
1752     $result = get_vocab("ord_" . $ord) . " " . day_name(RFC5545::convertDayToOrd($dow));
1753   }
1754   else
1755   {
1756     throw new Exception("Unknown monthly repeat type");
1757   }
1758 
1759   return $result;
1760 }

1771 // Returns a string representing the hour and minute for the nominal
1772 // seconds since the start of the day, $s
1773 function hour_min(int $s) : string
1774 {
1775   $following_day = ($s >= SECONDS_PER_DAY);
1776   $s = $s % SECONDS_PER_DAY;  // in case $s is on the next day
1777   // Choose a day that doesn't have any DST transitions in any timezone
1778   $t = mktime(0, 0, $s, 1, 1, 2000);
1779   $result = datetime_format(hour_min_format(), $t);
1780   if ($following_day)
1781   {
1782     $result = "* " . $result;
1783   }
1784   return $result;

1788 /**
1789  * Convert a timestamp into a date string, when using periods.
1790  *
1791  * @param bool $previous_period Whether the date string for the previous period should be used (useful for the end of a period)
1792  */
1793 function period_date_string(int $t, int $area_id, bool $previous_period=false) : string
1794 {
1795   global $datetime_formats;
1796 
1797   // The separator is a ',' as a '-' leads to an ambiguous
1798   // display in report.php when showing end times.
1799   return period_time_string($t, $area_id, $previous_period) . ', ' . datetime_format($datetime_formats['date'], $t);

1803 /**
1804  * Returns the name of the period in a given area for a given timestamp.
1805  *
1806  * @param bool $previous_period Whether the name of the previous period should be used (useful for the end of a period)
1807  */
1808 function period_time_string(int $t, int $area_id, bool $previous_period=false) : string
1809 {
1810   $periods = get_period_names();
1811 
1812   $n_periods = count($periods[$area_id]);
1813   $time = getdate($t);
1814   $p = $time['minutes'];
1815   if ($previous_period)
1816   {
1817     $p--;
1818   }
1819 
1820   // Make sure the period is valid
1821   $p = max($p, 0);
1822   $p = min($p, $n_periods - 1);
1823 
1824   return $periods[$area_id][$p];
1825 }
