1932 // Round time down to the nearest resolution
1933 function round_t_down(int $t, int $resolution, int $start_first_slot) : int
1934 {
1935   // The simple case when no DST transition is involved
1936   if (cross_dst($start_first_slot, $t) == 0)
1937   {
1938     return $t - (int)abs(($t - $start_first_slot) % $resolution);
1939   }
1940   // Otherwise we have to pay attention to DST transitions
1941   $date = new DateTime();
1942   $date->setTimestamp($start_first_slot);
1943   $nominal_seconds = nominal_seconds($start_first_slot);
1944   // Keep advancing the slot until we find the one that is closest to $t
1945   do {
1946     $candidate_slot = $date->getTimestamp();
1947     $nominal_seconds += $resolution;
1948     $date->setNominalSeconds($nominal_seconds);
1949   } while ($date->getTimestamp() <= $t);
1950 
1951   return $candidate_slot;
1952 }
1953 
1954 
1955 // Round time up to the nearest resolution
1956 function round_t_up(int $t, int $resolution, int $start_first_slot) : int
1957 {
1958   // The simple case when no DST transition is involved
1959   if (cross_dst($start_first_slot, $t) == 0)
1960   {
1961     if (($t - $start_first_slot) % $resolution != 0) {
1962       return $t + $resolution - abs(($t - $start_first_slot) % $resolution);
1963     }
1964     else {
1965       return $t;
1966     }
1967   }
1968   // Otherwise we have to pay attention to DST transitions
1969   $date = new DateTime();
1970   $date->setTimestamp($start_first_slot);
1971   $nominal_seconds = nominal_seconds($start_first_slot);
1972   // Keep advancing the slot until we find the one that is >= $t
1973   do {
1974     $candidate_slot = $date->getTimestamp();
1975     $nominal_seconds += $resolution;
1976     $date->setNominalSeconds($nominal_seconds);
1977   } while ($candidate_slot < $t);
1978 
1979   return $candidate_slot;
1980 }

1983 // Returns the nominal (ie ignoring DST transitions) seconds since the start of
1984 // the calendar day on the start of the booking day
1985 function nominal_seconds(int $t) : int
1986 {
1987   global $morningstarts, $morningstarts_minutes;
1988 
1989   $date = getdate($t);
1990   // check to see if the time is really on the next day
1991   if (hm_before($date,
1992                 array('hours' => $morningstarts, 'minutes' => $morningstarts_minutes)))
1993   {
1994     $date['hours'] += 24;
1995   }
1996   return (($date['hours'] * 60) + $date['minutes']) * 60;
1997 }

2047 // returns the numeric day of the week (0-6) in terms of the MRBS week as defined by
2048 // $weekstarts.   For example if $weekstarts is set to 2 (Tuesday) and a $time for
2049 // a Wednesday is given, then 1 is returned.

2057 
2058 // Compares two nominal dates which are indexed by 'hours', 'minutes', 'seconds',
2059 // 'mon', 'mday' and 'year', ie as in the output of getdate().  Returns -1 if the
2060 // first date is before the second, 0 if they are equal and +1 if the first date
2061 // is after the second.   NULL if a comparison can't be done.
2062 //
2063 // (Note that internally the function uses gmmktime() so the parameters do not
2064 // have to represent valid values.   For example you could pass '32' for day and
2065 // that would be interpreted as 4 days after '28'.)
2066 function nominal_date_compare(array $d1, array $d2) : int
2067 {
2068   // We compare the dates using gmmktime() because we are trying to compare nominal
2069   // dates and so do not want DST transitions
2070   $t1 = gmmktime($d1['hours'], $d1['minutes'], $d1['seconds'],
2071                  $d1['mon'], $d1['mday'], $d1['year']);
2072   $t2 = gmmktime($d2['hours'], $d2['minutes'], $d2['seconds'],
2073                  $d2['mon'], $d2['mday'], $d2['year']);
2074   if ($t1 < $t2)
2075   {
2076     return -1;
2077   }
2078   elseif ($t1 == $t2)
2079   {
2080     return 0;
2081   }
2082   else
2083   {
2084     return 1;
2085   }
2086 }

2089 // Determines whether there's a possibility that the interval between the two Unix
2090 // timestamps could contain nominal times that don't exist, for example from 0100 to
2091 // 0159 in Europe/London when entering DST.
2092 function is_possibly_invalid(int $start, int $end) : bool
2093 {
2094   // We err on the side of caution by widening the interval by a day at each end.   This
2095   // allows for the possibility that the start or end times have been calculated by using
2096   // mktime() on an invalid time!
2097   return (cross_dst($start - 86400, $end + 86400) < 0);
2098 }

2100 
2101 // Checks whether the nominal time given is an invalid date and time with respect to
2102 // DST transitions.   When entering DST there is a set of times that don't exist, for
2103 // example from 0100 to 0159 in Europe/London.
2104 // Returns NULL if MRBS is unable to determine an answer, otherwise TRUE or FALSE (so
2105 // a simple equality test will default to a valid time if MRBS can't determine an answer)
2106 function is_invalid_datetime(int $hour, int $minute, int $second, int $month, int $day, int $year, ?string $tz=null) : ?bool
2107 {
2108   global $timezone;
2109 
2110   // Do a quick check to see if there's a possibility of an invalid time by checking
2111   // whether there's a transition into DST from the day before to the day after
2112   if (empty($tz))
2113   {
2114     $tz = $timezone;  // default to the current timezone
2115   }
2116 
2117   $old_tz = date_default_timezone_get();  // save the current timezone
2118   date_default_timezone_set($tz);
2119 
2120   // If the day before is in DST then the datetime must be valid, because
2121   // you only get the gap when entering DST.
2122   $dayBefore = mktime($hour, $minute, $second, $month, $day-1, $year);
2123   if (date('I', $dayBefore))
2124   {
2125     $result = false;
2126   }
2127   else
2128   {
2129     // The day before is not in DST.   If the day after is also not in DST,
2130     // then there can have been no transition, so again the datetime must be valid.
2131     $dayAfter = mktime($hour, $minute, $second, $month, $day+1, $year);
2132     if (!date('I', $dayAfter))
2133     {
2134       $result = false;
2135     }
2136     else
2137     {
2138       $thisDateTimeZone = new DateTimeZone($tz);
2139       // Get the transition data (we assume there is one and only one transition),
2140       // in particular the time at which the transition happens and the new offset
2141       $transitions = $thisDateTimeZone->getTransitions($dayBefore, $dayAfter);
2142       // According to my reading of the PHP manual, getTransitions() should return
2143       // all transitions between the start and end date.   However what it seems to do
2144       // is return an array consisting of the time data for the start date followed by
2145       // the transition data.   So as a precaution we take the last element of the array
2146       // (we were only expecting one element, but seem to get two).
2147       $transition = array_pop($transitions);
2148       // If we failed for some reason to get any transition data, return NULL
2149       if (!isset($transition))
2150       {
2151         $result = null;
2152       }
2153       else
2154       {
2155         // Get the old offset and work out how many seconds the clocks change by
2156         $beforeDateTime = new DateTime(date('c', $dayBefore), $thisDateTimeZone);
2157         $change = $transition['offset'] - $beforeDateTime->getOffset();
2158 
2159         // See if the nominal date falls outside the gap
2160         $lastValidSecond = getdate($transition['ts'] - 1);
2161         $lastInvalidSecond = $lastValidSecond;
2162         $lastInvalidSecond['seconds'] += $change;
2163         $thisDate = array('hours' => $hour, 'minutes' => $minute, 'seconds' => $second,
2164                           'mon' => $month, 'mday' => $day, 'year' => $year);
2165 
2166         $result = ((nominal_date_compare($thisDate, $lastValidSecond) > 0) &&
2167                    (nominal_date_compare($thisDate, $lastInvalidSecond) <= 0));
2168       }
2169     }
2170   }
2171 
2172   date_default_timezone_set($old_tz);  // restore the old timezone
2173 
2174   return $result;
2175 }
2176 
2177 
2178 // Returns the modification (in seconds) necessary on account of any DST
2179 // transitions when going from $start to $end
2180 function cross_dst(int $start, int $end) : int
2181 {
2182   global $timezone;
2183 
2184   // Calculate the modification using the DateTimeZone information rather than date('I', $time),
2185   // because not all DST transitions are 1 hour.  For example, Lord Howe Island in Australia
2186   // has a 30 minute transition.
2187   $thisDateTimeZone = new DateTimeZone($timezone);
2188   $startDateTime = new DateTime(date('c', $start), $thisDateTimeZone);
2189   $endDateTime = new DateTime(date('c', $end), $thisDateTimeZone);
2190   $modification = $startDateTime->getOffset() - $endDateTime->getOffset();
2191 
2192   return $modification;
2193 }
2194 
2195 
2196 // If $time falls on a non-working day, shift it back to the end of the last
2197 // working day before that
2198 function shift_to_workday(int $time) : int
2199 {
2200   global $working_days;
2201 
2202   $dow = date('w', $time);  // get the day of the week
2203   $skip_back = 0;           // number of days to skip back
2204   // work out how many days to skip back to get to a working day
2205   while (!in_array($dow, $working_days))
2206   {
2207     if ($skip_back == DAYS_PER_WEEK)
2208     {
2209       break;
2210     }
2211     $skip_back++;
2212     $dow = ($dow + 6) % DAYS_PER_WEEK;  // equivalent to skipping back a day
2213   }
2214   if ($skip_back != 0)
2215   {
2216     // set the time to the end of the working day
2217     $d = intval(date('j', $time)) - $skip_back;
2218     $m = intval(date('n', $time));
2219     $y = intval(date('Y', $time));
2220     $time = mktime(23, 59, 59, $m, $d, $y);
2221   }
2222   return $time;
2223 }
2224 
2225 // Returns the difference in seconds between two timestamps, $now and $then
2226 // It gives $now - $then, less any seconds that were part of a non-working day
2227 function working_time_diff(int $now, int $then) : int
2228 {
2229   global $working_days;
2230 
2231   // Deal with the easy case
2232   if ($now == $then)
2233   {
2234     return 0;
2235   }
2236   // Sanitise the $working_days array in case it was malformed
2237   $working_week = array_unique(array_intersect(array(0,1,2,3,4,5,6), $working_days));
2238   $n_working_days = count($working_week);
2239   // Deal with the special case where there are no working days
2240   if ($n_working_days == 0)
2241   {
2242     return 0;
2243   }
2244   // and the special case where there are no holidays
2245   if ($n_working_days == DAYS_PER_WEEK)
2246   {
2247     return ($now - $then);
2248   }
2249 
2250   // For the rest we're going to assume that $last comes after $first
2251   $last = max($now, $then);
2252   $first = min($now, $then);
2253 
2254   // first of all, if $last or $first fall on a non-working day, shift
2255   // them back to the end of the last working day
2256   $last = shift_to_workday($last);
2257   $first = shift_to_workday($first);
2258   // So calculate the difference
2259   $diff = $last - $first;
2260   // Then we have to deduct all the non-working days in between.   This will be
2261   // (a) the number of non-working days in the whole weeks between them +
2262   // (b) the number of non-working days in the part week
2263 
2264   // First let's calculate (a)
2265   $last = mktime(12, 0, 0, (int)date('n', $last), (int)date('j', $last), (int)date('Y', $last));
2266   $first = mktime(12, 0, 0, (int)date('n', $first), (int)date('j', $first), (int)date('Y', $first));
2267   $days_diff = (int) round(($last - $first)/SECONDS_PER_DAY);  // the difference in days
2268   $whole_weeks = (int) floor($days_diff/DAYS_PER_WEEK);  // the number of whole weeks between the two
2269   $non_working_days = $whole_weeks * (DAYS_PER_WEEK - $n_working_days);
2270   // Now (b), ie we just have to calculate how many non-working days there are between the two
2271   // days of the week that are left
2272   $last_dow = date('w', $last);
2273   $first_dow = date('w', $first);
2274 
2275   while ($first_dow != $last_dow)
2276   {
2277     $first_dow = ($first_dow + 1) % DAYS_PER_WEEK;
2278     if (!in_array($first_dow, $working_week))
2279     {
2280       $non_working_days++;
2281     }
2282   }
2283 
2284   // So now subtract the number of weekend seconds
2285   $diff = $diff - ($non_working_days * SECONDS_PER_DAY);
2286 
2287   // Finally reverse the difference if $now was in fact before $then
2288   if ($now < $then)
2289   {
2290     $diff = -$diff;
2291   }
2292 
2293   return (int) $diff;
2294 }
2295

2316 // returns true if event should be considered private based on

2318 function is_private_event(bool $privacy_status) : bool
2319 {
2320   global $private_override;
2321   if ($private_override == "private" )
2322   {
2323     $privacy_status = true;
2324   }
2325   elseif ($private_override == "public" )
2326   {
2327     $privacy_status = false;
2328   }
2329 
2330   return $privacy_status;
2331 }

2333 // Generate a globally unique id
2334 //
2335 // We will generate a uid of the form "MRBS-uniqid-MD5hash@domain_name"
2336 // where uniqid is time based and is generated by uniqid() and the
2337 // MD5hash is the first 8 characters of the MD5 hash of $str concatenated
2338 // with a random number.
2339 function generate_global_uid(string $str) : string
2340 {
2341   global $server;
2342 
2343   $uid = uniqid('MRBS-');
2344   $uid .= "-" . substr(md5($str . rand(0,10000)), 0, 8);
2345   $uid .= "@";
2346   // Add on the domain name if possible, if not the server name,
2347   // otherwise 'MRBS'
2348   if (empty($server['SERVER_NAME']))
2349   {
2350     $uid .= 'MRBS';
2351   }
2352   elseif (mb_strpos($server['SERVER_NAME'], 'www.') === 0)
2353   {
2354     $uid .= mb_substr($server['SERVER_NAME'], 4);
2355   }
2356   else
2357   {
2358     $uid .= $server['SERVER_NAME'];
2359   }
2360 
2361   return $uid;
2362 }

2427 // Set and restore ignore_user_abort.   The function is designed to be used to
2428 // ensure a critical piece of code can't be aborted, and used in pairs of set and
2429 // restore calls.  The function keeps track of outstanding set requests so that
2430 // the original state isn't restored if there are other requests still outstanding.
2431 //
2432 // $set   TRUE    set ignore_user_abort
2433 //        FALSE   restore to the original state, if no other requests outstanding
2434 function mrbs_ignore_user_abort(bool $set) : void
2435 {
2436   static $original_state;
2437   static $outstanding_requests = 0;
2438 
2439   if (!isset($original_state))
2440   {
2441     $original_state = boolval(ignore_user_abort());
2442   }
2443 
2444   // Set ignore_user_abort
2445   if ($set)
2446   {
2447     if ($outstanding_requests == 0)
2448     {
2449       ignore_user_abort(true);
2450     }
2451     $outstanding_requests++;
2452   }
2453   else
2454   // Restore the original state, provided no other requests are outstanding
2455   {
2456     $outstanding_requests--;
2457     if ($outstanding_requests == 0)
2458     {
2459       ignore_user_abort($original_state);
2460     }
2461   }
2462 }

2484 function get_field_entry_input(array $params) : Field
2485 {
2486   global $select_options, $datalist_options, $text_input_max;
2487 
2488   if (isset($params['field']))
2489   {
2490     if (!empty($select_options[$params['field']]))
2491     {
2492       $class = 'FieldSelect';
2493     }
2494     elseif (!empty($datalist_options[$params['field']]))
2495     {
2496       $class = 'FieldInputDatalist';
2497     }
2498     else
2499     {
2500       $columns = Columns::getInstance(_tbl('entry'));
2501       $column_name = preg_replace('/^entry./', '', $params['field']);
2502       $column = $columns->getColumnByName($column_name);
2503       if (!in_array($column_name, ['name', 'create_by']) &&  // special cases
2504           ($column->getNature() === Column::NATURE_CHARACTER) &&
2505           ($column->getLength() > $text_input_max))
2506       {
2507         $class = 'FieldTextarea';
2508       }
2509       else
2510       {
2511         $class = 'FieldInputText';
2512       }
2513     }
2514   }
2515   else
2516   {
2517     $class = 'FieldInputText';
2518   }
2519 
2520   $full_class = __NAMESPACE__ . "\\Form\\$class";
2521   $field = new $full_class();
2522   $field->setLabel($params['label'])
2523     ->setControlAttribute('name', $params['name']);
2524 
2525   if (!empty($params['required']))
2526   {
2527     $field->setControlAttribute('required', true);
2528   }
2529   if (!empty($params['disabled']))
2530   {
2531     $field->setControlAttribute('disabled', true);
2532     $field->addHiddenInput($params['name'], $params['value']);
2533   }
2534 
2535   switch ($class)
2536   {
2537     case 'FieldSelect':
2538       $options = $select_options[$params['field']];
2539       $field->addSelectOptions($options, $params['value']);
2540       break;
2541 
2542     case 'FieldInputDatalist':
2543       $options = $datalist_options[$params['field']];
2544       $field->addDatalistOptions($options);
2545     // Drop through
2546 
2547     case 'FieldInputText':
2548       if (!empty($params['required']))
2549       {
2550         // Set a pattern as well as required to prevent a string of whitespace
2551         $field->setControlAttribute('pattern', REGEX_TEXT_POS);
2552       }
2553     // Drop through
2554 
2555     case 'FieldTextarea':
2556       if ($class == 'FieldTextarea')
2557       {
2558         $field->setControlText($params['value'] ?? '');
2559       }
2560       else
2561       {
2562         $field->setControlAttribute('value', $params['value']);
2563       }
2564       if (isset($params['field']) &&
2565         (null !== ($maxlength = maxlength($params['field']))))
2566       {
2567         $field->setControlAttribute('maxlength', $maxlength);
2568       }
2569       // Add a placeholder if necessary
2570       $tag = $params['field'] . '.placeholder';
2571       $placeholder = get_vocab($tag);
2572       if (isset($placeholder) && ($placeholder !== $tag))
2573       {
2574         $field->setControlAttribute('placeholder', $placeholder);
2575       }
2576       break;
2577 
2578     default:
2579       throw new \Exception("Unknown class '$class'");
2580       break;
2581   }
2582 
2583   return $field;
2584 }
2585 
2586 
2587 // Returns a Field object for selecting as user from the list of available users.
2588 // If $datalist is true a datalist is returned, otherwise a select element.
2589 // $params is an associative array with the following keys
2590 //    value       the value of the current selection
2591 //    disabled    boolean, whether the field should be disabled
2592 //    required    boolean
2593 //    field       the field name, eg 'entry.create_by'
2594 //    label       the field label
2595 //    name        the field name
2596 function get_user_field(array $params, bool $datalist=false) : Field
2597 {
2598   if (method_exists(auth(), 'getUsernames'))
2599   {
2600     // We can get a list of all users, so present a <select> or <datalist> element.
2601     // The options will actually be provided later via Ajax, so all we
2602     // do here is present one option, ie the create_by user.
2603     $options = array();
2604     $selected_user = auth()->getUser($params['value']);
2605     // It's possible that $selected_user no longer exists - may have left the
2606     // organisation and been deleted from the user list - so in that case
2607     // use their username for the displayname.
2608     if (isset($selected_user))
2609     {
2610       $options[$selected_user->username] = $selected_user->display_name;
2611     }
2612     else
2613     {
2614       $options[$params['value']] = $params['value'];
2615     }
2616 
2617     $field = new FieldSelect();
2618     $class = 'ajax_usernames';
2619     if ($datalist)
2620     {
2621       $class .= ' datalist';
2622     }
2623     $field->setLabel($params['label'])
2624       ->setControlAttributes(array('name'     => $params['name'],
2625                                    'class'    => $class,
2626                                    'disabled' => $params['disabled']))
2627       ->addSelectOptions($options, $params['value'], true);
2628   }
2629   else
2630   {
2631     // We don't know all the available users, so we'll just present
2632     // a text input field and rely on the user to enter a valid username.
2633     $field = get_field_entry_input($params);
2634   }
2635 
2636   return $field;
2637 }

 133 // Emulates the PHP 8 function str_contains()
 134 if (!function_exists('str_contains'))
 135 {
 136   function str_contains(string $haystack, string $needle) : bool
 137   {
 138     if (!isset($needle) || ($needle === ''))
 139     {
 140       // This is the way the PHP function behaves
 141       return true;
 142     }
 143     else
 144     {
 145       // This works with multibyte characters because
 146       // we are not worried about the actual position.
 147       return (strpos($haystack, $needle) !== false);
 148     }
 149   }
 150 }

 153 // Emulates the PHP 8 function str_starts_with()
 154 if (!function_exists('str_starts_with'))
 155 {
 156   function str_starts_with(string $haystack, string $needle) : bool
 157   {
 158     if (!isset($needle) || ($needle === ''))
 159     {
 160       // This is the way the PHP function behaves
 161       return true;
 162     }
 163     else
 164     {
 165       // This works with multibyte characters because
 166       // we are looking for position zero.
 167       return (strpos($haystack, $needle) === 0);
 168     }
 169   }
 170 }
 171 
 172 
 173 // Emulates the PHP 8 function str_ends_with()
 174 if (!function_exists('str_ends_with'))
 175 {
 176   function str_ends_with(string $haystack, string $needle) : bool
 177   {
 178     if (!isset($needle) || ($needle === ''))
 179     {
 180       // This is the way the PHP function behaves
 181       return true;
 182     }
 183     else
 184     {
 185       // This works with multibyte characters because strpos() and strlen()
 186       // will either both be overloaded with the mb_ versions or both not.
 187       return (strpos($haystack, $needle) === strlen($haystack) - strlen($needle));
 188     }
 189   }
 190 }

   1 <?php
   2 declare(strict_types=1);
   3 namespace MRBS;
   4 
   5 use GuzzleHttp\Client;
   6 use MRBS\DB\DBException;
   7 use MRBS\DB\DBStatement;
   8 use MRBS\ICalendar\RFC5545;
   9 use MRBS\ICalendar\RFC5545Exception;
  10 use MRBS\ICalendar\Series;
  11 use PHPMailer\PHPMailer\PHPMailer;
  12 
  13 
  14 // Gets a VTIMEZONE definition from the file system.
  15 // Returns NULL if none found or it's empty.
  16 function get_vtimezone_file(string $tz) : ?string
  17 {
  18   global $zoneinfo_outlook_compatible;
  19 
  20   $tz_dir = ($zoneinfo_outlook_compatible) ? TZDIR_OUTLOOK : TZDIR;
  21   $tz_file = "$tz_dir/$tz.ics";
  22 
  23   if (!is_readable($tz_file))
  24   {
  25     return null;
  26   }
  27 
  28   $vcalendar = file_get_contents($tz_file);
  29 
  30   if (empty($vcalendar))
  31   {
  32     return null;
  33   }
  34 
  35   $vtimezone = RFC5545::extractVtimezone($vcalendar);
  36 
  37   return (empty($vtimezone)) ? null : $vtimezone;
  38 }
  39 
  40 
  41 // Gets a VTIMEZONE definition from the TZURL defined in the $vtimezone component
  42 function get_vtimezone_url(string $vtimezone) : ?string
  43 {
  44   // (Note that a VTIMEZONE component can contain a TZURL property which
  45   // gives the URL of the most up-to-date version.  Calendar applications
  46   // should be able to check this themselves, but we might as well give them
  47   // the most up-to-date version in the first place).
  48   $properties = explode("\r\n", RFC5545::unfold($vtimezone));
  49   foreach ($properties as $property)
  50   {
  51     if (mb_strpos($property, "TZURL:") === 0)
  52     {
  53       $tz_url = mb_substr($property, 6);  // 6 is the length of "TZURL:"
  54       break;
  55     }
  56   }
  57 
  58   if (!isset($tz_url))
  59   {
  60     trigger_error("The VTIMEZONE component didn't contain a TZURL property.", E_USER_NOTICE);
  61     return null;
  62   }
  63 
  64   try {
  65     $vcalendar = (new Client())->get($tz_url)->getBody()->getContents();
  66   }
  67   catch (\Exception $e) {
  68     trigger_error(get_class($e) . ': ' . $e->getMessage(), E_USER_WARNING);
  69     trigger_error("MRBS: failed to download a new timezone definition from $tz_url", E_USER_WARNING);
  70     return null;
  71   }
  72 
  73   $new_vtimezone = RFC5545::extractVtimezone($vcalendar);
  74   if (empty($new_vtimezone))
  75   {
  76     trigger_error("MRBS: $tz_url did not contain a valid VTIMEZONE", E_USER_WARNING);
  77     return null;
  78   }
  79 
  80   return $new_vtimezone;
  81 }
  82 
  83 
  84 // Get a VTIMEZONE definition from the database.  Returns an array indexed by
  85 // 'vtimezone' and 'last_updated', or NULL if none found.
  86 function get_vtimezone_db(string $tz) : ?array
  87 {
  88   global $zoneinfo_outlook_compatible;
  89 
  90   $sql = "SELECT vtimezone, last_updated
  91             FROM " . _tbl('zoneinfo') . "
  92            WHERE timezone=:timezone
  93              AND outlook_compatible=:outlook_compatible
  94            LIMIT 1";
  95 
  96   $sql_params = array(
  97     ':timezone' => $tz,
  98     ':outlook_compatible' => ($zoneinfo_outlook_compatible) ? 1 : 0
  99   );
 100 
 101   $res = db()->query($sql, $sql_params);
 102 
 103   return ($res->count() === 0) ? null : $res->next_row_keyed();
 104 }
 105

 107 // Update the last_updated time for a timezone in the database
 108 function touch_vtimezone_db(string $tz) : void
 109 {
 110   global $zoneinfo_outlook_compatible;
 111 
 112   $sql = "UPDATE " . _tbl('zoneinfo') . "
 113              SET last_updated=:last_updated
 114            WHERE timezone=:timezone
 115              AND outlook_compatible=:outlook_compatible";
 116 
 117   $sql_params = array(
 118     ':last_updated' => time(),
 119     ':timezone' => $tz,
 120     ':outlook_compatible' => ($zoneinfo_outlook_compatible) ? 1 : 0
 121   );

 123   db()->command($sql, $sql_params);
 124 }

 127 // Insert a new VTIMEZONE definition for a timezone into the database
 128 function insert_vtimezone_db(string $tz, string $vtimezone) : void
 129 {
 130   global $zoneinfo_outlook_compatible;
 131 
 132   try
 133   {
 134     $sql = "INSERT INTO " . _tbl('zoneinfo') . "
 135                       (vtimezone, last_updated, timezone, outlook_compatible)
 136                VALUES (:vtimezone, :last_updated, :timezone, :outlook_compatible)";
 137 
 138     $sql_params = array(
 139       ':vtimezone' => $vtimezone,
 140       ':last_updated' => time(),
 141       ':timezone' => $tz,
 142       ':outlook_compatible' => ($zoneinfo_outlook_compatible) ? 1 : 0
 143     );
 144 
 145     db()->command($sql, $sql_params);
 146   }
 147   catch (DBException $e)
 148   {
 149     // Catch any database exception because it's just possible that someone else has inserted a row just
 150     // before us and then we'll get an error because of the unique constraint.   If we do then that's
 151     // fine and we can ignore it, but trigger an error anyway just in case it's some other kind of error.
 152     // (Ideally we'd want to be more specific about looking for constraint errors, but we have to consider
 153     // both MySQL and PostgreSQL).
 154     //
 155     // We could have used an INSERT IGNORE, but there isn't an easy PostgreSQL alternative until
 156     // PostgreSQL 9.5.
 157     //
 158     // We can't put a mutex lock round the SELECT - INSERT operation because we're normally already
 159     // inside another lock from edit_entry_handler and you can only, in the MYSQL implementation, have
 160     // one active lock.
 161     trigger_error($e->getMessage(), E_USER_NOTICE);
 162   }
 163 }
 164

 166 // Update the database with a new VTIMEZONE definition for a timezone
 167 function update_vtimezone_db(string $tz, string $vtimezone) : void
 168 {
 169   global $zoneinfo_outlook_compatible;
 170 
 171   $sql = "UPDATE " . _tbl('zoneinfo') . "
 172              SET vtimezone=:vtimezone,
 173                  last_updated=:last_updated
 174            WHERE timezone=:timezone
 175              AND outlook_compatible=:outlook_compatible";
 176 
 177   $sql_params = array(
 178     ':vtimezone' => $vtimezone,
 179     ':last_updated' => time(),
 180     ':timezone' => $tz,
 181     ':outlook_compatible' => ($zoneinfo_outlook_compatible) ? 1 : 0
 182   );
 183 
 184   db()->command($sql, $sql_params);
 185 }

 188 // Get a VTIMEZONE component for the timezone $tz.
 189 // If none available returns FALSE.
 190 //
 191 // We cache the latest VTIMEZONE component in the database.  If it has expired
 192 // we go to the web for the latest version or if there's nothing in the database
 193 // in the first place we try and populate it from the VTIMEZONE definitions in
 194 // the filesystem.
 195 function get_vtimezone(string $tz)
 196 {
 197   global $zoneinfo_update, $zoneinfo_expiry;
 198 
 199   static $vtimezones = array();  // Cache the components for performance
 200 
 201   if (!isset($vtimezones[$tz]))
 202   {
 203     // Look for a timezone definition in the database
 204     $vtimezone_db = get_vtimezone_db($tz);
 205     if (isset($vtimezone_db['vtimezone']))
 206     {
 207       $vtimezones[$tz] = $vtimezone_db['vtimezone'];
 208       // If the definition has expired, and we're updating it, then get a fresh definition from the URL
 209       if ($zoneinfo_update && ((time() - $vtimezone_db['last_updated']) >= $zoneinfo_expiry))
 210       {
 211         $vtimezone = get_vtimezone_url($vtimezone_db['vtimezone']);
 212         if (isset($vtimezone))
 213         {
 214           // We've got a valid VTIMEZONE, so we can update the database and the static variable
 215           update_vtimezone_db($tz, $vtimezone);
 216           $vtimezones[$tz] = $vtimezone;
 217         }
 218         else
 219         {
 220           // If we didn't manage to get a new VTIMEZONE, update the last_updated field
 221           // so that MRBS will not try again until after the expiry interval has passed.
 222           // This will mean that we don't keep encountering a timeout delay. (The most
 223           // likely reason that we couldn't get a new VTIMEZONE is that the site doesn't
 224           // have external internet access, so there's no point in retrying for a while).
 225           touch_vtimezone_db($tz);
 226         }
 227       }
 228     }
 229     else
 230     {
 231       // If there's nothing in the database, get one from the filesystem
 232       $vtimezone = get_vtimezone_file($tz);
 233       if (isset($vtimezone))
 234       {
 235         // And put it in the database if it's valid
 236         insert_vtimezone_db($tz, $vtimezone);
 237         $vtimezones[$tz] = $vtimezone;
 238       }
 239       else
 240       {
 241         // Everything has failed
 242         $vtimezones[$tz] = false;
 243       }
 244     }
 245   }
 246 
 247   return $vtimezones[$tz];
 248 }

 251 // Gets a username given an ORGANIZER value.   Returns NULL if none found
 252 function get_create_by(string $organizer) : ?string
 253 {
 254   // Get the email address.   Stripping off the 'mailto' is a very simplistic
 255   // method.  It will work in the majority of cases, but this needs to be improved
 256   $email = preg_replace('/^mailto:/', '', $organizer);
 257 
 258   return auth()->getUsernameByEmail($email);

 262 // Given an RFC 5545 recurrence rule, returns a RepeatRule object giving the MRBS repeat
 263 // details.
 264 // Returns FALSE on failure with error messages being returned in the array $errors
 265 function get_repeat_rule(string $rrule, int $start_time, array &$errors)
 266 {
 267   // Set up the result with safe defaults
 268   $repeat_rule = new RepeatRule();
 269   $repeat_rule->setType(RepeatRule::NONE);
 270   $repeat_rule->setInterval(1);
 271   $end_date = new DateTime();
 272   $end_date->setTimestamp(0);
 273   $repeat_rule->setEndDate($end_date);
 274 
 275   $rules = array();
 276   $recur_rule_parts = explode(';', $rrule);
 277   foreach ($recur_rule_parts as $recur_rule_part)
 278   {
 279     list($name, $value) = explode('=', $recur_rule_part);
 280     $rules[$name] = $value;
 281   }
 282 
 283   if (!isset($rules['FREQ']))
 284   {
 285     $errors[] = get_vocab("invalid_RRULE");
 286   }
 287 
 288   try
 289   {
 290     switch ($rules['FREQ'])
 291     {
 292       case 'DAILY':
 293         $repeat_rule->setType(RepeatRule::DAILY);
 294         break;
 295       case 'WEEKLY':
 296         $repeat_rule->setType(RepeatRule::WEEKLY);
 297         if (isset($rules['BYDAY']))
 298         {
 299           $repeat_rule->setDaysFromRFC5545(explode(',', $rules['BYDAY']));
 300         }
 301         else
 302         {
 303           // If there's no repeat day specified in the RRULE then
 304           // 'the day is gotten from "DTSTART"'
 305           $repeat_rule->setDays(array(date('w', $start_time)));
 306         }
 307         break;
 308       case 'MONTHLY':
 309         $repeat_rule->setType(RepeatRule::MONTHLY);
 310         if (!isset($rules['BYDAY']))
 311         {
 312           $repeat_rule->setMonthlyAbsolute((int)$rules['BYMONTHDAY']);
 313           $repeat_rule->setMonthlyType(RepeatRule::MONTHLY_ABSOLUTE);
 314         }
 315         else
 316         {
 317           $byday_days = explode(',', $rules['BYDAY']);
 318           if (count($byday_days) > 1)
 319           {
 320             $errors[] = get_vocab("more_than_one_BYDAY") . $rules['FREQ'];
 321           }
 322           foreach ($byday_days as $byday_day)
 323           {
 324             $rfc5545day = mb_substr($byday_day, -2);     // the last two characters of the string
 325             $nth = mb_substr($byday_day, 0, -2);  // everything except the last two characters
 326             if ($nth === '')
 327             {
 328               // "If an integer modifier is not present, it means all days of this
 329               // type within the specified frequency.  For example, within a MONTHLY
 330               // rule, MO represents all Mondays within the month." [RFC 5545]
 331               // So that comes to the same thing as a WEEKLY repeat
 332               $repeat_rule->setType(RepeatRule::WEEKLY);
 333               $repeat_rule->setDaysFromRFC5545(array($rfc5545day));
 334             }
 335             elseif (($nth == '5') || ($nth == '-5'))
 336             {
 337               $errors[] = get_vocab("BYDAY_equals_5") . " $nth$rfc5545day";
 338             }
 339             else
 340             {
 341               $repeat_rule->setMonthlyRelative($byday_day);
 342               $repeat_rule->setMonthlyType(RepeatRule::MONTHLY_RELATIVE);
 343             }
 344           }
 345         }
 346         break;
 347       case 'YEARLY':
 348         $repeat_rule->setType(RepeatRule::YEARLY);
 349         break;
 350       default:
 351         $errors[] = get_vocab("unsupported_FREQ") . $rules['FREQ'];
 352         break;
 353     }
 354   }
 355   catch (RFC5545Exception $e)
 356   {
 357     $errors[] = $e->getMessage();
 358   }
 359 
 360   if (isset($rules['INTERVAL']) && ($rules['INTERVAL'] > 1))
 361   {
 362     $repeat_rule->setInterval((int) $rules['INTERVAL']);
 363   }
 364   else
 365   {
 366     $repeat_rule->setInterval(1);
 367   }
 368 
 369   if (isset($rules['UNTIL']))
 370   {
 371     // Strictly speaking "the value of the UNTIL rule part MUST have the same
 372     // value type as the "DTSTART" property".   So we should really tell getTimestamp()
 373     // the value type.  But "if the "DTSTART" property is specified as a date with UTC
 374     // time or a date with local time and time zone reference, then the UNTIL rule
 375     // part MUST be specified as a date with UTC time" - so in nearly all cases
 376     // supported by MRBS the value will be a UTC time.
 377     $repeat_end_date = new DateTime();
 378     $repeat_end_date->setTimestamp(RFC5545::getTimestamp($rules['UNTIL']));
 379     $repeat_rule->setEndDate($repeat_end_date);
 380   }
 381   elseif (isset($rules['COUNT']))
 382   {
 383     // It would be quite easy to support COUNT, but we haven't done so yet
 384     $errors[] = get_vocab("unsupported_COUNT");
 385   }
 386   else
 387   {
 388     $errors[] = get_vocab("no_indefinite_repeats");
 389   }
 390 
 391   return (empty($errors)) ? $repeat_rule : false;
 392 }

 395 // Create an RFC 5545 iCalendar Event component
 396 function create_ical_event(string $method, array $data, ?array $addresses=null, bool $series=false) : string
 397 {
 398   require_once "functions_mail.inc";
 399 
 400   global $mail_settings, $timezone, $default_area_room_delimiter;
 401   global $partstat_accepted;
 402 
 403   $vtimezone = get_vtimezone($timezone);
 404 
 405   $results = array();
 406 
 407   $results[] = "BEGIN:VEVENT";
 408   $results[] = "UID:" . $data['ical_uid'];  // compulsory
 409   $results[] = "DTSTAMP:" . gmdate(RFC5545::DATETIME_FORMAT . '\Z');  // compulsory
 410   $last_modified = empty($data['last_updated']) ? time() : $data['last_updated'];
 411   $results[] = "LAST-MODIFIED:" . gmdate(RFC5545::DATETIME_FORMAT . '\Z', $last_modified);
 412 
 413 
 414   // Note: we try and write the event times in the format of a local time with
 415   // a timezone reference (ie RFC 5545 Form #3).   Only if we can't do that do we
 416   // fall back to a UTC time (ie RFC 5545 Form #2).
 417   //
 418   // The reason for this is that although this is not required by RFC 5545 (see
 419   // Appendix A.2), its predecessor, RFC 2445, did require it for recurring
 420   // events and is the standard against which older applications, notably Exchange
 421   // 2007, are written.   Note also that when using a local timezone format the
 422   // VTIMEZONE component must be provided (this is done in create_icalendar() ).  Some
 423   // applications will work without the VTIMEZONE component, but many follow the
 424   // standard and do require it.  Here is an extract from RFC 2445:
 425 
 426   // 'When used with a recurrence rule, the "DTSTART" and "DTEND" properties MUST be
 427   // specified in local time and the appropriate set of "VTIMEZONE" calendar components
 428   // MUST be included.'
 429 
 430   if ($vtimezone === false)
 431   {
 432     $results[] = "DTSTART:" . gmdate(RFC5545::DATETIME_FORMAT . '\Z', $data['start_time']);
 433     $results[] = "DTEND:" . gmdate(RFC5545::DATETIME_FORMAT . '\Z', $data['end_time']);
 434   }
 435   else
 436   {
 437     $results[] = "DTSTART;TZID=$timezone:" . date(RFC5545::DATETIME_FORMAT, $data['start_time']);
 438     $results[] = "DTEND;TZID=$timezone:" . date(RFC5545::DATETIME_FORMAT, $data['end_time']);
 439   }
 440 
 441   if ($series)
 442   {
 443     $results[] = "RRULE:" . $data['repeat_rule']->toRFC5545Rule();
 444     if (!empty($data['skip_list']))
 445     {
 446       $results[] = RFC5545::createExdateProperty(
 447         $data['skip_list'],
 448         ($vtimezone === false) ? null : $timezone
 449       );
 450     }
 451   }
 452   $results[] = "SUMMARY:" . RFC5545::escapeText($data['name']);
 453   if (isset($data['description']))
 454   {
 455     $results[] = "DESCRIPTION:" . RFC5545::escapeText($data['description']);
 456   }
 457   $results[] = "LOCATION:" . RFC5545::escapeText($data['area_name'] . $default_area_room_delimiter . $data['room_name']);
 458   $results[] = "SEQUENCE:" . $data['ical_sequence'];
 459   // If this is an individual member of a series then set the recurrence id
 460   if (!$series && ($data['entry_type'] != ENTRY_SINGLE))
 461   {
 462     $results[] = "RECURRENCE-ID:" . $data['ical_recur_id'];
 463   }
 464   // STATUS:  As we can have confirmed and tentative bookings we will send that information
 465   // in the Status property, as some calendar apps will use it.   For example Outlook 2007 will
 466   // distinguish between tentative and confirmed bookings.  However, having sent it we need to
 467   // send a STATUS:CANCELLED on cancellation.    It's not clear to me from the spec whether this
 468   // is strictly necessary, but it can do no harm and there are some apps that seem to need it -
 469   // for example Outlook 2003 (but not 2007).
 470   if ($method == "CANCEL")
 471   {
 472     $results[] = "STATUS:CANCELLED";
 473   }
 474   else
 475   {
 476     $results[] = "STATUS:" . ((empty($data['tentative'])) ? "CONFIRMED" : "TENTATIVE");
 477   }
 478 
 479   /*
 480   Class is commented out for the moment.  To be useful it probably needs to go
 481   hand in hand with an ORGANIZER, otherwise people won't be able to see their own
 482   bookings
 483   // CLASS
 484   $results[] = "CLASS:" . (($data['private']) ? "PRIVATE" : "PUBLIC");
 485   */
 486 
 487   // ORGANIZER
 488   // The organizer is MRBS.   We don't make the create_by user the organizer because there
 489   // are some mail systems such as IBM Domino that silently discard the email notification
 490   // if the organizer's email address is the same as the recipient's - presumably because
 491   // they assume that the recipient already knows about the event.
 492 
 493   $organizer_addresses = parse_addresses($mail_settings['organizer']);
 494   if (empty($organizer_addresses))
 495   {
 496     // TODO: Review whether the ORGANIZER property is required.
 497     // RFC 5545 states:
 498     // "This property MUST be specified in an iCalendar object
 499     // that specifies a group-scheduled calendar entity.  This property
 500     // MUST be specified in an iCalendar object that specifies the
 501     // publication of a calendar user's busy time.  This property MUST
 502     // NOT be specified in an iCalendar object that specifies only a time
 503     // zone definition or that defines calendar components that are not
 504     // group-scheduled components, but are components only on a single
 505     // user's calendar."
 506     // Does MRBS count as a user? If so, does this mean that as long as
 507     // there is at least one ATTENDEE the property MUST be specified?
 508     $message = "The value '" . $mail_settings['organizer'] . "' supplied for " . '$mail_settings["organizer"]' .
 509       " is not a valid RFC822-style email address.  Please check your MRBS config file.";
 510     throw new Exception($message);
 511   }
 512 
 513   $organizer = $organizer_addresses[0];
 514   if (!isset($organizer['name']) || ($organizer['name'] === ''))
 515   {
 516     $organizer['name'] = get_mail_vocab('mrbs');
 517   }
 518 
 519   if (isset($organizer['address']) && ($organizer['address'] !== ''))
 520   {
 521     $results[] = 'ORGANIZER;CN=' . RFC5545::escapeQuotedString($organizer['name']) . ':mailto:' . $organizer['address'];
 522   }
 523 
 524   // Put the people on the "to" list as required participants and those on the cc
 525   // list as non-participants.   In theory the email client can then decide whether
 526   // to enter the booking automatically on the user's calendar - although at the
 527   // time of writing (Dec 2010) there don't seem to be any that do so!
 528   if (!empty($addresses))
 529   {
 530     $attendees = $addresses;  // take a copy of $addresses as we're going to alter it
 531     $keys = array('to', 'cc');  // We won't do 'bcc' as they need to stay blind
 532     foreach ($keys as $key)
 533     {
 534       $attendees[$key] = parse_addresses($attendees[$key]);  // convert the list into an array
 535     }
 536     foreach ($keys as $key)
 537     {
 538       foreach ($attendees[$key] as $attendee)
 539       {
 540         if (!empty($attendee))
 541         {
 542           switch ($key)
 543           {
 544             case 'to':
 545               $role = "REQ-PARTICIPANT";
 546               break;
 547             default:
 548               if (in_array($attendee, $attendees['to']))
 549               {
 550                 // It's possible that an address could appear on more than one
 551                 // line, in which case we only want to have one ATTENDEE property
 552                 // for that address and we'll choose the REQ-PARTICIPANT.   (Apart
 553                 // from two conflicting ATTENDEES not making sense, it also breaks
 554                 // some applications, eg Apple Mail/iCal)
 555                 continue 2;  // Move on to the next attendeee
 556               }
 557               $role = "NON-PARTICIPANT";
 558               break;
 559           }
 560           // Use the common name if there is one
 561           $partstat = ($partstat_accepted) ? "ACCEPTED" : "NEEDS-ACTION";
 562           $results[] = "ATTENDEE;" .
 563                        ((isset($attendee['name']) && ($attendee['name'] !== '')) ? 'CN=' . RFC5545::escapeQuotedString($attendee['name']) . ';' : '') .
 564                        "PARTSTAT=$partstat;ROLE=$role:mailto:" . $attendee['address'];
 565         }
 566       }
 567       // TODO: custom fields
 568     }
 569   }
 570 
 571   // MRBS specific properties
 572   // Type
 573   $results[] = "X-MRBS-TYPE:" . RFC5545::escapeText(get_type_vocab($data['type']));
 574   // Registration properties
 575   if (isset($data['allow_registration']))
 576   {
 577     $properties = array(
 578       'allow_registration',
 579       'registrant_limit',
 580       'registrant_limit_enabled',
 581       'registration_opens',
 582       'registration_opens_enabled',
 583       'registration_closes',
 584       'registration_closes_enabled'
 585     );
 586     foreach ($properties as $property) {
 587       $results[] = "X-MRBS-" . strtoupper(str_replace('_', '-', $property)) . ":" . $data[$property];
 588     }
 589     // Registrants (but only for individual entries)
 590     if (!$series) {
 591       $registrants = get_registrants($data['id'], false);
 592       foreach ($registrants as $registrant) {
 593         // We can't use the ATTENDEE property because its value has to be a URI.
 594         $results[] = "X-MRBS-REGISTRANT;X-MRBS-REGISTERED=" . $registrant['registered'] .
 595           ';' . 'X-MRBS-CREATE-BY=' . RFC5545::escapeQuotedString($registrant['create_by']) .
 596           ':' . RFC5545::escapeText($registrant['username']);
 597       }
 598     }
 599   }
 600 
 601   $results[] = "END:VEVENT";
 602 
 603   // No CRLF at end: that will be added later
 604   return implode(RFC5545::EOL, $results);
 605 }
 606 
 607 
 608 // Creates an iCalendar object in RFC 5545 format
 609 //    $method      string   the RFC 5545 METHOD (eg "REQUEST", "PUBLISH", "CANCEL")
 610 //    $components  array    an array of iCalendar components, each a string
 611 function create_icalendar(string $method, array $components) : string
 612 {
 613   require_once "version.inc";
 614 
 615   global $timezone;
 616 
 617   $vtimezone = get_vtimezone($timezone);
 618 
 619   $results = array();
 620   $results[] = "BEGIN:VCALENDAR";
 621   // Compulsory properties
 622   $results[] = "PRODID:-//MRBS//NONSGML " . get_mrbs_version() . "//EN";
 623   $results[] = "VERSION:2.0";
 624   // Optional properties
 625   $results[] = "CALSCALE:GREGORIAN";
 626   $results[] = "METHOD:$method";
 627 
 628   // Add in the VTIMEZONE component if there is one (see the comment in
 629   // create_ical_event() above)
 630   if ($vtimezone)
 631   {
 632     $results[] = $vtimezone;
 633   }
 634 
 635   // Add in each component
 636   foreach ($components as $component)
 637   {
 638     $results[] = $component;
 639   }
 640 
 641   $results[] = "END:VCALENDAR";
 642 
 643   $result = implode(RFC5545::EOL, $results);
 644   $result .= RFC5545::EOL;  // Has to end with the correct line ending
 645   $result = RFC5545::fold($result);
 646 
 647   return $result;
 648 }
 649 
 650 
 651 // outputs an iCalendar based on the data in $res, the result of an SQL query.
 652 //
 653 //    &$res       resource  the result of an SQL query on the entry table, which
 654 //                          has been sorted by repeat_id, start_time (both ascending).
 655 //                          As well as all the fields in the entry table, the rows will
 656 //                          also contain the area name, the room name and the repeat
 657 //                          details (rep_type, end_date, rep_opt, rep_interval)
 658 //    $export_end int       a Unix timestamp giving the end limit for the export
 659 function export_icalendar(DBStatement $res, bool $keep_private, int $export_end=PHP_INT_MAX) : void
 660 {
 661   require_once "functions_view.inc";
 662   require_once "mrbs_sql.inc";
 663 
 664   // We construct an iCalendar by going through the rows from the SQL query.  Because
 665   // it was sorted by repeat_id we will
 666   //    - get all the individual entries (which will not have a repeat_id)
 667   //    - then get the series.    For each series we have to:
 668   //        - identify the series information.
 669   //        - identify any events that have been changed from the standard, ie events
 670   //          with entry_type == ENTRY_RPT_CHANGED
 671   //        - identify any events from the original series that have been cancelled.  We
 672   //          can do this because we know from the repeat information the events that
 673   //          should be there, and we can tell from the start times the events that are
 674   //          actually there.
 675 
 676   // We use PUBLISH rather than REQUEST because we're not inviting people to these meetings,
 677   // we're just exporting the calendar.   Furthermore, if we don't use PUBLISH then some
 678   // calendar apps (eg Outlook, at least 2010 and 2013) won't open the full calendar.
 679   $method = "PUBLISH";
 680 
 681   // Initialize an array to hold the events and a variable to keep track
 682   // of the last repeat id we've seen
 683   $ical_events = array();
 684   $n_rows = $res->count();
 685 
 686   for ($i=0; (false !== ($row = $res->next_row_keyed())); $i++)
 687   {
 688     row_cast_columns($row, 'entry');
 689     // Turn the last_updated column into an int (some MySQL drivers will return a string,
 690     // and it won't have been caught by row_cast_columns as it's a derived result).
 691     $row['last_updated'] = intval($row['last_updated']);
 692     unpack_status($row);
 693     // If this is an individual entry, then construct an event
 694     if (!isset($row['rep_type']) || ($row['rep_type'] == RepeatRule::NONE))
 695     {
 696       $ical_events[] = create_ical_event($method, $row);
 697     }
 698 
 699     // Otherwise it's a series
 700     else
 701     {
 702       // If we haven't started a series, then start one
 703       if (!isset($series))
 704       {
 705         $series = new Series($row, $export_end);
 706       }
 707 
 708       // Otherwise, if this row is a member of the current series, add the row to the series.
 709       elseif ($row['repeat_id'] == $series->repeat_id)
 710       {
 711         $series->addRow($row);
 712       }
 713 
 714       // If it's a series that we haven't seen yet, or we've got no more
 715       // rows, then process the series
 716       if (($row['repeat_id'] != $series->repeat_id) || ($i == $n_rows - 1))
 717       {
 718         $ical_events = array_merge($ical_events, $series->toEvents($method));
 719         // If we're at the start of a new series then create a new series
 720         if ($row['repeat_id'] != $series->repeat_id)
 721         {
 722           $series = new Series($row, $export_end);
 723           // And if this is the last row, ie the only member of the new series
 724           // then process the new series
 725           if ($i == $n_rows - 1)
 726           {
 727             $ical_events = array_merge($ical_events, $series->toEvents($method));
 728           }
 729         }
 730 
 731       }
 732     }
 733   }
 734 
 735   // Build the iCalendar from the array of events and output it
 736   $icalendar = create_icalendar($method, $ical_events);
 737   echo $icalendar;
 738 }

  67 // TODO: It's actually returning tablename.columnname at the moment if it

  78 /**
  79  * Format a timestamp in non-unicode output (for emails).
  80  *
  81  * @param   int         $t
  82  * @param   int         $mod_time
  83  * @return  array
  84  */
  85 function getMailPeriodDateString(int $t, int $mod_time=0) : array
  86 {
  87   global $periods, $datetime_formats;
  88 
  89   $time = getdate($t);
  90   $p_num = $time['minutes'] + $mod_time;
  91 
  92   // Make sure we have a valid period [should this be necessary??]
  93   if ($p_num < 0)
  94   {
  95     $p_num = 0;
  96   }
  97 
  98   if ($p_num > count($periods) - 1)
  99   {
 100     $p_num = count($periods) - 1;
 101   }
 102 
 103   $mailperiod = $periods[$p_num];
 104 
 105   // The separator is a ',' as a '-' leads to an ambiguous display in report.php when showing end times.
 106   return array($p_num, $mailperiod . ', ' . datetime_format($datetime_formats['date'], $t, get_mail_locale()));
 107 }
 108 
 109 // }}}
 110 // {{{ getMailTimeDateString()
 111 
 112 /**
 113  * Format a timestamp in non-unicode output (for emails).
 114  *
 115  * @param   int         $t         timestamp to format
 116  * @param   boolean     $inc_time  include time in return string
 117  * @return  string                 formatted string
 118  */
 119 function getMailTimeDateString(int $t, bool $inc_time=true) : string
 120 {
 121   global $datetime_formats;
 122 
 123   $format = ($inc_time) ? $datetime_formats['date_and_time'] : $datetime_formats['date'];
 124   return datetime_format($format, $t, get_mail_locale());
 125 }

 144 // get_address_list($array)
 145 //
 146 // Takes an array of email addresses and returns a comma separated
 147 // list of addresses with duplicates removed.
 148 function get_address_list(array $address_strings) : string
 149 {
 150   // Remove any leading and trailing whitespace and any empty strings
 151   $trimmed_array = array();
 152   foreach ($address_strings as $address_string)
 153   {
 154     $address_string = trim($address_string);
 155     if ($address_string !== '')
 156     {
 157       // Use parse_addresses to validate the address because it could contain a display name
 158       if (count(parse_addresses($address_string)) == 0)
 159       {
 160         $message = 'Invalid email address "' . $address_string . '"';
 161         mail_debug($message);
 162         trigger_error($message, E_USER_NOTICE);
 163       }
 164       $trimmed_array[] = $address_string;
 165     }
 166   }
 167   // remove duplicates
 168   $trimmed_array = array_unique($trimmed_array);
 169   // re-assemble the string
 170   return implode(',', $trimmed_array);
 171 }

 193 // Get the area_admin_email for an entry $id
 194 // If $series is set this is an entry in the repeat table, otherwise the entry table
 195 // Returns an empty string in the case of an error
 196 function get_area_admin_email($id, bool $series=false) : string
 197 {
 198   $id_table = ($series) ? "rep" : "e";
 199 
 200   $sql = "SELECT a.area_admin_email ";
 201   $sql .= "FROM " . _tbl('room') . " r, " . _tbl('area') . " a, " . _tbl('entry') . " e ";
 202   // If this is a repeating entry...
 203   if ($id_table == 'rep')
 204   {
 205     // ...use the repeat table
 206     $sql .= ", " . _tbl('repeat') . " rep ";
 207   }
 208   $sql .= "WHERE {$id_table}.id=?
 209              AND r.id={$id_table}.room_id
 210              AND a.id=r.area_id
 211            LIMIT 1";
 212   $email = db()->query_scalar_non_bool($sql, array($id));
 213 
 214   return (!isset($email) || ($email === false)) ? '' : $email;
 215 }

 242 // Create a row of a table in either plain text or HTML format.
 243 // Plain text:  returns "$label: $new" . MAIL_EOL
 244 // HTML:        returns "<tr><td>$label: </td><td>$new</td></tr>" . MAIL_EOL
 245 // $new and $old can be of type null|int|float|string (union declarations are not supported until PHP 8.0).
 246 // If $compare is TRUE then a third column is output with $old in parentheses
 247 function create_body_table_row(string $label, $new, $old, bool $compare=false, bool $as_html=false) : string
 248 {
 249   $new = $new ?? '';
 250   $old = $old ?? '';
 251 
 252   $result  = ($as_html) ? '<tr>' . MAIL_EOL : '';
 253 
 254   // The label
 255   $result .= ($as_html) ? '<td>' : '';
 256   $result .= ($as_html) ? escape_html("$label: ") : "$label: ";
 257   $result .= ($as_html) ? '</td>' . MAIL_EOL : '';
 258   // The new value
 259   $result .= ($as_html) ? '<td>' : '';
 260   $result .= ($as_html) ? escape_html($new) : "$new";
 261   $result .= ($as_html) ? '</td>' . MAIL_EOL : '';
 262   // The old value (if we're doing a comparison)
 263   if ($compare)
 264   {
 265     $result .= ($as_html) ? '<td>' : '';
 266     if ($new == $old)
 267     {
 268       $result .= ($as_html) ? "&nbsp;" : '';
 269     }
 270     else
 271     {
 272       // Put parentheses around the HTML version as well as the plain text
 273       // version in case the table is not rendered properly in HTML.  The
 274       // parentheses will make the old value stand out.
 275       $result .= ($as_html) ? escape_html(" ($old)") : " ($old)";
 276     }
 277     $result .= ($as_html) ? '</td>' . MAIL_EOL : '';
 278   }
 279 
 280   $result .= ($as_html) ? '</tr>' : '';
 281   $result .= MAIL_EOL;
 282   return $result;
 283 }
 284 
 285 
 286 // Generate a list of dates from an array of start times
 287 //
 288 //   $dates      an array of start times
 289 //   $as_html    (boolean) whether the list should be HTML or plain text
 290 function create_date_list(array $dates, bool $as_html) : string
 291 {
 292   $result = ($as_html) ? '<ul>' . MAIL_EOL : '';
 293   foreach ($dates as $date)
 294   {
 295     $result .= ($as_html) ? '<li>' : '';
 296     $date_string = getMailDateString($date);
 297     $result .= ($as_html) ? escape_html($date_string) : $date_string;
 298     $result .= ($as_html) ? '</li>' : '';
 299     // The newline is important to stop the line length exceeding 998 characters,
 300     // which will happen if there are a lot of dates.  See RFC 5322 2.1.1.
 301     $result .= MAIL_EOL;
 302   }
 303   $result .= ($as_html) ? '</ul>' . MAIL_EOL : '';
 304   return $result;
 305 }

 307 
 308 // Generate a list of repeat dates for a series
 309 //
 310 // $reps is an array of start_times that have been created/modified/deleted.
 311 function create_repeat_list(array $data, $action, bool $as_html, array $reps) : string
 312 {
 313   if (($data['repeat_rule']->getType() == RepeatRule::NONE) ||
 314        in_array($action, array('more_info', 'remind')))
 315   {
 316     return '';
 317   }
 318 
 319   // The introductory text
 320   $result = ($as_html) ? '<p>' : MAIL_EOL . MAIL_EOL;
 321   if (($action == "delete") || ($action == "reject"))
 322   {
 323     $result .= get_vocab("mail_body_repeats_deleted");
 324   }
 325   else
 326   {
 327     $result .= get_vocab("mail_body_repeats_booked");
 328   }
 329   $result .= ($as_html) ? '</p>' . MAIL_EOL : MAIL_EOL . MAIL_EOL;
 330 
 331   $result .= create_date_list($reps, $as_html);
 332 
 333   // Now add in the list of repeat bookings that could not be booked
 334   if (!empty($data['skip_list']))
 335   {
 336     // The introductory text
 337     $result .= ($as_html) ? '<p>' : MAIL_EOL . MAIL_EOL;
 338     $result .= get_vocab("mail_body_exceptions");
 339     $result .= ($as_html) ? '</p>' . MAIL_EOL : MAIL_EOL . MAIL_EOL;
 340     // Now the list of conflicts
 341     $result .= create_date_list($data['skip_list'], $as_html);
 342   }
 343 
 344   return $result;
 345 }
