 362 
 363 function get_date_heading(string $view, int $year, int $month, int $day) : string
 364 {
 365   global $datetime_formats, $display_timezone, $timezone,
 366          $weekstarts, $year_start, $view_week_number;
 367 
 368   $html = '';
 369   $time = mktime(12, 0, 0, $month, $day, $year);
 370 
 371   $html .= '<h2 class="date">';
 372 
 373   switch ($view)
 374   {
 375     case 'day':
 376       $html .= datetime_format($datetime_formats['view_day'], $time);
 377       break;
 378 
 379     case 'week':
 380       // Display the week number if required, provided the MRBS week starts on the first day
 381       // of the week, otherwise it's spanning two weeks and doesn't make sense.
 382       if ($view_week_number && ($weekstarts == DateTime::firstDayOfWeek($timezone, get_mrbs_locale())))
 383       {
 384         $html .= '<span class="week_number">' .
 385                  get_vocab('week_number', datetime_format($datetime_formats['week_number'], $time)) .
 386                  '</span>';
 387       }
 388       // Then display the actual dates
 389       $day_of_week = date('w', $time);
 390       $our_day_of_week = ($day_of_week + DAYS_PER_WEEK - $weekstarts) % DAYS_PER_WEEK;
 391       $ranger = new Ranger(get_mrbs_locale());
 392       $ranger
 393         ->setRangeSeparator(get_vocab('range_separator'))
 394         ->setDateType($datetime_formats['view_week']['date_type'] ?? IntlDateFormatter::LONG)
 395         ->setTimeType($datetime_formats['view_week']['time_type'] ?? IntlDateFormatter::NONE);
 396       $range = $ranger->format(
 397         format_iso_date($year, $month, $day - $our_day_of_week),
 398         format_iso_date($year, $month, $day +6 - $our_day_of_week)
 399       );
 400       $html .= $range;
 401       break;
 402 
 403     case 'month':
 404       $html .= datetime_format($datetime_formats['view_month'], $time);
 405       break;
 406 
 407     case 'year':
 408       $ranger = new YearRanger(get_mrbs_locale());
 409       $ranger->setSeparator(get_vocab('year_range_separator'));
 410       $start_date = (new DateTime())->setDate($year, $month, $day);
 411       $start_date->setMonthYearStart($year_start);
 412       $end_date = clone $start_date;
 413       $end_date->modifyMonthsNoOverflow(MONTHS_PER_YEAR - 1, true);
 414       $range = $ranger->format($start_date, $end_date);
 415       $html .= $range;
 416       break;
 417 
 418     default:
 419       throw new \Exception("Unknown view '$view'");
 420       break;
 421   }
 422 
 423   $html .= '</h2>';
 424 
 425   if ($display_timezone)
 426   {
 427     $html .= '<span class="timezone">';
 428     $html .= get_vocab("timezone") . ": " . datetime_format($datetime_formats['timezone'], $time);
 429     $html .= '</span>';
 430   }
 431 
 432   return $html;
 433 }
 434 
 435 
 436 function message_html() : string
 437 {
 438   $message = Message::getInstance();
 439   $message->load();
 440 
 441   if ($message->hasSomethingToDisplay())
 442   {
 443     return '<p class="message_top">' . $message->getEscapedText() . "</p>\n";
 444   }
 445 
 446   return '';
 447 }
 448 
 449 // Get non-standard form variables
 450 $refresh = get_form_var('refresh', 'int');
 451 $timetohighlight = get_form_var('timetohighlight', 'int');
 452 
 453 // The room select uses a negative value of $room to signify that we want to view all
 454 // rooms in an area.   The absolute value of $room is the current room.
 455 if ($room < 0)
 456 {
 457   $room = abs($room);
 458   $view_all = 1;
 459 }
 460 
 461 // We only support the day view in kiosk mode at the moment
 462 if (isset($kiosk))
 463 {
 464   $view = 'day';
 465 }
 466 
 467 $is_ajax = is_ajax();
 468 
 469 // If we're using an authentication type that supports the creation of users, eg 'db'
 470 // or an extension of that type, then check to see if MRBS has just been installed
 471 // and, if so, redirect to the edit_users page so that they can set up users.
 472 if (auth()->canCreateUsers() && (count(auth()->getUsers()) == 0))
 473 {
 474   location_header('edit_users.php');
 475 }
 476 
 477 // Check the user is authorised for this page
 478 if (!checkAuthorised(this_page(), $refresh))
 479 {
 480   exit;
 481 }
 482 
 483 $calendar = CalendarFactory::create($view, $view_all, $year, $month, $day, $area, $room, $timetohighlight, $kiosk);
 484 $inner_html = $calendar->innerHTML();
 485 $date_heading = get_date_heading($view, $year, $month, $day);
 486 
 487 if ($refresh)
 488 {
 489   echo json_encode(array(
 490     'date_heading' => $date_heading,
 491     'inner_html' => $inner_html
 492   ));
 493   exit;
 494 }
 495 
 496 // print the page header
 497 $context = array(
 498     'view'      => $view,
 499     'view_all'  => $view_all,
 500     'year'      => $year,
 501     'month'     => $month,
 502     'day'       => $day,
 503     'area'      => $area,
 504     'room'      => $room ?? null,
 505     'kiosk'     => $kiosk ?? null
 506   );
 507 
 508 print_header($context);
 509 
 510 echo "<div class=\"minicalendars\">\n";
 511 echo "</div>\n";
 512 
 513 echo "<div class=\"view_container js_hidden\">\n";
 514 echo "<div class=\"date_heading\">$date_heading</div>";
 515 echo get_calendar_nav($view, $view_all, $year, $month, $day, $area, $room);
 516 
 517 echo message_html();
 518 
 519 $classes = array('dwm_main');
 520 if ($times_along_top)
 521 {
 522   $classes[] .= 'times-along-top';
 523 }
 524 if (($view == 'year') || ($view_all && ($view !== 'day')))
 525 {
 526   // "all_rooms" is a bad description as we now also use the class for a single
 527   // room in the year view.  Something like "overview" would be better, but we
 528   // keep using "all_rooms" for the moment because there may be people with custom
 529   // CSS that have rules using "all_rooms".
 530   $classes[] = 'all_rooms';
 531 }
 532 
 533 echo "<div class=\"table_container\">\n";
 534 echo '<table class="' . implode(' ', $classes) . "\" id=\"{$view}_main\" data-resolution=\"$resolution\">\n";
 535 echo $inner_html;
 536 echo "</table>\n";
 537 echo "</div>\n";
 538 
 539 // The bottom navigation bar is controlled by JavaScript
 540 echo get_calendar_nav($view, $view_all, $year, $month, $day, $area, $room, true);
 541 
 542 echo get_color_key();
 543 echo "</div>\n";
 544 
 545 print_footer();

   1 <?php
   2 declare(strict_types=1);
   3 namespace MRBS;
   4 
   5 // Site-specific php.ini settings
   6 use MRBS\Errors\Errors;
   7 
   8 if (!empty($ini_directives))
   9 {
  10   foreach ($ini_directives as $option => $value)
  11   {
  12     ini_set($option, $value);
  13   }
  14 }
  15 
  16 // Set the session scheme if it hasn't been already
  17 if (!isset($auth['session']))
  18 {
  19   switch ($auth['type'])
  20   {
  21     case 'cas':
  22     case 'joomla':
  23     case 'saml':
  24     case 'wordpress':
  25       $auth['session'] = $auth['type'];
  26       break;
  27     default:
  28       $auth['session'] = 'php';
  29       break;
  30   }
  31 }
  32 
  33 // Initialise the session.  This is necessary because some session schemes, eg Joomla,
  34 // use the same third party interfaces, eg \Psr\Log\LoggerInterface, as MRBS, but of
  35 // different versions. The MRBS one tends to be an earlier version of the interface than
  36 // Joomla's, with less strict type declarations.  If the MRBS autoloader loads the MRBS
  37 // version first, then when the Joomla autoloader tries to load a class that implements
  38 // the interface you get errors such as
  39 //
  40 // "Declaration of Psr\Log\AbstractLogger::emergency(Stringable|string $message, array
  41 // $context = []): void must be compatible with Psr\Log\LoggerInterface::emergency($message,
  42 // array $context = [])"
  43 //
  44 // But if we initialise the session *before* calling Errors::init(), then this will force the
  45 // Joomla version of the interface to be loaded first, and there won't be any errors because
  46 // the MRBS classes implementing the interface are compatible (ie the MRBS type declarations
  47 // are a superset of the Joomla interface declarations).
  48 //
  49 // TODO: is there a better way of solving this problem?  Maybe use a REST API to communicate with
  50 // TODO: Joomla, rather than including Joomla files?  We'd then also be able to authenticate
  51 // TODO: against remote servers.
  52 session();
  53 
  54 // Initialise error reporting
  55 Errors::init();
  56 
  57 // Flush the mail queue on shutdown
  58 register_shutdown_function(__NAMESPACE__ . "\\MailQueue::flush");
  59 
  60 // Check extensions
  61 if ((version_compare(PHP_VERSION, '8.1.0') >= 0) && !extension_loaded('intl'))
  62 {
  63   // We suppress deprecation messages each time we use strftime() in MRBS's emulation of the IntlDateFormatter
  64   // class and just have a single message here, in order to avoid flooding the log with messages.
  65   $message = "MRBS has detected that you do not have the PHP 'intl' extension loaded on your server and " .
  66              "so it is using the deprecated strftime() function instead.  You are recommended to enable " .
  67              "the 'intl' extension.";
  68   trigger_error($message, E_USER_DEPRECATED);
  69 }
  70 
  71 if (method_exists(session(), 'processForm'))
  72 {
  73   session()->processForm();
  74 }
  75 
  76 // If we're in kiosk mode make sure somebody's not trying to get to anywhere other than
  77 // index.php with a kiosk query string parameter, kiosk.php or one of the js/***.js.php pages.
  78 if (is_kiosk_mode() &&
  79     !((isset($server['REQUEST_URI']) && preg_match('/index\.php\?.*kiosk=/', $server['REQUEST_URI'])) ||
  80       (isset($server['SCRIPT_NAME']) && preg_match('/kiosk\.php$|js\/.+\.js\.php$/', $server['SCRIPT_NAME']) )))
  81 {
  82   $location = (session()->isset('kiosk_url')) ? session()->get('kiosk_url') : "index.php?kiosk=$kiosk_default_mode";
  83   location_header(multisite($location));
  84 }

 160   if (in_array('room_id', $edit_entry_field_order))
 161   {
 162     array_splice($edit_entry_field_order, $key, 1);
 163   }
 164   else
 165   {
 166     $edit_entry_field_order[$key] = 'room_id';
 167   }
 168   $message = 'Please check your MRBS config file.  The value \'rooms\' in the variable ' .
 169              '$edit_entry_field_order has been replaced by \'room_id\'.';
 170   trigger_error($message, E_USER_NOTICE);
 171 }
 172 
 173 // Variables no longer used in versions of MRBS > 1.11.0
 174 if (isset($twentyfourhour_format))
 175 {
 176   $message = 'Please check your MRBS config file. The setting $twentyfourhour_format ' .
 177              'is no longer used and whether a 12 or 24-hour clock is used is determined ' .
 178              'by the locale. See systemdefaults.inc.php for more details.';
 179   trigger_error($message, E_USER_NOTICE);
 180 }
 181 
 182 if (isset($strftime_format))
 183 {
 184   $message = 'Please check your MRBS config file. The setting $strftime_format ' .
 185              'is no longer used and has been replaced by $datetime_formats. ' .
 186              'See systemdefaults.inc.php for more details.';
 187   trigger_error($message, E_USER_NOTICE);
 188 }

 191 /********************************************************
 192  * Checking
 193  ********************************************************/
 194 
 195 // Check that $timezone has been set
 196 if (!isset($timezone))
 197 {
 198   die('MRBS configuration error: $timezone has not been set.');
 199 }
 200 
 201 // Do some consistency checking of user settings from config.inc.php
 202 if ($enable_periods)
 203 {
 204   if (isset($periods) && (count($periods) > 60))
 205   {
 206     die('MRBS configuration error: too many periods defined');
 207   }
 208 }
 209 else
 210 {
 211   if (!isset($resolution))
 212   {
 213     die('MRBS configuration error: $resolution has not been set.');
 214   }
 215   if ($resolution <= 0)
 216   {
 217     die('MRBS configuration error: $resolution is less than or equal to zero.');
 218   }
 219   if ($resolution%60 != 0)
 220   {
 221     die('MRBS configuration error: $resolution is not an integral number of minutes.');
 222   }
 223   // Not safe to call get_start_first_slot() etc. here as the timezone won't necessarily have
 224   // been set yet(although quite often it will have been by php.ini using date.timezone)
 225   $start_first_slot = (($morningstarts * 60) + $morningstarts_minutes) * 60;
 226   $start_last_slot = (($eveningends * 60) + $eveningends_minutes) * 60;
 227   if ($start_last_slot < $start_first_slot)
 228   {
 229     $start_last_slot += 60*60*24;
 230   }
 231   $start_difference = $start_last_slot - $start_first_slot;    // seconds
 232   if ($start_difference%$resolution != 0)
 233   {
 234     die('MRBS configuration error: make sure that the length of the booking day is an integral multiple of $resolution.');
 235   }
 236 }

   6 // Generates the HTML for a <script> element
   7 function script_html(string $src, bool $add_version=false) : string
   8 {
   9   $html = '<script src="';
  10   $value = ($add_version) ? add_version($src) : $src;
  11   $html .= escape_html($value);
  12   $html .= "\"></script>\n";
  13 
  14   return $html;
  15 }
  16 
  17 
  18 global $area;
  19 global $multisite, $site;
  20 global $debug;
  21 global $custom_js_url;
  22 
  23 $page = this_page(false, '.php');
  24 
  25 // We need to construct a standard query string that can be passed to the *.js.php
  26 // pages.  That's because some of the settings they use are area dependent.
  27 // We also want the area to be in the query string so that the JavaScript page is
  28 // cached if the area is the same and not otherwise.
  29 $query_string = "area=$area";
  30 
  31 if ($multisite && isset($site) && ($site !== ''))
  32 {
  33   $query_string .= '&site=' . urlencode($site);
  34 }
  35 
  36 // Load the init file now so that it gets executed as soon as possible.  The init
  37 // file can't use jQuery.
  38 echo script_html('js/init.js.php', true);
  39 
  40 echo script_html(($debug) ? 'jquery/jquery-3.7.1.js' : 'jquery/jquery-3.7.1.min.js');
  41 
  42 // We need the migration script now that we are running jQuery 3.0+, or at least
  43 // until we are confident that our JavaScript is not using any features that have
  44 // been removed.   The uncompressed version will output warnings about removed and
  45 // deprecated features to the console
  46 echo script_html(($debug) ? 'jquery/jquery-migrate-3.5.0.js' : 'jquery/jquery-migrate-3.5.0.min.js');
  47 
  48 // We are using the jQuery UI library, which has been custom-built to include the following components:
  49 //   - Core
  50 //      - as defined by dependencies in order to support the required interactions and widgets
  51 //      - no need for jQuery 1.8 support
  52 //
  53 //   - Interactions
  54 //      - Draggable
  55 //      - Resizable
  56 //
  57 //   - Widgets
  58 //      - Autocomplete
  59 //      - Button
  60 //      - Dialog
  61 //      - Menu
  62 //      - Mouse
  63 //      - Tabs
  64 //
  65 //   - Cupertino theme
  66 // If you need any other components you will need to rebuild the custom UI library
  67 // See http://jqueryui.com/
  68 echo script_html(($debug) ? 'jquery/ui/jquery-ui.js' : 'jquery/ui/jquery-ui.min.js', true);
  69 
  70 // All pages
  71 echo script_html("js/functions.js.php?$query_string", true);
  72 echo script_html("js/general.js.php?$query_string", true);
  73 
  74 
  75 echo script_html("js/flatpickr/flatpickr.min.js", true);
  76 $datepicker_src = "js/datepicker.js.php?$query_string";
  77 $flatpickr_lang_path = get_flatpickr_lang_path();
  78 if (isset($flatpickr_lang_path))
  79 {
  80   // Add the localisation file
  81   echo script_html($flatpickr_lang_path, true);
  82   // And give the datepicker file a query string parameter to force the browser cache
  83   // to be flushed when the language changes.
  84   $datepicker_src .= '&lang=' . urlencode(get_flatpickr_property($flatpickr_lang_path));
  85 }
  86 echo script_html($datepicker_src, true);
  87 
  88 echo script_html("jquery/select2/dist/js/select2.full.min.js", true);
  89 
  90 if (null !== ($select2_lang_path = get_select2_lang_path()))
  91 {
  92   echo script_html($select2_lang_path, true);
  93 }
  94 
  95 // dataTables initialisation
  96 if (in_array($page, array('admin', 'edit_users', 'pending', 'report', 'search', 'view_entry')))
  97 {
  98   // Include the JavaScript for those pages that use dataTables
  99   // When constructing the DataTables download we want to include the following:
 100   //    DataTables styling framework
 101   //    DataTables package
 102   //    Buttons, and all sub-options
 103   //    ColReorder
 104   //    FixedColumns
 105   echo script_html(($debug) ? 'jquery/datatables/datatables.js' : 'jquery/datatables/datatables.min.js', true);
 106   echo script_html('jquery/datatables/plugins.js', true);
 107   echo script_html("js/datatables.js.php?$query_string", true);
 108 }
 109 
 110 // Get any page specific JavaScript
 111 if (is_readable("js/$page.js"))
 112 {
 113   echo script_html("js/$page.js?$query_string", true);
 114 }
 115 if (is_readable("js/$page.js.php"))
 116 {
 117   echo script_html("js/$page.js.php?$query_string", true);
 118 }
 119 
 120 // The day, week and month views do refresh by Ajax.
 121 // We need the resizable bookings for the day and week views
 122 if ($page == 'index')
 123 {
 124   echo script_html("js/refresh.js.php?$query_string", true);
 125   echo script_html("js/resizable.js.php?$query_string", true);
 126 }
 127 
 128 if (isset($custom_js_url))
 129 {
 130   echo script_html($custom_js_url, true);
 131 }
 132 
 133 // Include the HTML5 Shiv so that elements such as <header> etc. can be styled in IE8 and below.
 134 // (Even though we don't support IE8 and below, we still need the HTML5 Shiv for styling the
 135 // page which says we don't support them!).
 136 echo "<!--[if lte IE 8]>\n";
 137 echo script_html(($debug) ? 'js/html5shiv.js' : 'js/html5shiv.min.js', true);
 138 echo "<![endif]-->\n";

 103     var addDeleteButton = function addDeleteButton() {
 104 
 105       var data;
 106       var batches;
 107       var nBatches;
 108       var nEntries;
 109       var progressContainer = $('<div id="progress_container"></div>');
 110       var requests;
 111       var requestsCompleted;
 112       var requestsAborted;
 113 
 114       <?php // Initialise the delete button and progress bar ?>
 115       function initDeleteButton()
 116       {
 117         var title = '<?php echo get_js_vocab("deleting_n_entries") ?>';
 118         data = reportTable.rows({filter: 'applied'}).data().toArray();
 119         nEntries = data.length;
 120         requests = [];
 121         requestsCompleted = 0;
 122         requestsAborted = 0;
 123         title = title.replace('%d', nEntries.toLocaleString());
 124         progressContainer.find('span').text(title);
 125       }
 126 
 127       function reloadReport() {
 128         $('#report_table_processing').css('visibility', 'hidden');
 129 
 130         <?php
 131         // Reload the page to get the new dataset.   If we're using
 132         // an Ajax data source (for true Ajax data sources, not server
 133         // side processing) and there's no summary table we can be
 134         // slightly more elegant and just reload the Ajax data source.
 135         ?>
 136 
 137         if (reportTable.ajax.url() &&
 138           !reportTable.page.info().serverSide &&
 139           ($('#div_summary').length === 0))
 140         {
 141           reportTable.ajax.reload(function() {
 142             <?php
 143             // Once the report data has been reloaded we also need to update the number of entries,
 144             // hide the progress bar and reinitialise the delete button for the new data.
 145             ?>
 146             progressContainer.hide();
 147             initDeleteButton();
 148             $('#n_entries').text(nEntries);
 149           });
 150         }
 151         else
 152         {
 153           window.location.reload();
 154         }
 155       }
 156 
 157       <?php
 158       // Add a progress bar, with a title and a cancel button. The title text will be
 159       // added later, once we know how many entries there are to be deleted.
 160       ?>
 161       progressContainer.append('<span></span>')
 162         .append('<progress></progress>')
 163         .append('<button id="cancel_deletions"><?php echo get_js_vocab("cancel") ?></button>')
 164         .insertAfter('#report_table_paginate');
 165 
 166       <?php // Add a delete button ?>
 167       $('<button id="delete_button"><?php echo get_js_vocab("delete_entries") ?><\/button>')
 168         .on('click', function() {
 169             if (nEntries === 0) {
 170               return;
 171             }
 172 
 173             <?php
 174             // Fire off an Ajax POST request.  Upon completion fire off another one until there
 175             // are none left.
 176             ?>
 177             var postBatch = function(batch) {
 178               var params = {
 179                 csrf_token: getCSRFToken(),
 180                 <?php // The ids are JSON encoded to avoid hitting the php.ini max_input_vars limit ?>
 181                 ids: JSON.stringify(batch)
 182               };
 183               if (args.site) {
 184                 params.site = args.site;
 185               }
 186               <?php // Save the XHR request in case we need to abort it ?>
 187               requests.push($.post(
 188                   'ajax/del_entries.php',
 189                   params,
 190                   function (result) {
 191                     var isInt = /^\s*\d+\s*$/;
 192                     requestsCompleted++;
 193                     if (isInt.test(result)) {
 194                       totalDeleted += parseInt(result, 10);
 195                       progress.val(totalDeleted).text(totalDeleted);
 196                     } else {
 197                       success = false;
 198                     }
 199                     <?php // Fire off another request if there is one ?>
 200                     var batch = batches.pop();
 201                     if (batch !== undefined) {
 202                       postBatch(batch);
 203                     }
 204                     <?php // Otherwise check whether everything has finished ?>
 205                     else if (requestsCompleted + requestsAborted >= nBatches) {
 206                       <?php
 207                       // Log the time it took to delete the entries if we're got $debug set.
 208                       if ($debug)
 209                       {
 210                         ?>
 211                         console.log((Date.now() - startTime)/1000 + " seconds");
 212                         <?php
 213                       }
 214                       ?>
 215                       if (!success) {
 216                         window.alert("<?php echo get_js_vocab('delete_entries_failed') ?>");
 217                       }
 218                       reloadReport();
 219                     }
 220                   }
 221                 )
 222               )
 223             }
 224 
 225             var message = "<?php echo get_js_vocab('delete_entries_warning') ?>";
 226             message = message.replace('%s', nEntries.toLocaleString());
 227             if (!window.confirm(message)) {
 228               return;
 229             }
 230             var progress = progressContainer.find('progress');
 231             var success = true;
 232             var totalDeleted = 0;
 233             <?php
 234             // If $debug is set record how long it takes to delete the entries
 235             if ($debug)
 236             {
 237               ?>
 238               var startTime = Date.now();
 239               <?php
 240             }
 241             ?>
 242 
 243             progress.attr('max', nEntries).val(0).text('0');
 244             progressContainer.show();
 245             <?php
 246             // We're going to split the POST requests into batches because if a
 247             // single POST request is too large we could get a 406 error. The POST
 248             // requests are fired off asynchronously, so we need to count them all
 249             // back before we know that we've finished.
 250             ?>
 251             var batchSize = <?php echo $del_entries_ajax_batch_size ?>,
 252                 batch = [],
 253                 i;
 254 
 255             batches = [];
 256 
 257             for (i=0; i<nEntries; i++) {
 258               batch.push($(data[i][0]).siblings('a').data('id'));
 259               if (batch.length >= batchSize) {
 260                 batches.push(batch);
 261                 batch = [];
 262               }
 263             }
 264             if (batch.length > 0) {
 265               batches.push(batch);
 266             }
 267             <?php
 268             // Dispatch the batches (if any) setting off parallel Ajax requests up to the maximum
 269             // number determined by the config settings.  When each request completes it will set
 270             // off another one until all the batches have been processed.
 271             ?>
 272             nBatches = batches.length;
 273             if (nBatches > 0) {
 274               $('#report_table_processing').css('visibility', 'visible');
 275               for (i=0; i<<?php echo $del_entries_parallel_requests ?>; i++) {
 276                 batch = batches.pop();
 277                 if (batch !== undefined) {
 278                   postBatch(batch);
 279                 }
 280               }
 281             }
 282           })
 283         .insertAfter('#report_table_paginate');
 284 
 285       <?php // While deletion is in progress disable all interaction except with the cancel button ?>
 286       $(window).on('click keypress', function(e) {
 287         if (progressContainer.is(':visible'))
 288         {
 289           if (e.target.id === 'cancel_deletions')
 290           {
 291             $.each(requests, function(index, request) {
 292               <?php
 293               // Abort all requests that haven't yet been sent, ie all those where the
 294               // readyState hasn't yet reached 2 (HEADERS_RECEIVED).  For more details see
 295               // https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/XMLHttpRequest/readyState.
 296               // We don't abort those that have already been sent because we can't stop the
 297               // server processing the deletions, and we want to know the result.
 298               ?>
 299               if (request.readyState < 2)
 300               {
 301                 request.abort();
 302                 requestsAborted++;
 303                 if (requestsCompleted + requestsAborted + batches.length >= nBatches)
 304                 {
 305                   reloadReport();
 306                 }
 307               }
 308             });
 309           }
 310           e.preventDefault();
 311           return false;
 312         }
 313       });
 314 
 315       initDeleteButton();
 316     };
 317 
 318     if (args.isAdmin)
 319     {
 320       tableOptions.initComplete = addDeleteButton;
 321     }
 322     <?php
 323   }
 324   ?>
 325 
 326   <?php
 327   // If the sort columns are specified then tell DataTables to sort by those columns on
 328   // initialisation, otherwise it will sort by the default column.  We also need to
 329   // tell DataTables not to use the saved state, otherwise it will confuse the user
 330   // who has just changed the "Sort by" option on the report form.
 331   ?>
 332   var sortColumns = table.data('sortColumns');
 333   if ((sortColumns !== undefined) && (sortColumns.length))
 334   {
 335     tableOptions.order = [];
 336     sortColumns.forEach(function(column) {
 337       tableOptions.order.push([column, 'asc']);
 338     });
 339     tableOptions.stateSave = false;
 340   }
 341 
 342   <?php // If we're an admin then add a "Copy email addresses" button ?>
 343   if (args.isAdmin) {
 344     tableOptions.buttons = [
 345       {
 346         <?php // The first button is assumed to be the colvis button ?>
 347         extend: 'colvis'
 348       },
 349       {
 350         <?php
 351         // Add in an extra button to copy email addresses as a unique, sorted, comma separated
 352         // list so that they can be pasted into an address field in an email client.
 353         // Useful for sending messages to those booked on a certain day or in a certain room.
 354         ?>
 355         text: '<?php echo get_js_vocab('copy_email_addresses') ?>',
 356         action: function (e, dt, node, config) {
 357           extractEmailAddresses(dt, '#col_create_by', true);
 358         }
 359       }
 360     ];
 361   }
 362 
 363   reportTable = makeDataTable('#report_table', tableOptions, {leftColumns: 1});
 364 
 365 });

/language.inc

   1 <?php
   2 declare(strict_types=1);
   3 namespace MRBS;
   4 
   5 // Note that we are using MRBS\Intl\Locale because \Locale has some bugs in it (and also
   6 // isn't always installed).
   7 
   8 use IntlDateFormatter;
   9 use MRBS\Errors\Errors;
  10 use MRBS\Intl\IntlDateFormatterFactory;
  11 use MRBS\Intl\IntlDatePatternGenerator;
  12 use MRBS\Intl\Locale;
  13 use PHPMailer\PHPMailer\PHPMailer;
  14 
  15 require_once "functions.inc";
  16 
  17 
  18 // A map of browser locale aliases
  19 $lang_aliases = array
  20 (
  21   'no' => 'nb',         // Not all operating systems will accept a locale of 'no'
  22   'sh' => 'sr-latn-rs',
  23 );
  24 
  25 // Map non-standard language codes used by flatpickr onto BCP 47 language tags
  26 $flatpickr_lang_map = array(
  27   'at'      => 'de-at',
  28   'cat'     => 'ca',
  29   'ckb'     => 'ku',
  30   'gr'      => 'el',
  31   'kz'      => 'kk',
  32   'sr-cyr'  => 'sr-cyrl',
  33   'uz-latn' => 'uz-latn-uz',
  34   'vn'      => 'vi'
  35 );
  36 
  37 // Map flatpickr language file names onto flatpickr fp.l10ns properties
  38 // so that they can be used with flatpickr.localize.
  39 $flatpickr_property_map = array(
  40   'ar-dz'   => 'arDz',
  41   'sr-cyr'  => 'srCyr',
  42   'zh-tw'   => 'zh_tw'
  43 );
  44 
  45 // A list of languages that use Right to Left text
  46 $rtl_languages = array(
  47   'he'
  48 );
  49 
  50 
  51 // Set the default character encoding
  52 ini_set('default_charset', 'UTF-8');
  53 
  54 // Set up mb_string internal encoding
  55 if (function_exists('mb_internal_encoding'))
  56 {
  57   mb_internal_encoding('UTF-8');
  58 }
  59 
  60 language_debug('$disable_automatic_language_changing: ' . (($disable_automatic_language_changing) ? 'true' : 'false'));
  61 language_debug('$default_language_tokens: ' . ($default_language_tokens ?? 'NULL'));
  62 language_debug('$cli_language: ' . ($cli_language ?? 'NULL'));
  63 language_debug('$override_locale: ' . ($override_locale ?? 'NULL'));
  64 
  65 // Check and adjust if necessary the format of $override_locale which changed in versions
  66 // of MRBS > 1.7.1
  67 if (!empty($override_locale))
  68 {
  69   $new_override_locale = System::getBCPlocale($override_locale);
  70   if (mb_strtolower($override_locale) != mb_strtolower($new_override_locale))
  71   {
  72     $message = 'The config variable $override_locale should now be in BCP 47 format. ' .
  73       "Please change '$override_locale' to '$new_override_locale'.";
  74     trigger_error($message, E_USER_NOTICE);
  75     $override_locale = $new_override_locale;
  76     language_debug('Adjusted $override_locale: ' . $override_locale);
  77   }
  78 }
  79 
  80 // Determine locale and language to use.  MRBS's strategy is first to find the locale
  81 // that best fits the config settings and the user's browser preferences.  Then it
  82 // finds a language that best fits the locale, subject to any overriding config settings.
  83 //
  84 // Locales will also be needed for third party JavaScript libraries such as datepickers.
  85 // MRBS tries to find the best match for these depending on the localisations available
  86 // for the library.   This may sometimes mean that the locale for the library, eg the
  87 // datepicker, is different from the main locale.   But this is probably better than
  88 // trying to find a locale that is available on the server and has a translation available
  89 // in MRBS and has localisations available in all the third party libraries.
  90 
  91 $http_accept_language = $server['HTTP_ACCEPT_LANGUAGE'] ?? '';
  92 language_debug("HTTP_ACCEPT_LANGUAGE: $http_accept_language");
  93 
  94 // Translate languages in the header string to their aliases
  95 if (isset($server['HTTP_ACCEPT_LANGUAGE']))
  96 {
  97   $aliased_header = alias_header($server['HTTP_ACCEPT_LANGUAGE'], $lang_aliases);
  98 }
  99 else
 100 {
 101   $aliased_header = null;
 102 }
 103 language_debug('$aliased_header: ' . $aliased_header);
 104 
 105 // Get the locale that we should be using
 106 $locale = get_mrbs_locale($aliased_header);
 107 
 108 if (isset($locale))
 109 {
 110   language_debug('$locale: ' . $locale);
 111 }
 112 else
 113 {
 114   language_debug('None of the requested locales are available on this server');
 115 }
 116 
 117 // Then set the locale
 118 set_mrbs_locale($locale);
 119 
 120 // Find the best fit for the language that we should be using
 121 $lang = get_mrbs_lang($locale);
 122 
 123 if (isset($lang))
 124 {
 125   language_debug('$lang: ' . $lang);
 126 }
 127 else
 128 {
 129   language_debug('No suitable language file found');
 130 }
 131 
 132 // And then set that vocab
 133 set_vocab($lang);
 134 
 135 
 136 // Determines whether we are using a RTL language
 137 function using_rtl_lang() : bool
 138 {
 139   global $rtl_languages;
 140 
 141   $lang = get_mrbs_lang();
 142   return in_array(mb_strtolower($lang), $rtl_languages);
 143 }
 144 
 145 
 146 // Converts a locale to standard BCP 47 format
 147 function convert_to_BCP47(?string $locale) : ?string
 148 {
 149   if (!isset($locale))
 150   {
 151     return null;
 152   }
 153 
 154   // Parse it and then recompose it.  This will get the capitalisation correct, eg
 155   // "sr-Latn-RS".  Note though that BCP 47 language tags are case-insensitive and
 156   // the capitalisation is just a convention.
 157   $locale = Locale::composeLocale(Locale::parseLocale($locale));
 158   // Replace the underscores with hyphens.  The PHP Locale class will return underscores,
 159   // but the BCP 47 standard uses hyphens.
 160   return str_replace('_', '-', $locale);
 161 }
 162 
 163 
 164 function set_mrbs_locale($locale)
 165 {
 166   if (!isset($locale))
 167   {
 168     return;
 169   }
 170 
 171   $os_locale = System::getOSlocale($locale);
 172 
 173   if (false === setlocale(LC_ALL, $os_locale))
 174   {
 175     // $os_locale will be an array
 176     $message = "Server failed to set locale to " . json_encode($os_locale) .
 177                " for language tag '$locale'.  Either install the missing locale" .
 178                ' or set $override_locale in your MRBS config.inc.php file to a' .
 179                ' locale that is available on your server.';
 180     trigger_error($message, E_USER_NOTICE);
 181 
 182     if (false === setlocale(LC_ALL, array('C.UTF-8', 'C.utf-8', 'C.utf8', 'C')))
 183     {
 184       Errors::fatalError("Could not set locale at all, not even to 'C'");
 185     }
 186   }
 187 }
 188 
 189 
 190 // Work out which locale we want to use
 191 // Note: the first time this function is called, it should be called with a $header string.
 192 // Subsequent calls will just return the static $locale variable which was calculated on
 193 // the first call
 194 function get_mrbs_locale($header=null) : string
 195 {
 196   global $override_locale, $disable_automatic_language_changing, $default_language_tokens;
 197   global $cli_language;
 198 
 199   static $locale = null;
 200   static $have_locale = false;   // $locale could be null, even when we've got it
 201 
 202   if (!$have_locale)
 203   {
 204 
 205     // Use the override locale if we've been given one
 206     if (!empty($override_locale))
 207     {
 208       $locale = $override_locale;
 209     }
 210     // Otherwise, if we're running from the CLI, use the config setting
 211     elseif (!empty($cli_language) && is_cli())
 212     {
 213       $locale = $cli_language;
 214     }
 215     // Otherwise, if we've been told to use a fixed language, then use that
 216     elseif ($disable_automatic_language_changing &&
 217             isset($default_language_tokens) &&
 218             ($default_language_tokens !== ''))
 219     {
 220       $locale = $default_language_tokens;
 221     }
 222     // Otherwise, use the best available language following browser preferences
 223     elseif (!empty($header))
 224     {
 225       $locale = Locale::acceptFromHttp($header);
 226     }
 227 
 228     // If everything fails, use English
 229     if (!isset($locale) || ($locale === false))
 230     {
 231       $locale = 'en';
 232     }
 233 
 234     // Convert it to BCP 47 format (eg convert 'en_US' to 'en-US')
 235     $locale = convert_to_BCP47($locale);
 236     $have_locale = true;
 237   }
 238 
 239   return $locale;
 240 }
 241 
 242 
 243 // Returns a simple array of BCP 47 language tags in decreasing order of preference.  This
 244 // is designed for use with third party libraries (eg datepickers, datatables) where the
 245 // locale used by MRBS, and given by get_mrbs_locale(), may not be available.  So this function
 246 // returns as wide a list of languages as possible, in the hope that one of them may be
 247 // supported by the third party library.
 248 function get_lang_preferences() : array
 249 {
 250   global $cli_language, $disable_automatic_language_changing, $default_language_tokens;
 251   global $override_locale;
 252   global $aliased_header;
 253 
 254   static $lang_preferences = null;
 255 
 256   if (!isset($lang_preferences))
 257   {
 258     // Use the aliased browser preferences, if any, as a base.    Although we may add
 259     // higher priority languages later, these are a useful fall-back on the grounds
 260     // that it's better to have some language rather than none.
 261     $lang_preferences = get_browser_langs($aliased_header, true);
 262 
 263     // If we've been told not to use the browser languages then the default
 264     // language is more important
 265     if ($disable_automatic_language_changing &&
 266         isset($default_language_tokens) &&
 267         ($default_language_tokens) !== '')
 268     {
 269       array_unshift($lang_preferences, $default_language_tokens);
 270     }
 271 
 272     // If there's an override locale then that's more important still
 273     if (!empty($override_locale))
 274     {
 275       array_unshift($lang_preferences, $override_locale);
 276     }
 277 
 278     // If we're running from the CLI then put the CLI language at the top
 279     if (is_cli() && !empty($cli_language))
 280     {
 281       array_unshift($lang_preferences, $cli_language);
 282     }
 283 
 284     // Add the default language tokens as a fallback
 285     if (isset($default_language_tokens) && ($default_language_tokens !== ''))
 286     {
 287       array_push($lang_preferences, $default_language_tokens);
 288     }
 289 
 290     // Finally, add a backstop at the very bottom of the list
 291     array_push($lang_preferences, 'en');
 292   }
 293 
 294   return $lang_preferences;
 295 }
 296 
 297 
 298 // Note: the first time this function is called, it should be called with a $locale.
 299 // Subsequent calls will just return the static $lang variable which was calculated on
 300 // the first call
 301 function get_mrbs_lang(?string $locale=null)
 302 {
 303   global $disable_automatic_language_changing,
 304          $default_language_tokens,
 305          $cli_language;
 306 
 307   static $lang = null;
 308 
 309   if (!isset($lang))
 310   {
 311     // If we're running from the CLI, use the config setting
 312     if (!empty($cli_language) && is_cli())
 313     {
 314       $lang = $cli_language;
 315     }
 316     // Otherwise, if we've been told to use a fixed language, then use that
 317     elseif ($disable_automatic_language_changing &&
 318             isset($default_language_tokens) &&
 319             ($default_language_tokens !== ''))
 320     {
 321       $lang = $default_language_tokens;
 322     }
 323     // Otherwise, use the best available language following browser preferences
 324     elseif (isset($locale))
 325     {
 326       $available_languages = get_langtags(MRBS_ROOT . '/lang', 'lang.');
 327       $lang = Locale::lookup($available_languages, $locale, false, $default_language_tokens);
 328     }
 329   }
 330 
 331   return $lang;
 332 }

 335 // Returns a version of the Accept-Language request HTTP header with language
 336 // strings substituted for their aliases
 337 function alias_header(string $header, array $aliases) : string
 338 {
 339   if (!empty($aliases))
 340   {
 341     $patterns = array();
 342     $replacements = array();
 343 
 344     foreach ($aliases as $key => $value)
 345     {
 346       $patterns[] = "/(?<=^|,)($key)(?=,|;|$)/i";
 347       $replacements[] = $value;
 348     }
 349 
 350     $header = preg_replace($patterns, $replacements, $header);
 351   }
 352 
 353   return $header;
 354 }
 355 
 356 
 357 /**
 358  * Returns a sorted associative array of acceptable language qualifiers, indexed
 359  * by language.
 360  *
 361  * @param string|null $header an Accept-Language header string
 362  * @param bool $translate_wildcard If set then the wildcard language identifier ('*') is
 363  *                                 translated to a standard language - we use 'en'
 364  * @return array<string, float>
 365  */
 366 function get_qualifiers(?string $header, bool $translate_wildcard=false) : array
 367 {
 368   $result = array();
 369 
 370   if (!empty($header))
 371   {
 372     $lang_specifiers = explode(',', $header);
 373 
 374     foreach ($lang_specifiers as $specifier)
 375     {
 376       unset($weight);
 377       $specifier = trim($specifier);
 378 
 379       // The regular expressions below are not tight definitions of permissible language tags.
 380       // They let through some tags which are not permissible, but they do allow permissible
 381       // tags such as 'es-419'.
 382       if (preg_match('/^([a-zA-Z0-9\-]+|\*);q=([0-9.]+)$/', $specifier, $matches))
 383       {
 384         $language = $matches[1];
 385         $weight = (float) $matches[2];
 386       }
 387       else if (preg_match('/^([a-zA-Z0-9\-]+|\*)$/', $specifier, $matches))
 388       {
 389         $language = $matches[1];
 390         $weight = 1.0;
 391       }
 392       else
 393       {
 394         $message = "Unexpected specifier format '$specifier' in the Accept-Language request header sent by the client.";
 395         trigger_error($message, E_USER_NOTICE);
 396       }
 397 
 398       if (isset($weight))
 399       {
 400         if ($translate_wildcard && ($language == '*'))
 401         {
 402           // Handle the wildcard language by using English
 403           $language = 'en';
 404         }
 405         // If a language occurs twice (possibly as a result of a wildcard or aliasing) then
 406         // only change the weight if it's greater than the one we've already got.
 407         if (!isset($result[$language]) || ($weight > $result[$language]))
 408         {
 409           $result[$language] = $weight;
 410         }
 411       }
 412     }
 413   }
 414 
 415   arsort($result, SORT_NUMERIC);
 416 
 417   return $result;
 418 }
 419 
 420 // Returns a string of acceptable languages, sorted in decreasing order of preference
 421 // If $translate_wildcard is set then the wildcard language identifier ('*') is
 422 // translated to a standard language - we use 'en'.
 423 function get_browser_langs(?string $header, bool $translate_wildcard=false) : array
 424 {
 425   return array_keys(get_qualifiers($header, $translate_wildcard));
 426 }
 427 
 428 
 429 // Gets all the language tags in a directory where the filenames are of the format
 430 // $prefix . $lang . $suffix.  Returns an array.
 431 function get_langtags(string $dir, string $prefix='', string $suffix='') : array
 432 {
 433   $result = array();
 434 
 435   if (!is_dir($dir))
 436   {
 437     trigger_error("MRBS: directory '$dir' does not exist", E_USER_NOTICE);
 438     return $result;
 439   }
 440 
 441   $files = scandir($dir);
 442 
 443   foreach ($files as $file)
 444   {
 445     $path = $dir . '/' . $file;
 446     // . and .. will be included in the output of scandir(), so
 447     // we need to exclude them.  We also want to exclude files
 448     // that we can't read.
 449     if (!is_dir($path) && is_readable($path))
 450     {
 451       // Then strip out the language tag from the file name
 452       $pattern = sprintf('/%s(.+)%s/i', $prefix, $suffix);
 453       if (preg_match($pattern, $file, $matches))
 454       {
 455         if (isset($matches[1]))
 456         {
 457           $result[] = $matches[1];
 458         }
 459       }
 460     }
 461   }
 462 
 463   return $result;
 464 }
 465 
 466 
 467 /**
 468  * Get the best fit language file from a directory given the set of language preferences.
 469  *
 470  * The file names are assumed to be of the form `$prefix . $lang . $suffix`, eg 'datepicker-en-GB.js'.
 471  *
 472  * @param string[]|null $default_langtags an array of languages that are already built into the system and do not
 473  * need an explicit regional setting
 474  * @param array<string, string>|null $lang_map an associative array that maps a filename (less prefix and suffix)
 475  * onto a language tag, for example array('English' => 'en').  Useful when the localisation files do not follow a
 476  * language tag naming scheme.
 477  * @return string|null the filename, or NULL if no suitable file is available.
 478  */
 479 function get_best_lang_file(string $dir, string $prefix='', string $suffix='', ?array $default_langtags=null, ?array $lang_map=null) : ?string
 480 {
 481   if (!is_dir($dir))
 482   {
 483     trigger_error("MRBS: directory $dir does not exist", E_USER_NOTICE);
 484     return null;
 485   }
 486 
 487   $lang_preferences = get_lang_preferences();
 488 
 489   // Get the available languages
 490   $available_langtags = get_langtags($dir, $prefix, $suffix);
 491 
 492   // Translate the non-standard names into BCP 47 tags
 493   if (isset($lang_map))
 494   {
 495     foreach($available_langtags as $langtag)
 496     {
 497       if (isset($lang_map[$langtag]))
 498       {
 499         // Replace langtag with its mapping
 500         array_splice($available_langtags,
 501                      array_search($langtag, $available_langtags),
 502                      1,
 503                      $lang_map[$langtag]);
 504       }
 505     }
 506   }
 507 
 508   // Merge in the default languages
 509   if (isset($default_langtags))
 510   {
 511     $available_langtags = array_unique(array_merge($available_langtags, $default_langtags));
 512   }
 513 
 514   // Find the best fit.
 515   foreach ($lang_preferences as $lang)
 516   {
 517     // For some reason the third parameter to Locale::lookup() is mandatory in 5.3.0.
 518     // Can't see anything about it in the manual - must be a bug that was fixed in
 519     // later versions.
 520     $locale = Locale::lookup($available_langtags, $lang, $canonicalize = false);
 521 
 522     if (!empty($locale))
 523     {
 524       if (isset($default_langtags) && in_array($locale, $default_langtags))
 525       {
 526         return null;
 527       }
 528       $filename_body = (isset($lang_map)) ? array_search($locale, $lang_map) : false;
 529       $filename_body = ($filename_body === false) ? $locale : $filename_body;
 530       return $prefix . $filename_body . $suffix;
 531     }
 532   }
 533 
 534   return null;  // We failed to find anything acceptable
 535 }

 608 function load_vocab($lang)
 609 {
 610   global $vocab, $vocab_override;
 611 
 612   if (!isset($lang))
 613   {
 614     return;
 615   }
 616 
 617   $lang = mb_strtolower($lang);
 618   $lang_file = MRBS_ROOT . "/lang/lang.$lang";
 619 
 620   if (!is_readable($lang_file))
 621   {
 622     trigger_error("MRBS: could not set language to '$lang'", E_USER_WARNING);
 623   }
 624   else
 625   {
 626     // Load the language tokens
 627     include "$lang_file";
 628     // And apply any site overrides for this language
 629     if (isset($vocab_override[$lang]))
 630     {
 631       foreach ($vocab_override[$lang] as $tag => $str)
 632       {
 633         $vocab[$tag] = $str;
 634       }
 635     }
 636   }
 637 }

 640 // Set $vocab to $lang.  As some translations are incomplete, 'en' is set as a final
 641 // fallback language, with $default_language_tokens as a fallback before that.
 642 function set_vocab($lang)
 643 {
 644   global $default_language_tokens;
 645 
 646   // Set English as a final fallback language as some of the translations are incomplete.
 647   load_vocab('en');
 648 
 649   // Then set the default language as the fallback before that.
 650   if (isset($default_language_tokens) && ($default_language_tokens !== 'en'))
 651   {
 652     load_vocab($default_language_tokens);
 653   }
 654 
 655   // Finally set the language we want
 656   if (isset($lang) && !in_array($lang, array('en', $default_language_tokens)))
 657   {
 658     load_vocab($lang);
 659   }
 660 }

 709 // Get a vocab item, in UTF-8
 710 // Takes additional parameters as for sprintf()
 711 //
 712 // [Maybe in the future we should switch to using the MessageFormatter
 713 //  class as it is more powerful.   However the Intl extension isn't present
 714 //  in all PHP installations and so the class would have to be emulated]
 715 function get_vocab(string $tag, ...$values) : string
 716 {
 717   global $vocab;
 718 
 719   // Return the tag itself if we can't find a vocab string
 720   if (!isset($vocab[$tag]))
 721   {
 722     return $tag;
 723   }
 724 
 725   return (count($values) === 0) ? $vocab[$tag] : sprintf($vocab[$tag], ...$values);
 726 }

 752 // Same as get_vocab(), but uses the mailing language
 753 function get_mail_vocab(string $tag, ...$values) : string
 754 {
 755   global $vocab;
 756 
 757   static $mail_vocab = null;
 758 
 759   if (!isset($mail_vocab))
 760   {
 761     $web_vocab = $vocab;   // Save $vocab before it gets overwritten
 762     // Get the best language available for mail
 763     set_vocab(get_mail_lang());
 764     $mail_vocab = $vocab;
 765     $vocab = $web_vocab;  // Restore $vocab
 766   }
 767 
 768   // Return the tag itself if we can't find a vocab string
 769   if (!isset($mail_vocab[$tag]))
 770   {
 771     return $tag;
 772   }
 773 
 774   $result = (count($values) === 0) ? $mail_vocab[$tag] : sprintf($mail_vocab[$tag], ...$values);
 775 
 776   return str_replace('&nbsp;', ' ', $result);

 803 function datetime_format(array $format, ?int $timestamp=null, ?string $locale=null) : string
 804 {
 805   global $icu_override, $timezone;
 806 
 807   if (!isset($timestamp))
 808   {
 809     $timestamp = time();
 810   }
 811 
 812   if (!isset($locale))
 813   {
 814     $locale = get_mrbs_locale();
 815   }
 816 
 817   if (isset($format['skeleton']))
 818   {
 819     $pattern_generator = new IntlDatePatternGenerator($locale);
 820     $pattern = $pattern_generator->getBestPattern($format['skeleton']);
 821   }
 822 
 823   if (!isset($pattern) || ($pattern === false) || ($pattern === ''))
 824   {
 825     $pattern = $format['pattern'] ?? null;
 826   }
 827 
 828   $formatter = IntlDateFormatterFactory::create(
 829     $locale,
 830     $format['date_type'] ?? IntlDateFormatter::FULL,
 831     $format['time_type'] ?? IntlDateFormatter::FULL,
 832     null, null, $pattern
 833   );
 834 
 835   // If we're overriding the ICU value(s) then use those, provided that we're able to make use
 836   // of them with the IntlCalendar and (standard, not emulated - hence the check for the loaded
 837   // extension, rather than whether the class exists, which it always will) IntlDateFormatter classes.
 838   if (isset($icu_override[$locale]) && extension_loaded('intl') && class_exists('IntlCalendar'))
 839   {
 840     $cal = \IntlCalendar::createInstance($timezone, $locale);
 841     {
 842       if (isset($icu_override[$locale]['first_day_of_week']))
 843       {
 844         $cal->setFirstDayOfWeek($icu_override[$locale]['first_day_of_week']);
 845       }
 846       if (isset($icu_override[$locale]['minimal_days_in_first_week']))
 847       {
 848         $cal->setMinimalDaysInFirstWeek($icu_override[$locale]['minimal_days_in_first_week']);
 849       }
 850     }
 851     $cal->setTime($timestamp * 1000);
 852     return $formatter->format($cal);
 853   }
 854 
 855   return $formatter->format($timestamp);
 856 }

 859 // Determines whether a locale (default the current locale) uses a 12-hour clock.
 860 // Returns NULL if it can't be determined.
 861 function is_ampm(?string $locale=null) : ?bool
 862 {
 863   global $datetime_formats;
 864 
 865   if (!isset($locale))
 866   {
 867     $locale = get_mrbs_locale();
 868   }
 869 
 870   // Work out what pattern is being used for times.
 871   // If an explicit pattern has been set in the config file then use that.
 872   if (isset($datetime_formats['time']['pattern']))
 873   {
 874     $pattern = $datetime_formats['time']['pattern'];
 875   }
 876   // Otherwise get the pattern that would be used by default.
 877   else
 878   {
 879     $formatter = IntlDateFormatterFactory::create(
 880       $locale,
 881       $format['date_type'] ?? IntlDateFormatter::NONE,
 882       $format['time_type'] ?? IntlDateFormatter::SHORT
 883     );
 884     $pattern = $formatter->getPattern();
 885     if ($pattern === false)
 886     {
 887       trigger_error("Could not determine whether '$locale' uses a 12-hour clock");
 888       return null;
 889     }
 890   }
 891 
 892   // And see if it contains an 'a'
 893   return str_contains($pattern, 'a');
 894 }

  32     /*

  34      *              CIPHERTEXT (varies) || HMAC (32 bytes)

  39     /**

  41      *
  42      * @param string $ctr
  43      * @param int    $inc
  44      *
  45      * @throws Ex\EnvironmentIsBrokenException
  46      *
  47      * @return string
  48      *
  49      * @psalm-suppress RedundantCondition - It's valid to use is_int to check for overflow.
  50      */
  51     public static function incrementCounter($ctr, $inc)
  52     {

  54             Core::ourStrlen($ctr) === Core::BLOCK_BYTE_SIZE,
  55             'Trying to increment a nonce of the wrong size.'
  56         );
  57 
  58         Core::ensureTrue(
  59             \is_int($inc),
  60             'Trying to increment nonce by a non-integer.'
  61         );

  63         // The caller is probably re-using CTR-mode keystream if they increment by 0.
  64         Core::ensureTrue(
  65             $inc > 0,
  66             'Trying to increment a nonce by a nonpositive amount'
  67         );

  69         Core::ensureTrue(
  70             $inc <= PHP_INT_MAX - 255,
  71             'Integer overflow may occur'
  72         );

  74         /*
  75          * We start at the rightmost byte (big-endian)
  76          * So, too, does OpenSSL: http://stackoverflow.com/a/3146214/2224584
  77          */
  78         for ($i = Core::BLOCK_BYTE_SIZE - 1; $i >= 0; --$i) {

  81             /* Detect integer overflow and fail. */

 104             );

 109         } catch (\Exception $ex) {

 111                 'Your system does not have a secure random number generator.'
 112             );

 116     /**
 117      * Computes the HKDF key derivation function specified in
 118      * http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5869.
 119      *
 120      * @param string $hash   Hash Function
 121      * @param string $ikm    Initial Keying Material
 122      * @param int    $length How many bytes?
 123      * @param string $info   What sort of key are we deriving?
 124      * @param string $salt
 125      *
 126      * @throws Ex\EnvironmentIsBrokenException
 127      * @psalm-suppress UndefinedFunction - We're checking if the function exists first.
 128      *
 129      * @return string
 130      */
 131     public static function HKDF($hash, $ikm, $length, $info = '', $salt = null)
 132     {
 133         static $nativeHKDF = null;
 134         if ($nativeHKDF === null) {
 135             $nativeHKDF = \is_callable('\\hash_hkdf');
 136         }
 137         if ($nativeHKDF) {
 138             if (\is_null($salt)) {
 139                 $salt = '';
 140             }
 141             return \hash_hkdf($hash, $ikm, $length, $info, $salt);
 142         }
 143 
 144         $digest_length = Core::ourStrlen(\hash_hmac($hash, '', '', true));
 145 
 146         // Sanity-check the desired output length.
 147         Core::ensureTrue(
 148             !empty($length) && \is_int($length) && $length >= 0 && $length <= 255 * $digest_length,
 149             'Bad output length requested of HDKF.'
 150         );
 151 
 152         // "if [salt] not provided, is set to a string of HashLen zeroes."
 153         if (\is_null($salt)) {
 154             $salt = \str_repeat("\x00", $digest_length);
 155         }
 156 
 157         // HKDF-Extract:
 158         // PRK = HMAC-Hash(salt, IKM)
 159         // The salt is the HMAC key.
 160         $prk = \hash_hmac($hash, $ikm, $salt, true);
 161 
 162         // HKDF-Expand:
 163 
 164         // This check is useless, but it serves as a reminder to the spec.
 165         Core::ensureTrue(Core::ourStrlen($prk) >= $digest_length);
 166 
 167         // T(0) = ''
 168         $t          = '';
 169         $last_block = '';
 170         for ($block_index = 1; Core::ourStrlen($t) < $length; ++$block_index) {
 171             // T(i) = HMAC-Hash(PRK, T(i-1) | info | 0x??)
 172             $last_block = \hash_hmac(
 173                 $hash,
 174                 $last_block . $info . \chr($block_index),
 175                 $prk,
 176                 true
 177             );
 178             // T = T(1) | T(2) | T(3) | ... | T(N)
 179             $t .= $last_block;
 180         }
 181 
 182         // ORM = first L octets of T
 183         /** @var string $orm */
 184         $orm = Core::ourSubstr($t, 0, $length);
 185         Core::ensureTrue(\is_string($orm));

 189     /**
 190      * Checks if two equal-length strings are the same without leaking
 191      * information through side channels.
 192      *
 193      * @param string $expected
 194      * @param string $given
 195      *
 196      * @throws Ex\EnvironmentIsBrokenException
 197      *
 198      * @return bool
 199      */
 200     public static function hashEquals($expected, $given)
 201     {
 202         static $native = null;
 203         if ($native === null) {
 204             $native = \function_exists('hash_equals');
 205         }
 206         if ($native) {
 207             return \hash_equals($expected, $given);
 208         }

 210         // We can't just compare the strings with '==', since it would make
 211         // timing attacks possible. We could use the XOR-OR constant-time
 212         // comparison algorithm, but that may not be a reliable defense in an
 213         // interpreted language. So we use the approach of HMACing both strings
 214         // with a random key and comparing the HMACs.

 216         // We're not attempting to make variable-length string comparison
 217         // secure, as that's very difficult. Make sure the strings are the same
 218         // length.
 219         Core::ensureTrue(Core::ourStrlen($expected) === Core::ourStrlen($given));

 221         $blind           = Core::secureRandom(32);

 330         if ($start > $input_len) {

 371     /**

 376      * Hornby, with improvements from http://www.variations-of-shadow.com/.
 377      *
 378      * @param string $algorithm  The hash algorithm to use. Recommended: SHA256
 379      * @param string $password   The password.
 380      * @param string $salt       A salt that is unique to the password.
 381      * @param int    $count      Iteration count. Higher is better, but slower. Recommended: At least 1000.
 382      * @param int    $key_length The length of the derived key in bytes.
 383      * @param bool   $raw_output If true, the key is returned in raw binary format. Hex encoded otherwise.

 393         $salt,
 394         $count,
 395         $key_length,
 396         $raw_output = false

 398     {
 399         // Type checks:
 400         if (! \is_string($algorithm)) {
 401             throw new \InvalidArgumentException(
 402                 'pbkdf2(): algorithm must be a string'
 403             );
 404         }
 405         if (! \is_string($password)) {
 406             throw new \InvalidArgumentException(
 407                 'pbkdf2(): password must be a string'
 408             );
 409         }
 410         if (! \is_string($salt)) {
 411             throw new \InvalidArgumentException(
 412                 'pbkdf2(): salt must be a string'
 413             );
 414         }

 430         Core::ensureTrue(

 433         );

 435         Core::ensureTrue($count > 0 && $key_length > 0, 'Invalid PBKDF2 parameters.');
 436 
 437         if (\function_exists('hash_pbkdf2')) {
 438             // The output length is in NIBBLES (4-bits) if $raw_output is false!
 439             if (! $raw_output) {

 442             return \hash_pbkdf2($algorithm, $password, $salt, $count, $key_length, $raw_output);
 443         }
 444 
 445         $hash_length = Core::ourStrlen(\hash($algorithm, '', true));
 446         $block_count = \ceil($key_length / $hash_length);

 448         $output = '';
 449         for ($i = 1; $i <= $block_count; $i++) {
 450             // $i encoded as 4 bytes, big endian.
 451             $last = $salt . \pack('N', $i);

 453             $last = $xorsum = \hash_hmac($algorithm, $last, $password, true);

 461             $output .= $xorsum;
 462         }
 463 
 464         if ($raw_output) {
 465             return (string) Core::ourSubstr($output, 0, $key_length);
 466         } else {
 467             return Encoding::binToHex((string) Core::ourSubstr($output, 0, $key_length));
 468         }

 273         RuntimeTests::runtimeTest();

 276         $keys = $secret->deriveKeys($salt);

 278         $akey = $keys->getAuthenticationKey();

 291     /**
 292      * Decrypts a ciphertext to a string with either a key or a password.
 293      *
 294      * @param string        $ciphertext
 295      * @param KeyOrPassword $secret
 296      * @param bool          $raw_binary
 297      *
 298      * @throws Ex\EnvironmentIsBrokenException
 299      * @throws Ex\WrongKeyOrModifiedCiphertextException
 300      *
 301      * @return string
 302      */
 303     private static function decryptInternal($ciphertext, KeyOrPassword $secret, $raw_binary)

 305         RuntimeTests::runtimeTest();
 306 
 307         if (! $raw_binary) {
 308             try {
 309                 $ciphertext = Encoding::hexToBin($ciphertext);
 310             } catch (Ex\BadFormatException $ex) {
 311                 throw new Ex\WrongKeyOrModifiedCiphertextException(

 313                 );

 318             throw new Ex\WrongKeyOrModifiedCiphertextException(
 319                 'Ciphertext is too short.'
 320             );
 321         }

 323         // Get and check the version header.
 324         /** @var string $header */
 325         $header = Core::ourSubstr($ciphertext, 0, Core::HEADER_VERSION_SIZE);
 326         if ($header !== Core::CURRENT_VERSION) {

 328                 'Bad version header.'
 329             );
 330         }

 333         /** @var string $salt */

 335             $ciphertext,
 336             Core::HEADER_VERSION_SIZE,
 337             Core::SALT_BYTE_SIZE

 341         // Get the IV.
 342         /** @var string $iv */
 343         $iv = Core::ourSubstr(
 344             $ciphertext,
 345             Core::HEADER_VERSION_SIZE + Core::SALT_BYTE_SIZE,
 346             Core::BLOCK_BYTE_SIZE
 347         );

 349 
 350         // Get the HMAC.
 351         /** @var string $hmac */
 352         $hmac = Core::ourSubstr(
 353             $ciphertext,
 354             Core::ourStrlen($ciphertext) - Core::MAC_BYTE_SIZE,
 355             Core::MAC_BYTE_SIZE
 356         );

 358 
 359         // Get the actual encrypted ciphertext.
 360         /** @var string $encrypted */
 361         $encrypted = Core::ourSubstr(
 362             $ciphertext,
 363             Core::HEADER_VERSION_SIZE + Core::SALT_BYTE_SIZE +
 364                 Core::BLOCK_BYTE_SIZE,
 365             Core::ourStrlen($ciphertext) - Core::MAC_BYTE_SIZE - Core::SALT_BYTE_SIZE -

 385      * Raw unauthenticated encryption (insecure on its own).

 389      * @param string $iv
 390      *
 391      * @throws Ex\EnvironmentIsBrokenException
 392      *
 393      * @return string
 394      */
 395     protected static function plainEncrypt(
 396         $plaintext,
 397         #[\SensitiveParameter]
 398         $key,
 399         #[\SensitiveParameter]
 400         $iv
 401     )
 402     {
 403         Core::ensureConstantExists('OPENSSL_RAW_DATA');
 404         Core::ensureFunctionExists('openssl_encrypt');
 405         /** @var string $ciphertext */
 406         $ciphertext = \openssl_encrypt(
 407             $plaintext,
 408             Core::CIPHER_METHOD,
 409             $key,
 410             OPENSSL_RAW_DATA,
 411             $iv
 412         );
 413 
 414         Core::ensureTrue(\is_string($ciphertext), 'openssl_encrypt() failed');

 416         return $ciphertext;

 423      * @param string $key
 424      * @param string $iv
 425      * @param string $cipherMethod
 426      *
 427      * @throws Ex\EnvironmentIsBrokenException
 428      *
 429      * @return string
 430      */
 431     protected static function plainDecrypt(
 432         $ciphertext,
 433         #[\SensitiveParameter]
 434         $key,
 435         #[\SensitiveParameter]
 436         $iv,
 437         $cipherMethod
 438     )
 439     {
 440         Core::ensureConstantExists('OPENSSL_RAW_DATA');
 441         Core::ensureFunctionExists('openssl_decrypt');
 442 
 443         /** @var string $plaintext */
 444         $plaintext = \openssl_decrypt(
 445             $ciphertext,
 446             $cipherMethod,
 447             $key,
 448             OPENSSL_RAW_DATA,
 449             $iv
 450         );
 451         Core::ensureTrue(\is_string($plaintext), 'openssl_decrypt() failed.');
 452 
 453         return $plaintext;
 454     }

 456     /**
 457      * Verifies an HMAC without leaking information through side-channels.
 458      *
 459      * @param string $expected_hmac
 460      * @param string $message
 461      * @param string $key
 462      *
 463      * @throws Ex\EnvironmentIsBrokenException
 464      *
 465      * @return bool
 466      */
 467     protected static function verifyHMAC(
 468         $expected_hmac,
 469         $message,
 470         #[\SensitiveParameter]
 471         $key
 472     )
 473     {
 474         $message_hmac = \hash_hmac(Core::HASH_FUNCTION_NAME, $message, $key, true);
 475         return Core::hashEquals($message_hmac, $expected_hmac);
 476     }

  86      * number of trailing whitespace characters through side-channels.
  87      *
  88      * @param string $string
  89      * @return string
  90      */
  91     public static function trimTrailingWhitespace($string = '')
  92     {
  93         $length = Core::ourStrlen($string);
  94         if ($length < 1) {
  95             return '';
  96         }
  97         do {
  98             $prevLength = $length;
  99             $last = $length - 1;
 100             $chr = \ord($string[$last]);
 101 
 102             /* Null Byte (0x00), a.k.a. \0 */
 103             // if ($chr === 0x00) $length -= 1;
 104             $sub = (($chr - 1) >> 8 ) & 1;
 105             $length -= $sub;
 106             $last -= $sub;
 107 
 108             /* Horizontal Tab (0x09) a.k.a. \t */
 109             $chr = \ord($string[$last]);
 110             // if ($chr === 0x09) $length -= 1;
 111             $sub = (((0x08 - $chr) & ($chr - 0x0a)) >> 8) & 1;
 112             $length -= $sub;
 113             $last -= $sub;
 114 
 115             /* New Line (0x0a), a.k.a. \n */
 116             $chr = \ord($string[$last]);
 117             // if ($chr === 0x0a) $length -= 1;
 118             $sub = (((0x09 - $chr) & ($chr - 0x0b)) >> 8) & 1;
 119             $length -= $sub;
 120             $last -= $sub;
 121 
 122             /* Carriage Return (0x0D), a.k.a. \r */
 123             $chr = \ord($string[$last]);
 124             // if ($chr === 0x0d) $length -= 1;
 125             $sub = (((0x0c - $chr) & ($chr - 0x0e)) >> 8) & 1;
 126             $length -= $sub;
 127             $last -= $sub;
 128 
 129             /* Space */
 130             $chr = \ord($string[$last]);
 131             // if ($chr === 0x20) $length -= 1;
 132             $sub = (((0x1f - $chr) & ($chr - 0x21)) >> 8) & 1;
 133             $length -= $sub;
 134         } while ($prevLength !== $length && $length > 0);
 135         return (string) Core::ourSubstr($string, 0, $length);
 136     }
 137 
 138     /*
 139      * SECURITY NOTE ON APPLYING CHECKSUMS TO SECRETS:
 140      *
 141      *      The checksum introduces a potential security weakness. For example,
 142      *      suppose we apply a checksum to a key, and that an adversary has an
 143      *      exploit against the process containing the key, such that they can
 144      *      overwrite an arbitrary byte of memory and then cause the checksum to
 145      *      be verified and learn the result.
 146      *
 147      *      In this scenario, the adversary can extract the key one byte at
 148      *      a time by overwriting it with their guess of its value and then
 149      *      asking if the checksum matches. If it does, their guess was right.
 150      *      This kind of attack may be more easy to implement and more reliable
 151      *      than a remote code execution attack.
 152      *
 153      *      This attack also applies to authenticated encryption as a whole, in
 154      *      the situation where the adversary can overwrite a byte of the key
 155      *      and then cause a valid ciphertext to be decrypted, and then
 156      *      determine whether the MAC check passed or failed.
 157      *
 158      *      By using the full SHA256 hash instead of truncating it, I'm ensuring
 159      *      that both ways of going about the attack are equivalently difficult.
 160      *      A shorter checksum of say 32 bits might be more useful to the
 161      *      adversary as an oracle in case their writes are coarser grained.
 162      *
 163      *      Because the scenario assumes a serious vulnerability, we don't try
 164      *      to prevent attacks of this style.
 165      */
 166 
 167     /**
 168      * INTERNAL USE ONLY: Applies a version header, applies a checksum, and
 169      * then encodes a byte string into a range of printable ASCII characters.
 170      *
 171      * @param string $header
 172      * @param string $bytes
 173      *
 174      * @throws Ex\EnvironmentIsBrokenException
 175      *
 176      * @return string
 177      */
 178     public static function saveBytesToChecksummedAsciiSafeString(
 179         $header,
 180         #[\SensitiveParameter]
 181         $bytes
 182     )
 183     {
 184         // Headers must be a constant length to prevent one type's header from
 185         // being a prefix of another type's header, leading to ambiguity.
 186         Core::ensureTrue(
 187             Core::ourStrlen($header) === self::SERIALIZE_HEADER_BYTES,
 188             'Header must be ' . self::SERIALIZE_HEADER_BYTES . ' bytes.'
 189         );
 190 
 191         return Encoding::binToHex(
 192             $header .
 193             $bytes .
 194             \hash(
 195                 self::CHECKSUM_HASH_ALGO,
 196                 $header . $bytes,
 197                 true
 198             )
 199         );
 200     }
 201 
 202     /**
 203      * INTERNAL USE ONLY: Decodes, verifies the header and checksum, and returns
 204      * the encoded byte string.
 205      *
 206      * @param string $expected_header
 207      * @param string $string
 208      *
 209      * @throws Ex\EnvironmentIsBrokenException
 210      * @throws Ex\BadFormatException
 211      *
 212      * @return string
 213      */
 214     public static function loadBytesFromChecksummedAsciiSafeString(
 215         $expected_header,
 216         #[\SensitiveParameter]
 217         $string
 218     )
 219     {
 220         // Headers must be a constant length to prevent one type's header from
 221         // being a prefix of another type's header, leading to ambiguity.
 222         Core::ensureTrue(
 223             Core::ourStrlen($expected_header) === self::SERIALIZE_HEADER_BYTES,
 224             'Header must be 4 bytes.'
 225         );
 226 
 227         /* If you get an exception here when attempting to load from a file, first pass your
 228            key to Encoding::trimTrailingWhitespace() to remove newline characters, etc.      */
 229         $bytes = Encoding::hexToBin($string);
 230 
 231         /* Make sure we have enough bytes to get the version header and checksum. */
 232         if (Core::ourStrlen($bytes) < self::SERIALIZE_HEADER_BYTES + self::CHECKSUM_BYTE_SIZE) {
 233             throw new Ex\BadFormatException(
 234                 'Encoded data is shorter than expected.'
 235             );
 236         }
 237 
 238         /* Grab the version header. */
 239         $actual_header = (string) Core::ourSubstr($bytes, 0, self::SERIALIZE_HEADER_BYTES);
 240 
 241         if ($actual_header !== $expected_header) {
 242             throw new Ex\BadFormatException(
 243                 'Invalid header.'
 244             );
 245         }
 246 
 247         /* Grab the bytes that are part of the checksum. */
 248         $checked_bytes = (string) Core::ourSubstr(
 249             $bytes,
 250             0,
 251             Core::ourStrlen($bytes) - self::CHECKSUM_BYTE_SIZE
 252         );
 253 
 254         /* Grab the included checksum. */
 255         $checksum_a = (string) Core::ourSubstr(
 256             $bytes,
 257             Core::ourStrlen($bytes) - self::CHECKSUM_BYTE_SIZE,
 258             self::CHECKSUM_BYTE_SIZE
 259         );
 260 
 261         /* Re-compute the checksum. */
 262         $checksum_b = \hash(self::CHECKSUM_HASH_ALGO, $checked_bytes, true);
 263 
 264         /* Check if the checksum matches. */
 265         if (! Core::hashEquals($checksum_a, $checksum_b)) {
 266             throw new Ex\BadFormatException(
 267                 "Data is corrupted, the checksum doesn't match"
 268             );
 269         }
 270 
 271         return (string) Core::ourSubstr(
 272             $bytes,
 273             self::SERIALIZE_HEADER_BYTES,
 274             Core::ourStrlen($bytes) - self::SERIALIZE_HEADER_BYTES - self::CHECKSUM_BYTE_SIZE
 275         );
 276     }
 277 }

   1 <?php

   3 namespace Defuse\Crypto;
   4 
   5 use Defuse\Crypto\Exception as Ex;
   6 
   7 final class Key
   8 {
   9     const KEY_CURRENT_VERSION = "\xDE\xF0\x00\x00";
  10     const KEY_BYTE_SIZE       = 32;
  11 
  12     /**
  13      * @var string
  14      */
  15     private $key_bytes;
  16 
  17     /**
  18      * Creates new random key.
  19      *
  20      * @throws Ex\EnvironmentIsBrokenException
  21      *
  22      * @return Key
  23      */
  24     public static function createNewRandomKey()
  25     {
  26         return new Key(Core::secureRandom(self::KEY_BYTE_SIZE));
  27     }
  28 
  29     /**
  30      * Loads a Key from its encoded form.
  31      *
  32      * By default, this function will call Encoding::trimTrailingWhitespace()
  33      * to remove trailing CR, LF, NUL, TAB, and SPACE characters, which are
  34      * commonly appended to files when working with text editors.
  35      *
  36      * @param string $saved_key_string
  37      * @param bool $do_not_trim (default: false)
  38      *
  39      * @throws Ex\BadFormatException
  40      * @throws Ex\EnvironmentIsBrokenException
  41      *
  42      * @return Key
  43      */
  44     public static function loadFromAsciiSafeString(
  45         #[\SensitiveParameter]
  46         $saved_key_string,
  47         $do_not_trim = false
  48     )
  49     {
  50         if (!$do_not_trim) {
  51             $saved_key_string = Encoding::trimTrailingWhitespace($saved_key_string);
  52         }
  53         $key_bytes = Encoding::loadBytesFromChecksummedAsciiSafeString(self::KEY_CURRENT_VERSION, $saved_key_string);
  54         return new Key($key_bytes);
  55     }
  56 
  57     /**
  58      * Encodes the Key into a string of printable ASCII characters.
  59      *
  60      * @throws Ex\EnvironmentIsBrokenException
  61      *
  62      * @return string
  63      */
  64     public function saveToAsciiSafeString()
  65     {
  66         return Encoding::saveBytesToChecksummedAsciiSafeString(
  67             self::KEY_CURRENT_VERSION,
  68             $this->key_bytes
  69         );
  70     }
  71 
  72     /**
  73      * Gets the raw bytes of the key.
  74      *
  75      * @return string
  76      */
  77     public function getRawBytes()
  78     {
  79         return $this->key_bytes;
  80     }
  81 
  82     /**
  83      * Constructs a new Key object from a string of raw bytes.
  84      *
  85      * @param string $bytes
  86      *
  87      * @throws Ex\EnvironmentIsBrokenException
  88      */
  89     private function __construct(
  90         #[\SensitiveParameter]
  91         $bytes
  92     )
  93     {
  94         Core::ensureTrue(
  95             Core::ourStrlen($bytes) === self::KEY_BYTE_SIZE,
  96             'Bad key length.'
  97         );
  98         $this->key_bytes = $bytes;
  99     }
 100 
 101 }
