   1 <?php
   2 
   3 namespace Defuse\Crypto;
   4 
   5 use Defuse\Crypto\Exception as Ex;
   6 
   7 final class KeyOrPassword
   8 {
   9     const PBKDF2_ITERATIONS    = 100000;
  10     const SECRET_TYPE_KEY      = 1;
  11     const SECRET_TYPE_PASSWORD = 2;
  12 
  13     /**
  14      * @var int
  15      */
  16     private $secret_type = 0;
  17 
  18     /**
  19      * @var Key|string
  20      */
  21     private $secret;
  22 
  23     /**
  24      * Initializes an instance of KeyOrPassword from a key.
  25      *
  26      * @param Key $key
  27      *
  28      * @return KeyOrPassword
  29      */
  30     public static function createFromKey(Key $key)
  31     {
  32         return new KeyOrPassword(self::SECRET_TYPE_KEY, $key);
  33     }
  34 
  35     /**
  36      * Initializes an instance of KeyOrPassword from a password.
  37      *
  38      * @param string $password
  39      *
  40      * @return KeyOrPassword
  41      */
  42     public static function createFromPassword(
  43         #[\SensitiveParameter]
  44         $password
  45     )
  46     {
  47         return new KeyOrPassword(self::SECRET_TYPE_PASSWORD, $password);
  48     }
  49 
  50     /**
  51      * Derives authentication and encryption keys from the secret, using a slow
  52      * key derivation function if the secret is a password.
  53      *
  54      * @param string $salt
  55      *
  56      * @throws Ex\CryptoException
  57      * @throws Ex\EnvironmentIsBrokenException
  58      *
  59      * @return DerivedKeys
  60      */
  61     public function deriveKeys($salt)
  62     {
  63         Core::ensureTrue(
  64             Core::ourStrlen($salt) === Core::SALT_BYTE_SIZE,
  65             'Bad salt.'
  66         );
  67 
  68         if ($this->secret_type === self::SECRET_TYPE_KEY) {
  69             Core::ensureTrue($this->secret instanceof Key);
  70             /**
  71              * @psalm-suppress PossiblyInvalidMethodCall
  72              */
  73             $akey = Core::HKDF(
  74                 Core::HASH_FUNCTION_NAME,
  75                 $this->secret->getRawBytes(),
  76                 Core::KEY_BYTE_SIZE,
  77                 Core::AUTHENTICATION_INFO_STRING,
  78                 $salt
  79             );
  80             /**
  81              * @psalm-suppress PossiblyInvalidMethodCall
  82              */
  83             $ekey = Core::HKDF(
  84                 Core::HASH_FUNCTION_NAME,
  85                 $this->secret->getRawBytes(),
  86                 Core::KEY_BYTE_SIZE,
  87                 Core::ENCRYPTION_INFO_STRING,
  88                 $salt
  89             );
  90             return new DerivedKeys($akey, $ekey);
  91         } elseif ($this->secret_type === self::SECRET_TYPE_PASSWORD) {
  92             Core::ensureTrue(\is_string($this->secret));
  93             /* Our PBKDF2 polyfill is vulnerable to a DoS attack documented in
  94              * GitHub issue #230. The fix is to pre-hash the password to ensure
  95              * it is short. We do the prehashing here instead of in pbkdf2() so
  96              * that pbkdf2() still computes the function as defined by the
  97              * standard. */
  98 
  99             /**
 100              * @psalm-suppress PossiblyInvalidArgument
 101              */
 102             $prehash = \hash(Core::HASH_FUNCTION_NAME, $this->secret, true);
 103 
 104             $prekey = Core::pbkdf2(
 105                 Core::HASH_FUNCTION_NAME,
 106                 $prehash,
 107                 $salt,
 108                 self::PBKDF2_ITERATIONS,
 109                 Core::KEY_BYTE_SIZE,
 110                 true
 111             );
 112             $akey = Core::HKDF(
 113                 Core::HASH_FUNCTION_NAME,
 114                 $prekey,
 115                 Core::KEY_BYTE_SIZE,
 116                 Core::AUTHENTICATION_INFO_STRING,
 117                 $salt
 118             );
 119             /* Note the cryptographic re-use of $salt here. */
 120             $ekey = Core::HKDF(
 121                 Core::HASH_FUNCTION_NAME,
 122                 $prekey,
 123                 Core::KEY_BYTE_SIZE,
 124                 Core::ENCRYPTION_INFO_STRING,
 125                 $salt
 126             );
 127             return new DerivedKeys($akey, $ekey);
 128         } else {
 129             throw new Ex\EnvironmentIsBrokenException('Bad secret type.');
 130         }
 131     }
 132 
 133     /**
 134      * Constructor for KeyOrPassword.
 135      *
 136      * @param int   $secret_type
 137      * @param mixed $secret      (either a Key or a password string)
 138      */
 139     private function __construct(
 140         $secret_type,
 141         #[\SensitiveParameter]
 142         $secret
 143     )
 144     {
 145         // The constructor is private, so these should never throw.
 146         if ($secret_type === self::SECRET_TYPE_KEY) {
 147             Core::ensureTrue($secret instanceof Key);
 148         } elseif ($secret_type === self::SECRET_TYPE_PASSWORD) {
 149             Core::ensureTrue(\is_string($secret));
 150         } else {
 151             throw new Ex\EnvironmentIsBrokenException('Bad secret type.');
 152         }
 153         $this->secret_type = $secret_type;
 154         $this->secret = $secret;
 155     }
 156 }

/lib/Defuse/Crypto/RuntimeTests.php

   1 <?php
   2 
   3 namespace Defuse\Crypto;
   4 
   5 use Defuse\Crypto\Exception as Ex;
   6 
   7 /*
   8  * We're using static class inheritance to get access to protected methods
   9  * inside Crypto. To make it easy to know where the method we're calling can be
  10  * found, within this file, prefix calls with `Crypto::` or `RuntimeTests::`,
  11  * and don't use `self::`.
  12  */
  13 
  14 class RuntimeTests extends Crypto
  15 {
  16     /**
  17      * Runs the runtime tests.
  18      *
  19      * @throws Ex\EnvironmentIsBrokenException
  20      * @return void
  21      */
  22     public static function runtimeTest()
  23     {
  24         // 0: Tests haven't been run yet.
  25         // 1: Tests have passed.
  26         // 2: Tests are running right now.
  27         // 3: Tests have failed.
  28         static $test_state = 0;
  29 
  30         if ($test_state === 1 || $test_state === 2) {
  31             return;
  32         }
  33 
  34         if ($test_state === 3) {
  35             /* If an intermittent problem caused a test to fail previously, we
  36              * want that to be indicated to the user with every call to this
  37              * library. This way, if the user first does something they really
  38              * don't care about, and just ignores all exceptions, they won't get
  39              * screwed when they then start to use the library for something
  40              * they do care about. */
  41             throw new Ex\EnvironmentIsBrokenException('Tests failed previously.');
  42         }
  43 
  44         try {
  45             $test_state = 2;
  46 
  47             Core::ensureFunctionExists('openssl_get_cipher_methods');
  48             if (\in_array(Core::CIPHER_METHOD, \openssl_get_cipher_methods()) === false) {
  49                 throw new Ex\EnvironmentIsBrokenException(
  50                     'Cipher method not supported. This is normally caused by an outdated ' .
  51                     'version of OpenSSL (and/or OpenSSL compiled for FIPS compliance). ' .
  52                     'Please upgrade to a newer version of OpenSSL that supports ' .
  53                     Core::CIPHER_METHOD . ' to use this library.'
  54                 );
  55             }
  56 
  57             RuntimeTests::AESTestVector();
  58             RuntimeTests::HMACTestVector();
  59             RuntimeTests::HKDFTestVector();
  60 
  61             RuntimeTests::testEncryptDecrypt();
  62             Core::ensureTrue(Core::ourStrlen(Key::createNewRandomKey()->getRawBytes()) === Core::KEY_BYTE_SIZE);
  63 
  64             Core::ensureTrue(Core::ENCRYPTION_INFO_STRING !== Core::AUTHENTICATION_INFO_STRING);
  65         } catch (Ex\EnvironmentIsBrokenException $ex) {
  66             // Do this, otherwise it will stay in the "tests are running" state.
  67             $test_state = 3;
  68             throw $ex;
  69         }
  70 
  71         // Change this to '0' make the tests always re-run (for benchmarking).
  72         $test_state = 1;
  73     }
  74 
  75     /**
  76      * High-level tests of Crypto operations.
  77      *
  78      * @throws Ex\EnvironmentIsBrokenException
  79      * @return void
  80      */
  81     private static function testEncryptDecrypt()
  82     {
  83         $key  = Key::createNewRandomKey();
  84         $data = "EnCrYpT EvErYThInG\x00\x00";
  85 
  86         // Make sure encrypting then decrypting doesn't change the message.
  87         $ciphertext = Crypto::encrypt($data, $key, true);
  88         try {
  89             $decrypted = Crypto::decrypt($ciphertext, $key, true);
  90         } catch (Ex\WrongKeyOrModifiedCiphertextException $ex) {
  91             // It's important to catch this and change it into a
  92             // Ex\EnvironmentIsBrokenException, otherwise a test failure could trick
  93             // the user into thinking it's just an invalid ciphertext!
  94             throw new Ex\EnvironmentIsBrokenException();
  95         }
  96         Core::ensureTrue($decrypted === $data);
  97 
  98         // Modifying the ciphertext: Appending a string.
  99         try {
 100             Crypto::decrypt($ciphertext . 'a', $key, true);
 101             throw new Ex\EnvironmentIsBrokenException();
 102         } catch (Ex\WrongKeyOrModifiedCiphertextException $e) { /* expected */
 103         }
 104 
 105         // Modifying the ciphertext: Changing an HMAC byte.
 106         $indices_to_change = [
 107             0, // The header.
 108             Core::HEADER_VERSION_SIZE + 1, // the salt
 109             Core::HEADER_VERSION_SIZE + Core::SALT_BYTE_SIZE + 1, // the IV
 110             Core::HEADER_VERSION_SIZE + Core::SALT_BYTE_SIZE + Core::BLOCK_BYTE_SIZE + 1, // the ciphertext
 111         ];
 112 
 113         foreach ($indices_to_change as $index) {
 114             try {
 115                 $ciphertext[$index] = \chr((\ord($ciphertext[$index]) + 1) % 256);
 116                 Crypto::decrypt($ciphertext, $key, true);
 117                 throw new Ex\EnvironmentIsBrokenException();
 118             } catch (Ex\WrongKeyOrModifiedCiphertextException $e) { /* expected */
 119             }
 120         }
 121 
 122         // Decrypting with the wrong key.
 123         $key        = Key::createNewRandomKey();
 124         $data       = 'abcdef';
 125         $ciphertext = Crypto::encrypt($data, $key, true);
 126         $wrong_key  = Key::createNewRandomKey();
 127         try {
 128             Crypto::decrypt($ciphertext, $wrong_key, true);
 129             throw new Ex\EnvironmentIsBrokenException();
 130         } catch (Ex\WrongKeyOrModifiedCiphertextException $e) { /* expected */
 131         }
 132 
 133         // Ciphertext too small.
 134         $key        = Key::createNewRandomKey();
 135         $ciphertext = \str_repeat('A', Core::MINIMUM_CIPHERTEXT_SIZE - 1);
 136         try {
 137             Crypto::decrypt($ciphertext, $key, true);
 138             throw new Ex\EnvironmentIsBrokenException();
 139         } catch (Ex\WrongKeyOrModifiedCiphertextException $e) { /* expected */
 140         }
 141     }
 142 
 143     /**
 144      * Test HKDF against test vectors.
 145      *
 146      * @throws Ex\EnvironmentIsBrokenException
 147      * @return void
 148      */
 149     private static function HKDFTestVector()
 150     {
 151         // HKDF test vectors from RFC 5869
 152 
 153         // Test Case 1
 154         $ikm    = \str_repeat("\x0b", 22);
 155         $salt   = Encoding::hexToBin('000102030405060708090a0b0c');
 156         $info   = Encoding::hexToBin('f0f1f2f3f4f5f6f7f8f9');
 157         $length = 42;
 158         $okm    = Encoding::hexToBin(
 159             '3cb25f25faacd57a90434f64d0362f2a' .
 160             '2d2d0a90cf1a5a4c5db02d56ecc4c5bf' .
 161             '34007208d5b887185865'
 162         );
 163         $computed_okm = Core::HKDF('sha256', $ikm, $length, $info, $salt);
 164         Core::ensureTrue($computed_okm === $okm);
 165 
 166         // Test Case 7
 167         $ikm    = \str_repeat("\x0c", 22);
 168         $length = 42;
 169         $okm    = Encoding::hexToBin(
 170             '2c91117204d745f3500d636a62f64f0a' .
 171             'b3bae548aa53d423b0d1f27ebba6f5e5' .
 172             '673a081d70cce7acfc48'
 173         );
 174         $computed_okm = Core::HKDF('sha1', $ikm, $length, '', null);
 175         Core::ensureTrue($computed_okm === $okm);
 176     }
 177 
 178     /**
 179      * Test HMAC against test vectors.
 180      *
 181      * @throws Ex\EnvironmentIsBrokenException
 182      * @return void
 183      */
 184     private static function HMACTestVector()

 188         $data    = 'Hi There';
 189         $correct = 'b0344c61d8db38535ca8afceaf0bf12b881dc200c9833da726e9376c2e32cff7';

 191             \hash_hmac(Core::HASH_FUNCTION_NAME, $data, $key) === $correct

 195     /**
 196      * Test AES against test vectors.
 197      *
 198      * @throws Ex\EnvironmentIsBrokenException
 199      * @return void
 200      */
 201     private static function AESTestVector()
 202     {
 203         // AES CTR mode test vector from NIST SP 800-38A
 204         $key = Encoding::hexToBin(
 205             '603deb1015ca71be2b73aef0857d7781' .
 206             '1f352c073b6108d72d9810a30914dff4'
 207         );
 208         $iv        = Encoding::hexToBin('f0f1f2f3f4f5f6f7f8f9fafbfcfdfeff');
 209         $plaintext = Encoding::hexToBin(
 210             '6bc1bee22e409f96e93d7e117393172a' .
 211             'ae2d8a571e03ac9c9eb76fac45af8e51' .
 212             '30c81c46a35ce411e5fbc1191a0a52ef' .
 213             'f69f2445df4f9b17ad2b417be66c3710'
 214         );
 215         $ciphertext = Encoding::hexToBin(
 216             '601ec313775789a5b7a7f504bbf3d228' .
 217             'f443e3ca4d62b59aca84e990cacaf5c5' .
 218             '2b0930daa23de94ce87017ba2d84988d' .
 219             'dfc9c58db67aada613c2dd08457941a6'
 220         );
 221 
 222         $computed_ciphertext = Crypto::plainEncrypt($plaintext, $key, $iv);
 223         Core::ensureTrue($computed_ciphertext === $ciphertext);
 224 
 225         $computed_plaintext = Crypto::plainDecrypt($ciphertext, $key, $iv, Core::CIPHER_METHOD);
 226         Core::ensureTrue($computed_plaintext === $plaintext);
 227     }
 228 }

   2 declare(strict_types=1);

   4 
   5 use MRBS\User;

   7 use function MRBS\get_registrants;

  10 use function MRBS\in_arrayi;
  11 use function MRBS\session;
  12 use function MRBS\strcasecmp_locale;
  13 
  14 
  15 abstract class Auth
  16 {
  17   protected $getDisplayNamesAtOnce = true;
  18 
  19   /**
  20    * Checks if the specified username/password pair are valid.
  21    *
  22    * @return false|string the validated username or false
  23    */
  24   abstract public function validateUser(
  25     #[\SensitiveParameter]
  26     ?string $user,
  27     #[\SensitiveParameter]
  28     ?string $pass);
  29 
  30 
  31   protected function getUserFresh(string $username) : ?User
  32   {
  33     $user = new User($username);
  34     $user->display_name = $username;
  35     $user->level = $this->getDefaultLevel($username);
  36     $user->email = $this->getDefaultEmail($username);
  37 
  38     return $user;
  39   }
  40 
  41 
  42   public function getUser(string $username) : ?User
  43   {
  44     // Cache results for performance as getting user details in
  45     // most authentication types is expensive.
  46     static $users = array();
  47 
  48     // Use array_key_exists() rather than isset() in case the value is NULL
  49     if (!array_key_exists($username, $users))
  50     {
  51       // Check to see if this is the current user.  If it is, then we
  52       // can save ourselves a potentially expensive operation.
  53       // But we can only do this if we are not being called by getCurrentUser(), which
  54       // some session schemes do, as otherwise we'll end up with an infinite recursion.
  55       // TODO: is there a better way of handling this??
  56       $backtrace = debug_backtrace(DEBUG_BACKTRACE_IGNORE_ARGS);
  57       $backtrace_functions = array_column($backtrace, 'function');
  58       if (!in_array('getCurrentUser', $backtrace_functions))
  59       {
  60         $mrbs_user = session()->getCurrentUser();
  61       }
  62 
  63       if (isset($mrbs_user) && ($mrbs_user->username === $username))
  64       {
  65         $user = $mrbs_user;
  66       }
  67       else
  68       {
  69         $user = $this->getUserFresh($username);
  70         // Make sure we've got a sensible display name
  71         if (isset($user) &&
  72             (!isset($user->display_name) || ($user->display_name === '')))
  73         {
  74           $user->display_name = $user->username;
  75         }
  76       }
  77       $users[$username] = $user;
  78     }
  79 
  80     return $users[$username];
  81   }
  82 
  83 
  84   /**
  85    * Returns a username given an email address.
  86    *
  87    * Note that if two or more users share the same email address then the first
  88    * one found will be returned.  If no user is found then NULL is returned.
  89    */
  90   public function getUsernameByEmail(string $email) : ?string
  91   {
  92     global $mail_settings;
  93 
  94     // Default: return the email address, unless we're constructing email
  95     // addresses by adding a domain name onto the username.  In which case,
  96     // strip off the domain name and then add on any necessary suffix.
  97     // This should be the inverse of getDefaultEmail().
  98     $result = $email;
  99 
 100     if (isset($mail_settings['domain']) && ($mail_settings['domain'] !== ''))
 101     {
 102       $at_domain = '@' . self::trimDomain($mail_settings['domain']);
 103       if (str_ends_with($email, $at_domain))
 104       {
 105         // Strip the @domain
 106         $result = str_replace($at_domain, '', $result);
 107         // And add on the suffix if there is one
 108         if (isset($mail_settings['username_suffix']))
 109         {
 110           $result .= $mail_settings['username_suffix'];
 111         }
 112       }
 113     }
 114 
 115     return $result;
 116   }
 117 
 118 
 119   public function getDisplayName(?string $username) : ?string
 120   {
 121     global $get_display_names_all_at_once;
 122 
 123     static $display_names = null;  // Cache for performance
 124 
 125     // Easy case 1: $username is null
 126     if (!isset($username))
 127     {
 128       return null;
 129     }
 130 
 131     // Easy case 2: it's the current user
 132     $mrbs_user = session()->getCurrentUser();
 133     if (isset($mrbs_user) && ($mrbs_user->username === $username))
 134     {
 135       return $mrbs_user->display_name;
 136     }
 137 
 138     // If we can (and want to) then get all the usernames at the same time.  It's
 139     // much faster than getting them one at a time when they are stored externally.
 140     // Check to see if $display_names is set before getting the usernames, so that
 141     // if getUsernames returns false we don't keep on trying it for every username
 142     // (the else block will set $display_names).
 143     if ($get_display_names_all_at_once &&
 144         method_exists($this, 'getUsernames') &&
 145         !isset($display_names) &&
 146         (false !== ($usernames = $this->getUsernames())))
 147     {
 148       $display_names = array_column($usernames, 'display_name', 'username');
 149     }
 150     // Otherwise just get them one at a time
 151     else
 152     {
 153       if (!isset($display_names[$username]))
 154       {
 155         $user = $this->getUser($username);
 156         $display_names[$username] = (isset($user)) ? $user->display_name : $username;
 157       }
 158     }
 159 
 160     if (isset($display_names[$username]) && ($display_names[$username] !== ''))
 161     {
 162       return $display_names[$username];
 163     }
 164 
 165     return $username;
 166   }

 217   /**
 218    * Validates that the password conforms to the password policy.
 219    *
 220    * Ideally this function should also be matched by client-side
 221    * validation, but unfortunately JavaScript's native support for Unicode
 222    * pattern matching is very limited.   Would need to be implemented using
 223    * an add-in library.
 224    */
 225   public function validatePassword(
 226     #[\SensitiveParameter]
 227     string $password) : bool
 228   {
 229     global $pwd_policy;
 230 
 231     if (isset($pwd_policy))
 232     {
 233       // Set up regular expressions.  Use p{Ll} instead of [a-z] etc.
 234       // to make sure accented characters are included
 235       $pattern = array('alpha'   => '/\p{L}/',
 236                        'lower'   => '/\p{Ll}/',
 237                        'upper'   => '/\p{Lu}/',
 238                        'numeric' => '/\p{N}/',
 239                        'special' => '/[^\p{L}|\p{N}]/');
 240       // Check for conformance to each rule
 241       foreach($pwd_policy as $rule => $value)
 242       {
 243         switch($rule)
 244         {
 245           case 'length':
 246             if (mb_strlen($password) < $value)
 247             {
 248               return false;
 249             }
 250             break;
 251           default:
 252             // turn on Unicode matching
 253             $pattern[$rule] .= 'u';
 254 
 255             $n = preg_match_all($pattern[$rule], $password, $matches);
 256             if (($n === false) || ($n < $value))
 257             {
 258               return false;
 259             }
 260             break;
 261         }
 262       }
 263     }
 264 
 265     // Everything is OK
 266     return true;
 267   }

 270   /**
 271    * Returns an array of registrants' display names
 272    *
 273    * @return string[]
 274    */
 275   public function getRegistrantsDisplayNames (array $entry, bool $with_registered_by=false, bool $with_registrant_username=false) : array
 276   {
 277     $display_names = array();
 278 
 279     // Only bother getting the names if we don't already know how many there are,
 280     // or if we know there are definitely some
 281     if (!isset($entry['n_registered']) || ($entry['n_registered'] > 0))
 282     {
 283       $display_names = $this->getRegistrantsDisplayNamesUnsorted($entry['id'], $with_registered_by, $with_registrant_username);
 284       usort($display_names, 'MRBS\compare_display_names');
 285     }
 286 
 287     return $display_names;
 288   }

 290 
 291   /**
 292    * @return string[]
 293    */
 294   protected function getRegistrantsDisplayNamesUnsorted(int $id, bool $with_registered_by, bool $with_registrant_username) : array
 295   {
 296     $display_names = array();
 297     $registrants = get_registrants($id, false);
 298 
 299     foreach ($registrants as $registrant)
 300     {
 301       $display_name = $this->getDisplayName($registrant['username']);
 302       // Add in the name of the person who registered this user, if required and if different.
 303       if ($with_registered_by &&
 304         isset($registrant['create_by']) &&
 305         ($registrant['create_by'] !== $registrant['username']))
 306       {
 307         if ($with_registrant_username)
 308         {
 309           $display_names[] = get_vocab("registrant_username_and_registered_by",
 310                                        $registrant['username'],
 311                                        $display_name,
 312                                        $this->getDisplayName($registrant['create_by']));
 313         }
 314         else
 315         {
 316           $display_names[] = get_vocab("registrant_registered_by",
 317                                        $display_name,
 318                                        $this->getDisplayName($registrant['create_by']));
 319         }
 320       }
 321       else
 322       {
 323         $display_names[] = ($with_registrant_username) ? format_compound_name($registrant['username'], $display_name) : $display_name;
 324       }
 325     }
 326 
 327     return $display_names;
 328   }

 331   /**

 333    */
 334   protected function getDefaultLevel(?string $username) : int
 335   {
 336     global $auth, $max_level;
 337 
 338     // User not logged in, user level '0'
 339     if(!isset($username))
 340     {
 341       return 0;
 342     }
 343 
 344     // Check whether the user is an admin; if not they are level 1.
 345     return (isset($auth['admin']) && in_arrayi($username, $auth['admin'])) ? $max_level : 1;
 346   }

 349   /**
 350    * Gets the default email address using config file settings
 351    */
 352   protected function getDefaultEmail(?string $username) : string
 353   {
 354     global $mail_settings;
 355 
 356     if (!isset($username) || $username === '')
 357     {
 358       return '';
 359     }
 360 
 361     $email = $username;
 362 
 363     // Remove the suffix, if there is one
 364     if (isset($mail_settings['username_suffix']) && ($mail_settings['username_suffix'] !== ''))
 365     {
 366       $suffix = $mail_settings['username_suffix'];
 367       if (substr($email, -strlen($suffix)) === $suffix)
 368       {
 369         $email = substr($email, 0, -strlen($suffix));
 370       }
 371     }
 372 
 373     // Add on the domain, if there is one
 374     if (isset($mail_settings['domain']) && ($mail_settings['domain'] !== ''))
 375     {
 376       $email .= '@' . self::trimDomain($mail_settings['domain']);
 377     }
 378 
 379     return $email;
 380   }

 383   /**
 384    * Trim any leading '@' character.
 385    *
 386    * Older versions of MRBS required the '@' character to be included in $mail_settings['domain'],
 387    * and we still allow this for backwards compatibility.
 388    */
 389   private static function trimDomain(string $domain) : string
 390   {
 391     return ltrim($domain, '@');
 392   }
 393 
 394 
 395   /**
 396    * Callback function for comparing two users.
 397    *
 398    * Compares first by 'display_name' and then by 'username'.
 399    *
 400    * @param array{username: string, display_name: string} $user1
 401    * @param array{username: string, display_name: string} $user2
 402    */
 403   private static function compareUsers(array $user1, array $user2) : int
 404   {
 405     $display_name1 = get_sortable_name($user1['display_name']);
 406     $display_name2 = get_sortable_name($user2['display_name']);
 407     // Provide fallbacks just in case the display names are NULL or empty
 408     $display_name1 = (isset($display_name1) && ($display_name1 !== '')) ? $display_name1 : $user1['username'];
 409     $display_name2 = (isset($display_name2) && ($display_name2 !== '')) ? $display_name2 : $user2['username'];
 410 
 411     $display_name_comparison = strcasecmp_locale($display_name1, $display_name2);
 412 
 413     if ($display_name_comparison === 0)
 414     {
 415       return strcasecmp_locale($user1['username'], $user2['username']);
 416     }
 417 
 418     return $display_name_comparison;
 419   }
 420 
 421 
 422   /**
 423    * Sorts an array of users indexed by 'username' and 'display_name', eg the
 424    * output of getUsernames().
 425    *
 426    * Sorts by display_name then username.
 427    *
 428    * @param array{array{username: string, display_name: string}} $users
 429    * @return void
 430    */
 431   protected static function sortUsers(array &$users) : void
 432   {
 433     usort($users, [__CLASS__, 'compareUsers']);
 434   }
 435 
 436 
 437   /**
 438    * Check we've got the right session scheme for the type.
 439    *
 440    * To be called for those authentication types which require the same session scheme.
 441    *
 442    * @return void|never
 443    */
 444   protected function checkSessionMatchesType()
 445   {
 446     global $auth;
 447 
 448     if ($auth['session'] !== $auth['type'])
 449     {
 450       $class = get_called_class();
 451       $message = "MRBS configuration error: $class needs \$auth['session'] set to '" . $auth['type'] . "'";
 452       die($message);
 453     }
 454   }
 455 
 456 
 457   /**
 458    * Writes the debug message to the error log together with the calling method and line number.
 459    * It assumes that it has been called by a debug method.
 460    */
 461   protected static function logDebugMessage(string $message) : void
 462   {
 463     // Need to go three levels back to get the real calling method.
 464     list( , $called, $caller) = debug_backtrace(DEBUG_BACKTRACE_IGNORE_ARGS, 3);
 465     error_log(
 466         "[MRBS DEBUG] " .
 467         $caller['class'] . $caller['type'] . $caller['function'] . '(' . $called['line'] . ')' .
 468         ": $message"
 469       );
 470   }
 471 }

   1 <?php
   2 declare(strict_types=1);
   3 namespace MRBS\Auth;
   4 
   5 use MRBS\MailQueue;
   6 use MRBS\User;
   7 use PHPMailer\PHPMailer\PHPMailer;
   8 use function MRBS\_tbl;
   9 use function MRBS\auth;
  10 use function MRBS\db;
  11 use function MRBS\format_compound_name;
  12 use function MRBS\generate_token;
  13 use function MRBS\get_mail_charset;
  14 use function MRBS\get_vocab;
  15 use function MRBS\multisite;
  16 use function MRBS\parse_email;
  17 use function MRBS\row_cast_columns;
  18 use function MRBS\toTimeString;
  19 use function MRBS\url_base;
  20 
  21 class AuthDb extends Auth
  22 {
  23   /**
  24    * @param string|null $user a username or email address
  25    */
  26   public function validateUser(
  27     #[\SensitiveParameter]
  28     ?string $user,
  29     #[\SensitiveParameter]
  30     ?string $pass)
  31   {
  32     // The string $user that the user logged on with could be either a username or
  33     // an email address, or even possibly just the local part of an email address.
  34     // So it's just possible that there is more than one user with this password and
  35     // username | email address | local-part.    If we get more than one, then we don't
  36     // know which user it is, so we return false.
  37     $valid_usernames = array();
  38 
  39     if (($valid_username = $this->validateUsername($user, $pass)) !== false)
  40     {
  41       $valid_usernames[] = $valid_username;
  42     }
  43 
  44     $valid_usernames = array_merge($valid_usernames, $this->validateEmail($user, $pass));
  45     $valid_usernames = array_unique($valid_usernames);
  46 
  47     if (count($valid_usernames) == 1)
  48     {
  49       $result = $valid_usernames[0];
  50       // Update the database with this login, but don't change the timestamp
  51       $now = time();
  52       $sql = "UPDATE " . _tbl('users') . "
  53                  SET last_login=?, timestamp=timestamp
  54                WHERE name=?";
  55       $sql_params = array($now, $result);
  56       db()->command($sql, $sql_params);
  57       return $result;
  58     }
  59     else
  60     {
  61       return false;
  62     }
  63   }
  64 
  65 
  66   /* validateUsername($user, $pass)
  67    *
  68    * Checks if the specified username/password pair are valid
  69    *
  70    * $user  - The user name
  71    * $pass  - The password
  72    *
  73    * Returns:
  74    *   false    - The pair are invalid or do not exist
  75    *   string   - The validated username
  76    */
  77   private function validateUsername(
  78     #[\SensitiveParameter]
  79     ?string $user,
  80     #[\SensitiveParameter]
  81     ?string $pass)
  82   {
  83     $sql_params = array();
  84 
  85     // We use syntax_casesensitive_equals() rather than just '=' because '=' in MySQL
  86     // permits trailing spacings, eg 'john' = 'john '.   We could use LIKE, but that then
  87     // permits wildcards, so we could use a combination of LIKE and '=' but that's a bit
  88     // messy.  We could use STRCMP, but that's MySQL only.
  89 
  90     // Usernames are unique in the users table, so we only look for one.
  91     $sql = "SELECT password_hash, name
  92             FROM " . _tbl('users') . "
  93            WHERE " . db()->syntax_casesensitive_equals('name', mb_strtolower($user), $sql_params) . "
  94            LIMIT 1";
  95 
  96     $res = db()->query($sql, $sql_params);
  97 
  98     $row = $res->next_row_keyed();
  99 
 100     if (!isset($row['password_hash']))
 101     {
 102       // No user found with that name
 103       return false;
 104     }
 105 
 106     return ($this->checkPassword($pass, $row['password_hash'], 'name', $row['name'])) ? $row['name'] : false;
 107   }
 108 
 109 
 110   /* authValidateEmail($email, $pass)
 111    *
 112    * Checks if the specified email/password pair are valid
 113    *
 114    * $email - The email address
 115    * $pass  - The password
 116    *
 117    * Returns:
 118    *   array    - An array of valid usernames, empty if none found
 119    */
 120   private function validateEmail(
 121     #[\SensitiveParameter]
 122     string $email,
 123     #[\SensitiveParameter]
 124     string $pass) : array
 125   {
 126     $valid_usernames = array();
 127 
 128     // Email addresses are not unique in the users table, so we need to find all of them.
 129     $users = self::getUsersByEmail($email);
 130 
 131     // Check all the users that have this email address and password hash.
 132     foreach($users as $user)
 133     {
 134       if (isset($user['password_hash']) &&
 135           $this->checkPassword($pass, $user['password_hash'], 'email', $email))
 136       {
 137         $valid_usernames[] = $user['name'];
 138       }
 139     }
 140 
 141     return $valid_usernames;
 142   }
 143 
 144 
 145   protected function getUserFresh(string $username) : ?User
 146   {
 147     $row = $this->getUserByUsername($username);
 148 
 149     // The username doesn't exist - return NULL
 150     if (!isset($row))
 151     {
 152       return null;
 153     }
 154 
 155     // The username does exist - return a User object
 156     $user = new User($username);
 157 
 158     // $user->level and $user->display_name will be set as part of this
 159     foreach ($row as $key => $value)
 160     {
 161       if ($key == 'name')
 162       {
 163         // This has already been set as the 'username' property;
 164         continue;
 165       }
 166       $user->$key = $value;
 167     }
 168 
 169     return $user;
 170   }
 171 
 172 
 173   // Return an array of users, indexed by 'username' and 'display_name'
 174   public function getUsernames() : array
 175   {
 176     $sql = "SELECT name AS username,
 177                    CASE
 178                        WHEN display_name IS NOT NULL AND display_name!='' THEN display_name
 179                        ELSE name
 180                    END
 181                    AS display_name
 182               FROM " . _tbl('users') . "
 183           ORDER BY display_name";
 184 
 185     $res = db()->query($sql);
 186 
 187     $users =  $res->all_rows_keyed();
 188 
 189     // Although the users are probably already sorted, we sort them again because MRBS
 190     // offers an option for sorting by first or last name.
 191     self::sortUsers($users);
 192 
 193     return $users;
 194   }
 195 
 196 
 197   // Return an array of all users
 198   public function getUsers() : array
 199   {
 200     // Add in an extra column, last_updated, which is the SQL timestamp converted to a UNIX
 201     // timestamp.  We do the conversion in the SQL query so that it is converted using the
 202     // same timezone that it was stored with.
 203     $sql = "SELECT *, ". db()->syntax_timestamp_to_unix("timestamp") . " AS last_updated
 204               FROM " . _tbl('users') . "
 205              ORDER BY name";
 206 
 207     $res = db()->query($sql);
 208 
 209     $result = $res->all_rows_keyed();
 210 
 211     foreach ($result as &$row)
 212     {
 213       row_cast_columns($row, 'users');
 214       // Turn the last_updated column into an int (some MySQL drivers will return a string,
 215       // and it won't have been caught by row_cast_columns() as it's a derived result).
 216       $row['last_updated'] = intval($row['last_updated']);
 217     }
 218 
 219     return $result;
 220   }

 257   public function requestPassword(?string $login) : bool
 258   {
 259     if (!isset($login) || ($login === ''))
 260     {
 261       return false;
 262     }
 263 
 264     // Get the possible users given this login, which could be a username or email address.
 265     // However all the possible users must have the same email address, so check the email
 266     // addresses at the same time.
 267     $possible_users = array();
 268 
 269     $user = $this->getUserByUsername($login);
 270 
 271     // Users must have an email address otherwise we won't be able to mail a reset link
 272     if (isset($user) && isset($user['email']) && ($user['email'] !== ''))
 273     {
 274       $possible_users[] = $user;
 275     }
 276 
 277     if ($this->canValidateByEmail())
 278     {
 279       $users = $this->getUsersByEmail($login);
 280       if (!empty($users))
 281       {
 282         // Check that the email addresses are the same
 283         if (!empty($possible_users) &&
 284             (mb_strtolower($possible_users[0]['email']) !== mb_strtolower($login)))
 285         {
 286           return false;
 287         }
 288         foreach ($users as $user)
 289         {
 290           $possible_users[] = $user;
 291         }
 292       }
 293     }
 294 
 295     if (!empty($possible_users))
 296     {
 297       // Generate a key
 298       $key = generate_token(32);
 299 
 300       // Update the database
 301       if ($this->setResetKey($possible_users, $key))
 302       {
 303         // Email the user
 304         return $this->notifyUser($possible_users, $key);
 305       }
 306     }
 307 
 308     return false;
 309   }

 312   public function resetPassword(
 313     #[\SensitiveParameter]
 314     ?string $username,
 315     ?string $key,
 316     #[\SensitiveParameter]
 317     ?string $password) : bool
 318   {
 319     // Check that we've got a password and we're allowed to reset the password
 320     if (!isset($password) || !auth()->isValidReset($username, $key))
 321     {
 322       return false;
 323     }
 324 
 325     // Set the new password and clear the reset key
 326     $sql = "UPDATE " . _tbl('users') . "
 327                SET password_hash=:password_hash,
 328                    reset_key_hash=NULL,
 329                    reset_key_expiry=0
 330              WHERE name=:name";  // PostgreSQL does not support LIMIT with UPDATE
 331 
 332     $sql_params = array(
 333         ':password_hash' => password_hash($password, PASSWORD_DEFAULT),
 334         ':name' => $username
 335       );
 336 
 337     db()->command($sql, $sql_params);
 338 
 339     return true;
 340   }

 342 
 343   public function isValidReset(?string $user, ?string $key) : bool
 344   {
 345     if (!isset($user) || !isset($key) || ($user === '') || ($key === ''))
 346     {
 347       return false;
 348     }
 349 
 350     $sql = "SELECT reset_key_hash, reset_key_expiry
 351               FROM " . _tbl('users') . "
 352              WHERE name=:name
 353              LIMIT 1";
 354 
 355     $sql_params = array(':name' => $user);
 356     $res = db()->query($sql,$sql_params);
 357 
 358     // Check we've found a row
 359     if ($res->count() == 0)
 360     {
 361       return false;
 362     }
 363 
 364     $row = $res->next_row_keyed();
 365 
 366     // Check that the reset hasn't expired
 367     if (time() > $row['reset_key_expiry'])
 368     {
 369       return false;
 370     }
 371 
 372     // Check we've got the correct key
 373     return password_verify($key, $row['reset_key_hash']);
 374   }

 377   // Returns an unsorted array of registrants display names
 378   protected function getRegistrantsDisplayNamesUnsortedWithout(int $id, bool $with_registrant_username) : array
 379   {
 380     // For the 'db' auth type we can improve performance by doing a single query
 381     // on the participants table joined with the users table.  (Actually it's two
 382     // queries in a UNION: one getting the rows where there isn't an entry in the
 383     // users table and another the rows where there is.)
 384     $sql = "SELECT P.username as username,
 385                    P.username as display_name
 386               FROM " . _tbl('participants') . " P
 387          LEFT JOIN " . _tbl('users') . " U
 388                 ON P.username=U.name
 389              WHERE P.entry_id=:entry_id
 390                AND (U.display_name IS NULL OR U.display_name='')
 391              UNION
 392             SELECT U.name as username,
 393                    U.display_name as display_name
 394               FROM " . _tbl('participants') . " P
 395          LEFT JOIN " . _tbl('users') . " U
 396                 ON P.username=U.name
 397              WHERE P.entry_id=:entry_id
 398                AND U.display_name IS NOT NULL AND U.display_name!=''";
 399 
 400     $result = array();
 401     $res = db()->query($sql, array(':entry_id' => $id));
 402 
 403     while (false !== ($row = $res->next_row_keyed()))
 404     {
 405       $result[] = ($with_registrant_username) ? format_compound_name($row['username'], $row['display_name']) : $row['display_name'];
 406     }
 407 
 408     return $result;
 409   }

 412   // Returns an unsorted array of registrants display names, including, if
 413   // different, the display name of the person that registered them.
 414   protected function getRegistrantsDisplayNamesUnsortedWith(int $id, bool $with_registrant_username) : array
 415   {
 416     // For the 'db' auth type we can improve performance by doing a single query
 417     // on the participants table joined with the users table.  (Actually it's four
 418     // queries in a UNION: one getting the rows where there isn't an entry in the
 419     // users table and another the rows where there is, etc. for both the registrant
 420     // and the person that registered them.)
 421     $sql = "SELECT P.username as registrant_username,
 422                    P.username as registrant_display_name,
 423                    P.create_by as create_by_username,
 424                    P.create_by as create_by_display_name
 425               FROM " . _tbl('participants') . " P
 426          LEFT JOIN " . _tbl('users') . " U1
 427                 ON P.username=U1.name
 428          LEFT JOIN " . _tbl('users') . " U2
 429                 ON P.create_by=U2.name
 430              WHERE P.entry_id=:entry_id
 431                AND (U1.display_name IS NULL OR U1.display_name='')
 432                AND (U2.display_name IS NULL OR U2.display_name='')
 433 
 434              UNION
 435 
 436             SELECT P.username as registrant_username,
 437                    P.username as registrant_display_name,
 438                    P.create_by as create_by_username,
 439                    U2.display_name as registrant_display_name
 440               FROM " . _tbl('participants') . " P
 441          LEFT JOIN " . _tbl('users') . " U1
 442                 ON P.username=U1.name
 443          LEFT JOIN " . _tbl('users') . " U2
 444                 ON P.create_by=U2.name
 445              WHERE P.entry_id=:entry_id
 446                AND (U1.display_name IS NULL OR U1.display_name='')
 447                AND U2.display_name IS NOT NULL AND U2.display_name!=''
 448 
 449              UNION
 450 
 451             SELECT P.username as registrant_username,
 452                    U1.display_name as registrant_display_name,
 453                    P.create_by as create_by_username,
 454                    P.create_by as registrant_display_name
 455               FROM " . _tbl('participants') . " P
 456          LEFT JOIN " . _tbl('users') . " U1
 457                 ON P.username=U1.name
 458          LEFT JOIN " . _tbl('users') . " U2
 459                 ON P.create_by=U2.name
 460              WHERE P.entry_id=:entry_id
 461                AND U1.display_name IS NOT NULL AND U1.display_name!=''
 462                AND (U2.display_name IS NULL OR U2.display_name='')
 463 
 464              UNION
 465 
 466             SELECT P.username as registrant_username,
 467                    U1.display_name as registrant_display_name,
 468                    P.create_by as create_by_username,
 469                    U2.display_name as registrant_display_name
 470               FROM " . _tbl('participants') . " P
 471          LEFT JOIN " . _tbl('users') . " U1
 472                 ON P.username=U1.name
 473          LEFT JOIN " . _tbl('users') . " U2
 474                 ON P.create_by=U2.name
 475              WHERE P.entry_id=:entry_id
 476                AND U1.display_name IS NOT NULL AND U1.display_name!=''
 477                AND U2.display_name IS NOT NULL AND U2.display_name!=''";
 478 
 479     $result = array();
 480 
 481     $res =  db()->query($sql, array(':entry_id' => $id));
 482 
 483     while (false !== ($row = $res->next_row_keyed()))
 484     {
 485       if ($row['registrant_username'] === $row['create_by_username'])
 486       {
 487         if ($with_registrant_username)
 488         {
 489           $result[] = format_compound_name($row['registrant_username'], $row['registrant_display_name']);
 490         }
 491         else
 492         {
 493           $result[] = $row['registrant_display_name'];
 494         }
 495       }
 496       else
 497       {
 498         if ($with_registrant_username && ($row['registrant_username'] !== $row['registrant_display_name']))
 499         {
 500           $result[] = get_vocab('registrant_username_and_registered_by',
 501                                 $row['registrant_username'],
 502                                 $row['registrant_display_name'],
 503                                 $row['create_by_display_name']);
 504         }
 505         else
 506         {
 507           $result[] = get_vocab('registrant_registered_by',
 508                                 $row['registrant_display_name'],
 509                                 $row['create_by_display_name']);
 510         }
 511       }
 512     }
 513 
 514     return $result;
 515   }
 516 
 517 
 518   /**
 519    * @return string[]
 520    */
 521   protected function getRegistrantsDisplayNamesUnsorted(int $id, bool $with_registered_by, $with_registrant_username) : array
 522   {
 523     if ($with_registered_by)
 524     {
 525       return $this->getRegistrantsDisplayNamesUnsortedWith($id, $with_registrant_username);
 526     }
 527     else
 528     {
 529       return $this->getRegistrantsDisplayNamesUnsortedWithout($id, $with_registrant_username);
 530     }
 531   }

 534   private function notifyUser(array $users, string $key) : bool
 535   {
 536     global $auth, $mail_settings;
 537 
 538     if (empty($users) || !isset($users[0]['email']) || ($users[0]['email'] === ''))
 539     {
 540       return false;
 541     }
 542 
 543     $expiry_time = $auth['db']['reset_key_expiry'];
 544     toTimeString($expiry_time, $expiry_units, true, 'hours');
 545     $addresses = array(
 546         'from'  => $mail_settings['from']
 547       );
 548     // Add the To address, using the display name if possible (ie if it exists and there's
 549     // only one user).
 550     // Also get a name to use in the message body
 551     if ((count($users) == 1) &&
 552         isset($users[0]['display_name']) &&
 553         ($users[0]['display_name'] !== ''))
 554     {
 555       $mailer = new PHPMailer();
 556       $mailer->CharSet = get_mail_charset();
 557       // Note that addrFormat() returns a MIME-encoded address
 558       $addresses['to'] = $mailer->addrFormat(array($users[0]['email'], $users[0]['display_name']));
 559       $name = $users[0]['display_name'];
 560     }
 561     else
 562     {
 563       $addresses['to'] = $users[0]['email'];
 564       // If there's only one user we can use the username, otherwise we have to use the
 565       // email address which is the same for all users.
 566       $name = (count($users) == 1) ? $users[0]['name'] : $users[0]['email'];
 567     }
 568     $subject = get_vocab('password_reset_subject');
 569     $body = '<p>';
 570     $body .= get_vocab('password_reset_body', intval($expiry_time), $expiry_units, $name);
 571     $body .= "</p>\n";
 572 
 573     // Construct and add in the link
 574     $usernames = array();
 575     foreach ($users as $user)
 576     {
 577       $usernames[] = $user['name'];
 578     }
 579     $usernames = array_unique($usernames);
 580 
 581     $vars = array(
 582         'action'    => 'reset',
 583         'usernames' => $usernames,
 584         'key'       => $key
 585       );
 586     $query = http_build_query($vars, '', '&');
 587     $href = url_base() . multisite("reset_password.php?$query");
 588     $body .= "<p><a href=\"$href\">" . get_vocab('reset_password') . "</a>.</p>";
 589 
 590     MailQueue::add(
 591         $addresses,
 592         $subject,
 593         strip_tags($body),
 594         $body,
 595         null,
 596         get_mail_charset()
 597       );
 598 
 599     return true;
 600   }

 602   private function setResetKey(array $users, string $key) : bool
 603   {
 604     global $auth;
 605 
 606     if (empty($users))
 607     {
 608       return false;
 609     }
 610 
 611     $ids = array();
 612     foreach($users as $user)
 613     {
 614       // Use intval to make sure the string is safe for the SQL query
 615       $ids[] = intval($user['id']);
 616     }
 617 
 618     $sql = "UPDATE " . _tbl('users') . "
 619                SET reset_key_hash=:reset_key_hash,
 620                    reset_key_expiry=:reset_key_expiry
 621              WHERE id IN (" . implode(',', $ids) . ")";
 622 
 623     $sql_params = array(
 624         ':reset_key_hash' => password_hash($key, PASSWORD_DEFAULT),
 625         ':reset_key_expiry' => time() + $auth['db']['reset_key_expiry']
 626       );
 627 
 628     db()->command($sql, $sql_params);
 629 
 630     return true;
 631   }

 634   private function getUserByUsername(string $username) : ?array
 635   {
 636     $sql = "SELECT *
 637               FROM " . _tbl('users') . "
 638              WHERE name=:name
 639              LIMIT 1";
 640 
 641     $result = db()->query($sql, array(':name' => $username));
 642 
 643     // The username doesn't exist - return NULL
 644     if ($result->count() === 0)
 645     {
 646       return null;
 647     }
 648 
 649     return $result->next_row_keyed();
 650   }

 653   public function getUserByUserId(int $id) : ?User
 654   {
 655     $sql = "SELECT *
 656               FROM " . _tbl('users') . "
 657              WHERE id=:id
 658              LIMIT 1";
 659 
 660     $result = db()->query($sql, array(':id' => $id));
 661 
 662     // The username doesn't exist - return NULL
 663     if ($result->count() === 0)
 664     {
 665       return null;
 666     }
 667 
 668     // The username does exist - return a User object
 669     $user = new User();
 670     $row = $result->next_row_keyed();
 671 
 672     // $user->level and $user->display_name will be set as part of this
 673     foreach ($row as $key => $value)
 674     {
 675       if ($key == 'name')
 676       {
 677         $user->username = $value;
 678       }
 679       $user->$key = $value;
 680     }
 681 
 682     return $user;
 683   }

 688   public function getUsernameByEmail(string $email) : ?string

 691               FROM " . _tbl('users') . "
 692              WHERE email=?";
 693

 695

 697     {
 698       return null;
 699     }
 700 
 701     if ($res->count() > 1)
 702     {
 703       // Could maybe do something better here
 704       trigger_error("Email address not unique", E_USER_NOTICE);
 705     }

 711   // Returns an array of rows for all users with the email address $email.
 712   // Assumes that email addresses are case insensitive.
 713   // Allows equivalent Gmail addresses, ie ignores dots in the local part and
 714   // treats gmail.com and googlemail.com as equivalent domains.
 715   private function getUsersByEmail(string $email) : array
 716   {
 717     global $auth;
 718 
 719     $result = array();
 720 
 721     // For the moment we will assume that email addresses are case-insensitive.   Whilst it is true
 722     // on most systems, it isn't always true.  The domain is case-insensitive but the local-part can
 723     // be case-sensitive.  But before we can take account of this, the email addresses in the database
 724     // need to be normalised so that all the domain names are stored in lower case.  Then it will be
 725     // possible to do a case-sensitive comparison.
 726     if (mb_strpos($email, '@') === false)
 727     {
 728       if (!empty($auth['allow_local_part_email']))
 729       {
 730         // We're just checking the local-part of the email address
 731         $sql_params = array($email);
 732         $condition = "LOWER(?)=LOWER(" . db()->syntax_simple_split('email', '@', 1, $sql_params) .")";
 733       }
 734       else
 735       {
 736         return $result;
 737       }
 738     }
 739     else
 740     {
 741       $address = parse_email($email);
 742       // Invalid email address
 743       if ($address === false)
 744       {
 745         return $result;
 746       }
 747       // Special case for Gmail addresses: ignore dots in the local part and treat gmail.com and
 748       // googlemail.com as equivalent domains.
 749       elseif (in_array(mb_strtolower($address['domain']), array('gmail.com', 'googlemail.com')))
 750       {
 751         $sql_params = array(str_replace('.', '', $address['local']));
 752         $sql_params[] = $sql_params[0];
 753         $condition = "(LOWER(?) = REPLACE(TRIM(TRAILING '@gmail.com' FROM LOWER(email)), '.', '')) OR " .
 754                      "(LOWER(?) = REPLACE(TRIM(TRAILING '@googlemail.com' FROM LOWER(email)), '.', ''))";
 755       }
 756       // Everything else: check the complete email address
 757       else
 758       {
 759         $sql_params = array($email);
 760         $condition = "LOWER(?)=LOWER(email)";
 761       }
 762     }
 763 
 764     $sql = "SELECT *
 765               FROM " . _tbl('users') . "
 766              WHERE $condition";
 767 
 768     $res = db()->query($sql, $sql_params);
 769 
 770     while (false !== ($row = $res->next_row_keyed()))
 771     {
 772       $result[] = $row;
 773     }
 774 
 775     return $result;
 776   }
 777 
 778 
 779   private function rehash(
 780     #[\SensitiveParameter]
 781     string $password,
 782     string $column_name,
 783     string $column_value) : void
 784   {
 785     $sql_params = array(password_hash($password, PASSWORD_DEFAULT));
 786 
 787     switch ($column_name)
 788     {
 789       case 'name':
 790         $condition = db()->syntax_casesensitive_equals($column_name, mb_strtolower($column_value), $sql_params);
 791         break;
 792       case 'email':
 793         // For the moment we will assume that email addresses are case insensitive.   Whilst it is true
 794         // on most systems, it isn't always true.  The domain is case insensitive but the local-part can
 795         // be case sensitive.   But before we can take account of this, the email addresses in the database
 796         // need to be normalised so that all the domain names are stored in lower case.  Then it will be possible
 797         // to do a case sensitive comparison.
 798         $sql_params[] = $column_value;
 799         $condition = "LOWER($column_name)=LOWER(?)";
 800         break;
 801       default:
 802         trigger_error("Unsupported column name '$column_name'.", E_USER_NOTICE);
 803         return;
 804         break;
 805     }
 806 
 807     $sql = "UPDATE " . _tbl('users') . "
 808                SET password_hash=?
 809              WHERE $condition";
 810 
 811     db()->command($sql, $sql_params);
 812   }
 813 
 814 
 815   // Checks $password against $password_hash for the row in the user table
 816   // where $column_name=$column_value.  Typically $column_name will be either
 817   // 'name' or 'email'.
 818   // Returns a boolean: true if they match, otherwise false.
 819   private function checkPassword(
 820     #[\SensitiveParameter]
 821     string $password,
 822     string $password_hash,
 823     string $column_name,
 824     string $column_value) : bool
 825   {
 826     $result = false;
 827     $do_rehash = false;
 828 
 829     /* If the hash starts '$' it's a PHP password hash */
 830     if (substr($password_hash, 0, 1) == '$')
 831     {
 832       if (password_verify($password, $password_hash))
 833       {
 834         $result = true;
 835         if (password_needs_rehash($password_hash, PASSWORD_DEFAULT))
 836         {
 837           $do_rehash = true;
 838         }
 839       }
 840     }
 841     /* Otherwise it's a legacy MD5 hash */
 842     else
 843     {
 844       if (md5($password) == $password_hash)
 845       {
 846         $result = true;
 847         $do_rehash = true;
 848       }
 849     }
 850 
 851     if ($do_rehash)
 852     {
 853       $this->rehash($password, $column_name, $column_value);
 854     }
 855 
 856     return $result;
 857   }
 858 
 859 }

   2 namespace MRBS\Auth;
   3 
   4 class AuthFactory
   5 {
   6 
   7   public static function create(string $type)
   8   {
   9     // Transform the authentication type from lowercase_separated to LowercaseSeparated
  10     $parts = explode('_', $type);
  11     $parts = array_map('ucfirst', $parts);
  12     $class = __NAMESPACE__  . "\\Auth" . implode('', $parts);
  13     return new $class;
  14   }

  42   // Get a series of flex divs for a room in a day index interval for the map.
  43   protected function flexDivsHTML(int $room_id, int $start_day_index, int $end_day_index) : string
  44   {
  45     global $resolution;
  46 
  47     $html = '';
  48 
  49     // Get the time slots
  50     $n_time_slots = self::getNTimeSlots();
  51     $morning_slot_seconds = self::morningSlotsSeconds();
  52     $evening_slot_seconds = $morning_slot_seconds + (($n_time_slots - 1) * $resolution);
  53 
  54     // Loop through the days in the interval
  55     for ($i=$start_day_index; $i<=$end_day_index; $i++)
  56     {
  57       $s = $morning_slot_seconds;
  58 
  59       // Loop through the slots in the day
  60       while ($s <= $evening_slot_seconds)
  61       {
  62         // Get the entry for this slot
  63         $this_slot = $this->map->slot($room_id, $i, $s);
  64         // Start a FlexDiv if we haven't got one
  65         if (!isset($flex_div))
  66         {
  67           $flex_div = new FlexDiv($this_slot[0]['id'] ?? null);
  68           // If it's a booking, set the properties
  69           if (!empty($this_slot))
  70           {
  71             $this_entry = $this_slot[0];
  72             $flex_div->setClasses($this->getEntryClasses($this_entry));
  73             $flex_div->setLength($this_entry['n_slots']);
  74             $flex_div->setName($this_entry['name']);
  75           }
  76           // Work out how many slots to advance
  77           $n = $flex_div->getLength();
  78         }
  79         // Otherwise, look to see whether this is a continuation of the stored entry,
  80         // or else a change, in which case output the stored entry and reset.
  81         else
  82         {
  83           // Another free slot
  84           if (empty($this_slot) && !isset($flex_div->id))
  85           {
  86             $n = 1;
  87             $flex_div->addLength($n);
  88           }
  89           // A continuation of an existing booking
  90           elseif (!empty($this_slot) && isset($flex_div->id) && ($flex_div->id == $this_slot[0]['id']))
  91           {
  92             $n = $this_slot[0]['n_slots'];
  93             $flex_div->addLength($n);
  94           }
  95           // There's been a change.  Output the FlexDiv and reset
  96           else
  97           {
  98             $html .= $flex_div->html();
  99             unset($flex_div);
 100             $n = 0;
 101           }
 102         }
 103         $s = $s + ($n * $resolution);  // Advance n slots
 104       }
 105     }
 106 
 107     // Output the final FlexDiv
 108     if (isset($flex_div))
 109     {
 110       $html .= $flex_div->html();
 111     }
 112 
 113     return $html;
 114   }
 115

 117   protected function getDate(int $t) : string
 118   {
 119     global $datetime_formats;
 120 
 121     if (in_array($this->view, ['month', 'year']))
 122     {
 123       return datetime_format(['pattern' => 'd'], $t);
 124     }
 125     else
 126     {
 127       return datetime_format($datetime_formats['view_week_day_month'], $t);
 128     }
 129   }
 130 
 131 
 132   private function getDay(int $t) : string
 133   {
 134     // In the month view use a pattern which will tend to give a narrower result, to save space.
 135     $pattern = ($this->view == 'month') ? 'cccccc' : 'ccc';
 136 
 137     return datetime_format(['pattern' => $pattern], $t);
 138   }

 140 
 141   public static function morningSlotsSeconds() : int
 142   {
 143     global $morningstarts, $morningstarts_minutes;
 144 
 145     return (($morningstarts * 60) + $morningstarts_minutes) * 60;
 146   }
 147 
 148 
 149   // Gets the number of time slots between the beginning and end of the booking
 150   // day.   (This is the normal number on a non-DST transition day)
 151   public static function getNTimeSlots() : int
 152   {
 153     global $eveningends, $eveningends_minutes;
 154     global $resolution;
 155 
 156     $start_first = self::morningSlotsSeconds();           // seconds
 157     $end_last = ((($eveningends * 60) + $eveningends_minutes) * 60) + $resolution;  // seconds
 158     $end_last = $end_last % SECONDS_PER_DAY;
 159     if (day_past_midnight())
 160     {
 161       $end_last += SECONDS_PER_DAY;
 162     }
 163 
 164     // Force the result to be an int.  It normally will be, but might not be if, say,
 165     // $force_resolution is set.
 166     return intval(($end_last - $start_first)/$resolution);
 167   }
 168 
 169 
 170   // If we're not using periods, construct an array describing the slots to pass to the JavaScript so that
 171   // it can calculate where the timeline should be drawn.  (If we are using periods then the timeline is
 172   // meaningless because we don't know when periods begin and end.)
 173   //    $month, $day, $year   the start of the interval
 174   //    $n_days               the number of days in the interval
 175   //    $day_cells            if the columns/rows represent a full day (as in the week/month all rooms views)
 176   protected function getSlots(int $month, int $day, int $year, int $n_days=1, bool $day_cells=false) : ?array
 177   {
 178     global $enable_periods, $morningstarts, $morningstarts_minutes, $resolution;
 179 
 180     if ($enable_periods)
 181     {
 182       return null;
 183     }
 184 
 185     $slots = array();
 186 
 187     $n_time_slots = self::getNTimeSlots();
 188     $morning_slot_seconds = self::morningSlotsSeconds();
 189     $evening_slot_seconds = $morning_slot_seconds + (($n_time_slots - 1) * $resolution);
 190 
 191     for ($j = 0; $j < $n_days; $j++)
 192     {
 193       $d = $day + $j;
 194 
 195       // If there's more than one day in the interval then don't include the hidden days in the array, because
 196       // they don't appear in the DOM.  If there's only one day then we've managed to display the hidden day.
 197       if (($n_days > 1) &&
 198         is_hidden_day(intval(date('w', mktime($morningstarts, $morningstarts_minutes, 0, $month, $d, $year)))))
 199       {
 200         continue;
 201       }
 202 
 203       $this_day = array();
 204 
 205       if ($day_cells)
 206       {
 207         $this_day[] = mktime(0, 0, $morning_slot_seconds, $month, $d, $year);
 208         // Need to do mktime() again for the end of the slot as we can't assume that the end slot is $resolution
 209         // seconds after the start of the slot because of the possibility of DST transitions
 210         $this_day[] = mktime(0, 0, $evening_slot_seconds + $resolution, $month, $d, $year);
 211       }
 212       else
 213       {
 214         for ($s = $morning_slot_seconds;
 215              $s <= $evening_slot_seconds;
 216              $s += $resolution)
 217         {
 218           $this_slot = array();
 219           $this_slot[] = mktime(0, 0, $s, $month, $d, $year);
 220           // Need to do mktime() again for the end of the slot as we can't assume that the end slot is $resolution
 221           // seconds after the start of the slot because of the possibility of DST transitions
 222           $this_slot[] = mktime(0, 0, $s + $resolution, $month, $d, $year);
 223           $this_day[] = $this_slot;
 224         }
 225       }
 226       $slots[] = $this_day;
 227     }
 228 
 229     if ($day_cells)
 230     {
 231       $slots = array($slots);
 232     }
 233 
 234     return $slots;
 235   }
 236 
 237 
 238   // Get classes for weekends, holidays, etc.
 239   protected function getDateClasses(DateTime $date) : array
 240   {
 241     $result = [];
 242 
 243     if ($date->isWeekend())
 244     {
 245       $result[] = 'weekend';
 246     }
 247     if ($date->isHoliday())
 248     {
 249       $result[] = 'holiday';
 250     }
 251     if ($date->isToday())
 252     {
 253       $result[] = 'today';
 254     }
 255 
 256     return $result;
 257   }
 258 
 259 
 260   // Returns an array of classes to be used for the entry
 261   protected function getEntryClasses(array $entry) : array
 262   {
 263     global $approval_enabled, $confirmation_enabled;
 264 
 265     $classes = array($entry['type']);
 266 
 267     if ($entry['private'])
 268     {
 269       $classes[] = 'private';
 270     }
 271 
 272     if ($approval_enabled && ($entry['awaiting_approval']))
 273     {
 274       $classes[] = 'awaiting_approval';
 275     }
 276 
 277     if ($confirmation_enabled && ($entry['tentative']))
 278     {
 279       $classes[] = 'tentative';
 280     }
 281 
 282     if (isset($entry['repeat_id']))
 283     {
 284       $classes[] = 'series';
 285     }
 286 
 287     if ($entry['allow_registration'])
 288     {
 289       if ($entry['registrant_limit_enabled'] &&
 290         ($entry['n_registered'] >= $entry['registrant_limit']))
 291       {
 292         $classes[] = 'full';
 293       }
 294       else
 295       {
 296         $classes[] = 'spaces';
 297       }
 298     }
 299 
 300     return $classes;
 301   }
 302

 304   protected function multidayHeaderRowsHTML(int $day_start_interval, int $n_days, int $start_dow, string $label='') : array
 305   {
 306     global $row_labels_both_sides;
 307 
 308     $result = array();
 309     $n_rows = 2;
 310     // Loop through twice: one row for the days of the week, the next for the date.
 311     for ($i = 0; $i < $n_rows; $i++)
 312     {
 313       $result[$i] = "<tr>\n";
 314 
 315       // Could use a rowspan here, but we'd need to make sure the sticky cells work
 316       // and change the JavaScript in refresh.js.php
 317       $text = ($i == 0) ? '' : $label;
 318       $first_last_html = '<th class="first_last">' . escape_html($text) . "</th>\n";
 319       $result[$i] .= $first_last_html;
 320 
 321       $vars = [
 322         'view' => 'day',
 323         'view_all' => $this->view_all,
 324         'area' => $this->area_id,
 325         'room' => $this->room_id
 326       ];
 327 
 328       // the standard view, with days along the top and rooms down the side
 329       for ($j = 0; $j < $n_days; $j++)
 330       {
 331         if (is_hidden_day(($j + $start_dow) % DAYS_PER_WEEK))
 332         {
 333           continue;
 334         }
 335         $vars['page_date'] = format_iso_date($this->year, $this->month, $day_start_interval + $j);
 336         $link = "index.php?" . http_build_query($vars, '', '&');
 337         $link = multisite($link);
 338         $t = mktime(12, 0, 0, $this->month, $day_start_interval + $j, $this->year);
 339         $text = ($i === 0) ? $this->getDay($t) : $this->getDate($t);
 340         $date = new DateTime();
 341         $date->setTimestamp($t);
 342         $classes = $this->getDateClasses($date);
 343         $result[$i] .= '<th' .
 344           // Add the date for JavaScript.  Only really necessary for the first row in
 345           // the week view when not viewing all the rooms, but just add it always.
 346           ' data-date="' . escape_html($date->getISODate()) . '"' .
 347           ((!empty($classes)) ? ' class="' . implode(' ', $classes) . '"' : '') .
 348           '><a href="' . escape_html($link) . '">' . escape_html($text) . "</a></th>\n";
 349       }
 350 
 351       // next line to display rooms on right side
 352       if ($row_labels_both_sides)
 353       {
 354         $result[$i] .= $first_last_html;
 355       }
 356 
 357       $result[$i] .= "</tr>\n";
 358     }
 359 
 360     return $result;
 361   }
 362 
 363 
 364   // Draw a room cell to be used in the header rows/columns of the calendar views
 365   //    $room    contains the room details
 366   //    $vars    an associative array containing the variables to be used to build the link
 367   protected function roomCellHTML(array $room, array $vars) : string
 368   {
 369     $link = 'index.php?' . http_build_query($vars, '', '&');
 370     $link = multisite($link);
 371 
 372     switch ($vars['view'])
 373     {
 374       case 'day':
 375         $tag = 'viewday';
 376         break;
 377       case 'week':
 378         $tag = 'viewweek';
 379         break;
 380       case 'month':
 381         $tag = 'viewmonth';
 382         break;
 383       case 'year':
 384         $tag = 'viewyear';
 385         break;
 386       default:
 387         trigger_error("Unknown view '" . $vars['view'] . "'", E_USER_NOTICE);
 388         $tag = 'viewweek';
 389         break;
 390     }
 391 
 392     $title = get_vocab($tag) . "\n\n" . $room['description'];
 393     $html = '';
 394     $html .= '<th data-room="' . escape_html($room['id']) . '">';
 395     $html .= '<a href="' . escape_html($link) . '"' .
 396       ' title = "' . escape_html($title) . '">';
 397     $html .= escape_html($room['room_name']);
 398     // Put the capacity in a span to give flexibility in styling
 399     $html .= '<span class="capacity';
 400     if ($room['capacity'] == 0)
 401     {
 402       $html .= ' zero';
 403     }
 404     $html .= '">' . escape_html($room['capacity']);
 405     $html .= '</span>';
 406     $html .= '</a>';
 407     $html .= "</th>\n";
 408     return $html;
 409   }
 410 
 411 }

   1 <?php
   2 declare(strict_types=1);
   3 namespace MRBS\Calendar;
   4 
   5 use InvalidArgumentException;
   6 
   7 class CalendarFactory
   8 {
   9   public static function create(
  10     string $view,
  11     int $view_all,
  12     int $year,
  13     int $month,
  14     int $day,
  15     int $area_id,
  16     int $room_id,
  17     ?int $timetohighlight=null,
  18     ?string $kiosk=null) : Calendar
  19   {
  20     switch ($view)
  21     {
  22       case 'day':
  23         return new CalendarMultislotDay($view, $view_all, $year, $month, $day, $area_id, $room_id, $timetohighlight, $kiosk);
  24         break;
  25       case 'week':
  26         if ($view_all)
  27         {
  28           return new CalendarMultidayMultiroom($view, $view_all, $year, $month, $day, $area_id, $room_id);
  29         }
  30         return new CalendarMultislotWeek($view, $view_all, $year, $month, $day, $area_id, $room_id, $timetohighlight);
  31         break;
  32       case 'month':
  33         if ($view_all)
  34         {
  35           return new CalendarMultidayMultiroom($view, $view_all, $year, $month, $day, $area_id, $room_id);
  36         }
  37         return new CalendarMonthOneRoom($view, $view_all, $year, $month, $day, $area_id, $room_id);
  38         break;
  39       case 'year':
  40         if ($view_all)
  41         {
  42           return new CalendarMultimonthMultiroom($view, $view_all, $year, $month, $day, $area_id, $room_id);
  43         }
  44         return new CalendarMultimonthOneRoom($view, $view_all, $year, $month, $day, $area_id, $room_id);
  45         break;
  46       default:
  47         throw new InvalidArgumentException("Invalid view: $view");
  48         break;
  49     }
  50   }
  51 }

   2 declare(strict_types=1);
   3 namespace MRBS\Calendar;

   5 use MRBS\DateTime;
   6 use function MRBS\escape_html;
   7 use function MRBS\get_vocab;
   8 use function MRBS\getWritable;
   9 use function MRBS\hm_before;
  10 use function MRBS\hour_min;
  11 use function MRBS\is_book_admin;
  12 use function MRBS\multisite;
  13 use function MRBS\period_index_nominal;
  14 use function MRBS\period_name_nominal;

  16 
  17 abstract class CalendarMultislot extends Calendar
  18 {
  19   protected $timetohighlight;
