  21 
  22   // $s is nominal seconds
  23   protected function getQueryVars(int $room, int $month, int $day, int $year, int $s) : array
  24   {
  25     global $morningstarts, $morningstarts_minutes;
  26 
  27     $result = [];
  28 
  29     // check to see if the time is really on the next day
  30     $date = getdate(mktime(0, 0, $s, $month, $day, $year));
  31     if (hm_before($date, ['hours' => $morningstarts, 'minutes' => $morningstarts_minutes]))
  32     {
  33       $date['hours'] += 24;
  34     }
  35     $hour = $date['hours'];
  36     $minute = $date['minutes'];
  37     $period = period_index_nominal($s);
  38 
  39     $vars = [
  40       'view'  => $this->view,
  41       'year'  => $year,
  42       'month' => $month,
  43       'day'   => $day,
  44       'area'  => $this->area_id
  45     ];
  46 
  47     $result['booking']     = $vars;
  48     $result['new_periods'] = array_merge($vars, ['room' => $room, 'period' => $period]);
  49     $result['new_times']   = array_merge($vars, ['room' => $room, 'hour' => $hour, 'minute' => $minute]);
  50 
  51     return $result;
  52   }
  53 
  54 
  55   protected function tdHTML(array $cell, array $query_vars, bool $is_invalid = false) : string
  56   {
  57     // Draws a single cell in the main table of the day and week views
  58     //
  59     // $cell is an array of entries that occupy that cell.  There can be none, one or many
  60     // bookings in a cell.  If there are no bookings, then a blank cell is drawn with a link
  61     // to the edit entry form.  If there is one booking, then the booking is shown in that
  62     // cell.  If there is more than one booking, then all the bookings are shown.
  63 
  64     // $query_vars is an array containing the query vars to be used in the link for the cell.
  65     // It is indexed as follows:
  66     //    ['new_periods']   the vars to be used for an empty cell if using periods
  67     //    ['new_times']     the vars to be used for an empty cell if using times
  68     //    ['booking']       the vars to be used for a full cell
  69     //
  70     // $is_invalid specifies whether the slot actually exists or is one of the non-existent
  71     // slots in the transition to DST
  72 
  73     global $enable_periods, $show_plus_link, $prevent_booking_on_holidays, $prevent_booking_on_weekends;
  74 
  75     $html = '';
  76     $classes = array();
  77 
  78     // Don't put in a <td> cell if the slot contains a single booking whose n_slots is NULL.
  79     // This would mean that it's the second or subsequent slot of a booking and so the
  80     // <td> for the first slot would have had a rowspan that extended the cell down for
  81     // the number of slots of the booking.
  82 
  83     if (empty($cell) || !is_null($cell[0]['n_slots']))
  84     {
  85       if (!empty($cell))
  86       {
  87         $classes[] = 'booked';
  88         if (count($cell) > 1)
  89         {
  90           $classes[] = 'multiply';
  91         }
  92       }
  93       elseif ($is_invalid)
  94       {
  95         $classes[] = 'invalid';
  96       }
  97       else
  98       {
  99         $classes[] = 'new';
 100         // Add classes for weekends and holidays
 101         $date = new DateTime();
 102         $date->setDate(
 103           $query_vars['new_times']['year'],
 104           $query_vars['new_times']['month'],
 105           $query_vars['new_times']['day']
 106         );
 107         $classes = array_merge($classes, $this->getDateClasses($date));
 108       }
 109 
 110       // If there's no booking, or if there are multiple bookings, then make the slot one unit long
 111       $slots = (count($cell) == 1) ? $cell[0]['n_slots'] : 1;
 112 
 113       $html .= $this->tdOpeningTagHTML($classes, $slots);
 114 
 115       // If the room isn't booked, then allow it to be booked
 116       if (empty($cell))
 117       {
 118         // Don't provide a link if the slot doesn't really exist or if the user is logged in, but not a booking admin,
 119         // and it's a holiday/weekend and bookings on holidays/weekends are not allowed.  (We provide a link if they
 120         // are not logged in because they might want to click and login as an admin).
 121         if ($is_invalid ||
 122           ((null !== session()->getCurrentUser()) && !is_book_admin($query_vars['new_times']['room']) &&
 123             (($prevent_booking_on_holidays && in_array('holiday', $classes)) ||
 124               ($prevent_booking_on_weekends && in_array('weekend', $classes)))))
 125         {
 126           $html .= '<span class="not_allowed"></span>';
 127         }
 128         else
 129         {
 130           $vars = ($enable_periods) ? $query_vars['new_periods'] : $query_vars['new_times'];
 131           $query = http_build_query($vars, '', '&');
 132 
 133           $html .= '<a href="' . escape_html(multisite("edit_entry.php?$query")) . '"' .
 134             ' aria-label="' . escape_html(get_vocab('create_new_booking')) . "\">";
 135           if ($show_plus_link)
 136           {
 137             $html .= "<img src=\"images/new.gif\" alt=\"New\" width=\"10\" height=\"10\">";
 138           }
 139           $html .= "</a>";
 140         }
 141       }
 142       else  // if it is booked, then show the booking
 143       {
 144         foreach ($cell as $booking)
 145         {
 146           $vars = $query_vars['booking'];
 147           $vars['id'] = $booking['id'];
 148           $query = http_build_query($vars, '', '&');
 149 
 150           // We have to wrap the booking in a <div> because we want the booking itself to be given
 151           // an absolute position, and we can't use position relative on a <td> in IE11 and below.
 152           // We also need the bookings in a container because jQuery UI resizable has problems
 153           // with border-box (see https://stackoverflow.com/questions/18344272). And we need
 154           // border-box for the bookings because we are using padding on the bookings and we want
 155           // 'width: 100%' and 'height: 100%' to fill the table-cell with the entire booking
 156           // including content.
 157 
 158           $classes = $this->getEntryClasses($booking);
 159           $classes[] = 'booking';
 160 
 161           if ($booking['is_multiday_start'])
 162           {
 163             $classes[] = 'multiday_start';
 164           }
 165 
 166           if ($booking['is_multiday_end'])
 167           {
 168             $classes[] = 'multiday_end';
 169           }
 170 
 171           // Tell JavaScript to make bookings resizable
 172           if ((count($cell) == 1) &&
 173             getWritable($booking['create_by'], $booking['room_id']))
 174           {
 175             $classes[] = 'writable';
 176           }
 177 
 178           $html .= '<div class="' . implode(' ', $classes) . '">';
 179           $html .= '<a href="' . escape_html(multisite("view_entry.php?$query")) . '"' .
 180             ' title="' . escape_html($booking['description'] ?? '') . '"' .
 181             ' class="' . $booking['type'] . '"' .
 182             ' data-id="' . $booking['id'] . '"' .
 183             ' data-type="' . $booking['type'] . '">';
 184           $html .= escape_html($booking['name']) . '</a>';
 185           $html .= "</div>";
 186         }
 187       }
 188 
 189       $html .= "</td>\n";
 190     }
 191 
 192     return $html;
 193   }
 194

 196   // Output a start table cell tag <td> with class of $classes.
 197   // $classes can be either a string or an array of classes
 198   // empty or row_highlight if highlighted.
 199   // $slots is the number of time slots high that the cell should be
 200   //
 201   // $data is an optional third parameter which if set passes an
 202   // associative array of name-value pairs to be used in data attributes
 203   private function tdOpeningTagHTML(array $classes, int $slots, ?array $data=null) : string
 204   {
 205     global $times_along_top;
 206 
 207     $html = '<td';
 208 
 209     if (!empty($classes))
 210     {
 211       $html.= ' class="' . implode(' ', $classes) . '"';
 212     }
 213 
 214     if ($slots > 1)
 215       // No need to output more HTML than necessary
 216     {
 217       $html .= (($times_along_top) ? ' colspan' : ' rowspan') . "=\"$slots\"";
 218     }
 219 
 220     if (isset($data))
 221     {
 222       foreach ($data as $name => $value)
 223       {
 224         $html .= " data-$name=\"$value\"";
 225       }
 226     }
 227 
 228     $html .= ">";
 229 
 230     return $html;
 231   }

 261   protected function theadThTimeCellsHTML(int $start, int $end, int $increment) : string
 262   {

 265     $html = '';
 266 
 267     for ($s = $start; $s <= $end; $s += $increment)
 268     {

 277         $html .= escape_html(period_name_nominal($s));
 278       }
 279       else
 280       {
 281         $html .= escape_html($this->timeslotText($s, $increment));
 282       }
 283       $html .= "</span>";
 284       $html .= "</th>\n";
 285     }
 286

 291   private function timeslotText(int $s, int $resolution) : string

   3 namespace MRBS\Calendar;

   5 use MRBS\DateTime;
   6 use function MRBS\escape_html;

   8 use function MRBS\get_room_details;
   9 use function MRBS\get_rooms;

  16 
  17 class CalendarMultislotDay extends CalendarMultislot
  18 {
  19   private $kiosk;
  20 
  21 
  22   public function __construct(string $view, int $view_all, int $year, int $month, int $day, int $area_id, int $room_id, ?int $timetohighlight=null, ?string $kiosk=null)
  23   {
  24     parent::__construct($view, $view_all, $year, $month, $day, $area_id, $room_id);
  25     $this->timetohighlight = $timetohighlight;
  26     $this->kiosk = $kiosk;
  27   }
  28 
  29   public function innerHTML() : string
  30   {
  31     global $enable_periods;
  32     global $times_along_top, $row_labels_both_sides, $column_labels_both_ends;
  33     global $resolution, $morningstarts, $morningstarts_minutes;
  34 
  35     if ($this->kiosk === 'room')
  36     {
  37       $rooms = array(get_room_details($this->room_id));
  38     }
  39     else
  40     {
  41       $rooms = get_rooms($this->area_id);
  42     }
  43 
  44     $n_rooms = count($rooms);
  45 
  46     if ($n_rooms == 0)
  47     {
  48       // Add an 'empty' data flag so that the JavaScript knows whether this is a real table or not
  49       return "<tbody data-empty=1><tr><td><h1>" . get_vocab("no_rooms_for_area") . "</h1></td></tr></tbody>";
  50     }
  51 
  52     $start_first_slot = get_start_first_slot($this->month, $this->day, $this->year);
  53     $start_last_slot = get_start_last_slot($this->month, $this->day, $this->year);
  54     // Keep a count of the number of slots at the start of the day that we're
  55     // not showing (will only be relevant in kiosk mode).
  56     $skipped_slots = 0;
  57 
  58     // If we are in kiosk mode we are not interested in what has already happened.
  59     // But if we are in periods mode we don't know when the periods occur, so show them all.
  60     if (isset($kiosk) && !$enable_periods)
  61     {
  62       $now = time();
  63       $start_next_slot = $start_first_slot + $resolution;
  64       while (($now > $start_next_slot) && ($start_next_slot < $start_last_slot))
  65       {
  66         $start_first_slot = $start_next_slot;
  67         $skipped_slots++;
  68         $start_next_slot = $start_first_slot + $resolution;
  69       }
  70     }
  71 
  72     // Work out whether there's a possibility that a time slot is invalid,
  73     // in other words whether the booking day includes a transition into DST.
  74     // If we know that there's a transition into DST then some of the slots are
  75     // going to be invalid.   Knowing whether or not there are possibly invalid slots
  76     // saves us bothering to do the detailed calculations of which slots are invalid.
  77     $is_possibly_invalid = !$enable_periods && is_possibly_invalid($start_first_slot, $start_last_slot);
  78 
  79     $start_date = (new DateTime())->setTimestamp($start_first_slot);
  80     $end_date = (new DateTime())->setTimestamp($start_last_slot + $resolution);
  81 
  82     $entries = get_entries_by_area($this->area_id, $start_date, $end_date);
  83 
  84     // We want to build a map containing all the data we want to show
  85     // and then spit it out.
  86     $map = new Map($start_date, $end_date, $resolution);
  87     $map->addEntries($entries);
  88 
  89     $n_time_slots = self::getNTimeSlots() - $skipped_slots;
  90     $morning_slot_seconds = ((($morningstarts * 60) + $morningstarts_minutes) * 60) + ($skipped_slots * $resolution);
  91     $evening_slot_seconds = $morning_slot_seconds + (($n_time_slots - 1) * $resolution);
  92 
  93     // TABLE HEADER
  94     $thead = '<thead';
  95 
  96     $slots = $this->getSlots($this->month, $this->day, $this->year);
  97     if (isset($slots))
  98     {
  99       // Remove the skipped slots from the start of the first day's array
 100       for ($i=0; $i<$skipped_slots; $i++)
 101       {
 102         array_shift($slots[0]);
 103       }
 104       // Add some data to enable the JavaScript to draw the timeline
 105       $thead .= ' data-slots="' . escape_html(json_encode($slots)) . '"';
 106       $thead .= ' data-timeline-vertical="' . (($times_along_top) ? 'true' : 'false') . '"';
 107       $thead .= ' data-timeline-full="true"';
 108     }
 109 
 110     $thead .= ">\n";
 111 
 112     $header_inner = "<tr>\n";
 113 
 114     if ($times_along_top)
 115     {
 116       $tag = 'room';
 117     }
 118     elseif ($enable_periods)
 119     {
 120       $tag = 'period';
 121     }
 122     else
 123     {
 124       $tag = 'time';
 125     }
 126 
 127     $first_last_html = '<th class="first_last">' . get_vocab($tag) . "</th>\n";
 128     $header_inner .= $first_last_html;
 129 
 130     // We can display the table in two ways
 131     if ($times_along_top)
 132     {
 133       $header_inner .= $this->theadThTimeCellsHTML($morning_slot_seconds, $evening_slot_seconds, $resolution);
 134     }
 135     else
 136     {
 137       $vars = [
 138         'view'     => 'week',
 139         'view_all' => 0,
 140         'year'     => $this->year,
 141         'month'    => $this->month,
 142         'day'      => $this->day,
 143         'area'     => $this->area_id
 144       ];
 145 
 146       $header_inner .= $this->roomsHeaderCellsHTML($rooms, $vars);
 147     }  // end standard view (for the header)
 148 
 149     // next: line to display times on right side
 150     if ($row_labels_both_sides)
 151     {
 152       $header_inner .= $first_last_html;
 153     }
 154 
 155     $header_inner .= "</tr>\n";
 156     $thead .= $header_inner;
 157     $thead .= "</thead>\n";
 158 
 159     // Now repeat the header in a footer if required
 160     $tfoot = ($column_labels_both_ends) ? "<tfoot>\n$header_inner</tfoot>\n" : '';
 161 
 162     // TABLE BODY LISTING BOOKINGS
 163     $tbody = "<tbody>\n";
 164 
 165     // This is the main bit of the display
 166     // We loop through time and then the rooms we just got
 167 
 168     // if the today is a day which includes a DST change then use
 169     // the day after to generate timesteps through the day as this
 170     // will ensure a constant time step
 171 
 172     // We can display the table in two ways
 173     if ($times_along_top)
 174     {
 175       // with times along the top and rooms down the side
 176       foreach ($rooms as $room)
 177       {
 178         $tbody .= "<tr>\n";
 179 
 180         $vars = array('view'     => 'week',
 181           'view_all' => 0,
 182           'year'     => $this->year,
 183           'month'    => $this->month,
 184           'day'      => $this->day,
 185           'area'     => $this->area_id,
 186           'room'     => $room['id']);
 187 
 188         $row_label = $this->roomCellHTML($room, $vars);
 189         $tbody .= $row_label;
 190         $is_invalid = array();
 191         for ($s = $morning_slot_seconds;
 192              $s <= $evening_slot_seconds;
 193              $s += $resolution)
 194         {
 195           // Work out whether this timeslot is invalid and save the result, so that we
 196           // don't have to repeat the calculation for every room
 197           if (!isset($is_invalid[$s]))
 198           {
 199             $is_invalid[$s] = $is_possibly_invalid && is_invalid_datetime(0, 0, $s, $this->month, $this->day, $this->year);
 200           }
 201           // set up the query vars to be used for the link in the cell
 202           $query_vars = $this->getQueryVars($room['id'], $this->month, $this->day, $this->year, $s);
 203 
 204           // and then draw the cell
 205           $tbody .= $this->tdHTML($map->slot($room['id'], 0, $s), $query_vars, $is_invalid[$s]);
 206         }  // end for (looping through the times)
 207         if ($row_labels_both_sides)
 208         {
 209           $tbody .= $row_label;
 210         }
 211         $tbody .= "</tr>\n";
 212       }  // end for (looping through the rooms)
 213     }  // end "times_along_top" view (for the body)
 214 
 215     else
 216     {
 217       // the standard view, with rooms along the top and times down the side
 218       for ($s = $morning_slot_seconds;
 219            $s <= $evening_slot_seconds;
 220            $s += $resolution)
 221       {
 222         // Show the time linked to the URL for highlighting that time
 223         $classes = array();
 224 
 225         $vars = array(
 226           'view' => 'day',
 227           'year' => $this->year,
 228           'month' => $this->month,
 229           'day' => $this->day,
 230           'area' => $this->area_id
 231         );
 232 
 233         if (isset($this->room_id))
 234         {
 235           $vars['room'] = $this->room_id;
 236         }
 237 
 238         if (isset($this->timetohighlight) && ($s == $this->timetohighlight))
 239         {
 240           $classes[] = 'row_highlight';
 241         }
 242         else
 243         {
 244           $vars['timetohighlight'] = $s;
 245         }
 246 
 247         $url = "index.php?" . http_build_query($vars, '', '&');
 248         $url = multisite($url);
 249 
 250         $tbody .= '<tr';
 251         if (!empty($classes))
 252         {
 253           $tbody .= ' class="' . implode(' ', $classes) . '"';
 254         }
 255         $tbody .= ">\n";
 256 
 257         $tbody .= $this->tbodyThTimeCellHTML($s, $url);
 258         $is_invalid = $is_possibly_invalid && is_invalid_datetime(0, 0, $s, $this->month, $this->day, $this->year);
 259         // Loop through the list of rooms we have for this area
 260         foreach ($rooms as $room)
 261         {
 262           // set up the query vars to be used for the link in the cell
 263           $query_vars = $this->getQueryVars($room['id'], $this->month, $this->day, $this->year, $s);
 264           $tbody .= $this->tdHTML($map->slot($room['id'], 0, $s), $query_vars, $is_invalid);
 265         }
 266 
 267         // next lines to display times on right side
 268         if ($row_labels_both_sides)
 269         {
 270           $tbody .= $this->tbodyThTimeCellHTML($s, $url);
 271         }
 272 
 273         $tbody .= "</tr>\n";
 274       }
 275     }  // end standard view (for the body)
 276 
 277     $tbody .= "</tbody>\n";
 278 
 279     return $thead . $tfoot . $tbody;
 280   }
 281 
 282 
 283   private function roomsHeaderCellsHTML(array $rooms, array $vars) : string
 284   {
 285     $html = '';
 286 
 287     foreach($rooms as $room)
 288     {
 289       $vars['room'] = $room['id'];
 290       $html .= $this->roomCellHTML($room, $vars);
 291     }
 292 
 293     return $html;
 294   }

   1 <?php
   2 declare(strict_types=1);
   3 namespace MRBS;
   4 
   5 use ReflectionClass;
   6 
   7 
   8 class Column
   9 {
  10   const NATURE_BINARY = 0;
  11   const NATURE_BOOLEAN = 1;
  12   const NATURE_CHARACTER = 2;
  13   const NATURE_DECIMAL = 3;
  14   const NATURE_INTEGER = 4;
  15   const NATURE_JSON = 5;
  16   const NATURE_REAL = 6;
  17   const NATURE_TIME = 7;
  18   const NATURE_TIMESTAMP = 8;
  19 
  20   public $table;
  21   public $name;
  22 
  23   private $default;
  24   private $is_nullable;
  25   private $length;
  26   private $nature;
  27   private $type;
  28 
  29 
  30   public function __construct(string $table, string $name)
  31   {
  32     $this->table = $table;
  33     $this->name = $name;
  34   }
  35 
  36 
  37   public function getDefault()
  38   {
  39     return $this->default;
  40   }
  41 
  42 
  43   public function setDefault($default) : void
  44   {
  45     $this->default = $default;
  46   }
  47 
  48 
  49   public function getIsNullable() : bool
  50   {
  51     return $this->is_nullable;
  52   }
  53 
  54 
  55   public function setIsNullable(bool $is_nullable) : void
  56   {
  57     $this->is_nullable = $is_nullable;
  58   }
  59 
  60 
  61   // Returns the column length.  Can be null|int|string
  62   // For example a DECIMAL might return "5,2".
  63   public function getLength()
  64   {
  65     return $this->length;
  66   }
  67 
  68 
  69   // $length can be null|int|string
  70   public function setLength($length) : void
  71   {
  72     $this->length = $length;
  73   }
  74 
  75 
  76   public function getNature() : int
  77   {
  78     return $this->nature;
  79   }
  80 
  81 
  82   public function setNature(int $nature) : void
  83   {
  84     $reflectionClass = new ReflectionClass($this);
  85     $constants = $reflectionClass->getConstants();
  86     if (!in_array($nature, array_values($constants), true))
  87     {
  88       throw new \Exception("Invalid nature '$nature'");
  89     }
  90     $this->nature = $nature;
  91   }
  92 
  93 
  94   public function getType() : ?string
  95   {
  96     return $this->type;
  97   }
  98 
  99 
 100   public function setType(string $type) : void
 101   {
 102     $this->type = $type;
 103   }
 104 
 105   // Gets the type ('bool', 'decimal', 'float', 'int' or 'string') to be used with get_form_var().
 106   // TODO: this method maybe doesn't belong here.
 107   public function getFormVarType() : string
 108   {
 109     switch ($this->nature)
 110     {
 111       case self::NATURE_CHARACTER:
 112         $var_type = 'string';
 113         break;
 114       case self::NATURE_DECIMAL:
 115         $var_type = 'decimal';
 116         break;
 117       case self::NATURE_INTEGER:
 118         $var_type = ($this->isBooleanLike()) ? 'bool' : 'int';
 119         break;
 120       case self::NATURE_REAL:
 121         $var_type = 'float';
 122         break;
 123       // We can only really deal with the types above at the moment
 124       default:
 125         $var_type = 'string';
 126         break;
 127     }
 128 
 129     return $var_type;
 130   }
 131 
 132 
 133   // Sanitize a value ready for insertion in the database
 134   public function sanitizeValue($value)
 135   {
 136     // Turn the booleans into 0/1 values (necessary for PostgreSQL)
 137     if (is_bool($value))
 138     {
 139       $value = ($value) ? 1 : 0;
 140     }
 141     // Trim the strings and truncate them to the maximum field length
 142     // (necessary for PostgreSQL which doesn't truncate them itself
 143     // but instead will throw an error)
 144     elseif (is_string($value))
 145     {
 146       // Some variables, eg decimals, will also be PHP strings, so only
 147       // trim columns with a database nature of 'character'.
 148       if ($this->nature === Column::NATURE_CHARACTER)
 149       {
 150         $value = trim($value);
 151         $value = $this->truncate($value);
 152       }
 153     }
 154 
 155     return $value;
 156   }
 157 
 158   public function isBooleanLike() : bool
 159   {
 160     // Smallints and tinyints are considered to be booleans
 161     return (($this->nature == self::NATURE_BOOLEAN) ||
 162             (($this->nature == self::NATURE_INTEGER) &&
 163              (isset($this->length) && ($this->length <= 2))));
 164   }
 165 
 166 
 167   // Truncate any fields that have a maximum length as a precaution.
 168   // Although the MAXLENGTH attribute may be used in the <input> tag, this can
 169   // sometimes be ignored by the browser, for example by Firefox when
 170   // autocompletion is used.  The user could also edit the HTML and remove
 171   // the MAXLENGTH attribute.    Another problem is that the <datalist> tag
 172   // does not accept a maxlength attribute.  Passing an oversize string to some
 173   // databases (eg some versions of PostgreSQL) results in an SQL error,
 174   // rather than silent truncation of the string.
 175   //
 176   // We truncate to a maximum number of UTF8 characters rather than bytes.
 177   // This is OK in current versions of MySQL and PostgreSQL, though in earlier
 178   // versions of MySQL (I haven't checked PostgreSQL) this could cause problems
 179   // as a VARCHAR(n) was n bytes long rather than n characters.
 180   private function truncate($value)
 181   {
 182     $result = $value;
 183 
 184     if (($this->nature == self::NATURE_CHARACTER) &&
 185         isset($this->length) &&
 186         ($this->length < 256))
 187     {
 188       $result = mb_substr($value, 0, intval($this->length));
 189     }
 190 
 191     return $result;
 192   }
 193 }

   1 <?php
   2 declare(strict_types=1);
   3 namespace MRBS;
   4 
   5 use Countable;
   6 use Iterator;
   7 
   8 // Holds information about table columns
   9 // Implemented as a singleton class for performance reasons: it is
  10 // expensive getting the field info in the constructor.
  11 class Columns implements Countable, Iterator
  12 {
  13 
  14   private static $instances = array();
  15   private $data;
  16   private $index = 0;
  17   private $table_name;
  18 
  19 
  20   private function __construct($table_name)
  21   {
  22     assert(version_compare(MRBS_MIN_PHP_VERSION, '7.4.0', '<'), "The __wakeup() method is now redundant.");
  23     $this->table_name = $table_name;
  24     // Get the column info
  25     $this->data = db()->field_info($table_name);
  26   }
  27 
  28 
  29   private function __clone()
  30   {
  31   }
  32 
  33 
  34   public function __unserialize(array $data) : void
  35   {
  36     // __unserialize() must have public visibility
  37     throw new \Exception("Cannot unserialize a singleton.");
  38   }
  39 
  40 
  41   // __wakeup() is deprecated from PHP 8.5.
  42   // "The __wakeup() serialization magic method has been deprecated. Implement __unserialize()
  43   // instead (or in addition, if support for old PHP versions is necessary)".
  44   // __unserialize() is only available from PHP 7.4.0
  45   public function __wakeup()
  46   {
  47     // __wakeup() must have public visibility
  48     throw new \Exception("Cannot unserialize a singleton.");
  49   }
  50 
  51 
  52   public static function getInstance(string $table_name) : Columns
  53   {
  54     if (!isset(self::$instances[$table_name]))
  55     {
  56       self::$instances[$table_name] = new self($table_name);
  57     }
  58 
  59     return self::$instances[$table_name];
  60   }
  61 
  62 
  63   public function getNames() : array
  64   {
  65     $result = array();
  66 
  67     foreach ($this as $column)
  68     {
  69       $result[] = $column->name;
  70     }
  71 
  72     return $result;
  73   }
  74 
  75 
  76   public function hasIdColumn() : bool
  77   {
  78     $column = $this->getColumnByName('id');
  79     return isset($column);
  80   }
  81 
  82 
  83   public function getColumnByName(string $name) : ?Column
  84   {
  85     foreach ($this as $column)
  86     {
  87       if ($column->name == $name)
  88       {
  89         return $column;
  90       }
  91     }
  92 
  93     return null;
  94   }
  95 
  96 
  97   public function current() : Column
  98   {
  99     $info = $this->data[$this->index];
 100     $column = new Column($this->table_name, $info['name']);
 101     $column->setLength($info['length']);
 102     $column->setDefault($info['default']);
 103     $column->setIsNullable($info['is_nullable']);
 104     $column->setType($info['type']);
 105 
 106     switch ($info['nature'])
 107     {
 108       case 'binary':
 109         $column->setNature(Column::NATURE_BINARY);
 110         break;
 111       case 'boolean':
 112         $column->setNature(Column::NATURE_BOOLEAN);
 113         break;
 114       case 'character':
 115         $column->setNature(Column::NATURE_CHARACTER);
 116         break;
 117       case 'decimal':
 118         $column->setNature(Column::NATURE_DECIMAL);
 119         break;
 120       case 'integer':
 121         $column->setNature(Column::NATURE_INTEGER);
 122         break;
 123       case 'json':
 124         $column->setNature(Column::NATURE_JSON);
 125         break;
 126       case 'real':
 127         $column->setNature(Column::NATURE_REAL);
 128         break;
 129       case 'timestamp':
 130         $column->setNature(Column::NATURE_TIMESTAMP);
 131         break;
 132       default:
 133         throw new \Exception("Unknown nature '" . $info['nature'] . "'");
 134         break;
 135     }
 136 
 137     return $column;
 138   }
 139 
 140 
 141   public function next() : void
 142   {
 143     $this->index++;
 144   }
 145 
 146   public function key() : int
 147   {
 148     return $this->index;
 149   }
 150 
 151 
 152   public function valid() : bool
 153   {
 154     return isset($this->data[$this->key()]);
 155   }
 156 
 157 
 158   public function rewind() : void
 159   {
 160     $this->index = 0;
 161   }
 162 
 163 
 164   public function count() : int
 165   {
 166     return count($this->data);
 167   }
 168 }

   1 <?php
   2 declare(strict_types=1);
   3 namespace MRBS\DB;
   4 
   5 use MRBS\Column;
   6 use MRBS\Columns;
   7 use MRBS\Exception;
   8 use PDO;
   9 use PDOException;
  10 use Throwable;
  11 use function MRBS\mrbs_ignore_user_abort;
  12 
  13 
  14 abstract class DB
  15 {
  16   const DB_SCHEMA_VERSION = 82;
  17   const DB_SCHEMA_VERSION_LOCAL = 1;
  18 
  19   const DB_DEFAULT_PORT = null;
  20   const DB_DBO_DRIVER = null;
  21   const DB_CHARSET = 'UTF8';
  22 
  23   protected $dbh = null;
  24   protected $mutex_locks = array();
  25   protected $version_string = null;
  26 
  27 
  28   // The SensitiveParameter attribute needs to be on a separate line for PHP 7.
  29   // The attribute is only recognised by PHP 8.2 and later.
  30   abstract public function __construct(
  31     string $db_host,
  32     #[\SensitiveParameter]
  33     string $db_username,
  34     #[\SensitiveParameter]
  35     string $db_password,
  36     #[\SensitiveParameter]
  37     string $db_name,
  38     bool   $persist = false,
  39     ?int   $db_port = null,
  40     array  $db_options = []
  41   );
  42 
  43 
  44   // Destructor cleans up the connection if there is one
  45   public function __destruct()
  46   {
  47     try {
  48       // Release any forgotten locks
  49       $this->mutex_unlock_all();
  50 
  51       // Rollback any outstanding transactions
  52       $this->rollback();
  53     }
  54     catch (Throwable $e) {
  55       // Don't do anything, except raise an error.  This is the destructor and if we get an
  56       // exception or error it's probably because the connection has been lost or timed out,
  57       // in which case the locks will have been released and the transaction rolled back anyway.
  58       trigger_error($e->getMessage(), E_USER_NOTICE);
  59     }
  60   }
  61 
  62 
  63   // Build a DSN.
  64   // The SensitiveParameter attribute needs to be on a separate line for PHP 7.
  65   // The attribute is only recognised by PHP 8.2 and later.
  66   public static function dsn(
  67     string $db_host,
  68     #[\SensitiveParameter]
  69     string $db_name,
  70     ?int   $db_port = null
  71   ) : string
  72   {
  73     // Early error handling
  74     if (is_null(static::DB_DBO_DRIVER) ||
  75         is_null(static::DB_DEFAULT_PORT)) {
  76       throw new Exception("Encountered a fatal bug in DB abstraction code!");
  77     }
  78 
  79     // Prefix
  80     $result = static::DB_DBO_DRIVER . ':';
  81 
  82     // Host
  83     if ($db_host !== '') {
  84       $result .= 'host=' . $db_host . ';';
  85     }
  86 
  87     // Port
  88     if (empty($db_port)) {
  89       $db_port = static::DB_DEFAULT_PORT;
  90     }
  91     $result .= 'port=' . $db_port . ';';
  92 
  93     // Database name
  94     $result .= 'dbname=' . $db_name;
  95 
  96     return $result;
  97   }
  98 
  99 
 100   // The SensitiveParameter attribute needs to be on a separate line for PHP 7.
 101   // The attribute is only recognised by PHP 8.2 and later.
 102   // $driver_options is an optional array of options that supplements/overrides the
 103   // default options.
 104   protected function connect(
 105     string $db_host,
 106     #[\SensitiveParameter]
 107     string $db_username,
 108     #[\SensitiveParameter]
 109     string $db_password,
 110     #[\SensitiveParameter]
 111     string $db_name,
 112     bool   $persist = false,
 113     ?int   $db_port = null,
 114     ?array $driver_options = null
 115   ): void
 116   {
 117     // Establish a database connection.
 118     $default_options = array(
 119       PDO::ATTR_PERSISTENT => $persist,
 120       PDO::ATTR_ERRMODE => PDO::ERRMODE_EXCEPTION
 121     );
 122     // The LHS of the array + operator overrides the RHS if the keys are the same
 123     $options = (empty($driver_options)) ? $default_options : $driver_options + $default_options;
 124 
 125     $this->dbh = new PDO(
 126       static::dsn($db_host, $db_name, $db_port),
 127       $db_username,
 128       $db_password,
 129       $options
 130     );
 131     $this->command("SET NAMES '" . static::DB_CHARSET . "'");
 132   }
 133

 135   //
 136   public function error(): string
 137   {
 138     $error = "No database connection!";
 139 
 140     if ($this->dbh) {
 141       $error_info = $this->dbh->errorInfo();
 142       $error = $error_info[2];
 143     }
 144     return $error;
 145   }

 148   public function getAttribute(int $attribute)

 151   }

 154   // Execute a non-SELECT SQL command (insert/update/delete).
 155   // Returns the number of tuples matched (whether affected or not) if OK (a number >= 0).
 156   // Throws a DBException on error.
 157   public function command(string $sql, array $params = array()): int
 158   {
 159     try {
 160       $sth = $this->dbh->prepare($sql);
 161       $sth->execute($params);
 162     } catch (PDOException $e) {
 163       throw new DBException($e->getMessage(), 0, $e, $sql, $params);
 164     }
 165 
 166     return $sth->rowCount();
 167   }

 170   // Execute an SQL query which should return a single non-negative integer value.
 171   // This is a lightweight alternative to query(), good for use with count(*)
 172   // and similar queries.
 173   // It returns -1 if the query returns no result, or a single NULL value, such as from
 174   // a MIN or MAX aggregate function applied over no rows.
 175   // Throws a DBException on error.
 176   public function query1(string $sql, array $params = array()) : int
 177   {
 178     $result = $this->query_scalar_non_bool($sql, $params);
 179 
 180     if (is_null($result) || ($result === false))
 181     {
 182       return -1;
 183     }
 184 
 185     // Check that the result looks like an integer, even though it may be a string, and then cast
 186     // it to an integer.  For example "2" is OK, but "2.0" is not.
 187     $result = filter_var($result, FILTER_VALIDATE_INT);
 188 
 189     if ($result === false)
 190     {
 191       throw new \UnexpectedValueException("query1() should only be used for selecting integer values.");
 192     }
 193 
 194     return $result;
 195   }
 196 
 197 
 198   // Execute an SQL query which should return a single scalar value that can be anything
 199   // other than a boolean (because the function returns FALSE if there is no value).
 200   public function query_scalar_non_bool(string $sql, array $params = array())
 201   {
 202     try
 203     {
 204       $sth = $this->dbh->prepare($sql);
 205       $sth->execute($params);
 206       return $sth->fetchColumn();
 207     }
 208     catch (PDOException $e)
 209     {
 210       throw new DBException($e->getMessage(), 0, $e, $sql, $params);
 211     }
 212   }
 213 
 214 
 215   // Run an SQL query that returns a simple one dimensional array of results.
 216   // The SQL query must select only one column.   Returns an empty array if
 217   // no results; throws a DBException if there's an error
 218   public function query_array(string $sql, array $params = array()): array
 219   {
 220     $stmt = $this->query($sql, $params);
 221 
 222     $result = array();
 223 
 224     while (false !== ($row = $stmt->next_row())) {
 225       $result[] = $row[0];
 226     }
 227 
 228     return $result;
 229   }

 232   // Execute an SQL query. Returns a DBStatement object, a class with a number
 233   // of methods like row() and row_keyed() to get the results.
 234   // Throws a DBException on error
 235   public function query(string $sql, array $params = array()): DBStatement
 236   {
 237     try {
 238       $sth = $this->dbh->prepare($sql);
 239       $sth->execute($params);
 240     } catch (PDOException $e) {
 241       throw new DBException($e->getMessage(), 0, $e, $sql, $params);
 242     }
 243 
 244     return new DBStatement($this, $sth);
 245   }

 248   //
 249   public function begin(): void
 250   {
 251     // Turn off ignore_user_abort until the transaction has been committed or rolled back.
 252     // See the warning at http://php.net/manual/en/features.persistent-connections.php
 253     // (Only applies to persistent connections, but we'll do it for all cases to keep
 254     // things simple)
 255     mrbs_ignore_user_abort(TRUE);
 256     if (!$this->dbh->inTransaction()) {
 257       $this->dbh->beginTransaction();
 258     }
 259   }
 260 
 261 
 262   // Commit (end) a transaction. See begin().
 263   public function commit(): void
 264   {
 265     if ($this->dbh->inTransaction()) {
 266       $this->dbh->commit();
 267     }
 268     mrbs_ignore_user_abort(FALSE);
 269   }
 270 
 271 
 272   // Roll back a transaction, aborting it. See begin().
 273   public function rollback(): void
 274   {
 275     if ($this->dbh && $this->dbh->inTransaction()) {
 276       $this->dbh->rollBack();
 277     }
 278     mrbs_ignore_user_abort(FALSE);
 279   }

 282   // Checks if inside a transaction
 283   public function inTransaction(): bool
 284   {
 285     return $this->dbh->inTransaction();
 286   }

 289   // Dies with a message that the database version is lower than the minimum required
 290   protected function versionDie(string $database, string $this_version, string $min_version): void
 291   {

 298   // Returns the version string, eg "8.0.28",
 299   // "10.3.36-MariaDB-log-cll-lve" or
 300   // "PostgreSQL 14.2, compiled by Visual C++ build 1914, 64-bit".
 301   protected function versionString(): string
 302   {
 303     if (!isset($this->version_string)) {
 304       // Don't use getAttribute(PDO::ATTR_SERVER_VERSION) because that will
 305       // sometimes also give you the version prefix (so-called "replication
 306       // version hack") with MariaDB.
 307       $result = $this->query_scalar_non_bool("SELECT VERSION()");
 308 
 309       $this->version_string = ($result === false) ? '' : $result;
 310     }
 311 
 312     return $this->version_string;
 313   }

 316   // Replaces the keys in the array $array according to $key_map.  Elements with
 317   // value NULL are dropped.
 318   protected static function replaceOptionKeys(array $array, array $key_map): array
 319   {
 320     $result = array();
 321 
 322     foreach ($array as $key => $value) {
 323       if (isset($value)) {
 324         if (array_key_exists($key, $key_map)) {
 325           $result[$key_map[$key]] = $value;
 326         }
 327         else {
 328           trigger_error("Unsupported database driver option '$key'");
 329         }
 330       }
 331     }
 332 
 333     return $result;
 334   }

 337   // Return a boolean depending on whether $field exists in $table

 350   // Checks whether a table has duplicate values for a field
 351   public function tableHasDuplicates(string $table, string $field): bool
 352   {
 353     $sql = "SELECT $field, COUNT(*)
 354               FROM $table
 355           GROUP BY $field
 356             HAVING COUNT(*) > 1";
 357     $res = $this->query($sql);

 435   // Returns the syntax for a column being in a list of values
 436   public function syntax_in_list(string $column_name, array $list, array &$params) : string
 437   {

 439     if (count($list) === 0)
 440     {
 441       return 'FALSE';

 444     $params = array_merge($params, $list);

 446     return $this->quote($column_name) . " IN (" . implode(',', array_fill(0, count($list), '?')) . ")";

 458   // Returns the syntax for an "upsert" query.  Unfortunately getting the id of the
 459   // last row differs between MySQL and PostgreSQL.   In PostgreSQL the query will
 460   // return a row with the id in the 'id' column.  However there isn't a corresponding
 461   // way of doing this in MySQL, but db()->insert_id() will work, regardless of whether
 462   // an insert or update was performed.
 463   //
 464   //  $conflict_keys     the key(s) which is/are unique; can be a scalar or an array
 465   //  $assignments       an array of assignments for the UPDATE clause
 466   //  $has_id_column     whether the table has an id column
 467   abstract public function syntax_on_duplicate_key_update(
 468     $conflict_keys,
 469     array $assignments,
 470     bool $has_id_column=false
 471   ) : string;

 474   // Determines whether the driver returns native types (eg a PHP int

 481   // Returns the syntax for an "upsert" query.  Unfortunately getting the id of the
 482   // last row differs between MySQL and PostgreSQL.   In PostgreSQL the query will
 483   // return a row with the id in the 'id' column.  However there isn't a corresponding
 484   // way of doing this in MySQL, but db()->insert_id() will work, regardless of whether
 485   // an insert or update was performed.
 486   //
 487   //  $data             an associative array of values indexed by column name
 488   //  $table            the table to insert into or update
 489   //  &$params          an array which will hold the SQL params
 490   //  $conflict_keys    the key(s) which is/are unique; can be a scalar or an array
 491   //  $has_id_column    whether the table has an id column
 492   public function syntax_upsert(array $data, string $table, array &$params, $conflict_keys=[], array $ignore_columns=[], bool $has_id_column = false): string
 493   {
 494     if (is_scalar($conflict_keys))
 495     {
 496       $conflict_keys = array($conflict_keys);
 497     }
 498 
 499     list('columns' => $columns, 'values' => $values, 'sql_params' => $params) = $this->prepareData($data, $table, $ignore_columns);
 500     $quoted_columns = array_map(array(\MRBS\db(), 'quote'), $columns);
 501     $sql = "INSERT INTO " . $this->quote($table) . "
 502                         (" . implode(', ', $quoted_columns) . ")
 503                  VALUES (" . implode(', ', $values) . ") ";
 504 
 505     // Go through the columns we've just found and turn them into assignments
 506     // for the update part
 507     $assignments = array();
 508     for ($i=0; $i<count($columns); $i++)
 509     {
 510       $column = $columns[$i];
 511       $value = $values[$i];
 512       $assignments[] = $this->quote($column) . "=$value";
 513     }
 514 
 515     $sql .= \MRBS\db()->syntax_on_duplicate_key_update(
 516       $conflict_keys,
 517       $assignments,
 518       $has_id_column
 519     );
 520 
 521     return $sql;
 522   }
 523 
 524 
 525   // Prepares $data for an SQL query. If $table is given then it will also sanitize values,
 526   // eg by trimming and truncating strings and converting booleans into 0/1.
 527   private function prepareData(array $data, ?string $table=null, array $ignore_columns=[]): array
 528   {
 529     $columns = array();
 530     $values = array();
 531     $sql_params = array();
 532 
 533     $cols = (isset($table)) ? Columns::getInstance($table) : array_keys($data);
 534 
 535     $i = 0;
 536     foreach ($cols as $col)
 537     {
 538       // We are only interested in those elements of $data that have a corresponding
 539       // column in the table - except for those that we have been told to ignore.
 540       // Examples might be 'id' which normally auto-increments, and 'timestamp' which
 541       // normally auto-updates.
 542       if (is_object($col) && in_array($col->name, $ignore_columns))
 543       {
 544         continue;
 545       }
 546 
 547       $column_name = (is_object($col)) ? $col->name : $col;
 548       $columns[] = $column_name;
 549 
 550       if (!isset($data[$column_name]) && (!is_object($col) || $col->getIsNullable()))
 551       {
 552         $values[] = 'NULL';
 553       }
 554       else
 555       {
 556         // Need to make sure the placeholder only uses allowed characters which are
 557         // [a-zA-Z0-9_].   We can't use the column name because the column name might
 558         // contain characters which are not allowed.   And we can't use '?' because
 559         // we may want to use the placeholders twice, once for an insert and once for an
 560         // update.  Besides, debugging is easier with named parameters.
 561         $named_parameter = ":p$i";
 562         $values[] = $named_parameter;
 563         if (isset($data[$column_name]))
 564         {
 565           $sql_param = $data[$column_name];
 566           if (is_object($col))
 567           {
 568             // NB MariaDB doesn't support the JSON data type.  It treats it as an
 569             // alias of LONG TEXT.
 570             if ($col->getNature() === Column::NATURE_JSON)
 571             {
 572               if (!is_string($sql_param) || !json_validate($sql_param))
 573               {
 574                 throw new Exception('Invalid JSON string');
 575               }
 576             }
 577             else
 578             {
 579               $sql_param = $col->sanitizeValue($sql_param);
 580             }
 581           }
 582         }
 583         else
 584         {
 585           // The column is not nullable and $col is an object if we got here
 586           $sql_param = $col->getDefault();
 587         }
 588         $sql_params[$named_parameter] = $sql_param;
 589         $i++;
 590       }
 591     }
 592 
 593     return array(
 594       'columns' => $columns,
 595       'values' => $values,
 596       'sql_params' => $sql_params
 597     );
 598   }
 599 
 600 }

   1 <?php
   2 declare(strict_types=1);
   3 namespace MRBS\DB;
   4 
   5 
   6 // A helper class to build a DB object, dependent on the database type required
   7 use Throwable;
   8 
   9 class DBFactory
  10 {
  11   // The SensitiveParameter attribute needs to be on a separate line for PHP 7.
  12   // The attribute is only recognised by PHP 8.2 and later.
  13   public static function create(
  14     string $db_system,
  15     string $db_host,
  16     #[\SensitiveParameter]
  17     string $db_username,
  18     #[\SensitiveParameter]
  19     string $db_password,
  20     #[\SensitiveParameter]
  21     string $db_name,
  22     bool $persist=false,
  23     ?int $db_port=null,
  24     array $db_options=[]) : DB
  25   {
  26     self::checkExtensionEnabled($db_system);
  27     $class_name = self::getClassName($db_system);
  28     return new $class_name($db_host, $db_username, $db_password, $db_name, $persist, $db_port, $db_options);
  29   }
  30 
  31 
  32   public static function createDsn(
  33     string $db_system,
  34     string $db_host,
  35     #[\SensitiveParameter]
  36     string $db_name,
  37     ?int   $db_port = null
  38   ) : string
  39   {
  40     $class_name = self::getClassName($db_system);
  41     return $class_name::dsn($db_host, $db_name, $db_port);
  42   }
  43 
  44 
  45   // Check that the appropriate PDO extension is enabled.  This can't always be
  46   // done in the constructor of the class itself because the class can refer to a
  47   // driver-specific constant.
  48   private static function checkExtensionEnabled(string $db_system) : void
  49   {
  50     // Check for the existence of a driver-specific constant
  51     switch ($db_system)
  52     {
  53       case 'mysql':
  54       case 'mysqli':
  55         $constant_name = 'Pdo\Mysql::ATTR_FOUND_ROWS';
  56         $extension = 'pdo_mysql';
  57         break;
  58 
  59       case 'pgsql':
  60         $constant_name = 'Pdo\Pgsql::ATTR_DISABLE_PREPARES';
  61         $extension = 'pdo_pgsql';
  62         break;
  63 
  64       default:
  65         return;
  66     }
  67 
  68     // We have to test for the constant in a try/catch block, because if we are using the Pdo\Mysql or
  69     // Pdo\Pgsql emulations (ie we are not running PHP 8.4 or later) then the emulations will throw
  70     // an error.
  71     try
  72     {
  73       if (!defined($constant_name))
  74       {
  75         throw new Exception("Undefined constant $constant_name.");
  76       }
  77     }
  78     catch (Throwable $e)
  79     {
  80       $message = "Undefined constant $constant_name.  Check that the $extension extension is enabled " .
  81         "in your php.ini file.";
  82       throw new Exception($message);
  83     }
  84 
  85   }
  86 
  87   private static function getClassName(string $db_system) : string
  88   {
  89     switch ($db_system)
  90     {
  91       case 'mysql':
  92       case 'mysqli':
  93         $class_name = 'DB_mysql';
  94         break;
  95 
  96       case 'pgsql':
  97         $class_name = 'DB_pgsql';
  98         break;
  99 
 100       default:
 101         throw new Exception("Unsupported database driver '$db_system'");
 102         break;
 103     }
 104 
 105     return __NAMESPACE__ . '\\' . $class_name;
 106   }
 107 
 108 }

   2 declare(strict_types=1);
   3 namespace MRBS\DB;
   4 
   5 use PDO;
   6 use PDOStatement;
   7 
   8 
   9 //
  10 class DBStatement
  11 {
  12   protected $db_object = null;
  13   protected $statement = null;
  14 
  15   //
  16   public function __construct(DB $db_obj, PDOStatement $sth)
  17   {
  18     $this->db_object = $db_obj;
  19     $this->statement = $sth;
  20   }
  21 
  22 
  23   // Returns the next row from a statement.
  24   // The row is returned as an array with index 0=first column, etc.
  25   // Returns FALSE if there are no more rows.
  26   public function next_row()
  27   {
  28     return $this->statement->fetch(PDO::FETCH_NUM);
  29   }
  30 
  31 
  32   // Return a row from a statement as an associative array keyed by field name.
  33   // Returns FALSE if there are no more rows.
  34   public function next_row_keyed()
  35   {
  36     return $this->statement->fetch(PDO::FETCH_ASSOC);
  37   }
  38 
  39 
  40   // Return all the rows from a statement object, as an array of arrays
  41   // keyed on the column name
  42   public function all_rows_keyed() : array
  43   {
  44     $result = array();
  45 
  46     while (false !== ($row = $this->next_row_keyed()))
  47     {
  48       $result[] = $row;
  49     }
  50 
  51     return $result;
  52   }
  53 
  54   // Return the number of rows returned by a statement from query().
  55   public function count() : int
  56   {
  57     return $this->statement->rowCount();
  58   }
  59 
  60   // Returns the number of fields in a statement.
  61   public function num_fields() : int
  62   {
  63     return $this->statement->columnCount();
  64   }

   2 declare(strict_types=1);
   3 namespace MRBS\DB;
   4 
   5 use Error;
   6 use MRBS\Errors\Errors;
   7 use PDO;
   8 use Pdo\Mysql;
   9 use PDOException;
  10 use function MRBS\get_vocab;
  11 
  12 //
  13 class DB_mysql extends DB
  14 {
  15   const DB_DEFAULT_PORT = 3306;
  16   const DB_DBO_DRIVER = "mysql";
  17   const DB_CHARSET = "utf8mb4";
  18 
  19   const DB_MARIADB = 0;
  20   const DB_MYSQL   = 1;
  21   const DB_PERCONA = 2;
  22   const DB_OTHER   = 3;
  23 
  24   // For a full list of error codes see https://mariadb.com/kb/en/mariadb-error-codes/
  25   // (That page doesn't list codes only used by MySQL)
  26   const ER_CON_COUNT_ERROR            = 1040; // Too many connections
  27   const ER_TOO_MANY_USER_CONNECTIONS  = 1203; // User %s already has more than 'max_user_connections' active connections
  28   const ER_USER_LIMIT_REACHED         = 1226; // User '%s' has exceeded the '%s' resource (current value: %ld)
  29 
  30   private const OPTIONS = [
  31     Mysql::ATTR_FOUND_ROWS => true  // Return the number of found (matched) rows, not the number of changed rows.
  32   ];
  33 
  34   private const MIN_VERSIONS = array(
  35       self::DB_MARIADB => '5.5.3', // '10.0.2' recommended for multiple lock support
  36       self::DB_MYSQL   => '5.5.3', // '5.7.5' recommended for multiple lock support
  37       self::DB_PERCONA => '5.5.3'  // '5.7.5' recommended for multiple lock support
  38     );
  39 
  40   private const DB_NAMES = array(
  41     self::DB_MARIADB => 'MariaDB',
  42     self::DB_MYSQL   => 'MySQL',
  43     self::DB_PERCONA => 'Percona'
  44   );
  45 
  46   private $db_type = null;
  47   private $returns_native_types = null;
  48   private $supports_multiple_locks = null;
  49   private $version_comment = null;
  50 
  51   // The SensitiveParameter attribute needs to be on a separate line for PHP 7.
  52   // The attribute is only recognised by PHP 8.2 and later.
  53   public function __construct(
  54     string $db_host,
  55     #[\SensitiveParameter]
  56     string $db_username,
  57     #[\SensitiveParameter]
  58     string $db_password,
  59     #[\SensitiveParameter]
  60     string $db_name,
  61     bool $persist=false,
  62     ?int $db_port=null,
  63     array $db_options=[])
  64   {
  65     global $db_retries, $db_delay;
  66 
  67     $driver_options =  self::siteOptions() + self::OPTIONS;
  68 
  69     // We allow retries if the connection fails due to a resource constraint, possibly because
  70     // this database user already has max_user_connections open (through other instances of users
  71     // accessing MRBS) or other database users on the same server have reached the maximum number of
  72     // connections for the database.
  73     $attempts_left = max(1, $db_retries + 1);
  74 
  75     while ($attempts_left > 0)
  76     {
  77       try
  78       {
  79         $this->connect(
  80             $db_host,
  81             $db_username,
  82             $db_password,
  83             $db_name,
  84             $persist,
  85             $db_port,
  86             $driver_options
  87           );
  88         // Set $attempts_left to zero as we won't have got here if an exception has been thrown
  89         $attempts_left = 0;
  90         $this->checkVersion();
  91         // Turn off ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY mode (which is the default in MySQL 5.7.5 and later) to prevent SQL
  92         // errors of the type "Syntax error or access violation: 1055 'mrbs.E.start_time' isn't in GROUP BY".
  93         // TODO: However the proper solution is probably to rewrite the offending queries.
  94         $this->command("SET sql_mode=(SELECT REPLACE(@@sql_mode,'ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY',''))");
  95         // Set STRICT_TRANS_TABLES so that we can detect invalid values being inserted in the database
  96         $this->command("SET SESSION sql_mode = 'STRICT_TRANS_TABLES'");
  97       }
  98       catch (PDOException $e)
  99       {
 100         $code = $e->getCode();
 101         $message = $e->getMessage();
 102 
 103         if (in_array($code, array(
 104                 self::ER_CON_COUNT_ERROR,
 105                 self::ER_TOO_MANY_USER_CONNECTIONS,
 106                 self::ER_USER_LIMIT_REACHED
 107               )))
 108         {
 109           $attempts_left--;
 110         }
 111         else
 112         {
 113           // It's some kind of error other than a resource error, so retrying won't help
 114           $attempts_left = 0;
 115           if ($code == 2054) // The server requested authentication method unknown to the client [MySQL specific]
 116           {
 117             $message .= ".\n[MRBS note] It looks like you may have an old style MySQL password stored, which cannot be " .
 118                         "used with PDO (though it is possible that mysqli may have accepted it).  Try " .
 119                         "deleting the MySQL user and recreating it with the same password.";
 120           }
 121         }
 122 
 123         if ($attempts_left > 0)
 124         {
 125           trigger_error($message . ". Retrying ...", E_USER_NOTICE);
 126           usleep($db_delay * 1000);
 127         }
 128         else
 129         {
 130           throw new DBException($message);
 131         }
 132       }
 133     }
 134   }

 137   // Translates $db_options['mysql'] into an array of options indexed by their
 138   // PDO constants.
 139   // Note that we cannot declare a constant array to hold this mapping as not all
 140   // systems support all the PDO constants.
 141   private static function siteOptions() : array
 142   {
 143     global $db_options;
 144 
 145     $result = array();
 146 
 147     foreach ($db_options['mysql'] as $key => $value)
 148     {
 149       // Only try and set the option if we need to. Otherwise, we could trigger an
 150       // 'undefined class constant' error unnecessarily.
 151       if (isset($value))
 152       {
 153         try
 154         {
 155           switch ($key)
 156           {
 157             case 'ssl_ca':
 158               $index = Mysql::ATTR_SSL_CA;
 159               break;
 160             case 'ssl_capath':
 161               $index = Mysql::ATTR_SSL_CAPATH;
 162               break;
 163             case 'ssl_cert':
 164               $index = Mysql::ATTR_SSL_CERT;
 165               break;
 166             case 'ssl_cipher':
 167               $index = Mysql::ATTR_SSL_CIPHER;
 168               break;
 169             case 'ssl_key':
 170               $index = Mysql::ATTR_SSL_KEY;
 171               break;
 172             case 'ssl_verify_server_cert':
 173               $index = Mysql::ATTR_SSL_VERIFY_SERVER_CERT;
 174               break;
 175             default:
 176               $index = null;
 177               trigger_error("Unsupported option '$key'");
 178               break;
 179           }
 180           if (isset($index))
 181           {
 182             $result[$index] = $value;
 183           }
 184         }
 185         catch (Error $e)
 186         {
 187           $message = $e->getMessage() . ". Try using the 'nd_pdo_mysql' extension instead of 'pdo_mysql'.";
 188           trigger_error($message, E_USER_WARNING);
 189           Errors::fatalError(get_vocab("fatal_error"));
 190         }
 191       }
 192     }
 193 
 194     return $result;
 195   }

 198   // Quote a table or column name (which could be a qualified identifier, eg 'table.column')
 199   public function quote(string $identifier) : string
 200   {
 201     $quote_char = '`';
 202     $parts = explode('.', $identifier);
 203     return $quote_char . implode($quote_char . '.' . $quote_char, $parts) . $quote_char;
 204   }

 230   // Determines whether the driver returns native types (eg a PHP int
 231   // for an SQL INT).
 232   public function returnsNativeTypes() : bool
 233   {
 234     if (!isset($this->returns_native_types))
 235     {
 236       // MySQL will return native types if PDO::ATTR_STRINGIFY_FETCHES is false
 237       // and we're using a native driver and (the PHP version is at least 8.1 or
 238       // PDO::ATTR_EMULATE_PREPARES is false).
 239       // See https://stackoverflow.com/questions/1197005/how-to-get-numeric-types-from-mysql-using-pdo
 240       // and https://stackoverflow.com/questions/20079320/how-do-i-return-integer-and-numeric-columns-from-mysql-as-integers-and-numerics
 241       $this->returns_native_types =
 242         !$this->getStringifyFetches()&&
 243         str_contains($this->getAttribute(PDO::ATTR_CLIENT_VERSION), 'mysqlnd') &&
 244         ((version_compare(PHP_VERSION, '8.1.0') >= 0) || !$this->getAttribute(PDO::ATTR_EMULATE_PREPARES));
 245     }
 246 
 247     return $this->returns_native_types;
 248   }

 250   // Determines whether the database supports multiple locks.
 251   // This method should not be called for the first time while
 252   // locks are in place, because it will release them.
 253   // WARNING! This method should not be used as RELEASE_ALL_LOCKS
 254   //  is not supported by MariaDB Galera Cluster.
 255   public function supportsMultipleLocks() : bool
 256   {
 257     if (!isset($this->supports_multiple_locks))
 258     {
 259       if (!empty($this->mutex_locks))
 260       {
 261         throw new Exception(__METHOD__ . " called when there are locks in place.");
 262       }
 263 
 264       try
 265       {
 266         // We could check version numbers, but then we have to test for different
 267         // version numbers in MySQL and MariaDB, and possibly others.  It's
 268         // probably cleaner to check for the capability to RELEASE_ALL_LOCKS(), which
 269         // was introduced at the same time as support for multiple locks.
 270         $this->query("SELECT RELEASE_ALL_LOCKS()");
 271         $this->supports_multiple_locks = true;
 272       }
 273       catch (DBException $e)
 274       {
 275         $this->supports_multiple_locks = false;
 276       }
 277     }
 278 
 279     return $this->supports_multiple_locks;
 280   }

 283   // Since MySQL 5.7.5 lock names are restricted to 64 characters.
 284   // Truncating them is probably sufficient to ensure uniqueness.
 285   private static function hash(string $name) : string
 286   {
 287     return substr($name, 0, 64);
 288   }

 291   // Acquire a mutual-exclusion lock.
 292   // Returns true if the lock is acquired successfully, otherwise false.
 293   // WARNING! This method should not be used as GET_LOCK is not supported
 294   // by MariaDB Galera Cluster.
 295   public function mutex_lock(string $name) : bool
 296   {
 297     $timeout = 20;  // seconds
 298 
 299     if (!$this->supportsMultipleLocks() && !empty($this->mutex_locks))
 300     {
 301       $message = "Trying to set lock '$name', but lock '" . $this->mutex_locks[0] .
 302                  "' already exists.  Only one lock is allowed at any one time.";
 303       trigger_error($message, E_USER_WARNING);
 304       return false;
 305     }
 306 
 307     // GET_LOCK returns 1 if the lock was obtained successfully, 0 if the attempt
 308     // timed out (for example, because another client has previously locked the name),
 309     // or NULL if an error occurred (such as running out of memory or the thread was
 310     // killed with mysqladmin kill)
 311     try
 312     {
 313       $sql_params = array(':str' => self::hash($name),
 314                           ':timeout' => $timeout);
 315       $stmt = $this->query("SELECT GET_LOCK(:str, :timeout)", $sql_params);
 316     }
 317     catch (DBException $e)
 318     {
 319       trigger_error($e->getMessage(), E_USER_WARNING);
 320       return false;
 321     }
 322 
 323     if (($stmt->count() != 1) ||
 324         ($stmt->num_fields() != 1))
 325     {
 326       trigger_error("Unexpected number of rows and columns in result", E_USER_WARNING);
 327       return false;
 328     }
 329 
 330     $result = $stmt->next_row()[0];
 331 
 332     if ($result == '1')
 333     {
 334       $this->mutex_locks[] = $name;
 335       return true;
 336     }
 337 
 338     // Otherwise there's been some kind of failure to get a lock
 339     switch ($result)
 340     {
 341       case '0':
 342         $message = "GET_LOCK timed out after $timeout seconds";
 343         break;
 344       case null:
 345         $message = "GET_LOCK: an error occurred (such as running out of memory " .
 346                    "or the thread was killed with mysqladmin kill)";
 347         break;
 348       default:
 349         $message = "GET_LOCK: unexpected result '$result'";
 350         break;
 351     }
 352 
 353     trigger_error($message, E_USER_WARNING);
 354     return false;
 355   }
 356 
 357 
 358   // Release a mutual-exclusion lock.
 359   // Returns true if the lock is released successfully, otherwise false.
 360   // WARNING! This method should not be used as RELEASE_LOCK
 361   // is not supported by MariaDB Galera Cluster.
 362   public function mutex_unlock(string $name) : bool
 363   {
 364     // First do some sanity checking before executing the SQL query
 365     if (!in_array($name, $this->mutex_locks))
 366     {
 367       trigger_error("Trying to release a lock ('$name') which hasn't been set", E_USER_WARNING);
 368       return false;
 369     }
 370 
 371     // If this request looks OK, then execute the SQL query
 372     try
 373     {
 374       $stmt = $this->query("SELECT RELEASE_LOCK(?)", array(self::hash($name)));
 375     }
 376     catch (DBException $e)
 377     {
 378       trigger_error($e->getMessage(), E_USER_WARNING);
 379       return false;
 380     }
 381 
 382     if (($stmt->count() != 1) ||
 383         ($stmt->num_fields() != 1))
 384     {
 385       trigger_error("Unexpected number of rows and columns in result", E_USER_WARNING);
 386       return false;
 387     }
 388 
 389     $result = $stmt->next_row()[0];
 390 
 391     if ($result == '1')
 392     {
 393       if (($key = array_search($name, $this->mutex_locks)) !== false)
 394       {
 395         unset($this->mutex_locks[$key]);
 396       }
 397       return true;
 398     }
 399 
 400     // Otherwise there's been some kind of failure to release a lock.  These should in theory
 401     // have been caught by the sanity checking above, but just in case ...
 402     switch ($result)
 403     {
 404       case '0':
 405         $message = "RELEASE_LOCK: the lock '$name' was not established by this thread and so could not be released";
 406         break;
 407       case null:
 408         $message = "RELEASE_LOCK: the lock '$name' does not exist";
 409         break;
 410       default:
 411         $message = "RELEASE_LOCK: unexpected result '$result'";
 412         break;
 413     }
 414 
 415     trigger_error($message, E_USER_WARNING);
 416     return false;
 417   }
 418 
 419 
 420   // Release all mutual-exclusion locks.
 421   // WARNING! This method should not be used as RELEASE_ALL_LOCKS
 422   // is not supported by MariaDB Galera Cluster.
 423   public function mutex_unlock_all() : void
 424   {
 425     if ($this->supportsMultipleLocks())
 426     {
 427       $this->query("SELECT RELEASE_ALL_LOCKS()");
 428     }
 429     else
 430     {
 431       foreach ($this->mutex_locks as $lock)
 432       {
 433         $this->mutex_unlock($lock);
 434       }
 435     }
 436   }

 439   private function dbType() : ?int
 440   {
 441     global $debug;
 442 
 443     if (!isset($this->db_type))
 444     {
 445       if ((false !== mb_stripos($this->versionComment(), 'maria')) || (false !== mb_stripos($this->version(), 'maria')))
 446       {
 447         $this->db_type = self::DB_MARIADB;
 448       }
 449       elseif ((false !== mb_stripos($this->versionComment(), 'mysql')) || (false !== mb_stripos($this->version(), 'mysql')))
 450       {
 451         $this->db_type = self::DB_MYSQL;
 452       }
 453       // Most Ubuntu packages will identify the database type - see https://github.com/meeting-room-booking-system/mrbs-code/issues/72.
 454       // But there are some packages that don't seem to include the database type in any of the version information, for example
 455       // see SF Bugs #545 (https://sourceforge.net/p/mrbs/bugs/545/).  Let's assume that they are MySQL databases, though this isn't
 456       // necessarily true as it seems Ubuntu can be packaged with either MySQL or MariaDB - see for example https://launchpad.net/ubuntu.
 457       // However, if we assume MySQL then the required MySQL version number will be less than or equal to the required MariaDB version
 458       // number and the initial version check will pass, though the code may fail later on when it tries to use an unsupported feature.
 459       // TODO: something better. Perhaps we could also look at version numbers and then make some assumptions about whether the database
 460       // TODO: is MySQL or MariaDB, but that could become dangerous in the future. Or perhaps there's some other way.
 461       elseif ((false !== mb_stripos($this->versionComment(), 'ubuntu')) || (false !== mb_stripos($this->version(), 'ubuntu')))
 462       {
 463         $this->db_type = self::DB_MYSQL;
 464       }
 465       elseif ((false !== mb_stripos($this->versionComment(), 'percona')) || (false !== mb_stripos($this->version(), 'percona')))
 466       {
 467         $this->db_type = self::DB_PERCONA;
 468       }
 469       // The Altervista.org hosting platform will give this version comment
 470       elseif ($this->versionComment() == 'Source distribution')
 471       {
 472         $this->db_type = self::DB_MYSQL;
 473       }
 474       else
 475       {
 476         if ($debug)
 477         {
 478           trigger_error("Unknown database type '" . $this->versionComment() . "'");
 479         }
 480         $this->db_type = self::DB_OTHER;
 481       }
 482     }
 483 
 484     return $this->db_type;
 485   }

 488   // Checks that the database version meets the minimum requirement and dies if not
 489   private function checkVersion() : void
 490   {
 491     $db_version = $this->versionNumber();
 492     $db_type = $this->dbType();
 493 
 494     if (isset(self::MIN_VERSIONS[$db_type]) &&
 495         (version_compare($db_version, self::MIN_VERSIONS[$db_type]) < 0))
 496     {
 497       $this->versionDie(self::DB_NAMES[$db_type], $db_version, self::MIN_VERSIONS[$db_type]);
 498     }
 499     // If it's another type of database we'll have to add some minimum version requirements fot it
 500   }
