 548   // Get information about the columns in a table
 549   // Returns an array with the following indices for each column
 550   //
 551   //  'name'        the column name
 552   //  'type'        the type as reported by MySQL
 553   //  'nature'      the type mapped onto one of a generic set of types
 554   //                (boolean, integer, real, character, binary).   This enables
 555   //                the nature to be used by MRBS code when deciding how to
 556   //                display fields, without MRBS having to worry about the
 557   //                differences between MySQL and PostgreSQL type names.
 558   //  'length'      the maximum length of the field in bytes, octets or characters
 559   //                (Note:  this could be NULL)
 560   //  'is_nullable' whether the column can be set to NULL (boolean)
 561   //
 562   //  NOTE: the type mapping is incomplete and just covers the types commonly
 563   //  used by MRBS
 564   public function field_info(string $table) : array
 565   {
 566     // Map MySQL types on to a set of generic types
 567     $nature_map = array(
 568       'bigint'      => 'integer',
 569       'blob'        => 'binary',
 570       'char'        => 'character',
 571       'date'        => 'timestamp',
 572       'datetime'    => 'timestamp',
 573       'decimal'     => 'decimal',
 574       'double'      => 'real',
 575       'float'       => 'real',
 576       'int'         => 'integer',
 577       'longblob'    => 'binary',
 578       'longtext'    => 'character',
 579       'mediumblob'  => 'binary',
 580       'mediumint'   => 'integer',
 581       'mediumtext'  => 'character',
 582       'numeric'     => 'decimal',
 583       'smallint'    => 'integer',
 584       'text'        => 'character',
 585       'time'        => 'timestamp',
 586       'timestamp'   => 'timestamp',
 587       'tinyblob'    => 'binary',
 588       'tinyint'     => 'integer',
 589       'tinytext'    => 'character',
 590       'varchar'     => 'character',
 591       'year'        => 'timestamp'
 592     );
 593 
 594     // Length in bytes of MySQL integer types
 595     $int_bytes = array(
 596       'bigint'    => 8, // bytes
 597       'int'       => 4,
 598       'mediumint' => 3,
 599       'smallint'  => 2,
 600       'tinyint'   => 1
 601     );
 602 
 603     $stmt = $this->query("SHOW COLUMNS FROM $table", array());
 604 
 605     $fields = array();
 606 
 607     while (false !== ($row = $stmt->next_row_keyed()))
 608     {
 609       $name = $row['Field'];
 610       $type = $row['Type'];
 611       $default = $row['Default'];
 612       // Get the type and optionally length in parentheses, ignoring any attributes.  Note that the
 613       // length could be of the form (6,2) for a decimal.  Examples that we have to cope with:
 614       //    tinyint
 615       //    tinyint unsigned
 616       //    decimal(6,2)
 617       //    varchar(255)
 618       //    mediumint(4) unsigned zerofill
 619       // The type will be in the first group and the length in the optional second group
 620       preg_match('/(\w+)[\s(]?([\d,]+)?/', $type, $matches);
 621       $short_type = $matches[1];
 622       // map the type onto one of the generic natures, if a mapping exists
 623       $nature = (array_key_exists($short_type, $nature_map)) ? $nature_map[$short_type] : $short_type;
 624       // now work out the length
 625       if ($nature == 'integer')
 626       {
 627         // Convert the default to an int (unless it's NULL)
 628         if (isset($default))
 629         {
 630           $default = (int) $default;
 631         }
 632         // if it's one of the ints, then look up the length in bytes
 633         $length = (array_key_exists($short_type, $int_bytes)) ? $int_bytes[$short_type] : 0;
 634       }
 635       elseif (($nature == 'character') || ($nature == 'decimal'))
 636       {
 637         // if it's a character or decimal type then use the length that was in parentheses
 638         // eg if it was a varchar(25), we want the 25 and if a decimal(6,2) we want the 6,2
 639         if (isset($matches[2]))
 640         {
 641           $length = $matches[2];
 642         }
 643         // otherwise it could be any length (eg if it was a 'text')
 644         else
 645         {
 646           $length = defined('PHP_INT_MAX') ? PHP_INT_MAX : 9999;
 647         }
 648       }
 649       else  // we're only dealing with a few simple cases at the moment
 650       {
 651         $length = null;
 652       }
 653       // Convert the is_nullable field to a boolean
 654       $is_nullable = (mb_strtolower($row['Null']) == 'yes');
 655 
 656       $fields[] = array(
 657         'name' => $name,
 658         'type' => $type,
 659         'nature' => $nature,
 660         'length' => $length,
 661         'is_nullable' => $is_nullable,
 662         'default' => $default
 663       );
 664     }
 665 
 666     return $fields;
 667   }
 668 
 669   // Syntax methods
 670 
 671   // Generate non-standard SQL for LIMIT clauses:
 672   public function syntax_limit(int $count, int $offset) : string
 673   {
 674    return "LIMIT $offset,$count";
 675   }
 676 
 677 
 678   // Generate non-standard SQL to output a TIMESTAMP as a Unix-time:
 679   public function syntax_timestamp_to_unix(string $fieldname) : string
 680   {
 681     return "UNIX_TIMESTAMP($fieldname)";
 682   }
 683 
 684 
 685   // Returns the syntax for a case-sensitive string "equals" function
 686   // (By default MySQL is case-insensitive, so we force a binary comparison)
 687   //
 688   // Also takes a required pass-by-reference parameter to modify the SQL
 689   // parameters appropriately.
 690   //
 691   // NB:  This function is also assumed to do a strict comparison, ie
 692   // take account of trailing spaces.  (The '=' comparison in MySQL allows
 693   // trailing spaces, eg 'john' = 'john ').
 694   public function syntax_casesensitive_equals(string $fieldname, string $string, array &$params) : string
 695   {
 696     $params[] = $string;
 697 
 698     // We cannot assume that the database column has utf8 collation.  We may for example be
 699     // authenticating a user against an external database.  See the post at
 700     // https://stackoverflow.com/questions/5629111/how-can-i-make-sql-case-sensitive-string-comparison-on-mysql#answer-56283818
 701     // for an explanation of the query.
 702     return $this->quote($fieldname) . "=CONVERT(? using utf8mb4) COLLATE utf8mb4_bin";
 703   }
 704 
 705   // Generate non-standard SQL to match a string anywhere in a field's value
 706   // in a case-insensitive manner. $s is the un-escaped/un-slashed string.
 707   //
 708   // Also takes a required pass-by-reference parameter to modify the SQL
 709   // parameters appropriately.
 710   //
 711   // In MySQL, REGEXP seems to be case-sensitive, so use LIKE instead. But this
 712   // requires quoting of % and _ in addition to the usual.
 713   public function syntax_caseless_contains(string $fieldname, string $string, array &$params) : string
 714   {
 715     $string = str_replace("\\", "\\\\", $string);
 716     $string = str_replace("%", "\\%", $string);
 717     $string = str_replace("_", "\\_", $string);
 718 
 719     $params[] = "%$string%";
 720 
 721     return "$fieldname LIKE ?";
 722   }
 723 
 724 
 725   // Generate non-standard SQL to add a table column after another specified
 726   // column
 727   public function syntax_addcolumn_after(string $fieldname) : string
 728   {
 729     return "AFTER $fieldname";
 730   }
 731 
 732 
 733   // Generate non-standard SQL to specify a column as an auto-incrementing
 734   // integer while doing a CREATE TABLE
 735   public function syntax_createtable_autoincrementcolumn() : string
 736   {
 737     return "int NOT NULL auto_increment";
 738   }
 739 
 740 
 741   // Returns the syntax for a bitwise XOR operator
 742   public function syntax_bitwise_xor() : string
 743   {
 744     return "^";
 745   }
 746 
 747   // Returns the syntax for a simple split of a column's value into two
 748   // parts, separated by a delimiter.  $part can be 1 or 2.
 749   // Also takes a required pass-by-reference parameter to modify the SQL
 750   // parameters appropriately.
 751   public function syntax_simple_split(string $fieldname, string $delimiter, int $part, array &$params) : string
 752   {
 753     switch ($part)
 754     {
 755       case 1:
 756         $count = 1;
 757         break;
 758       case 2:
 759         $count = -1;
 760         break;
 761       default:
 762         throw new Exception("Invalid value ($part) given for " . '$part.');
 763         break;
 764     }
 765 
 766     $params[] = $delimiter;
 767     return "SUBSTRING_INDEX($fieldname, ?, $count)";
 768   }
 769 
 770 
 771   // Returns the syntax for aggregating a number of rows as a delimited string
 772   public function syntax_group_array_as_string(string $fieldname, string $delimiter=',') : string
 773   {
 774     // Use DISTINCT to eliminate duplicates which can arise when the query
 775     // has joins on two or more junction tables.  Maybe a different query
 776     // would eliminate the duplicates and the need for DISTINCT, and it may
 777     // or may not be more efficient.
 778     return "GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT $fieldname SEPARATOR '$delimiter')";
 779   }
 780 
 781 
 782   // Returns the syntax for an "upsert" query.  Unfortunately getting the id of the
 783   // last row differs between MySQL and PostgreSQL.   In PostgreSQL the query will
 784   // return a row with the id in the 'id' column.  However there isn't a corresponding
 785   // way of doing this in MySQL, but db()->insert_id() will work, regardless of whether
 786   // an insert or update was performed.
 787   //
 788   //  $conflict_keys     the key(s) which is/are unique; can be a scalar or an array
 789   //                     (ignored in MySQL)
 790   //  $assignments       an array of assignments for the UPDATE clause
 791   //  $has_id_column     whether the table has an id column
 792   public function syntax_on_duplicate_key_update($conflict_keys, array $assignments, bool $has_id_column=false) : string
 793   {
 794     if ($has_id_column)
 795     {
 796       // In order to make lastInsertId() work even after an UPDATE
 797       $assignments[] = "id=LAST_INSERT_ID(id)";
 798     }
 799 
 800     return "ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE " . implode(', ', $assignments);
 801   }
 802 
 803 }

   2 declare(strict_types=1);
   3 namespace MRBS;

   5 use IntlCalendar;
   6 use MRBS\ICalendar\RFC5545;

   9 class DateTime extends \DateTime
  10 {
  11   private static $isHoliday = array();
  12   private static $validHolidays = array();
  13 
  14   public const ISO8601_DATE = 'Y-m-d';
  15   private const HOLIDAY_RANGE_OPERATOR = '..';
  16 
  17 
  18   // Before PHP 8 a child of DateTime::createFromFormat() returned an instance of the
  19   // parent, rather than the child.  So we have to force createFromFormat() to return
  20   // an instance of the child.  See https://bugs.php.net/bug.php?id=79975 and also
  21   // https://stackoverflow.com/questions/5450197/make-datetimecreatefromformat-return-child-class-instead-of-parent
  22   // This method will no longer be necessary when the minimum PHP version is > 7.
  23   #[\ReturnTypeWillChange]
  24   public static function createFromFormat($format, $datetime, ?\DateTimeZone $timezone = null)
  25   {
  26     assert(version_compare(MRBS_MIN_PHP_VERSION, '8.0.0', '<'), "This method is now redundant.");
  27 
  28     $parent = parent::createFromFormat($format, $datetime, $timezone);
  29 
  30     if ($parent === false)
  31     {
  32       return false;
  33     }
  34 
  35     return new static($parent->format('Y-m-d\TH:i:s.u'), $parent->getTimezone());
  36   }
  37 
  38 
  39   // Returns the first day of the week (0 = Sunday) for a given timezone and locale.
  40   // If $timezone is null, the default timezone will be used.
  41   // If $locale is null, the default locale will be used.
  42   // The method relies on the IntlCalendar class.  If it doesn't exist, or there's an error,
  43   // the method assumes that the week starts on a Monday.
  44   public static function firstDayOfWeek(?string $timezone = null, ?string $locale = null) : int
  45   {
  46     global $icu_override;
  47 
  48     $default = 1; // Monday
  49 
  50     if (!class_exists('\\IntlCalendar'))
  51     {
  52       return $default;
  53     }
  54 
  55     $calendar = IntlCalendar::createInstance($timezone, $locale);
  56     if (!isset($calendar))
  57     {
  58       trigger_error("Could not create IntlCalendar for timezone '$timezone' and locale '$locale'", E_USER_WARNING);
  59       return $default;
  60     }
  61 
  62     // If we're overriding the ICU library then use that value
  63     if (isset($icu_override[$locale]['first_day_of_week']))
  64     {
  65       $first_day =  $icu_override[$locale]['first_day_of_week'];
  66       // Check that it's a valid day
  67       if (!in_array($first_day, array(
  68           IntlCalendar::DOW_SUNDAY,
  69           IntlCalendar::DOW_MONDAY,
  70           IntlCalendar::DOW_TUESDAY,
  71           IntlCalendar::DOW_WEDNESDAY,
  72           IntlCalendar::DOW_THURSDAY,
  73           IntlCalendar::DOW_FRIDAY,
  74           IntlCalendar::DOW_SATURDAY
  75         )))
  76       {
  77         throw new Exception('$icu_override[' . $locale . "]['first_day_of_week'] must be in the range [1..7]");
  78       }
  79     }
  80     // Otherwise just get the standard value from ICU
  81     else
  82     {
  83       $first_day = $calendar->getFirstDayOfWeek();
  84       if ($first_day === false) {
  85         trigger_error($calendar->getErrorMessage(), E_USER_WARNING);
  86         return $default;
  87       }
  88     }
  89 
  90     return $first_day - 1;  // IntlCalendar::DOW_SUNDAY = 1, so we need to subtract 1
  91   }
  92 
  93 
  94   // Tests whether this is the first day of the week in the locale.
  95   // If $locale is null, the default locale will be used.
  96   public function isFirstDayOfWeek(?string $locale = null) : bool
  97   {
  98     return ($this->getDayOfWeek() === self::firstDayOfWeek($this->getTimezone()->getName(), $locale));
  99   }
 100 
 101 
 102   // TODO: make $relative an object?
 103   // Sets the day to $relative, where relative is an RFC5545 relative day,
 104   // eg "-2SU".  Returns FALSE if the relative day doesn't exist in this
 105   // month, otherwise TRUE.
 106   public function setRelativeDay(string $relative) : bool
 107   {
 108     $clone = clone $this;
 109 
 110     // Get the ordinal number and the day of the week
 111     list('ordinal' => $ord, 'day' => $dow) = RFC5545::parseByday($relative);
 112     // Set the starting day of the month, either to the first or last day of
 113     // the month, depending on whether we are counting forwards or backwards.
 114     $clone->setDay(($ord > 0) ? 1 : (int) $clone->format('t'));
 115     // Advance/go back to the first day of the week that is required
 116     // TODO: this could be optimised slightly by calculating the exact number of days required
 117     while ($clone->format('w') != RFC5545::convertDayToOrd($dow))
 118     {
 119       $modifier = ($ord > 0) ? '+1 day' : '-1 day';
 120       $clone->modify($modifier);
 121     }
 122     // Advance/go back the required number of weeks
 123     if (abs($ord) > 1)
 124     {
 125       $modifier = (($ord > 0) ? '+' : '-') . ($ord - 1) . 'weeks';
 126       $clone->modify($modifier);
 127     }
 128     // See if we are still in the same month.  If not, then the relative day doesn't
 129     // exist in this month and return FALSE.  If so, then set this date to be the
 130     // clone's and return TRUE.
 131     if ($clone->getMonth() !== $this->getMonth())
 132     {
 133       return false;
 134     }
 135     $this->setTimestamp($clone->getTimestamp());
 136     return true;
 137   }

 140   // Sets the time to the start of the first slot of the day
 141   public function setStartFirstSlot() : self
 142   {
 143     global $morningstarts, $morningstarts_minutes, $enable_periods;
 144 
 145     if ($enable_periods)
 146     {
 147       return $this->setTime(12, 0);
 148     }
 149 
 150     return $this->setTime($morningstarts, $morningstarts_minutes);
 151   }

 153 
 154   // Sets the time to the start of the last slot of the day.
 155   // (Note that if the booking day extends beyond midnight, then this will
 156   // be on the next day.)
 157   public function setStartLastSlot() : self
 158   {
 159     global $morningstarts, $morningstarts_minutes, $eveningends, $eveningends_minutes, $enable_periods, $periods;
 160 
 161     if ($enable_periods)
 162     {
 163       return $this->setTime(12, count($periods) - 1);
 164     }
 165 
 166     // Work out if $evening_ends is really on the next day
 167     if (hm_before(
 168       ['hours' => $eveningends, 'minutes' => $eveningends_minutes],
 169       ['hours' => $morningstarts, 'minutes' => $morningstarts_minutes])
 170     )
 171     {
 172       $this->modify('+1 day');
 173     }
 174 
 175     return $this->setTime($eveningends, $eveningends_minutes);
 176   }

 185

 187     $this->modify("+$resolution seconds");
 188

 193   // Adds $n (which can be negative) months to this date, without overflowing
 194   // into the next month.  For example modifying 2023-01-31 by +1 month gives
 195   // 2023-02-28 rather than 2023-03-03.
 196   public function modifyMonthsNoOverflow(int $n, bool $allow_hidden_days = false) : void
 197   {
 198     if ($n == 0)
 199     {
 200       return;
 201     }
 202 
 203     $modifier = "$n months";
 204     $day = $this->format('j');
 205     $this->modify('first day of this month');
 206     $this->modify($modifier);
 207     $this->modify('+' . (min($day, $this->format('t')) - 1) . ' days');
 208 
 209     if (!$allow_hidden_days)
 210     {
 211       $this->findNearestUnhiddenDayInMonth();
 212     }
 213   }

 216   // Adds $n (which can be negative) years to this date, without overflowing
 217   // into the next month.  For example modifying 2024-02-29 by +1 year gives
 218   // 2025-02-28 rather than 2025-03-01.
 219   public function modifyYearsNoOverflow(int $n, bool $allow_hidden_days = false) : void
 220   {
 221     $this->modifyMonthsNoOverflow(12 * $n, $allow_hidden_days);
 222   }

 287   // Winds the date back to the first $month that is at or before
 288   // this date.  Useful for aligning with financial or academic years.
 289   // If $month is 0, then no change is made.
 290   public function setMonthYearStart(int $month) : self
 291   {
 292     if ($month !== 0)
 293     {
 294       $this_month = $this->getMonth();
 295       $modification = $month - $this_month;
 296       if ($modification > 0)
 297       {
 298         $modification -= MONTHS_PER_YEAR;
 299       }
 300       $this->modifyMonthsNoOverflow($modification, true);
 301     }
 302 
 303     return $this;
 304   }

 307   // Checks whether the config setting of holidays for $year consists
 308   // of a valid set of dates.
 309   private static function validateHolidays(string $year) : bool
 310   {
 311     global $holidays;
 312 
 313     // Only need to validate a year once, so store the answer in a static property
 314     if (!isset(self::$validHolidays[$year]))
 315     {
 316       try
 317       {
 318         foreach ($holidays[$year] as $holiday)
 319         {
 320           $limits = explode(self::HOLIDAY_RANGE_OPERATOR, $holiday);
 321 
 322           foreach ($limits as $limit)
 323           {
 324             // Check that the dates are valid
 325             if (!validate_iso_date($limit))
 326             {
 327               throw new UnexpectedValueException("invalid holiday date '$limit'.");
 328             }
 329             // Check that the year is correct
 330             if ($year != split_iso_date($limit)[0])
 331             {
 332               throw new UnexpectedValueException("the holiday '$limit' does not occur in the year '$year'.");
 333             }
 334           }
 335 
 336           // Check that we haven't got more than two limits
 337           if (count($limits) > 2)
 338           {
 339             throw new UnexpectedValueException("invalid range '$holiday'; there is more than one " .
 340               "range operator (" . self::HOLIDAY_RANGE_OPERATOR . ").");
 341           }
 342           // Check that the end of the range isn't before the beginning
 343           elseif ((count($limits) == 2) && ($limits[1] < $limits[0]))
 344           {
 345             throw new UnexpectedValueException("invalid range '$holiday'; the end is before the beginning.");
 346           }
 347         }
 348 
 349         self::$validHolidays[$year] = true;
 350       }
 351       catch (UnexpectedValueException $e)
 352       {
 353         self::$validHolidays[$year] = false;
 354         trigger_error('Check the config setting of $holidays: ' . $e->getMessage(), E_USER_WARNING);
 355       }
 356     }
 357 
 358     return self::$validHolidays[$year];
 359   }

 362   // Move the date to the nearest unhidden day in this month.
 363   private function findNearestUnhiddenDayInMonth() : void
 364   {
 365     // Trivial case: it's already unhidden
 366     if (!$this->isHiddenDay())
 367     {
 368       return;
 369     }
 370 
 371     // Keep track of whether we've already tried looking beyond the ends
 372     // of the month, to avoid doing it again unnecessarily.
 373     $end_of_month_reached = false;
 374     $start_of_month_reached =false;
 375 
 376     // Create a series of modifiers going progressively +1, -1, +2, -2 ..
 377     // +6, -6 days away from this day and test each one to check that the
 378     // modified day is both in the same month as the original date and is
 379     // not hidden.
 380     for ($i=1; $i<DAYS_PER_WEEK; $i++)
 381     {
 382       $unsigned_modifier = "$i days";
 383       foreach (['+', '-'] as $sign)
 384       {
 385         // Check whether we've already been past the end/start of the
 386         // month, and if so try the next modifier.
 387         if ((($sign == '+') && $end_of_month_reached) ||
 388             (($sign == '-') && $start_of_month_reached))
 389         {
 390           continue;
 391         }
 392         // Otherwise, create a clone and test it with this modifier
 393         $clone = clone $this;
 394         $modifier = $sign . $unsigned_modifier;
 395         $clone->modify($modifier);
 396         if ($clone->getMonth() == $this->getMonth())
 397         {
 398           if (!$clone->isHiddenDay())
 399           {
 400             // Success! The clone is in the same month and not hidden,
 401             // so apply the same modifier to the original.
 402             $this->modify($modifier);
 403             return;
 404           }
 405         }
 406         else
 407         {
 408           if ($sign == '+')
 409           {
 410             $end_of_month_reached = true;
 411           }
 412           else
 413           {
 414             $start_of_month_reached = true;
 415           }
 416         }
 417         unset($clone);
 418       }
 419     }
 420   }
 421 
 422 
 423   // Determines whether the date is a holiday, as defined
 424   // in the config variable $holidays.
 425   private function isHolidayConfig() : bool
 426   {
 427     global $holidays;
 428 
 429     $year = $this->format('Y');
 430     $iso_date = $this->getISODate();
 431 
 432     // Only need to check if a date is a holiday once, so store the answer in a
 433     // static property
 434     if (!isset(self::$isHoliday[$iso_date]))
 435     {
 436       self::$isHoliday[$iso_date] = false;
 437       if (!empty($holidays[$year]) && self::validateHolidays($year))
 438       {
 439         foreach ($holidays[$year] as $holiday)
 440         {
 441           $limits = explode('..', $holiday);
 442 
 443           if (count($limits) == 1)
 444           {
 445             // It's a single date of the form '2022-01-01'
 446             if ($iso_date == $limits[0])
 447             {
 448               self::$isHoliday[$iso_date] = true;
 449               break;
 450             }
 451           }
 452           elseif (count($limits) == 2)
 453           {
 454             // It's a range of the form '2022-07-01..2022-07-31'
 455             if (($iso_date >= $limits[0]) && ($iso_date <= $limits[1]))
 456             {
 457               self::$isHoliday[$iso_date] = true;
 458               break;
 459             }
 460           }
 461           else
 462           {
 463             trigger_error("Invalid holiday element '$holiday'");
 464           }
 465         }
 466       }
 467     }
 468 
 469     return self::$isHoliday[$iso_date];
 470   }
 471 
 472 
 473   // Determines whether a given date is supposed to be hidden in the display
 474   public function isHiddenDay() : bool
 475   {
 476     global $hidden_days;
 477 
 478     return (isset($hidden_days) && in_array($this->format('w'), $hidden_days));
 479   }
 480 
 481 
 482   // Determines whether the date is a holiday.
 483   public function isHoliday() : bool
 484   {
 485     if ($this->isHolidayConfig())
 486     {
 487       return true;
 488     }
 489 
 490     // This method can be extended to check other sources, eg a .ics
 491     // file or a database table.
 492     return false;
 493   }
 494 
 495 
 496   public function isToday() : bool
 497   {
 498     $today = new DateTime();
 499     return ($this->getISODate() == $today->getISODate());
 500   }
 501 
 502 
 503   public function isWeekend() : bool
 504   {
 505     return is_weekend(intval($this->format('w')));
 506   }
 507 
 508 
 509   // Set the time to $s, where $s is the nominal number of
 510   // seconds after midnight, ignoring DST changes.
 511   public function setNominalSeconds(int $s) : self
 512   {
 513     $second = $s % 60;
 514     $s -= $second;
 515     $m = $s/60;
 516     $minute = $m % 60;
 517     $m -= $minute;
 518     $hour = $m/60;
 519 
 520     while ($hour > 24)
 521     {
 522       $this->modify('+1 day');
 523       $hour -= 24;
 524     }
 525 
 526     return $this->setTime($hour, $minute, $second);
 527   }
 528 }

  27 /**

  36     LogLevel::ERROR,
  37     LogLevel::WARNING,
  38     LogLevel::NOTICE,

  40     LogLevel::DEBUG

  46     LogLevel::CRITICAL,
  47     LogLevel::ERROR,
  48     LogLevel::WARNING

  51   private static $errno_levels = [
  52     E_ERROR => LogLevel::CRITICAL,
  53     E_WARNING => LogLevel::WARNING,
  54     E_NOTICE => LogLevel::NOTICE,
  55     E_CORE_ERROR => LogLevel::CRITICAL,
  56     E_CORE_WARNING => LogLevel::WARNING,
  57     E_COMPILE_ERROR => LogLevel::CRITICAL,
  58     E_COMPILE_WARNING => LogLevel::WARNING,
  59     E_DEPRECATED => LogLevel::WARNING,
  60     E_USER_ERROR => LogLevel::CRITICAL,
  61     E_USER_WARNING => LogLevel::WARNING,
  62     E_USER_NOTICE => LogLevel::NOTICE,
  63     E_USER_DEPRECATED => LogLevel::WARNING,
  64     E_RECOVERABLE_ERROR => LogLevel::CRITICAL

  68   /**
  69    * Initialise the class
  70    *
  71    * @throws Exception
  72    */
  73   public static function init(): void
  74   {

  77     if ($debug && function_exists('opcache_reset'))

  79       // Useful for making compile-time errors more obvious
  80       opcache_reset();

  83     // Add in the E_STRICT level for old versions of PHP
  84     assert(version_compare(MRBS_MIN_PHP_VERSION, '8.0.0', '<'), "The if block below can be removed.");
  85     if (version_compare(phpversion(), '8.0.0', '<'))
  86     {

  90     self::setDisplayErrors();
  91     self::setErrorLog();
  92     $error_level = self::getErrorLevel();
  93     error_reporting($error_level);
  94     self::initLogger();
  95 
  96     set_error_handler([__CLASS__, 'errorHandler'], $error_level);
  97     set_exception_handler([__CLASS__, 'exceptionHandler']);
  98     register_shutdown_function([__CLASS__, 'shutdownFunction']);

 102   public static function errorHandler(int $errno, string $errstr, string $errfile, int $errline): bool
 103   {
 104     // "If the function returns false then the normal error handler continues."
 105     // (https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.set-error-handler.php)
 106 
 107     // Check to see whether error reporting has been disabled by
 108     // the error suppression operator (@), because the custom error
 109     // handler is still called even if errors are suppressed.
 110     if (!(error_reporting() & $errno))
 111     {
 112       return true;
 113     }
 114 
 115     $details = self::get_error_name($errno) . " in $errfile at line $errline";
 116 
 117     if (!array_key_exists($errno, self::$errno_levels))
 118     {
 119       throw new RuntimeException("Cannot find mapping for ERRNO level $errno");
 120     }
 121 
 122     self::output_error(self::$errno_levels[$errno], $errstr, $details);
 123 
 124     return true;
 125   }
 126 
 127 
 128   /**
 129    * Custom exception handler.  Logs the error and then outputs a fatal error message.
 130    *
 131    * @return never
 132    */
 133   public static function exceptionHandler(Throwable $exception): void
 134   {
 135     // Log the exception
 136     $class = get_class($exception);
 137     $details = "Uncaught exception '$class' in " . $exception->getFile() . " at line " . $exception->getLine();
 138     $message = $exception->getMessage();
 139     self::output_error(LogLevel::CRITICAL, $message, $details, $exception);
 140 
 141     // Then output a fatal error
 142     $namespace_root = strtok(__NAMESPACE__, '\\');
 143     switch (get_class($exception))
 144     {
 145       case $namespace_root . '\DB\DBExternalException':
 146         $fatal_message = get_vocab("fatal_db_ext_error");
 147         break;
 148       case $namespace_root . '\DB\DBException':
 149       case 'PDOException':
 150         $fatal_message = get_vocab("fatal_db_error");
 151         break;
 152       default:
 153         $fatal_message = get_vocab("fatal_error");
 154         break;
 155     }
 156 
 157     self::fatalError($fatal_message);
 158   }
 159 
 160 
 161   /**
 162    * Converts an error into an exception
 163    *
 164    * @return never
 165    * @throws \Exception
 166    */
 167   public static function exceptionThrower(int $errno, string $errstr) : void
 168   {
 169     throw new \Exception($errstr, $errno);
 170   }

 173   /**
 174    * Error handler - this is used to display serious errors such as database
 175    * errors without sending incomplete HTML pages. This is only used for
 176    * errors which "should never happen", not those caused by bad inputs.
 177    * Always outputs the bottom of the page and exits.
 178    *
 179    * @return never
 180    */
 181   public static function fatalError(string $message): void
 182   {
 183     print_simple_header();
 184     echo "<p>\n". escape_html($message) . "</p>\n";
 185     print_footer();
 186     exit;
 187   }

 190   public static function shutdownFunction() : void
 191   {
 192     $error = error_get_last();
 193 
 194     if (isset($error) &&
 195         (mb_strpos($error['message'], 'iconv()') !== false) &&
 196         !function_exists('iconv'))
 197     {
 198       // Help new admins understand what to do in case the iconv error occurs...
 199       $message = "MRBS - iconv module not installed. ";
 200       $details = "The iconv module, which provides PHP support for Unicode, is not " .
 201                  "installed on your system." .
 202                  "Unicode gives MRBS the ability to easily support languages other " .
 203                  "than English. Without Unicode, support for non-English-speaking " .
 204                  "users will be crippled." .
 205                  "To fix this error, you need to install and enable the iconv module." .
 206                  "On a Windows server, enable php_iconv.dll in %windir%\\php.ini, and " .
 207                  "make sure both %phpdir%\\dlls\\iconv.dll and %phpdir%\\extensions\\php_iconv.dll " .
 208                  "are in the path. One way to do this is to copy these two files to %windir%." .
 209                  "On a Unix server, recompile your PHP module with the appropriate option for " .
 210                  "enabling the iconv extension. Consult your PHP server documentation for " .
 211                  "more information about enabling iconv support.\n";
 212       self::output_error(LogLevel::NOTICE, $message, $details);
 213     }
 214   }

 217   private static function setDisplayErrors(): void
 218   {
 219     global $debug;

 221     if ($debug)
 222     {

 224       ini_set('display_startup_errors', '1');  // ini_set() only accepts non-string values from PHP 8.1.0

 229   private static function setErrorLog() : void
 230   {
 231     // If the error log file is a relative path then turn it into an absolute one in
 232     // order to avoid problems in shutdown when the working directory can change.
 233     // (See the notes in https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.register-shutdown-function.php).
 234     // Check for both Windows and Unix style separators because Unix separators can be used
 235     // on Windows.
 236     $error_log = ini_get('error_log');
 237     if (($error_log !== '') &&
 238         (mb_strpos($error_log, '/') === false) &&
 239         (mb_strpos($error_log, '\\') === false))
 240     {
 241       ini_set('error_log', getcwd() . '/' . $error_log);
 242     }
 243   }

 246   private static function getErrorLevel() : int
 247   {
 248     global $debug;
 249 
 250     if ($debug)
 251     {
 252       return -1;
 253     }
 254 
 255     // Make sure notice errors are not reported; they can break mrbs code.
 256     $error_level = E_ALL & ~E_NOTICE & ~E_USER_NOTICE;
 257 
 258     if (defined("E_DEPRECATED"))
 259     {
 260       $error_level = $error_level & ~E_DEPRECATED;
 261     }
 262 
 263     // The Mail and Net libraries generate E_STRICT errors, so disable E_STRICT (which became
 264     // part of E_ALL in PHP 5.4).  E_STRICT is deprecated from PHP 8.4 (and not used since PHP 7).
 265     assert(version_compare(MRBS_MIN_PHP_VERSION, '8.0.0', '<'), "The if block below can be removed.");
 266     if (defined("E_STRICT") && (version_compare(PHP_VERSION, '8.4') < 0))
 267     {
 268       $error_level = $error_level & ~E_STRICT;
 269     }
 270 
 271     return $error_level;
 272   }

 275   /**
 276    * @throws Exception
 277    */
 278   private static function initLogger() : void
 279   {
 280     global $mail_settings, $sendmail_settings, $smtp_settings, $logger_settings;
 281 
 282     $logger = new Logger($logger_settings['channel_name']);
 283     $logger->pushProcessor(new IntrospectionProcessor());
 284 
 285     if (ini_get('display_errors'))
 286     {
 287       $handler = new StreamHandler('php://output');
 288       $handler->setFormatter(new BrowserFormatter());
 289       if ($logger_settings['stream']['browser'])
 290       {
 291         $logger->pushHandler($handler);
 292       }
 293       if ($logger_settings['stream']['console'])
 294       {
 295         $logger->pushHandler(new BrowserConsoleHandler());
 296       }
 297     }
 298 
 299     if (ini_get('log_errors'))
 300     {
 301       $handler = new ErrorLogHandler();
 302       $handler->setFormatter(new ErrorLogFormatter());
 303       $logger->pushHandler($handler);
 304     }
 305 
 306     if ($logger_settings['mail']['enabled'])
 307     {
 308       $mailer = new Mailer($mail_settings, $sendmail_settings, $smtp_settings, true);
 309       $mailer->CharSet = get_charset();
 310       $mailer->setFromRFC822($logger_settings['mail']['from']);
 311       $mailer->addAddressesRFC822($logger_settings['mail']['to']);
 312       $handler = new PHPMailerHandler($mailer, $logger_settings['mail']['level']);
 313       $logger->pushHandler($handler);
 314     }
 315 
 316     Registry::addLogger($logger);
 317   }

 320   /**
 321    * Logs an exception
 322    */
 323   private static function output_exception_error(Throwable $exception) : void
 324   {
 325     $class = get_class($exception);
 326     $details = "Uncaught exception '$class' in " . $exception->getFile() . " at line " . $exception->getLine();
 327     $message = $exception->getMessage();
 328     self::output_error(LogLevel::CRITICAL, $message, $details, $exception);
 329   }

 332   private static function output_error(string $level, string $message, string $details, ?Throwable $e = null) : void
 333   {
 334     global $debug, $auth, $get, $post;
 335 
 336     static $default_timezone_set = false;
 337 
 338     // We can't start outputting any error messages unless the default timezone has been set,
 339     // so if we are not sure that it has been set, then set it.
 340     if (!$default_timezone_set)
 341     {
 342       mrbs_default_timezone_set();
 343       $default_timezone_set = true;
 344     }
 345 
 346     if (!in_array($level, self::LOG_LEVELS))
 347     {
 348       throw new InvalidArgumentException("Invalid log level '$level'.");
 349     }
 350 
 351     $context = [];
 352 
 353     if (in_array($level, self::MAJOR_LEVELS))
 354     {
 355       if (isset($get))
 356       {
 357         $context['get'] = $get;
 358       }
 359       if (isset($post))
 360       {
 361         $context['post'] = $post;
 362         if (!$auth['log_credentials'])
 363         {
 364           // Overwrite the username and password to stop them appearing
 365           // in error logs.
 366           foreach (array('username', 'password') as $var)
 367           {
 368             if (isset($context['post'][$var]) && ($context['post'][$var] !== ''))
 369             {
 370               $context['post'][$var] = '****';
 371             }
 372           }
 373         }
 374       }
 375     }
 376 
 377     if ($debug || in_array($level, self::MAJOR_LEVELS))
 378     {
 379       $backtrace = self::generateBacktrace($e);
 380       $context['backtrace'] = $backtrace;
 381     }
 382 
 383     $context['details'] = $details;
 384     Registry::MRBS()->log($level, $message, $context);
 385   }
 386 
 387 
 388   /**
 389    * Generate a backtrace.  This function allows us to format the output slightly better
 390    * than debug_print_backtrace().
 391    *
 392    * @return string[]
 393    */
 394   private static function generateBacktrace(?Throwable $e = null) : array
 395   {
 396     global $debug;
 397 
 398     $result = [];
 399 
 400     // Get the backtrace. If we've been given a throwable then use that to get the
 401     // trace as it goes further back in the stack.
 402     if (isset($e))
 403     {
 404       $calls = $e->getTrace();
 405     }
 406     else
 407     {
 408       $options = DEBUG_BACKTRACE_PROVIDE_OBJECT;
 409       // Unless we are debugging ignore arguments as these can give away
 410       // database credentials
 411       if (!$debug)
 412       {
 413         $options = $options | DEBUG_BACKTRACE_IGNORE_ARGS;
 414       }
 415       $calls = debug_backtrace($options);
 416     }
 417 
 418     // Get rid of calls on the stack which are just concerned with error handling and logging.
 419     while (!empty($calls) && isset($calls[0]['class']) && ($calls[0]['class'] === __CLASS__))
 420     {
 421       array_shift($calls);
 422     }
 423 
 424     // Turn each call into a string
 425     foreach ($calls as $i => $call)
 426     {
 427       $trace = "#$i " . self::callToString($call);
 428       $result[] = $trace;
 429     }
 430 
 431     return $result;
 432   }
 433 
 434 
 435   private static function callToString(array $call) : string
 436   {
 437     $result = '';
 438 
 439     if (isset($call['class']) && isset($call['type']))
 440     {
 441       $result .= $call['class'] . $call['type'];
 442     }
 443 
 444     if (isset($call['function']))
 445     {
 446       $result .= $call['function'];
 447       $result .= '(';
 448       // Add in the args if required, unless it was trigger_error() that was called
 449       // because that will just repeat the error message.
 450       if (isset($call['args']) && ($call['function'] !== 'trigger_error'))
 451       {
 452         $result .= self::getArgString($call['args']);
 453       }
 454       $result .= ')';
 455     }
 456 
 457     if (isset($call['file']) && isset($call['line']))
 458     {
 459       $result .= ' called at [' . $call['file'] . ':' . $call['line'] . ']';
 460     }
 461 
 462     return $result;
 463   }
 464 
 465 
 466   private static function getArgString(array $args) : string
 467   {
 468     $result = array();
 469 
 470     foreach ($args as $arg)
 471     {
 472       $type = gettype($arg);
 473 
 474       switch ($type)
 475       {
 476         case 'boolean':
 477           $result[] = ($arg) ? 'true' : 'false';
 478           break;
 479 
 480         case 'integer':
 481         case 'double':
 482         case 'string':
 483           $result[] = $arg;
 484           break;
 485 
 486         case 'object':
 487           $class = get_class($arg);
 488           $result[] = ($class == 'SensitiveParameterValue') ? "[$class]" : $type;
 489           break;
 490 
 491         default:
 492           $result[] = $type;
 493           break;
 494       }
 495     }
 496 
 497     return implode(', ', $result);
 498   }
 499 
 500 
 501   /**
 502    * Translate an error constant value into the name of the constant
 503    */
 504   private static function get_error_name(int $errno) : string
 505   {
 506     $constants = get_defined_constants(true);
 507     $keys = array_keys($constants['Core'], $errno);
 508     $keys = array_filter($keys, function($value) {
 509       return (mb_strpos($value, 'E_') === 0);
 510     });
 511     return implode('|', $keys); // There should only be one member of the array, all being well.
 512   }
 513 
 514 }

   1 <?php
   2 declare(strict_types=1);
   3 namespace MRBS\Errors\Formatter;
   4 
   5 use Monolog\Formatter\NormalizerFormatter;
   6 use function MRBS\escape_html;
   7 
   8 abstract class GeneralFormatter extends NormalizerFormatter
   9 {
  10   private $useHTML;
  11 
  12   public function __construct(?string $dateFormat = null, $useHTML=false)
  13   {
  14     $this->useHTML = $useHTML;
  15     parent::__construct($dateFormat);
  16   }
  17 
  18 
  19   public function format(array $record): string
  20   {
  21     $lines = [];
  22 
  23     if (!isset($record['context']['details']))
  24     {
  25       // This will be when the logger is called directly from the MRBS code, rather than the Errors class.
  26       $record['context']['details'] = $record['channel'] . '.' .$record['level_name'] . ' in ' . $record['extra']['file'] . ' at line ' . $record['extra']['line'];
  27     }
  28 
  29     $lines[] = $this->escape($record['context']['details']);
  30     $lines[] = $this->escape($record['message']);
  31 
  32     // Add in any stacktrace
  33     if (!empty($record['context']['backtrace']))
  34     {
  35       foreach ($record['context']['backtrace'] as $call)
  36       {
  37         $lines[] = $this->escape($call);
  38       }
  39     }
  40 
  41     // Add in the GET and POST variables
  42     foreach(['$_GET' => 'get', '$_POST' => 'post'] as $name => $var)
  43     {
  44       if (isset($record['context'][$var]))
  45       {
  46         $line = $this->escape(print_r($record['context'][$var], true));
  47         if ($this->useHTML)
  48         {
  49           // Replace spaces with non-breaking spaces
  50           $line = str_replace(' ', '&nbsp;', $line);
  51         }
  52         // Remove the final new line
  53         $line = rtrim($line);
  54         if ($this->useHTML)
  55         {
  56           $line = str_replace("\n", "<br>\n", $line);
  57         }
  58         $lines[] = "$name: $line";
  59       }
  60     }
  61 
  62     if ($this->useHTML)
  63     {
  64       // Make the first line bold.
  65       $lines[0] = '<b>' . $lines[0] . '</b>';
  66     }
  67 
  68     $result = implode(($this->useHTML) ? "<br>\n" : "\n", $lines);
  69 
  70     if ($this->useHTML)
  71     {
  72       // Wrap it in a paragraph
  73       $result = "<p>\n" . $result . "\n</p>\n";
  74     }
  75 
  76     return $result;
  77   }
  78 
  79 
  80   private function escape(string $value): string
  81   {
  82     return ($this->useHTML) ? escape_html($value) : $value;
  83   }
  84 }

 204   // Add a set of select options to an element, eg to a <select> or <datalist> element.
 205   //    $options      An array of options for the select element.   Can be a one- or two-dimensional
 206   //                  array.  If it's two-dimensional then the keys of the outer level represent
 207   //                  <optgroup> labels.  The inner level can be a simple array or an associative
 208   //                  array with value => text members for each <option> in the <select> element.
 209   //    $selected     The value(s) of the option(s) that are selected.  Can be a single value
 210   //                  or an array of values.
 211   //    $associative  Whether to treat the options as a simple or an associative array.  (This
 212   //                  parameter is necessary because if you index an array with strings that look
 213   //                  like integers then PHP casts the keys to integers and the array becomes a
 214   //                  simple array).   Can take the following values:
 215   //                      true    treat as an associative array
 216   //                      false   treat as a simple array
 217   //                      null    auto-detect
 218   //    $for_datalist Whether the options are intended for use in a <datalist>.
 219   public function addSelectOptions(array $options, $selected=null, ?bool $associative=null, bool $for_datalist=false) : Element
 220   {
 221     // Trivial case
 222     if (empty($options))
 223     {
 224       return $this;
 225     }
 226 
 227     if (!isset($associative))
 228     {
 229       $associative = is_assoc($options);
 230     }
 231 
 232     // It's possible to have multiple options selected
 233     if (!is_array($selected))
 234     {
 235       $selected = array($selected);
 236     }
 237 
 238     // Test whether $options is a one-dimensional or two-dimensional array.
 239     // If two-dimensional then we need to use <optgroup>s.
 240     if (is_array(reset($options)))   // cannot use $options[0] because $options may be associative
 241     {
 242       if ($for_datalist)
 243       {
 244         throw new \InvalidArgumentException("Datalists cannot have <optgroup> elements.");
 245       }
 246       foreach ($options as $group => $group_options)
 247       {
 248         $optgroup = new ElementOptgroup();
 249         $optgroup->setAttribute('label', $group)
 250                  ->addSelectOptions($group_options, $selected, $associative);
 251         $this->addElement($optgroup);
 252       }
 253     }
 254     else
 255     {
 256       foreach ($options as $key => $text)
 257       {
 258         $option = new ElementOption();
 259 
 260         // We need to be careful about strings with multiple consecutive spaces in them.  If we have a <select> element
 261         // with simple options of the form <option>Joe  Smith</option>, then the text "Joe  Smith" will be contracted
 262         // to "Joe Smith".  This means that (a) it will look wrong on the form and (b) the wrong value will be passed
 263         // through to the form handler.  One way of getting round this would be to substitute the extra spaces with
 264         // non-breaking space characters.  However, although this will now look correct on the form, the value that is
 265         // passed through to the form handler will contain non-breaking spaces instead of ordinary spaces.  A query
 266         // using this value to find a row in the database will rely on the database engine treating ordinary and non-
 267         // breaking spaces as equivalent. While this will be true for many collations, it won't always be so.
 268         //
 269         // The solution is to place the text as is in the value attribute, but to replace the spaces in the text node
 270         // with non-breaking spaces, eg <option value="Joe  Smith">Joe  Smith</option>.  Because extra spaces in
 271         // attributes are preserved, the correct string will be passed through to the form handler.  And because
 272         // there are now non-breaking spaces in the text node, the string is displayed properly in the browser.  If the
 273         // options are in the form of an associative array with values and text, then the value will be used for the
 274         // value attribute and the text can have its spaces replaced.
 275         //
 276         // This solution doesn't work though for <datalist> elements, at least not when using Chrome or Safari.
 277         // According to https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/datalist "Each <option>
 278         // element should have a value attribute, which represents a suggestion to be entered into the input. It can
 279         // also have a label attribute, or, missing that, some text content, which may be displayed by the browser
 280         // instead of value (Firefox), or in addition to value (Chrome and Safari, as supplemental text). The exact
 281         // content of the drop-down menu depends on the browser, but when clicked, content entered into control field
 282         // will always come from the value attribute."  In other words, if the value and text are different - even in
 283         // the type of space character used - then, when using Chrome and Safari, they are both displayed by the
 284         // browser, which looks a little odd, when they are essentially the same string.
 285         //
 286         // So for <datalist> elements, which are never associative anyway, we just use the value attribute and have an
 287         // empty text node, eg <option value="Joe  Smith"></option>.
 288         //
 289         // See also https://github.com/meeting-room-booking-system/mrbs-code/issues/3871 and
 290         // https://stackoverflow.com/questions/79629259/does-mysql-distinguish-betwen-ordinary-and-non-breaking-spaces-in-a-query
 291 
 292         $value = ($associative) ? $key : $text;
 293         $option->setAttribute('value', $value);
 294 
 295         if (!$for_datalist || $associative)
 296         {
 297           // If it's a string replace the second and subsequent spaces with non-breaking spaces
 298           $text = (is_string($text)) ? preg_replace('/(?<= ) /', "\xc2\xa0", $text) : strval($text);
 299           $option->setText($text);
 300         }
 301 
 302         if (!$for_datalist && in_array($value, $selected))
 303         {
 304           $option->setAttribute('selected');
 305         }
 306 
 307         $this->addElement($option);
 308       }
 309     }
 310 
 311     return $this;
 312   }
 313 
 314 
 315   // $checked is either a scalar or an array of keys that are checked
 316   public function addCheckboxOptions(array $options, string $name, $checked=null, $associative=null, bool $disabled=false): Element
 317   {
 318     // Trivial case
 319     if (empty($options))
 320     {
 321       return $this;
 322     }
 323 
 324     if (is_scalar($checked))
 325     {
 326       $checked = array($checked);
 327     }
 328 
 329     if (!isset($associative))
 330     {
 331       $associative = is_assoc($options);
 332     }
 333 
 334     foreach ($options as $key => $value)
 335     {
 336       if (!$associative)
 337       {
 338         $key = $value;
 339       }
 340       $checkbox = new ElementInputCheckbox();
 341       $checkbox->setAttributes(array('name'  => $name,
 342                                      'value' => $key));
 343       if (isset($checked) && (in_array($key, $checked)))
 344       {
 345         $checkbox->setChecked(true);
 346       }
 347 
 348       if ($disabled)
 349       {
 350         $checkbox->setAttribute('disabled', true);
 351       }
 352 
 353       $label = new ElementLabel();
 354       $label->setText(strval($value))
 355             ->addElement($checkbox);
 356 
 357       $this->addElement($label);
 358     }
 359 
 360     return $this;
 361   }
 362 
 363 
 364   public function addRadioOptions(array $options, string $name, $checked=null, $associative=null, bool $disabled=false): Element
 365   {
 366     // Trivial case
 367     if (empty($options))
 368     {
 369       return $this;
 370     }
 371 
 372     if (!isset($associative))
 373     {
 374       $associative = is_assoc($options);
 375     }
 376 
 377     foreach ($options as $key => $value)
 378     {
 379       if (!$associative)
 380       {
 381         $key = $value;
 382       }
 383       $radio = new ElementInputRadio();
 384       $radio->setAttributes(array('name'     => $name,
 385                                   'value'    => $key,
 386                                   'disabled' => $disabled));
 387       if (isset($checked) && ($key == $checked))
 388       {
 389         $radio->setAttribute('checked');
 390       }
 391       $label = new ElementLabel();
 392       $label->setText(strval($value))
 393             ->addElement($radio);
 394 
 395       $this->addElement($label);
 396     }
 397 
 398     return $this;
 399   }
 400 
 401 
 402   public function render() : void
 403   {
 404     echo $this->toHTML();
 405   }
 406 
 407 
 408   // Turns the form into HTML.   HTML escaping is done here.
 409   // If $no_whitespace is true, then don't put any whitespace after opening or
 410   // closing tags.   This is useful for structures such as
 411   // <label><input>text</label> where whitespace after the <input> tag would
 412   // affect what the browser displays on the screen.
 413   public function toHTML(bool $no_whitespace=false): string
 414   {
 415     $html = "";
 416 
 417     $prev = $this->prev();
 418     if (isset($prev))
 419     {
 420       $html .= $prev->toHTML();
 421     }
 422 
 423     $terminator = ($no_whitespace) ? '' : "\n";
 424     $html .= "<" . $this->tag;
 425 
 426     foreach ($this->attributes as $key => $value)
 427     {
 428       if (!isset($value) || ($value === false))
 429       {
 430         // a boolean attribute, or else an empty attribute, that should be omitted.
 431         // We allow the empty string, '',  because that can be used, for example, in
 432         // 'value=""' as an attribute for the <option> element in a <select> element
 433         // that has the 'required' attribute set.
 434         continue;
 435       }
 436 
 437       $html .= " $key";
 438       if ($value !== true)
 439       {
 440         // boolean attributes, eg 'required', don't need a value
 441         $html .= '="' . escape_html($value) . '"';
 442       }
 443     }
 444 
 445     $html .= ">";
 446 
 447     if ($this->self_closing)
 448     {
 449       $html .= $terminator;
 450     }
 451     else
 452     {
 453       if (isset($this->text) && $this->text_at_start)
 454       {
 455         $html .= self::escapeText($this->text, $this->raw);
 456       }
 457 
 458       if (!empty($this->elements))
 459       {
 460         // If this element contains text, then don't use a terminator, otherwise
 461         // unwanted whitespace will be introduced.
 462         if (!isset($this->text))
 463         {
 464           $html .= $terminator;
 465         }
 466         foreach ($this->elements as $element)
 467         {
 468           $html .= $element->toHTML(isset($this->text));
 469         }
 470       }
 471 
 472       if (isset($this->text) && !$this->text_at_start)
 473       {
 474         $html .= self::escapeText($this->text, $this->raw);
 475       }
 476 
 477       $html .= "</" . $this->tag . ">$terminator";
 478     }
 479 
 480     $next = $this->next();
 481     if (isset($next))
 482     {
 483       $html .= $next->toHTML();
 484     }
 485 
 486     return $html;
 487   }
 488 
 489 
 490   private static function escapeText($text, bool $raw=false)
 491   {
 492     return ($raw) ? $text : escape_html($text);
 493   }
 494 
 495 }

/lib/MRBS/Form/ElementInputDatalist.php

   1 <?php
   2 declare(strict_types=1);
   3 namespace MRBS\Form;
   4 
   5 class ElementInputDatalist extends ElementInput
   6 {
   7   private static $list_prefix = "mrbs_";
   8   private static $list_number = 1;
   9 
  10   public function __construct()
  11   {
  12     // One problem with using a datalist with an input element is the way different browsers
  13     // handle autocomplete.  If you have autocomplete on, and also an id or name attribute, then some
  14     // browsers, eg Edge, will bring the history up on top of the datalist options so that you can't
  15     // see the first few options.  But if you have autocomplete off, then other browsers, eg Chrome,
  16     // will not present the datalist options at all.  This can be fixed in JavaScript by having a second,
  17     // hidden, input which holds the actual form value and mirrors the visible input.  Because we can't
  18     // rely on JavaScript being enabled we will create the basic HTML using autocomplete on, ie the default,
  19     // which is the least bad alternative.   One disadvantage of this method is that the label is no longer
  20     // tied to the visible input, but this isn't as important for a text input as it is, say, for a checkbox
  21     // or radio button.
  22     parent::__construct();
  23 
  24     // Provide a unique id to link the list with the input.
  25     // Doesn't matter what it is as it won't be used elsewhere.
  26     $list_id = self::$list_prefix . self::$list_number;
  27     self::$list_number++;
  28 
  29     $this->setAttributes(array('type' => 'text',
  30                                'list' => $list_id));
  31 
  32     $datalist = new ElementDatalist();
  33     $datalist->setAttribute('id', $list_id);
  34 
  35     $this->next($datalist);
  36   }
  37 
  38 
  39   public function addDatalistOptions(array $options, ?bool $associative=null): ElementInputDatalist
  40   {
  41     // Put a <select> wrapper around the options so that browsers that don't
  42     // support <datalist> will still have the options in their DOM and then
  43     // the JavaScript polyfill can find them and do something with them
  44     $select = new ElementSelect();
  45     $select->addClass('none');
  46     $select->addSelectOptions($options, null, $associative, true);
  47 
  48     $this->next($this->next()->addElement($select));
  49 
  50     return $this;
  51   }
  52 
  53 }

   1 <?php
   2 declare(strict_types=1);
   3 namespace MRBS\Form;
   4 
   5 
   6 // Fields consider of a 'label' element, ie a <label>, and a control
   7 // element, eg an <input> or <select>, all wrapped in a <div>.  For example
   8 //    <div>
   9 //      <label></label>
  10 //      <input>
  11 //    </div>
  12 
  13 abstract class Field extends Element
  14 {
  15   // $is_group records whether the field consists of a group of controls
  16   // (eg radio buttons) or just a single control, in which case a label
  17   // can be associated with it.
  18   protected $is_group = false;
  19 
  20   public function __construct()
  21   {
  22     // Wrap all fields in a <div> ... </div>
  23     parent::__construct('div');
  24     $this->addElement(new ElementLabel(), 'label');
  25   }
  26 
  27 
  28   public function addControl(Element $element): Field
  29   {
  30     $this->addElement($element, 'control');
  31     return $this;
  32   }
  33 
  34 
  35   public function getControl(): Element
  36   {
  37     return $this->getElement('control');
  38   }
  39 
  40 
  41   public function setControl(Element $element): Field
  42   {
  43     $this->setElement('control', $element);
  44     return $this;
  45   }
  46 
  47 
  48   public function removeControl(): Field
  49   {
  50     $this->removeElement('control');
  51     return $this;
  52   }
  53 
  54 
  55   // If $raw is true then the text will not be put through escape_html().  Only to
  56   // be used for trusted text.
  57   public function setLabel($text, bool $text_at_start=false, bool $raw=false): Field
  58   {
  59     $label = $this->getElement('label');
  60     $label->setText($text, $text_at_start, $raw);
  61     $this->setElement('label', $label);
  62     return $this;
  63   }
  64 
  65 
  66   // Sets an attribute for the field control.  Also takes care of the label
  67   // by associating the label with the control using a 'for' attribute, by
  68   // using the 'id' if one is given, or if not, by assuming that the 'id'
  69   // is the same as the 'name' (unless $add_id is FALSE, in which case an id
  70   // won't be added).
  71   public function setControlAttribute(string $name, $value=true, bool $add_id=true): Field
  72   {
  73     $elements = $this->getElements();
  74 
  75     // If this is the name attribute and we haven't yet got an id, then
  76     // make the id the same as the name - unless $add_id is FALSE
  77     if ($add_id && ($name == 'name') && (null === $elements['control']->getAttribute('id')))
  78     {
  79       $this->setControlAttribute('id', $value);
  80     }
  81 
  82     // If this is an id and it's not a group field, then associate the
  83     // label with the id
  84     if (!$this->is_group && ($name == 'id'))
  85     {
  86       $elements['label']->setAttribute('for', $value);
  87     }
  88 
  89     $elements['control']->setAttribute($name, $value);
  90 
  91     $this->setElements($elements);
  92     return $this;
  93   }
  94 
  95 
  96   // Sets the attributes for the field control.
  97   public function setControlAttributes(array $attributes, bool $add_id=true): Field
  98   {
  99     foreach ($attributes as $key => $value)
 100     {
 101       $this->setControlAttribute($key, $value, $add_id);
 102     }
 103     return $this;
 104   }
 105 
 106 
 107   public function addControlClass(string $class): Field
 108   {
 109     $elements = $this->getElements();
 110     $elements['control']->addClass($class);
 111     $this->setElements($elements);
 112     return $this;
 113   }
 114 
 115 
 116   public function addLabelClass(string $class): Field
 117   {
 118     $elements = $this->getElements();
 119     $elements['label']->addClass($class);
 120     $this->setElements($elements);
 121     return $this;
 122   }
 123 
 124 
 125   public function setControlChecked($checked=true): Field
 126   {

   1 <?php
   2 declare(strict_types=1);
   3 namespace MRBS\Form;
   4 
   5 use MRBS\Errors\Errors;
   6 use MRBS\Exception;
   7 use function MRBS\generate_token;
   8 use function MRBS\get_form_var;
   9 use function MRBS\get_vocab;
  10 use function MRBS\session;
  11 
  12 
  13 class Form extends Element
  14 {
  15   public const METHOD_GET = 0;
  16   public const METHOD_POST = 1;
  17   private const TOKEN_NAME = 'csrf_token';
  18 
  19   private static $token = null;
  20   private static $cookie_set = false;
  21 
  22 
  23   // Creates a new form, automatically adding a CSRF token and a MAX_FILE_SIZE value
  24   // as hidden inputs if the method is POST.  The GET method should only be used for
  25   // navigating between pages and not for submitting form data which could change the
  26   // database contents or reveal data to which the user is not entitled.
  27   public function __construct(int $method=self::METHOD_GET)
  28   {
  29     parent::__construct('form');
  30     $this->setMethod($method);
  31   }
  32 
  33 
  34   // Sets the form method.  If the method is POST then a CSRF token and a MAX_FILE_SIZE
  35   // value are also added as hidden inputs.  If the method is GET then these hidden
  36   // inputs are removed because, in the case of the CSRF token we don't want it to
  37   // appear in the URL for security reasons, and in the case of MAX_FILE_SIZE it should
  38   // only be needed for POST requests.
  39   // TODO: if this method is called after the constructor then make sure the MAX_FILE_SIZE
  40   // TODO: hidden input is at the beginning, before any possible file input elements.
  41   private function setMethod(int $method) : Element
  42   {
  43     if ($method === self::METHOD_GET)
  44     {
  45       $this->removeHiddenInput('MAX_FILE_SIZE');
  46       $this->removeHiddenInput(self::TOKEN_NAME);
  47     }
  48 
  49     elseif ($method === self::METHOD_POST)
  50     {
  51       // Add a MAX_FILE_SIZE hidden input for use by forms that have a file
  52       // upload input.  This hidden input must come before the file input
  53       // element if it is to be used by PHP. Although at the time of writing
  54       // it is not used by any browsers, we can add some JavaScript to check
  55       // the file size when it is selected and thus save a failed upload attempt.
  56       $max_file_size = ini_get('upload_max_filesize');
  57       if ($max_file_size !== false)
  58       {
  59         $max_file_size = self::convertToBytes($max_file_size);
  60         $this->addHiddenInput('MAX_FILE_SIZE', $max_file_size, 'MAX_FILE_SIZE');
  61       }
  62       // Add a CSRF token
  63       $this->addCSRFToken();
  64     }
  65 
  66     return parent::setAttribute('method', self::methodToString($method));
  67   }
  68 
  69 
  70   // Converts a method string (eg 'get' or 'GET') to a method constant (eg self::METHOD_GET)
  71   private static function methodToInt(string $string) : int
  72   {
  73     if (strcasecmp($string, 'get') === 0)
  74     {
  75       return self::METHOD_GET;
  76     }
  77 
  78     if (strcasecmp($string, 'post') === 0)
  79     {
  80       return self::METHOD_POST;
  81     }
  82 
  83     throw new Exception("Unsupported method $string");
  84   }
  85 
  86 
  87   // Converts a method constant (eg self::METHOD_GET) to a method string (eg 'get')
  88   private static function methodToString(int $int) : string
  89   {
  90     if ($int === self::METHOD_GET)
  91     {
  92       return 'get';
  93     }
  94 
  95     if ($int === self::METHOD_POST)
  96     {
  97       return 'post';
  98     }
  99 
 100     throw new Exception("Unsupported method constant $int");
 101   }
 102 
 103 
 104   // Sets a form attribute, taking special action in the case of the
 105   // method attribute to set/unset the CSRF token and MAX_FILE_SIZE
 106   // hidden inputs.  Can cope with either string or integer method values.
 107   public function setAttribute(string $name, $value=true): Element
 108   {
 109     if (strcasecmp($name, 'method') === 0)
 110     {
 111       if (is_string($value))
 112       {
 113         $value = self::methodToInt($value);
 114       }
 115       if ($value === self::METHOD_POST)
 116       {
 117         $message = "Changing the form method after the form has been created may result " .
 118                    "in the MAX_FILE_SIZE hidden input coming after a file input, thus " .
 119                    "making it unusable by the server.";
 120         trigger_error($message, E_USER_WARNING);
 121       }
 122       return $this->setMethod($value);
 123     }
 124 
 125     return parent::setAttribute($name, $value);
 126   }
 127 
 128 
 129   // Adds a hidden input to the form.  Optionally give the element a key
 130   // so that it can be removed later using the same key.
 131   public function addHiddenInput(string $name, $value, ?string $key=null) : Form
 132   {
 133     $element = new ElementInputHidden($name, $value);
 134     $this->addElement($element, $key);
 135     return $this;
 136   }
 137 
 138 
 139   // Adds an array of hidden inputs to the form
 140   public function addHiddenInputs(array $hidden_inputs) : Form
 141   {
 142     foreach ($hidden_inputs as $key => $value)
 143     {
 144       $this->addHiddenInput($key, $value);
 145     }
 146     return $this;
 147   }
 148 
 149 
 150   // Removes a hidden input from the form.
 151   private function removeHiddenInput(string $key) : Form
 152   {
 153     $this->removeElement($key);
 154     return $this;
 155   }
 156 
 157 
 158   // Returns the HTML for a hidden field containing a CSRF token
 159   public static function getTokenHTML() : string
 160   {
 161     $element = new ElementInputHidden();
 162     $element->setAttributes(array('name'  => self::TOKEN_NAME,
 163                                   'value' => self::getToken()));
 164     return $element->toHTML();
 165   }
 166 
 167 
 168   // Checks the CSRF token against the stored value and dies with a fatal error
 169   // if they do not match.   Note that:
 170   //    (1) The CSRF token is always looked for in the POST data, never anywhere else.
 171   //        GET requests should only be used for operations that do not modify data or
 172   //        grant access.
 173   //    (2) Forms should normally use a POST method.
 174   //    (3) Actions should normally be taken by handler pages which are not designed to be
 175   //        accessed directly by the user and are only expecting POST requests.  These pages
 176   //        will look for the CSRF token however they are requested.  If they are requested via
 177   //        GET then they will still look for the token in the POST data and so fail.
 178   //    (4) There are some MRBS pages that can be accessed either via a URL with query string,
 179   //        or via a POST request.   These pages should not take any action, but as a matter of
 180   //        good practice should check the token anyway if they have been requested by a POST.
 181   //        To cater for these pages the $post_only parameter should be set to TRUE.
 182   public static function checkToken(bool $post_only=false) : void
 183   {
 184     global $server;
 185 
 186     if ($post_only && ($server['REQUEST_METHOD'] != 'POST'))
 187     {
 188       return;
 189     }
 190 
 191     $token = get_form_var(self::TOKEN_NAME, 'string', null, INPUT_POST);
 192     $stored_token = self::getStoredToken();
 193 
 194     if (!self::compareTokens($stored_token, $token))
 195     {
 196       if (isset($stored_token))
 197       {
 198         // Only report a possible CSRF attack if the stored token exists.   If it doesn't
 199         // it's normally because the user session has expired in between the form being
 200         // displayed and submitted.
 201         trigger_error('Possible CSRF attack from IP address ' . $server['REMOTE_ADDR'], E_USER_NOTICE);
 202       }
 203 
 204       if (method_exists(session(), 'logoffUser'))
 205       {
 206         session()->logoffUser();
 207       }
 208 
 209       Errors::fatalError(get_vocab("session_expired"));
 210     }
 211   }
 212 
 213 
 214   // $max_unit can be set to 'seconds', 'minutes', 'hours', etc. and
 215   // can be used to specify the maximum unit to return.
 216   public static function getTimeUnitOptions($max_unit=null) : array
 217   {
 218     $options = array();
 219     $units = array('seconds', 'minutes', 'hours', 'days', 'weeks');
 220 
 221     foreach ($units as $unit)
 222     {
 223       $options[$unit] = get_vocab($unit);
 224       if (isset($max_unit) && ($max_unit == $unit))
 225       {
 226         break;
 227       }
 228     }
 229     return $options;
 230   }
 231 
 232 
 233   private function addCSRFToken() : Form
 234   {
 235     $this->addHiddenInput(self::TOKEN_NAME, self::getToken(), self::TOKEN_NAME);
 236     return $this;
 237   }
 238 
 239 
 240   // Get a CSRF token
 241   public static function getToken() : string
 242   {
 243     $token_length = 32;
 244 
 245     if (!isset(self::$token))
 246     {
 247       $stored_token = self::getStoredToken();
 248       // The test below should really be isset() rather than !empty().  However occasionally MRBS has the
 249       // value 0 stored in the session variable.  It's not clear how or why this is happening.  Until the
 250       // root cause is found we test for empty() and if the token is set but empty we generate a new token.
 251       // Update: it seems that when the token is 0, so are all the other session variables.  So the problem
 252       // is probably not in the form code, but elsewhere.
 253       if (!empty($stored_token))
 254       {
 255         self::$token = $stored_token;
 256       }
 257       else
 258       {
 259         if (isset($stored_token))
 260         {
 261           // The token is set but empty
 262           $message = "Stored token is '$stored_token'.  This should not be possible. " .
 263                      "Generating a new token.";
 264           trigger_error($message,E_USER_WARNING);
 265         }
 266         self::$token = generate_token($token_length);
 267         self::storeToken(self::$token);
 268       }
 269     }
 270 
 271     return self::$token;
 272   }
 273 
 274 
 275   // Compare two tokens in a timing attack safe manner.
 276   // Returns true if they are equal, otherwise false.
 277   // Note: it is important to provide the user-supplied string as the
 278   // second parameter, rather than the first.
 279   private static function compareTokens($known_token, $user_token) : bool
 280   {
 281     if (is_null($known_token) || is_null($user_token))
 282     {
 283       return false;
 284     }
 285 
 286     if (function_exists('hash_equals'))
 287     {
 288       return hash_equals($known_token, $user_token);
 289     }
 290 
 291     // Could do fancier things here to give a timing attack safe comparison,
 292     // For example https://github.com/indigophp/hash-compat
 293     return ($known_token === $user_token);
 294   }
 295 
 296 
 297   private static function storeToken($token) : void
 298   {
 299     session()->set(self::TOKEN_NAME, $token);
 300   }
 301 
 302 
 303   private static function getStoredToken() : ?string
 304   {
 305     $result = session()->get(self::TOKEN_NAME);
 306 
 307     // For some unknown reason the integer value 0 is sometimes stored in the session
 308     // variable.  It's not clear how this can happen.
 309     if (isset($result) && !is_string($result))
 310     {
 311       trigger_error("Stored token is of type " . gettype($result) . ", value $result", E_USER_WARNING);
 312       $result = strval($result);
 313     }
 314 
 315     return $result;
 316   }
 317 
 318 
 319   // Convert a file size to bytes
 320   // See https://www.php.net/manual/en/faq.using.php#faq.using.shorthandbytes
 321   private static function convertToBytes(string $size) : int
 322   {
 323     // Split the size into value and units (if any)
 324     $values = preg_split('/(?<=[0-9])(?=[^0-9]+)/i', $size);
 325 
 326     if (count($values) == 2)
 327     {
 328       $result = intval($values[0]);
 329       switch ($values[1])
 330       {
 331         case 'G':
 332           $result = 1024 * $result;
 333           // Fall through
 334         case 'M':
 335           $result = 1024 * $result;
 336           // Fall through
 337         case 'K':
 338           $result = 1024 * $result;
 339           return $result;
 340           break;
 341         default:
 342           // Unrecognised suffix
 343           break;
 344       }
 345     }
 346 
 347     return intval($size);
 348   }
 349 
 350 }
