   3 namespace MRBS\Intl;
   4 
   5 // An interface for converting ICU datetime patterns to another format, eg strftime
   6 interface Formatter
   7 {
   8   // Convert an ICU pattern token into the nearest equivalent token.
   9   // Throws an exception if the token can't be converted.
  10   public function convert(string $token) : string;
  11 
  12   public function escape(string $char) : string;
  13 }

/lib/MRBS/Intl/FormatterStrftime.php

   1 <?php
   2 declare(strict_types=1);
   3 namespace MRBS\Intl;
   4 
   5 class FormatterStrftime implements Formatter
   6 {
   7   // Convert an ICU pattern token into the nearest equivalent token.
   8   // Throws an exception if the token can't be converted.
   9   public function convert(string $token) : string
  10   {
  11     switch ($token) {
  12       // AM or PM
  13       case 'a':       // PM [abbrev]
  14       case 'aa':      // PM [abbrev]
  15       case 'aaa':     // PM [abbrev]
  16       case 'aaaa':    // PM [wide]
  17       case 'aaaaa':   // p
  18         // am, pm, noon, midnight
  19       case 'b':       // mid.
  20       case 'bb':      // mid.
  21       case 'bbb':     // mid.
  22       case 'bbbb':    // midnight
  23       case 'bbbbb':   // md
  24         // flexible day periods
  25       case 'B':       // at night [abbrev]
  26       case 'BB':      // at night [abbrev]
  27       case 'BBB':     // at night [abbrev]
  28       case 'BBBB':    // at night [wide]
  29       case 'BBBBB':   // at night [narrow]
  30         $format = '%P';  // lower-case 'am' or 'pm' based on the given time
  31         break;
  32 
  33       // stand-alone local day of week
  34       case 'cccc':    // Tuesday
  35         // day of week
  36       case 'EEEE':    // Tuesday
  37         // local day of week
  38       case 'eeee':    // Tuesday
  39         $format = '%A';  // A full textual representation of the day, eg Sunday through Saturday
  40         break;
  41 
  42       // stand-alone local day of week
  43       case 'ccc':     // Tue
  44       case 'ccccc':   // T
  45       case 'cccccc':  // Tu
  46         // day of week
  47       case 'E':       // Tue
  48       case 'EE':      // Tue
  49       case 'EEE':     // Tue
  50       case 'EEEEE':   // T
  51       case 'EEEEEE':  // Tu
  52         // local day of week
  53       case 'eee':     // Tue
  54       case 'eeeee':   // T
  55       case 'eeeeee':  // Tu
  56         $format = '%a';   // An abbreviated textual representation of the day, eg Sun through Sat
  57         break;
  58 
  59       // day in month
  60       case 'd':       // 2
  61         $format = '%i';   // One/two digit day of the month, eg 1 to 31
  62         break;
  63 
  64       // day in month
  65       case 'dd':      // 02
  66         $format = '%d';   // Two-digit day of the month (with leading zeros), eg 01 to 31
  67         break;
  68 
  69       // day of year
  70       case 'D':       // 189
  71         $format = '%E';   // Day of the year without leading zeroes
  72         break;
  73 
  74       // hour in day (0~23)
  75       case 'H':       // 0
  76         $format = '%k';   // Hour in 24-hour format, with a space preceding single digits, eg 0 through 23
  77         break;
  78 
  79       // hour in day (0~23)
  80       case 'HH':      // 00
  81         $format = '%H';   // Two digit representation of the hour in 24-hour format, eg 00 through 23
  82         break;
  83 
  84       // hour in am/pm (1~12)
  85       case 'h':       // 7
  86         $format = '%o';   // Hour in 12-hour format, with no space preceding single digits
  87         break;
  88 
  89       // hour in am/pm (1~12)
  90       case 'hh':      // 07
  91         $format = '%I';   // Two digit representation of the hour in 12-hour format, eg 01 through 12
  92         break;
  93 
  94       // stand-alone month in year
  95       case 'L':       // 9
  96         // month in year
  97       case 'M':       // 9
  98         $format = '%f';   // One/two digit representation of the month, eg 1 (for January) through 12 (for December)
  99         break;
 100 
 101       // stand-alone month in year
 102       case 'LL':      // 09
 103         // month in year
 104       case 'MM':      // 09
 105         $format = '%m';   // Two digit representation of the month, eg 01 (for January) through 12 (for December)
 106         break;
 107 
 108       // stand-alone month in year
 109       case 'LLL':     // Sep
 110         // month in year
 111       case 'MMM':     // Sep
 112         $format = '%b';   // Abbreviated month name, based on the locale, eg Jan through Dec
 113         break;
 114 
 115       // stand-alone month in year
 116       case 'LLLL':    // September
 117         // month in year
 118       case 'MMMM':    // September
 119         $format = '%B';   // Full month name, based on the locale, eg January through December
 120         break;
 121 
 122       // minute in hour
 123       case 'm':       // 4
 124         $format = '%q';   // Minute in the hour, with no leading zero
 125         break;
 126 
 127       // minute in hour
 128       case 'mm':      // 04
 129         $format = '%M';   // Minute in the hour, with leading zeroes
 130         break;
 131 
 132       // second in minute
 133       case 's':       // 5
 134         $format = '%v';   // Seconds, with no leading zeroes
 135         break;
 136 
 137       // second in minute
 138       case 'ss':      // 05
 139         $format = '%S';   // Two digit representation of the second, eg 00 through 59
 140         break;
 141 
 142       // week of year
 143       // The ICU documentation isn't very clear what is meant by "week of year", but it seems to be locale
 144       // dependent. In many locales it is the ISO week number, but in some locales it isn't.  It (partly?)
 145       // depends on the locale's first day of the week, which can be got from IntlCalendar::getFirstDayOfWeek().
 146       case 'w':       // 7
 147         $format = '%J';   // ISO-8601:1988 week number of the given year without leading zeroes, eg 1 through 53
 148         break;
 149 
 150       case 'ww':      // 07
 151         $format = '%V';   // ISO-8601:1988 week number of the given year, eg 01 through 53
 152         break;
 153 
 154       // year
 155       case 'y':       // 1996
 156       case 'yyyy':    // 1996
 157         $format = '%Y';   // Four digit representation for the year, eg 2038
 158         break;
 159 
 160       // year
 161       case 'yy':      // 96
 162         $format = '%y';   // Two digit representation of the year, eg 09 for 2009, 79 for 1979
 163         break;
 164 
 165       // Time Zone: specific non-location
 166       case 'z':       // PDT
 167       case 'zz':      // PDT
 168       case 'zzz':     // PDT
 169       case 'zzzz':    // Pacific Daylight Time
 170         $format = '%Z';   // The time zone abbreviation, eg EST for Eastern Time
 171         break;            // Windows: The %z and %Z modifiers both return the time zone name instead of the offset or abbreviation
 172 
 173       default:
 174         throw new \MRBS\Exception("Could not convert '$token'");
 175         break;
 176     }
 177 
 178     return $format;
 179   }
 180 
 181 
 182   public function escape(string $char): string
 183   {
 184     switch ($char)
 185     {
 186       case "\n":
 187         return '%n';
 188         break;
 189       case "\t":
 190         return '%t';
 191         break;
 192       case "%":
 193         return '%%';
 194         break;
 195       default:
 196         return $char;
 197         break;
 198     }
 199   }
 200 }

   5 // A class provides a basic emulation of PHP's IntlDateFormatter class.
   6 //
   7 // The emulation uses the deprecated function strftime() and is only necessary for older
   8 // PHP systems where the Intl extension isn't available.  Eventually the emulation can be
   9 // dispensed with.
  10 //

  12 // easily.  In those cases better results can sometimes be achieved by using strftime() and
  13 // this can be forced by explicitly using this class.

  15 use DateTimeInterface;

  19 use function MRBS\get_mrbs_locale;

  22 // We need to check that the 'intl' extension is loaded because earlier versions of

  24 // have upgraded by just overwriting files without deleting that file, then it will
  25 // be picked up by the class_exists() test and used instead of the more up-to-date
  26 // emulation below.

  28 // Note that there is a polyfill for IntlDateFormatter available at
  29 // https://github.com/symfony/polyfill-intl-icu, but it is limited to the 'en' locale.
  30 // There are also backwards compatibility versions of strftime() available, but
  31 // IntlDateFormatter is a more powerful solution.
  32 class IntlDateFormatter
  33 {
  34   const FULL = 0;
  35   const LONG = 1;
  36   const MEDIUM = 2;
  37   const SHORT = 3;
  38   const NONE = -1;
  39   const RELATIVE_FULL = 128; // Available as of PHP 8.0.0, for dateType only
  40   const RELATIVE_LONG = 129; // Available as of PHP 8.0.0, for dateType only
  41   const RELATIVE_MEDIUM = 130; // Available as of PHP 8.0.0, for dateType only
  42   const RELATIVE_SHORT = 131; // Available as of PHP 8.0.0, for dateType only
  43   const GREGORIAN = 1;
  44   const TRADITIONAL = 0;
  45 
  46 
  47   private const TYPE_NAMES = array(
  48     self::FULL => 'full',
  49     self::LONG => 'long',
  50     self::MEDIUM => 'medium',
  51     self::SHORT => 'short',
  52     self::NONE => 'none'
  53   );
  54 
  55   private const DEFAULT_LOCALE = 'en';
  56 
  57   private $locale;
  58   private $dateType;
  59   private $timeType;
  60   private $timezone;

  62   private $pattern;

  64   public function __construct(

  66     int     $dateType = self::FULL,
  67     int     $timeType = self::FULL,
  68             $timezone = null,
  69             $calendar = null,
  70     ?string $pattern = null)

  74       throw new Exception("Neither the IntlDateFormatter class nor the strftime() function exist on this server");

 180 // Format a local time/date according to locale settings, returning the
 181 // result as a UTF-8 string.  This function is based on strftime()
 182 // $time can be an int or a float (union type declarations not supported until PHP 8.0)
 183 // $locale can either be a string or an array of locales.  If $locale
 184 // is not set then the current locale is used.
 185 //
 186 // This method extends the standard PHP strftime() function and adds extra formats:
 187 //
 188 //  %f  Numeric representation of the month 	      1 (for January) through 12 (for December)
 189 //      without leading zeroes.  Won't
 190 //      necessarily work in locales that don't
 191 //      use [0..9] for the month.
 192 //
 193 //  %i  One/two digit day of the month, with no     1 to 31
 194 //      leading space
 195 //
 196 //  %o  Hour in 12-hour format, with no space       1 through 12
 197 //      preceding single digits
 198 //
 199 //  %q  Minute in the hour, with no leading zero    4
 200 //
 201 //  %v  Seconds, with no leading zero
 202 //
 203 //  %E  Day of year, with no leading zeroes
 204   private function strftimePlus(string $format, int $timestamp): string
 205   {
 206     $server_os = System::getServerOS();
 207 
 208     // Set the temporary locale.  Note that $this->locale could be an array of locales,
 209     // so we need to find out which locale actually worked.
 210     if (!empty($this->locale)) {
 211       $old_locale = setlocale(LC_TIME, '0');
 212       if (false === ($new_locale = setlocale(LC_TIME, System::getOSlocale($this->locale))))
 213       {
 214         $new_locale = $old_locale;
 215         $locale = is_array($this->locale) ? json_encode($this->locale) : "'$this->locale'";
 216         $message = "Could not set locale to $locale; continuing to use '$old_locale'";
 217         trigger_error($message, E_USER_WARNING);
 218       }
 219     }
 220     elseif ($server_os == "windows") {
 221       // If we are running Windows we have to set the locale again in case another script
 222       // running in the same process has changed the locale since we first set it.  See the
 223       // warning on the PHP manual page for setlocale():
 224       //
 225       // "The locale information is maintained per process, not per thread. If you are
 226       // running PHP on a multithreaded server API like IIS or Apache on Windows, you may
 227       // experience sudden changes in locale settings while a script is running, though
 228       // the script itself never called setlocale(). This happens due to other scripts
 229       // running in different threads of the same process at the same time, changing the
 230       // process-wide locale using setlocale()."
 231       $new_locale = get_mrbs_locale();
 232       set_mrbs_locale($new_locale);
 233     }
 234     else {
 235       $new_locale = null;
 236     }
 237 
 238     $result = self::doStrftimePlus($format, $timestamp, $new_locale);
 239 
 240     // Restore the original locale
 241     if (!empty($this->locale)) {
 242       setlocale(LC_TIME, $old_locale);
 243     }
 244 
 245     return $result;
 246   }
 247 
 248 
 249   // Wrapper for strftime()
 250   private static function doStrftime(string $format, ?int $timestamp = null)
 251   {
 252     // Temporarily suppress deprecation errors so that we are not flooded with them.
 253     // We have a single message in init.inc.
 254     $error_level = error_reporting();
 255     error_reporting($error_level & ~E_DEPRECATED);
 256     $result = strftime($format, $timestamp);
 257     error_reporting($error_level);
 258 
 259     return $result;
 260   }
 261 
 262 
 263   private static function doStrftimePlus(string $format, int $timestamp, ?string $locale): string
 264   {
 265     $server_os = System::getServerOS();
 266 
 267     if ($server_os == "windows") {
 268       // Some formats not supported on Windows.   Replace with suitable alternatives
 269       $format = str_replace("%R", "%H:%M", $format);
 270       $format = str_replace("%P", "%p", $format);
 271       $format = str_replace("%l", "%I", $format);
 272       $format = str_replace("%e", "%#d", $format);
 273     }
 274 
 275     // %p doesn't actually work in some locales, we have to patch it up ourselves
 276     if (preg_match('/%p/', $format)) {
 277       $ampm = self::doStrftime('%p', $timestamp);
 278       if ($ampm == '') {
 279         $ampm = date('a', $timestamp);
 280       }
 281 
 282       $format = preg_replace('/%p/', $ampm, $format);
 283     }
 284 
 285     $result = '';
 286 
 287     // Split the format into individual tokens so that we can process our extensions
 288     $tokens = self::parseStrftimeFormat($format);
 289 
 290     foreach ($tokens as $token) {
 291       if (mb_strlen($token) === 1) {
 292         $result .= $token;
 293       }
 294       else {
 295         switch ($token) {
 296           case '%E':
 297             // We want the day of the year without leading zeroes.
 298             $formatted = self::doStrftimePlus('%j', $timestamp, $locale);
 299             $formatted = ltrim($formatted, '0');
 300             break;
 301           case '%f':
 302             // We want a month number without leading zeroes.  We can't use date('n', $time)
 303             // because date will return an English answer with a month made up of the characters
 304             // [0..9] which won't be correct for all locales.
 305             $formatted = self::doStrftimePlus('%m', $timestamp, $locale);
 306             $formatted = ($formatted === '00') ? '0' : ltrim($formatted, '0');
 307             break;
 308           case '%i':
 309             $formatted = ltrim(self::doStrftimePlus('%e', $timestamp, $locale));
 310             break;
 311           case '%J':
 312             // We want the week of the year without leading zeroes.
 313             $formatted = self::doStrftimePlus('%V', $timestamp, $locale);
 314             $formatted = ltrim($formatted, '0');
 315             break;
 316           case '%o':
 317             $formatted = ltrim(self::doStrftimePlus('%l', $timestamp, $locale));
 318             break;
 319           case '%q':
 320             // We want a minute without leading zeroes.
 321             $formatted = self::doStrftimePlus('%M', $timestamp, $locale);
 322             $formatted = ($formatted === '00') ? '0' : ltrim($formatted, '0');
 323             break;
 324           case '%v':
 325             // We want seconds without leading zeroes.
 326             $formatted = self::doStrftimePlus('%S', $timestamp, $locale);
 327             $formatted = ($formatted === '00') ? '0' : ltrim($formatted, '0');
 328             break;
 329           default:
 330             $formatted = self::doStrftime($token, $timestamp);
 331             break;
 332         }
 333         $result .= System::utf8ConvertFromLocale($formatted, $locale);
 334       }
 335     }
 336 
 337     return $result;
 338   }
 339 
 340 
 341   // Parses a strftime format into an array of strings, which will either be two or three-character
 342   // formats or one-character text strings.
 343   private static function parseStrftimeFormat(string $format): array
 344   {
 345     $result = array();
 346 
 347     // Split the format into an array of multibyte characters
 348     $chars = preg_split("//u", $format, 0, PREG_SPLIT_NO_EMPTY);
 349 
 350     while (null !== ($char = array_shift($chars))) {
 351       if ($char !== '%') {
 352         // It's ordinary text
 353         $result[] = $char;
 354       }
 355       else {
 356         // Get the next character which will either be a conversion specifier or an escaped character
 357         $char = array_shift($chars);
 358         switch ($char) {
 359           case null:
 360             throw new Exception("Invalid format '$format'");
 361             break;
 362           case 'n':
 363             $result[] = "\n";
 364             break;
 365           case 't':
 366             $result[] = "\t";
 367             break;
 368           case '%':
 369             $result[] = "%";
 370             break;
 371           case '#':
 372             // This covers the case of '%#d' on Windows
 373             $char = array_shift($chars);
 374             if (!isset($char)) {
 375               throw new Exception("Invalid format '$format'");
 376             }
 377             else {
 378               $result [] = "%#$char";
 379             }
 380             break;
 381           default:
 382             $result [] = "%$char";
 383             break;
 384         }
 385       }
 386     }
 387 
 388     return $result;
 389   }
 390 
 391 }

   2 // Note that we cannot use strict types here as some early versions of PHP (eg 7.2.34) throw
   3 // a TypeError if null is passed as the sixth parameter to \IntlDateFormatter::_construct(),
   4 // despite the signature on the manual page.
   5 // declare(strict_types=1);
   6 namespace MRBS\Intl;
   7 
   8 // A factory class for creating either an instance of \IntlDateFormatter or \MRBS\Intl\IntlDateFormatter,
   9 // depending on the setting of the $force_strftime config variable.
  10 class IntlDateFormatterFactory
  11 {
  12   public static function create(
  13     ?string $locale,
  14     int     $dateType = \IntlDateFormatter::FULL,
  15     int     $timeType = \IntlDateFormatter::FULL,
  16             $timezone = null,
  17             $calendar = null,
  18     ?string $pattern = null)
  19   {
  20     global $force_strftime;
  21 
  22     if ($force_strftime)
  23     {
  24       // This will return an instance of the emulation
  25       return new IntlDateFormatter($locale, $dateType, $timeType, $timezone, $calendar, $pattern);
  26     }
  27     else
  28     {
  29       // This will return an instance of the standard PHP class if the 'intl' extension is loaded,
  30       // otherwise an instance of the emulation
  31       return new \IntlDateFormatter($locale, $dateType, $timeType, $timezone, $calendar, $pattern);
  32     }
  33   }
  34 
  35 }

/lib/MRBS/Intl/IntlDatePatternConverter.php

   1 <?php
   2 declare(strict_types=1);
   3 namespace MRBS\Intl;
   4 
   5 class IntlDatePatternConverter
   6 {
   7   private const QUOTE_CHAR = "'";
   8 
   9   private $formatter;
  10 
  11   public function __construct(Formatter $formatter)
  12   {
  13     $this->formatter = $formatter;
  14   }
  15 
  16 
  17   public function convert(string $pattern) : string
  18   {
  19     // Parse the pattern
  20     // See https://unicode-org.github.io/icu/userguide/format_parse/datetime/
  21     // "Note: Any characters in the pattern that are not in the ranges of [‘a’..’z’] and
  22     // [‘A’..’Z’] will be treated as quoted text. For instance, characters like ':', '.',
  23     // ' ', '#' and '@' will appear in the resulting time text even they are not enclosed
  24     // within single quotes. The single quote is used to ‘escape’ letters. Two single
  25     // quotes in a row, whether inside or outside a quoted sequence, represent a ‘real’
  26     // single quote."
  27     $format = '';
  28     $token = '';
  29     $token_char = null;
  30     $in_quotes = false;
  31     // Split the string into an array of multibyte characters
  32     $chars = preg_split("//u", $pattern, 0, PREG_SPLIT_NO_EMPTY);
  33 
  34     while (null !== ($char = array_shift($chars)))
  35     {
  36       $is_token_char = !$in_quotes && preg_match("/^[a-z]$/i", $char);
  37       if ($is_token_char)
  38       {
  39         // The start of a token
  40         if (!isset($token_char))
  41         {
  42           $token_char = $char;
  43           $token = $char;
  44         }
  45         // The continuation of a token
  46         elseif ($char === $token_char)
  47         {
  48           $token .= $char;
  49         }
  50         // The end of a token and the beginning of a new one
  51         else
  52         {
  53           $format .= $this->formatter->convert($token);
  54           $token_char = $char;
  55           $token = $char;
  56         }
  57       }
  58       // Check to see if a token has just ended, ie we've either got
  59       // a non-token character or there are no more characters left.
  60       if (($token !== '') && (!$is_token_char || empty($chars)))
  61       {
  62         $format .= $this->formatter->convert($token);
  63         $token = '';
  64         $token_char = null;
  65       }
  66 
  67       // Quoted text
  68       if (!$is_token_char)
  69       {
  70         // If it's not a quote just add the character to the format
  71         if ($char !== self::QUOTE_CHAR)
  72         {
  73           $format .= $this->formatter->escape($char);
  74         }
  75         // Otherwise we have to work out whether the quote is the start or end of a
  76         // quoted sequence, or part of an escaped quote
  77         else
  78         {
  79           // Get the next character
  80           $char = array_shift($chars);
  81           if (isset($char))
  82           {
  83             // If it is a quote then it's an escaped quote and add it to the format
  84             if ($char === self::QUOTE_CHAR)
  85             {
  86               $format .= $this->formatter->escape($char);
  87             }
  88             // Otherwise it's either the start or end of a quoted section.
  89             // Toggle $in_quotes and add the character to the format if we're in quotes,
  90             // or else replace it so that it gets handled properly next time round.
  91             else
  92             {
  93               $in_quotes = !$in_quotes;
  94               if ($in_quotes)
  95               {
  96                 $format .= $this->formatter->escape($char);
  97               }
  98               else
  99               {
 100                 array_unshift($chars, $char);
 101               }
 102             }
 103           }
 104         }
 105       }
 106     }
 107 
 108     return $format;
 109   }
 110 
 111 }

   2 declare(strict_types=1);
   3 namespace MRBS\Intl;
   4 
   5 // A partial emulation of the \Locale class.   We use the emulation because
   6 //  (a) the standard class in the intl extension has some bugs in it, in particular when using
   7 //      Locale::acceptFromHttp('zh-TW') [See https://www.php.net/manual/en/locale.acceptfromhttp.php#122623]
   8 //      [See also https://sourceforge.net/p/mrbs/support-requests/2178/]
   9 //  (b) the intl extension isn't enabled on all sites.
  10 //
  11 // If \Locale were working properly then one possibility would be to add conditional code as for the
  12 // other MRBS\Intl classes, do that the emulation is only a fallback if the PHP class doesn't exist eg
  13 /*
  14 if (class_exists('\Locale') && extension_loaded('intl'))
  15 {
  16   class Locale extends \Locale
  17   {
  18   }
  19 }
  20 else
  21 {
  22   class Locale
  23   {
  24     // this code
  25   }
  26 }
  27 */
  28 
  29 use InvalidArgumentException;
  30 use MRBS\System;
  31 use function MRBS\get_qualifiers;
  32 
  33 class Locale
  34 {
  35   const LANG_TAG               = 'language';
  36   const EXTLANG_TAG            = 'extlang';
  37   const SCRIPT_TAG             = 'script';
  38   const REGION_TAG             = 'region';
  39   const VARIANT_TAG            = 'variant';
  40   const GRANDFATHERED_LANG_TAG = 'grandfathered';
  41   const PRIVATE_TAG            = 'private';
  42   const ACTUAL_LOCALE = 0;
  43   const VALID_LOCALE = 1;
  44 
  45 
  46   /**
  47    * Tries to find out best available locale based on HTTP "Accept-Language" header.
  48    *
  49    * @return string|false the corresponding locale identifier, or FALSE if none found
  50    */
  51   public static function acceptFromHttp(string $header)
  52   {
  53     $accept_languages = self::toSortedArray($header);
  54 
  55     foreach($accept_languages as $accept_language => $value)
  56     {
  57       if (System::isAvailableLocale($accept_language))
  58       {
  59         return $accept_language;
  60       }
  61     }
  62 
  63     return false;
  64   }
  65 
  66 
  67   // Returns a correctly ordered and delimited locale ID
  68   public static function composeLocale(array $subtags)
  69   {
  70     if (isset($subtags[self::GRANDFATHERED_LANG_TAG]))
  71     {
  72       return $subtags[self::GRANDFATHERED_LANG_TAG];
  73     }
  74 
  75     $pieces = array();
  76 
  77     foreach (array(self::LANG_TAG, self::EXTLANG_TAG, self::SCRIPT_TAG, self::REGION_TAG) as $subtag_label)
  78     {
  79       if (isset($subtags[$subtag_label]))
  80       {
  81         $pieces[] = $subtags[$subtag_label];
  82       }
  83     }
  84 
  85     if (array_key_exists(self::VARIANT_TAG . '0', $subtags))
  86     {
  87       for ($i=0; $i<15; $i++)
  88       {
  89         if (isset($subtags[self::VARIANT_TAG . $i]))
  90         {
  91           $pieces[] = $subtags[self::VARIANT_TAG . $i];
  92         }
  93       }
  94     }
  95 
  96     if (array_key_exists(self::PRIVATE_TAG . '0', $subtags))
  97     {
  98       $pieces[] = 'x';
  99       for ($i=0; $i<15; $i++)
 100       {
 101         if (isset($subtags[self::PRIVATE_TAG . $i]))
 102         {
 103           $pieces[] = $subtags[self::PRIVATE_TAG . $i];
 104         }
 105       }
 106     }
 107 
 108     return implode('_', $pieces);
 109   }

 112   // Returns a key-value array of locale ID subtag elements.
 113   // Parses a language tag according to BCP 47
 114   // See http://tools.ietf.org/html/bcp47
 115   public static function parseLocale(string $locale) : ?array
 116   {
 117     static $regex = array('extlang' => '/^[[:alpha:]]{3}$/',  // 3ALPHA
 118                           'script'  => '/^[[:alpha:]]{4}$/',  // 4ALPHA
 119                           'region'  => '/^[[:alpha:]]{2}$|^[[:digit:]]{3}$/', // 2ALPHA or 3DIGIT
 120                           'variant' => '/^[[:alnum:]]{5,8}$|^[[:digit:]][[:alnum:]]{3}$/');  // 5*8alphanum or (DIGIT 3alphanum)
 121 
 122     static $grandfathered = array('en-GB-oed',      // Irregular
 123                                   'i-ami',
 124                                   'i-bnn',
 125                                   'i-default',
 126                                   'i-enochian',
 127                                   'i-hak',
 128                                   'i-klingon',
 129                                   'i-lux',
 130                                   'i-mingo',
 131                                   'i-navajo',
 132                                   'i-pwn',
 133                                   'i-tao',
 134                                   'i-tay',
 135                                   'i-tsu',
 136                                   'sgn-BE-FR',
 137                                   'sgn-BE-NL',
 138                                   'sgn-CH-DE',
 139                                   'art-lojban',     // Regular
 140                                   'cel-gaulish',
 141                                   'no-bok',
 142                                   'no-nyn',
 143                                   'zh-guoyu',
 144                                   'zh-hakka',
 145                                   'zh-min',
 146                                   'zh-min-nan',
 147                                   'zh-xiang');
 148 
 149     // First check for a grandfathered tag
 150     if (isset($locale) && in_array($locale, $grandfathered))
 151     {
 152       return array(self::GRANDFATHERED_LANG_TAG => $locale);
 153     }
 154 
 155     // Otherwise parse the subtags
 156     $result = array();
 157 
 158     if (isset($locale))
 159     {
 160       $subtags = preg_split('/[-_]/', $locale);
 161     }
 162     else
 163     {
 164       $subtags = array();
 165     }
 166 
 167     while (null !== ($subtag = array_shift($subtags)))
 168     {
 169       // Tags are case-insensitive, so convert to lowercase before processing and then
 170       // later convert as necessary according to convention
 171       $subtag = strtolower($subtag);
 172 
 173       if ($subtag == 'x')
 174       {
 175         // If the subtag is an 'x' then everything else is a private subtag,
 176         // even if it occurs as the first subtag:
 177         // "The single-character subtag 'x' as the primary subtag indicates
 178         // that the language tag consists solely of subtags whose meaning is
 179         // defined by private agreement"
 180         $i = 0;
 181         while (null !== ($subtag = array_shift($subtags)))
 182         {
 183           $result[self::PRIVATE_TAG . $i] = $subtag;
 184           $i++;
 185         }
 186       }
 187 
 188       // The primary language subtag is the first subtag in a language tag and
 189       // cannot be omitted, with two exceptions:
 190       //
 191       //  o  The single-character subtag 'x' as the primary subtag ...
 192       //  o  The single-character subtag 'i' is used by some grandfathered tags ...
 193       elseif (!isset($result[self::LANG_TAG]))
 194       {
 195         // [ISO639-1] recommends that language codes be written in lowercase ('mn' Mongolian).
 196         // As the subtag will already be lowercase there's no need to do anything else
 197         $result[self::LANG_TAG] = $subtag;
 198         // Check if the next subtag looks like a language extension
 199         if (count($subtags) > 0)
 200         {
 201           if (preg_match($regex['extlang'], $subtags[0]))
 202           {
 203             $result[self::EXTLANG_TAG] = strtolower(array_shift($subtags));
 204           }
 205         }
 206       }
 207 
 208       // Script
 209       elseif (preg_match($regex['script'], $subtag))
 210       {
 211         // [ISO15924] recommends that script codes use lowercase with the
 212         // initial letter capitalized ('Cyrl' Cyrillic).
 213         $result[self::SCRIPT_TAG] = ucfirst($subtag);
 214       }
 215 
 216       // Region
 217       elseif (preg_match($regex['region'], $subtag))
 218       {
 219         // [ISO3166-1] recommends that country codes be capitalized ('MN'
 220         // Mongolia).
 221         $result[self::REGION_TAG] = strtoupper($subtag);
 222       }
 223 
 224       // Variants
 225       elseif (preg_match($regex['variant'], $subtag))
 226       {
 227         $i = 0;
 228         do
 229         {
 230           // If the subtag doesn't look like a variant then we've got them all
 231           // and gone one subtag too far, so put it back
 232           if (!preg_match($regex['variant'], $subtag))
 233           {
 234             array_unshift($subtags, $subtag);
 235             break;
 236           }
 237           $result[self::VARIANT_TAG . $i] = $subtag;
 238         }
 239         while (null !== ($subtag = array_shift($subtags)));
 240       }
 241 
 242       else
 243       {
 244         trigger_error("parseLocale: could not parse subtag '$subtag'", E_USER_NOTICE);
 245         // This is how the PHP version behaves: if it can't parse the locale completely
 246         // it returns an empty array.
 247         $result = array();
 248       }
 249     }
 250 
 251     return $result;
 252   }
 253 
 254 
 255   // Searches the items in the array $langtag for the best match to the language range
 256   // specified in $locale according to RFC 4647's lookup algorithm.   The langtags and
 257   // locale can have subtags separated by '-' or '_' and the search is case-insensitive.
 258   // Charsets (eg '.UTF-8') are stripped off $locale
 259   //
 260   // Returns the best match, or else an empty string if no match
 261   public static function lookup(array $langtag, string $locale, bool $canonicalize=false, ?string $default=null) : ?string
 262   {
 263     if ($canonicalize)
 264     {
 265       throw new InvalidArgumentException('MRBS: the MRBS version of Locale::lookup() does not yet support $canonicalize = true');
 266     }
 267 
 268     // Get the langtags and locale in the same format, ie separated by '-' and
 269     // all lower case
 270     $standard_langtags = self::standardise($langtag);
 271     // Strip off any charset (eg '.UTF-8');
 272     $locale = preg_replace('/\..*$/', '', $locale);
 273     $standard_locale = self::standardise($locale);
 274 
 275     // Look for a match.   If there isn't one remove the last subtag from the end
 276     // of the locale and try again.
 277     while (false === ($index = array_search($standard_locale, $standard_langtags)))
 278     {
 279       if (false === ($pos = strrpos($standard_locale, '-')))
 280       {
 281         return (isset($default)) ? $default : '';
 282       }
 283       $standard_locale = substr($standard_locale, 0, $pos);
 284     }
 285 
 286     return $langtag[$index];  // Return the match in its original format
 287   }
 288 
 289 
 290   // Converts $langtag, which can be a string or an array, into a standard form with
 291   // subtags all in lower case and separated by '-';
 292   private static function standardise($langtag)
 293   {
 294     $glue = ',';
 295     $result = (is_array($langtag)) ? implode($glue, $langtag) : $langtag;
 296     $result = mb_strtolower(str_replace('_', '-', $result));
 297     return (is_array($langtag)) ? explode($glue, $result) : $result;
 298   }
 299 
 300 
 301   /**
 302    * Converts an Accept-Language request-header to an array of acceptable languages
 303    * with the language as the key and the quality value as the value, sorted in
 304    * decreasing order of quality value.  A wildcard in the header is translated.
 305    *
 306    * @return array<string, float>
 307    */
 308   private static function toSortedArray(string $header) : array
 309   {
 310     return get_qualifiers($header, true);
 311   }
 312 
 313 }

  11 // A class for handling a mail queue.   Normally the queue is flushed on shutdown using a
  12 // register_shutdown_function() callback.  However the class could easily be extended so that the
  13 // mail queue is held in the database and emptied by a cron job.  This would enable rate limits to
  14 // be adhered to more accurately, as there would be just one queue.
  15 class MailQueue

  17   protected static $mails = array();

  19 
  20   /**
  21    * Add an email to the queue for sending
  22    *
  23    * @param array       $addresses    an array of addresses, each being a comma
  24    *                                  separated list of email addresses.  Indexed by
  25    *                                    'from'
  26    *                                    'reply_to'
  27    *                                    'to'
  28    *                                    'cc'
  29    *                                    'bcc'
  30    * @param string      $subject      email subject
  31    * @param string      $text_body    text part of body
  32    * @param string|null $html_body    HTML part of body
  33    * @param array|null  $attachment   file to attach.   An array consisting of
  34    *                                    'content' the file or data to attach
  35    *                                    'method'  the iCalendar METHOD
  36    *                                    'name'    the name to give it
  37    * @param string      $charset      character set used in body
  38    * @return void
  39    */
  40   public static function add(
  41       array $addresses,
  42       string $subject,
  43       string $text_body,
  44       ?string $html_body,
  45       ?array $attachment,
  46       string $charset = 'us-ascii'
  47     ) : void
  48   {
  49     global $mail_settings;
  50 
  51     // Don't do anything if mail has been disabled.   Useful for testing MRBS without
  52     // sending emails to those who don't want them
  53     if ($mail_settings['disabled'])
  54     {
  55       mail_debug("Mail disabled: not adding message to queue");
  56       return;
  57     }
  58 
  59     // And no point in doing anything if there are no recipients
  60     if (self::getNRecipients($addresses) == 0)
  61     {
  62       mail_debug("No recipients: not adding message to queue");
  63       return;
  64     }
  65 
  66     $mail = array();
  67     foreach(array('addresses', 'subject', 'text_body', 'html_body', 'attachment', 'charset') as $var)
  68     {
  69       $mail[$var] = $$var;
  70     }
  71     self::$mails[] = $mail;
  72   }
  73 
  74 
  75   public static function flush() : void
  76   {
  77     foreach (self::$mails as $mail)
  78     {
  79       self::sendMail(
  80         $mail['addresses'],
  81         $mail['subject'],
  82         $mail['text_body'],
  83         $mail['html_body'],
  84         $mail['attachment'],
  85         $mail['charset']
  86       );
  87     }
  88   }

  91   protected static function getNRecipients(array $addresses) : int
  92   {
  93     if (empty($addresses))
  94     {
  95       return 0;
  96     }
  97 
  98     $recipients = (!empty($addresses['to'])) ? $addresses['to'] : '';
  99     $recipients .= (!empty($addresses['cc'])) ? ',' . $addresses['cc'] : '';
 100     $recipients .= (!empty($addresses['bcc'])) ? ',' . $addresses['bcc'] : '';
 101     $parsed_addresses = parse_addresses($recipients);
 102 
 103     return count($parsed_addresses);
 104   }

 107   /**

 111    *                                  separated list of email addresses.  Indexed by
 112    *                                    'from'
 113    *                                    'reply_to'

 115    *                                    'cc'

 118    * @param string      $text_body    text part of body

 120    * @param array|null  $attachment   file to attach.   An array consisting of
 121    *                                    'content' the file or data to attach
 122    *                                    'method'  the iCalendar METHOD

 148     // discussion at https://github.com/PHPMailer/PHPMailer/issues/175

 152     static $last_mail_sent = null;
 153     static $last_n_addresses = null;
 154 
 155     $mail = new Mailer($mail_settings, $sendmail_settings, $smtp_settings);

 160       $mail->Debugoutput = ($mail_settings['debug_output'] == 'log') ? 'error_log' : 'html';

 199       $mail->addAddress($to_address['address'], $to_address['name']);

 386         mail_debug($message);
 387         trigger_error($message, E_USER_NOTICE);
 388         $result = @$mail->postSend();
 389       }
 390       else
 391       {
 392         $result = $mail->postSend();
 393       }
 394 
 395       if ($result)
 396       {
 397         mail_debug('Email sent successfully');
 398         return true;
 399       }
 400     }
 401 
 402     error_log('Error sending email: ' . $mail->ErrorInfo);
 403     mail_debug('Failed to send email: ' . $mail->ErrorInfo);
 404 
 405     return false;
 406   }
 407 
 408 }

   1 <?php
   2 declare(strict_types=1);
   3 namespace MRBS;
   4 
   5 
   6 // A class for managing the optional message that is displayed at the top of the calendar
   7 class Message
   8 {
   9   private const FORMAT_DATE = 'Y-m-d';
  10   private const FORMAT_DATETIME = 'Y-m-d\TH:i:s';
  11   private static $instance = null;
  12   private $text = '';
  13   private $from = '';
  14   private $until = '';
  15 
  16 
  17   private function __construct(string $text = '', string $from_date = '', string $until_date = '')
  18   {
  19     assert(version_compare(MRBS_MIN_PHP_VERSION, '7.4.0', '<'), "The __wakeup() method is now redundant.");
  20     $this->setText($text);
  21     $this->setFromDate($from_date);
  22     $this->setUntilDate($until_date);
  23   }
  24 
  25 
  26   private function __clone()
  27   {
  28   }
  29 
  30 
  31   public function __unserialize(array $data) : void
  32   {
  33     // __unserialize() must have public visibility
  34     throw new \Exception("Cannot unserialize a singleton.");
  35   }
  36 
  37 
  38   // __wakeup() is deprecated from PHP 8.5.
  39   // "The __wakeup() serialization magic method has been deprecated. Implement __unserialize()
  40   // instead (or in addition, if support for old PHP versions is necessary)".
  41   // __unserialize() is only available from PHP 7.4.0
  42   public function __wakeup()
  43   {
  44     // __wakeup() must have public visibility
  45     throw new \Exception("Cannot unserialize a singleton.");
  46   }
  47 
  48 
  49   public static function getInstance(string $text = '', string $from_date = '', string $until_date = ''): Message
  50   {
  51     if (!isset(self::$instance))
  52     {
  53       self::$instance = new self($text, $from_date, $until_date);
  54     }
  55 
  56     return self::$instance;
  57   }
  58 
  59 
  60   // Loads a message from the database
  61   public function load() : void
  62   {
  63     $sql = "SELECT variable_content
  64               FROM " . _tbl('variables') . "
  65              WHERE variable_name='message'
  66              LIMIT 1";
  67     $res = db()->query_array($sql);
  68 
  69     $message = (count($res) === 0) ? [] : json_decode($res[0], true);
  70 
  71     $this->setText($message['text'] ?? '');
  72     $this->setFrom($message['from'] ?? '');
  73     $this->setUntil($message['until'] ?? '');
  74   }
  75 
  76 
  77   // Saves a message to the database
  78   public function save() : bool
  79   {
  80     $sql_params = array();
  81     $data = array(
  82       'variable_name' => 'message',
  83       'variable_content' => json_encode([
  84         'text' => $this->text,
  85         'from' => $this->from,
  86         'until' => $this->until
  87       ])
  88     );
  89     $sql = db()->syntax_upsert($data, _tbl('variables'), $sql_params, 'variable_name', ['id'], true);
  90 
  91     return (0 < db()->command($sql, $sql_params));
  92   }
  93 
  94 
  95   // Gets the message text
  96   public function getText() : string
  97   {
  98     return $this->text;
  99   }
 100 
 101 
 102   public function getEscapedText() : string
 103   {
 104     global $message_allowed_tags;
 105 
 106     if (empty($message_allowed_tags))
 107     {
 108       return escape_html($this->text);
 109     }
 110 
 111     return self::stripTags($this->text, $message_allowed_tags);
 112   }
 113 
 114   // Gets the message end date
 115   public function getFromDate() : string
 116   {
 117     if ($this->from === '')
 118     {
 119       return '';
 120     }
 121 
 122     if (false === ($date = DateTime::createFromFormat(self::FORMAT_DATETIME, $this->from)))
 123     {
 124       return '';
 125     }
 126 
 127     return $date->format(self::FORMAT_DATE);
 128   }
 129 
 130 
 131   // Gets the message end date
 132   public function getUntilDate() : string
 133   {
 134     if ($this->until === '')
 135     {
 136       return '';
 137     }
 138 
 139     if (false === ($date = DateTime::createFromFormat(self::FORMAT_DATETIME, $this->until)))
 140     {
 141       return '';
 142     }
 143 
 144     return $date->modify('-1 day')->format(self::FORMAT_DATE);
 145   }
 146 
 147 
 148   // Gets the message start timestamp
 149   public function getFromTimestamp() : ?int
 150   {
 151     if ($this->from === '')
 152     {
 153       return null;
 154     }
 155 
 156     if (false === ($date = DateTime::createFromFormat(self::FORMAT_DATETIME, $this->from)))
 157     {
 158       return null;
 159     }
 160 
 161     return $date->getTimestamp();
 162   }
 163 
 164 
 165   // Gets the message end timestamp
 166   public function getUntilTimestamp() : ?int
 167   {
 168     if ($this->until === '')
 169     {
 170       return null;
 171     }
 172 
 173     if (false === ($date = DateTime::createFromFormat(self::FORMAT_DATETIME, $this->until)))
 174     {
 175       return null;
 176     }
 177 
 178     return $date->getTimestamp();
 179   }
 180 
 181 
 182   // Get the message start time as a string in the user's locale
 183   public function getFromLocalString() : ?string
 184   {
 185     global $datetime_formats;
 186 
 187     $timestamp = $this->getFromTimestamp();
 188 
 189     if (!isset($timestamp))
 190     {
 191       return null;
 192     }
 193 
 194     return datetime_format($datetime_formats['date_and_time'], $timestamp);
 195   }
 196 
 197 
 198   // Get the message end time as a string in the user's locale
 199   public function getUntilLocalString() : ?string
 200   {
 201     global $datetime_formats;
 202 
 203     $timestamp = $this->getUntilTimestamp();
 204 
 205     if (!isset($timestamp))
 206     {
 207       return null;
 208     }
 209 
 210     return datetime_format($datetime_formats['date_and_time'], $timestamp);
 211   }
 212 
 213 
 214   // Sets the message text
 215   public function setText(string $text) : void
 216   {
 217     $this->text = $text;
 218   }
 219 
 220 
 221   // Sets the message end date
 222   public function setFromDate(string $from_date) : void
 223   {
 224     if ($from_date !== '')
 225     {
 226       // Set the date to the beginning of the day and save it with a time.
 227       // This allows a time to be added to the form in the future.
 228       // Note that the time is without timezone, so will be the time in the
 229       // timezone of the area that the message will be displayed in.
 230       $date = DateTime::createFromFormat(self::FORMAT_DATE, $from_date);
 231       if ($date === false)
 232       {
 233         trigger_error("Could not create date from '$from_date'; expecting format '" . self::FORMAT_DATE . "'.", E_USER_WARNING);
 234         $this->setFrom('');
 235       }
 236       else
 237       {
 238         $date->setTime(0, 0);
 239         $this->setFrom($date->format(self::FORMAT_DATETIME));
 240       }
 241     }
 242   }
 243 
 244 
 245   // Sets the message end date
 246   public function setUntilDate(string $until_date) : void
 247   {
 248     if ($until_date !== '')
 249     {
 250       // Set the date to the beginning of the next day and save it with a time.
 251       // This allows a time to be added to the form in the future.
 252       // Note that the time is without timezone, so will be the time in the
 253       // timezone of the area that the message will be displayed in.
 254       $date = DateTime::createFromFormat(self::FORMAT_DATE, $until_date);
 255       if ($date === false)
 256       {
 257         trigger_error("Could not create date from '$until_date'; expecting format '" . self::FORMAT_DATE . "'.", E_USER_WARNING);
 258         $this->setUntil('');
 259       }
 260       else
 261       {
 262         $date->setTime(0, 0)->modify('+1 day');
 263         $this->setUntil($date->format(self::FORMAT_DATETIME));
 264       }
 265     }
 266   }
 267 
 268 
 269   // Determines whether there is a message that should be displayed, ie
 270   // the message exists and the expiry date hasn't passed.
 271   public function hasSomethingToDisplay() : bool
 272   {
 273     $text = $this->getText();
 274 
 275     if ($text === '')
 276     {
 277       return false;
 278     }
 279 
 280     $from_timestamp = $this->getFromTimestamp();
 281     $until_timestamp = $this->getUntilTimestamp();
 282 
 283     // Check to see whether we're in the time interval in which to display the message
 284     return ((!isset($from_timestamp)  || (time() >= $from_timestamp)) &&
 285             (!isset($until_timestamp)  || (time() < $until_timestamp)));
 286   }
 287 
 288 
 289   private function setFrom(string $date_time_string) : void
 290   {
 291     $this->from = $date_time_string;
 292   }
 293 
 294 
 295   private function setUntil(string $date_time_string) : void
 296   {
 297     $this->until = $date_time_string;
 298   }
 299 
 300 
 301   // Wrapper for PHP's strip_tags() function which converts $allowed tags to a string
 302   // if PHP < 7.4.0
 303   private static function stripTags(string $string, array $allowed_tags) : string
 304   {
 305     assert(version_compare(MRBS_MIN_PHP_VERSION, '7.4.0', '<'), "This method is now redundant.");
 306 
 307     if (version_compare(PHP_VERSION, '7.4.0', '>='))
 308     {
 309       return strip_tags($string, $allowed_tags);
 310     }
 311 
 312     $tag_string = '';
 313     foreach ($allowed_tags as $tag)
 314     {
 315       $tag_string .= "<$tag>";
 316     }
 317 
 318     return strip_tags($string, $tag_string);
 319   }
 320 }

   1 <?php
   2 declare(strict_types=1);
   3 namespace MRBS\Session;
   4 
   5 use MRBS\SessionHandlerDb;
   6 use MRBS\SessionHandlerDbException;
   7 use MRBS\User;
   8 use SessionHandler;
   9 use function MRBS\db;
  10 use function MRBS\db_schema_version;
  11 use function MRBS\get_cookie_path;
  12 use function MRBS\is_https;
  13 
  14 abstract class Session
  15 {
  16   protected const SAMESITE_NONE = 'None';
  17   protected const SAMESITE_LAX = 'Lax';
  18   protected const SAMESITE_STRICT = 'Strict';
  19 
  20   protected $samesite = null;
  21 
  22   public function __construct()
  23   {
  24     global $auth, $cookie_samesite_lax;
  25 
  26     // Child classes can set $this->samesite
  27     if (!isset($this->samesite))
  28     {
  29       $this->samesite = ($cookie_samesite_lax) ? self::SAMESITE_LAX : self::SAMESITE_STRICT;
  30     }
  31 
  32     // Start up sessions
  33     // Default to the behaviour of previous versions of MRBS, use only
  34     // session cookies - no persistent cookie.
  35     $lifetime = $auth['session_php']['session_expire_time'] ?? 0;
  36     $this->init($lifetime);
  37   }
  38 
  39 
  40   // Normally there's no need to call init() from outside the Session classes.
  41   // It only needs to be called to restart sessions, after for example a user
  42   // has been logged off and you need to use session variables.
  43   public function init(int $lifetime) : void
  44   {
  45     global $auth;
  46 
  47     if (session_status() === PHP_SESSION_ACTIVE)
  48     {
  49       // We've already started sessions
  50       return;
  51     }
  52 
  53     // Session settings, for security
  54     // ini_set() only accepts string values prior to PHP 8.1.0
  55     ini_set('session.cookie_httponly', '1');
  56     if (version_compare(PHP_VERSION, '7.3', '>='))
  57     {
  58       // Only introduced in PHP Version 7.3
  59       ini_set('session.cookie_samesite', $this->samesite);
  60     }
  61     ini_set('session.cookie_secure', (is_https()) ? '1' : '0');
  62 
  63     // More settings, as a defence against session fixation.
  64     ini_set('session.use_only_cookies', '1');
  65     ini_set('session.use_strict_mode', '1');
  66     ini_set('session.use_trans_sid', '0');
  67 
  68     $cookie_path = get_cookie_path();
  69 
  70     // We don't want the session garbage collector to delete the session before it has expired
  71     if ($lifetime !== 0)
  72     {
  73       assert(version_compare(MRBS_MIN_PHP_VERSION, '8.1') < 0, 'The strval() in the line below is no longer required.');
  74       ini_set('session.gc_maxlifetime', strval(max(ini_get('session.gc_maxlifetime'), $lifetime)));
  75     }
  76 
  77     if (isset($auth['session_php']['session_name']))
  78     {
  79       // call before session_set_cookie_params() - see PHP manual
  80       session_name($auth['session_php']['session_name']);
  81     }
  82     session_set_cookie_params($lifetime, $cookie_path);
  83 
  84     $current_db_schema_version = db_schema_version(db());
  85     // The session table was created in Upgrade 56.   Before that we will ignore any errors
  86     // to do with DB sessions.
  87     $session_table_should_exist = ($current_db_schema_version >= 56);
  88 
  89     try
  90     {
  91       // The DB session handler uses locks and because we use locks elsewhere
  92       // this means we need support for multiple locks.  We need to test now,
  93       // rather than catching an exception, because resetting the session
  94       // handler will reset the session id causing us to lose session data.
  95       if (db()->supportsMultipleLocks())
  96       {
  97         $handler = new SessionHandlerDb();
  98         session_set_save_handler($handler, true);
  99       }
 100       $session_started = session_start();
 101     }
 102     catch(SessionHandlerDbException $e)
 103     {
 104       if ($session_table_should_exist &&
 105         ($e->getCode() === SessionHandlerDbException::TABLE_NOT_EXISTS))
 106       {
 107         trigger_error($e->getMessage(), E_USER_WARNING);
 108         $message = "Could not start DB sessions, trying ordinary PHP sessions.";
 109         trigger_error($message, E_USER_WARNING);
 110       }
 111       $session_started = false;
 112     }
 113 
 114     if ($session_started === false)
 115     {
 116       $handler = new SessionHandler();
 117       session_set_save_handler($handler, true);
 118 
 119       if (false === session_start())
 120       {
 121         throw new \Exception("MRBS: could not start sessions");
 122       }
 123     }
 124   }
 125 
 126 
 127   protected function destroy() : void
 128   {
 129     // Delete the session data encryption key cookie. If we don't do this then, when
 130     // a new session is created, unless the expiry is set to 0 (ie on browser close),
 131     // it will have a longer lifetime than the key cookie, which when it was created
 132     // was given the same lifetime as the session cookie.  Once the key cookie expires,
 133     // the session handler will create a new cookie with a new key.  So when the session
 134     // handler comes to decrypt the session data it will be doing so with the new key,
 135     // and not the key used to encrypt it.  This will result in the Crypto library
 136     // throwing a WrongKeyOrModifiedCiphertextException with the message "Integrity
 137     // check failed".
 138     //
 139     // This needs to be done before the session is destroyed, otherwise the
 140     // deleteKeyCookie method won't be able to get the session name (which it needs
 141     // in order to delete the key cookie).
 142     SessionHandlerDb::deleteKeyCookie();
 143 
 144     // Unset the session variables
 145     // Note that session_unset() only works if a session is active.
 146     $_SESSION = [];
 147     // Check whether a session is active before destroying it in order to avoid a
 148     // "Trying to destroy uninitialized session" warning.
 149     if (session_status() === PHP_SESSION_ACTIVE)
 150     {
 151       session_destroy();
 152     }
 153 
 154     // Problems have been reported on Windows IIS with session data not being
 155     // written out without a call to session_write_close(). [Is this necessary
 156     // after session_destroy() ??]
 157     session_write_close();
 158   }
 159 
 160 
 161   protected function regenerate() : void
 162   {
 163     // Regenerate the session id
 164     session_regenerate_id(true);
 165 
 166     // Change the lifetime of the key cookie to match the new expiry - see the
 167     // comment in destroy().
 168     SessionHandlerDb::regenerateKeyCookie();
 169   }
 170 
 171 
 172   public function get(string $name)
 173   {
 174     return $_SESSION[$name] ?? null;
 175   }
 176 
 177 
 178   public function isset(string $name) : bool
 179   {
 180     return isset($_SESSION[$name]);
 181   }
 182 
 183   public function set(string $name, $value) : void
 184   {
 185     $_SESSION[$name] = $value;
 186   }
 187 
 188 
 189   public function unset(string $name) : void
 190   {
 191     unset($_SESSION[$name]);
 192   }
 193 
 194 
 195   // Returns the currently logged-in user
 196   // This method provides the fallback user for un-logged in users.
 197   // Subclasses are expected to override this method, calling it as the parent
 198   // if they cannot find a current user.
 199   public function getCurrentUser() : ?User
 200   {
 201     global $auth;
 202 
 203     if (empty($auth['allow_anonymous_booking']))
 204     {
 205       return null;
 206     }
 207 
 208     // Use an empty string for anonymous bookings
 209     return new User('');
 210   }
 211 
 212 
 213   // Allows this to be extended with strategies for getting the referer when
 214   // HTTP_REFERER is going to be unreliable, eg when the Referrer-Policy is
 215   // set to strict-origin.
 216   public function getReferrer() : ?string
 217   {
 218     global $server;
 219 
 220     return $server['HTTP_REFERER'] ?? null;
 221   }
 222 
 223 
 224   // Updates the current and previous pages
 225   public function updatePage(string $url) : void
 226   {
 227   }
 228 
 229 }

   1 <?php
   2 declare(strict_types=1);
   3 namespace MRBS\Session;
   4 
   5 class SessionFactory
   6 {
   7 
   8   public static function create(string $type)
   9 
  10   {
  11     // Transform the session type from lowercase_separated to LowercaseSeparated
  12     $parts = explode('_', $type);
  13     $parts = array_map('ucfirst', $parts);
  14     $class = __NAMESPACE__  . "\\Session" . implode('', $parts);
  15     return new $class;
  16   }
  17 
  18 }

   1 <?php
   2 declare(strict_types=1);
   3 namespace MRBS\Session;
   4 
   5 use MRBS\User;
   6 use function MRBS\auth;
   7 use function MRBS\get_form_var;
   8 use function MRBS\is_ajax;
   9 use function MRBS\str_ends_with_array;
  10 use function MRBS\url_base;
  11 
  12 // Uses PHP's built-in session handling
  13 
  14 class SessionPhp extends SessionWithLogin
  15 {
  16 
  17   public function __construct()
  18   {
  19     global $auth, $server;
  20 
  21     parent::__construct();
  22 
  23     // Check to see if we've been inactive for longer than allowed and if so log out the user.
  24     // Don't log out the user if we're in kiosk mode because the kiosk will normally be inactive.
  25     // Note that we cannot use is_kiosk_mode() here as that will create an infinite loop calling session().
  26     if (!empty($auth['session_php']['inactivity_expire_time']) && !isset($_SESSION['kiosk_password_hash']))
  27     {
  28       if (isset($_SESSION['LastActivity']) &&
  29           ((time() - $_SESSION['LastActivity']) > $auth['session_php']['inactivity_expire_time']))
  30       {
  31         $this->logoffUser();
  32       }
  33       // Ajax requests don't count as activity, unless it's the special Ajax request used
  34       // to record client side activity.
  35       $activity = get_form_var('activity', 'int');
  36       if ($activity || !is_ajax() || !isset($_SESSION['LastActivity'])) {
  37         $_SESSION['LastActivity'] = time();
  38       }
  39     }
  40 
  41     // Move the current page to the last page, so it can be used as a referrer, and store the new current page -
  42     // but only if (a) we are at the top level of the MRBS web directory (eg index.php) so as to eliminate all
  43     // the ./js, ./ajax and ./css pages and (b) this is not otherwise an Ajax request, eg one of the prefetch
  44     // calls to index.php.
  45     if (isset($server['SCRIPT_FILENAME']) && (MRBS_ROOT === dirname($server['SCRIPT_FILENAME'])) &&
  46         !(isset($server['HTTP_X_REQUESTED_WITH']) && ($server['HTTP_X_REQUESTED_WITH'] === 'XMLHttpRequest')))
  47     {
  48       $this->updatePage($server['REQUEST_URI'] ?? $server['PHP_SELF'] ?? null);
  49     }
  50   }
  51 
  52 
  53   // If the server has a Referrer-Policy of strict-origin then HTTP_REFERER will be unreliable
  54   // and it is better to use the last page that we have stored in the $_SESSION variable.
  55   public function getReferrer(): ?string
  56   {
  57     $result = parent::getReferrer();
  58 
  59     // If the last page is known, and it's well-formed (parse_url() doesn't return false), and it's
  60     // not already a fully-qualified URL (ie the scheme is empty), and we've got a url base that
  61     // isn't the empty string, then return everything after the last '/' from the last page, prefixed
  62     // by the url base, in case there's a proxy in use.
  63     if (isset($_SESSION['last_page']))
  64     {
  65       $last_page = $_SESSION['last_page'];
  66       $scheme = parse_url($last_page, PHP_URL_SCHEME);
  67       if (($scheme === null) && ('' !== ($base = url_base())))
  68       {
  69         // Get everything after the last '/'
  70         $array = explode('/', $last_page);
  71         $result = $base . array_pop($array);
  72       }
  73     }
  74 
  75     return $result;
  76   }
  77 
  78 
  79   public function updatePage(?string $url): void
  80   {
  81     // Don't update the page if the URL as the same as the one we've already got
  82     // stored for this page.  This will be the case if the user has refreshed the
  83     // browser, and if we update the page then we'll lose the last page, which is
  84     // sometimes needed for MRBS to know where to go back to.
  85     if (isset($_SESSION['this_page']) && ($url === $_SESSION['this_page']))
  86     {
  87       return;
  88     }
  89 
  90     $_SESSION['last_page'] = $_SESSION['this_page'] ?? null;
  91     $_SESSION['this_page'] = $url;
  92   }
  93 
  94 
  95   public function getCurrentUser() : ?User
  96   {
  97     $result = $_SESSION['user'] ?? null;
  98 
  99     // For some unknown reason the integer value 0 is sometimes stored in the session
 100     // variable.  It's not clear how this can happen.
 101     if (isset($result) && !(is_object($result) && is_a($result, 'MRBS\User')))
 102     {
 103       trigger_error('$_SESSION["user"] is expected to be a User object, not ' . json_encode($result), E_USER_WARNING);
 104       $result = null;
 105     }
 106 
 107     return $_SESSION['user'] ?? parent::getCurrentUser();
 108   }
 109 
 110 
 111   protected function logonUser(string $username) : void
 112   {
 113     $user = auth()->getUser($username);
 114 
 115     // As a defence against session fixation, regenerate
 116     // the session id and delete the old session.
 117     $this->regenerate();
 118     $_SESSION['user'] = $user;
 119 
 120     // Problems have been reported on Windows IIS with session data not being
 121     // written out without a call to session_write_close()
 122     session_write_close();
 123   }
 124 
 125 
 126   public function logoffUser() : void
 127   {
 128     global $cookie_path_override;
 129 
 130     if (ini_get("session.use_cookies"))
 131     {
 132       // Delete the session cookie
 133       $params = session_get_cookie_params();
 134       setcookie(session_name(), '', time() - 42000, $params['path'], $params['domain'], $params['secure'], isset($params['httponly']));
 135 
 136       // Delete any cookies which may have previously been set, incorrectly, before the fixes to get_cookie_path (see
 137       // https://github.com/meeting-room-booking-system/mrbs-code/commit/90ceeb8a0bc5f4850065695a3e085114c5ecae8e and
 138       // https://github.com/meeting-room-booking-system/mrbs-code/commit/cb74320048149c4199281b88d50fb69988a41312).
 139       // Note that the problem didn't occur if $cookie_path_override was set.
 140       // In time, once all the incorrect cookies have expired naturally, this block can be deleted.
 141       if (!isset($cookie_path_override))
 142       {
 143         $suffixes = array('ajax/', 'js/');
 144         // If the path ends with one of the suffixes we'll already have deleted it above
 145         if (!str_ends_with_array($params['path'], $suffixes))
 146         {
 147           foreach ($suffixes as $suffix)
 148           {
 149             setcookie(session_name(), '', time() - 42000, $params['path'] . $suffix, $params['domain'], $params['secure'], isset($params['httponly']));
 150           }
 151         }
 152       }
 153     }
 154 
 155     $this->destroy();
 156   }
 157 }

   1 <?php
   2 declare(strict_types=1);
   3 namespace MRBS\Session;
   4 
   5 use MRBS\Form\ElementA;
   6 use MRBS\Form\ElementFieldset;
   7 use MRBS\Form\ElementP;
   8 use MRBS\Form\FieldDiv;
   9 use MRBS\Form\FieldInputPassword;
  10 use MRBS\Form\FieldInputSubmit;
  11 use MRBS\Form\FieldInputText;
  12 use MRBS\Form\Form;
  13 use function MRBS\auth;
  14 use function MRBS\get_form_var;
  15 use function MRBS\get_vocab;
  16 use function MRBS\location_header;
  17 use function MRBS\multisite;
  18 use function MRBS\print_footer;
  19 use function MRBS\print_header;
  20 use function MRBS\this_page;
  21 
  22 
  23 // An abstract class for those session schemes that implement a login form
  24 abstract class SessionWithLogin extends Session
  25 {
  26   protected $form = array();
  27 
  28 
  29   public function __construct()
  30   {
  31     parent::__construct();
  32 
  33     // Get non-standard form variables
  34     foreach (array('action', 'username', 'password', 'returl') as $var)
  35     {
  36       $this->form[$var] = get_form_var($var, 'string', null, INPUT_POST);
  37     }
  38 
  39     // Allow the target_url to be a GET or POST value to help password managers (the target_url can
  40     // be stored as a query string parameter in the password manager).
  41     $this->form['target_url'] = get_form_var('target_url');
  42 
  43     if (isset($this->form['username']))
  44     {
  45       // It's easy for extra spaces to appear, especially on a mobile device
  46       $this->form['username'] = trim($this->form['username']);
  47     }
  48   }
  49 
  50 
  51   // Gets the username and password.  Returns: Nothing
  52   //
  53   //    $target_url   The URL to go to after successful login
  54   //    $returl       The URL to return to eventually
  55   public function authGet(?string $target_url=null, ?string $returl=null, ?string $error=null, bool $raw=false) : void
  56   {
  57     if (!isset($target_url))
  58     {
  59       $target_url = $this->form['target_url'] ?? this_page(true);
  60     }
  61 
  62     // Omit the Login link in the header when we're on the login page itself
  63     print_header(null, false, true);
  64     $action = multisite(this_page());
  65     $this->printLoginForm($action, $target_url, $returl, $error, $raw);
  66     exit;
  67   }
  68 
  69 
  70   // Returns the parameters ('method', 'action' and 'hidden_inputs') for a
  71   // Logon form.  Returns an array.
  72   public function getLogonFormParams() : ?array
  73   {
  74     return array(
  75         'action' => multisite('admin.php'),
  76         'method' => Form::METHOD_POST,
  77         'hidden_inputs' =>  array('target_url' => this_page(true),
  78                                   'action'     => 'QueryName')
  79       );
  80   }
  81 
  82 
  83   // Returns the parameters ('method', 'action' and 'hidden_inputs') for a
  84   // logoff form.  Returns an array of parameters, or null if no form is to be
  85   // shown.
  86   public function getLogoffFormParams() : ?array
  87   {
  88     return array(
  89         'action' => multisite('admin.php'),
  90         'method' => Form::METHOD_POST,
  91         'hidden_inputs' =>  array('target_url' => this_page(true),
  92                                   'action'     => 'SetName',
  93                                   'username'   => '',
  94                                   'password'   => '')
  95       );
  96   }
  97 
  98 
  99   public function processForm() : void
 100   {
 101     if (isset($this->form['action']))
 102     {
 103       // Target of the form with sets the URL argument "action=QueryName".
 104       // Will eventually return to URL argument "target_url=whatever".
 105       if ($this->form['action'] == 'QueryName')
 106       {
 107         $this->authGet($this->form['target_url']);
 108         exit(); // unnecessary because authGet() exits, but just included for clarity
 109       }
 110 
 111       // Target of the form with sets the URL argument "action=SetName".
 112       // Will eventually return to URL argument "target_url=whatever".
 113       if ($this->form['action'] == 'SetName')
 114       {
 115         // First make sure the password is valid
 116         if (!isset($this->form['username']) || ($this->form['username'] == ''))
 117         {
 118           $this->logoffUser();
 119         }
 120         else
 121         {
 122           // If we're going to do something then check the CSRF token first.
 123           // (Don't check the token before logging off the user because if the session has
 124           // expired due to inactivity, the token will be invalid, but that won't matter because
 125           // the result will be the same anyway - logging off the user - and we avoid
 126           // generating an unnecessary CSRF error message.)
 127           Form::checkToken();
 128 
 129           // Get a valid user
 130           $valid_username = $this->getValidUser($this->form['username'], $this->form['password']);
 131 
 132           // Successful login.   You can't get out of getValidUser() without a valid username and password
 133           $this->logonUser($valid_username);
 134 
 135           if (!empty($this->form['returl']))
 136           {
 137             // check to see whether there's a query string already
 138             $this->form['target_url'] .= (mb_strpos($this->form['target_url'], '?') === false) ? '?' : '&';
 139             $this->form['target_url'] .= 'returl=' . urlencode($this->form['returl']);
 140           }
 141         }
 142 
 143         location_header($this->form['target_url']); // Redirect browser to initial page
 144       }
 145     }
 146   }
 147 
 148 
 149   // Can only return a valid username.  If the username and password are not valid it will ask for new ones.
 150   protected function getValidUser(
 151     #[\SensitiveParameter]
 152     ?string $username,
 153     #[\SensitiveParameter]
 154     ?string $password) : string
 155   {
 156     if (!isset($this->form['password']) ||
 157         (($valid_username = auth()->validateUser($this->form['username'], $this->form['password'])) === false))
 158     {
 159       $this->authGet($this->form['target_url'], $this->form['returl'], get_vocab('unknown_user'));
 160       exit(); // unnecessary because authGet() exits, but just included for clarity
 161     }
 162 
 163     return $valid_username;
 164   }
 165 
 166 
 167   protected function logonUser(string $username) : void
 168   {
 169   }
 170 
 171 
 172   public function logoffUser() : void
 173   {
 174   }
 175 
 176 
 177   // Displays the login form.
 178   // Will eventually return to $target_url with query string returl=$returl
 179   // If $error is set then an $error is printed.
 180   // If $raw is true then the message is not HTML escaped
 181   private function printLoginForm(string $action, ?string $target_url, ?string $returl, ?string $error=null, bool $raw=false) : void
 182   {
 183     $form = new Form(Form::METHOD_POST);
 184     $form->setAttributes(array('class'  => 'standard',
 185                                'id'     => 'logon',
 186                                'action' => $action));
 187 
 188     // Hidden inputs
 189     $hidden_inputs = array('returl'     => $returl,
 190                            'target_url' => $target_url,
 191                            'action'     => 'SetName');
 192     $form->addHiddenInputs($hidden_inputs);
 193 
 194     // Now for the visible fields
 195     if (isset($error))
 196     {
 197       $p = new ElementP();
 198       $p->setText($error, false, $raw);
 199       $form->addElement($p);
 200     }
 201 
 202     $fieldset = new ElementFieldset();
 203     $fieldset->addLegend(get_vocab('please_login'));
 204 
 205     // The username field
 206     if (auth()->canValidateByEmail() && auth()->canValidateByUsername())
 207     {
 208       $tag = 'username_or_email';
 209     }
 210     elseif (auth()->canValidateByUsername())
 211     {
 212       $tag = 'users.name';
 213     }
 214     else
 215     {
 216       $tag = 'users.email';
 217     }
 218 
 219     $placeholder = get_vocab($tag);
 220 
 221     $field = new FieldInputText();
 222     $field->setLabel(get_vocab('user'))
 223           ->setLabelAttributes(array('title' => $placeholder))
 224           ->setControlAttributes(array('id'           => 'username',
 225                                        'name'         => 'username',
 226                                        'placeholder'  => $placeholder,
 227                                        'required'     => true,
 228                                        'autofocus'    => true,
 229                                        'autocomplete' => 'username'));
 230     $fieldset->addElement($field);
 231 
 232     // The password field
 233     $field = new FieldInputPassword();
 234     $field->setLabel(get_vocab('users.password'))
 235           ->setControlAttributes(array('id'           => 'password',
 236                                        'name'         => 'password',
 237                                        'autocomplete' => 'current-password'));
 238     $fieldset->addElement($field);
 239 
 240     $form->addElement($fieldset);
 241 
 242     // The submit button
 243     $fieldset = new ElementFieldset();
 244     $field = new FieldInputSubmit();
 245     $field->setControlAttributes(array('value' => get_vocab('login')));
 246     $fieldset->addElement($field);
 247 
 248     $form->addElement($fieldset);
 249 
 250     if (auth()->canResetPassword())
 251     {
 252       $fieldset = new ElementFieldset();
 253       $field = new FieldDiv();
 254       $a = new ElementA();
 255       $a->setAttribute('href', multisite('reset_password.php'))
 256         ->setText(get_vocab('lost_password'));
 257       $field->addControl($a);
 258       $fieldset->addElement($field);
 259       $form->addElement($fieldset);
 260     }
 261 
 262     $form->render();
 263 
 264 
 265 
 266     // Print footer and exit
 267     print_footer(true);
 268   }
 269 
 270 
 271   // Check we've got the right authentication type for the session scheme.
 272   // To be called for those session schemes which require the same
 273   // authentication type
 274   protected function checkTypeMatchesSession() : void
 275   {
 276     global $auth;
 277 
 278     if ($auth['type'] !== $auth['session'])
 279     {
 280       $class = get_called_class();
 281       $message = "MRBS configuration error: $class needs \$auth['type'] set to '" . $auth['session'] . "'";
 282       die($message);
 283     }
 284   }
 285 }
