1570 // Get information about custom fields
1571 $fields = db()->field_info(_tbl('entry'));
1572 $custom_fields = array();
1573 $field_natures = array();
1574 $field_lengths = array();
1575 foreach ($fields as $field)
1576 {
1577   $key = $field['name'];
1578   if (!in_array($key, $standard_fields['entry']))
1579   {
1580     $custom_fields[$key] = '';
1581     // Add the field to the end of the report search field order, if it's
1582     // not already present
1583     if (!in_array($key, $report_search_field_order))
1584     {
1585       $report_search_field_order[] = $key;
1586     }
1587   }
1588   $field_natures[$key] = $field['nature'];
1589   $field_lengths[$key] = $field['length'];
1590 }
1591 
1592 // Get the custom form inputs
1593 foreach ($custom_fields as $key => $value)
1594 {
1595   $var = "match_$key";
1596   // Get the field as a string to check whether it is empty (ie match anything)
1597   $$var = get_form_var($var, 'string');
1598   if (($field_natures[$key] == 'integer') &&
1599       ($field_lengths[$key] > 2) &&
1600       isset($$var))
1601   {
1602     $$var = trim($$var);
1603     if ($$var !== '')
1604     {
1605       $$var = intval($$var);
1606     }
1607   }
1608 }
1609 
1610 // Set the field order list
1611 $field_order_list = array('name', 'area_name', 'room_name', 'start_time', 'end_time',
1612                           'description', 'type', 'allow_registration', 'create_by', 'confirmation_enabled',
1613                           'approval_enabled');
1614 foreach ($custom_fields as $key => $value)
1615 {
1616   $field_order_list[] = $key;
1617 }
1618 $field_order_list[] = 'last_updated';
1619 
1620 
1621 
1622 // PHASE 2:  SQL QUERY.  We do the SQL query now to see if there's anything there
1623 if ($phase == 2)
1624 {
1625   // Start and end times are also used to clip the times for summary info.
1626   // createFromFormat() gives the current time.  We want the report to
1627   // start at the beginning of the start day and end of the day, so set the
1628   // times accordingly.
1629   if (false === ($report_start = DateTime::createFromFormat(DateTime::ISO8601_DATE, $from_date)))
1630   {
1631     throw new Exception("Invalid from_date '$from_date'");
1632   }
1633   $report_start = $report_start->setTime(0, 0)->getTimestamp();
1634 
1635   if (false === ($report_end = DateTime::createFromFormat(DateTime::ISO8601_DATE, $to_date)))
1636   {
1637     throw new Exception("Invalid to_date '$to_date'");
1638   }
1639   $report_end = $report_end->setTime(24, 0)->getTimestamp();
1640 
1641 
1642   // Construct the SQL query
1643   $sql_params = array();
1644   $sql = "SELECT E.*, "
1645        .  db()->syntax_timestamp_to_unix("E.timestamp") . " AS last_updated, "
1646        . "A.area_name, A.sort_key AS area_sort_key, R.room_name, R.sort_key AS room_sort_key, R.area_id, "
1647        . "A.approval_enabled, A.confirmation_enabled, A.enable_periods";
1648   if ($output_format == OUTPUT_ICAL)
1649   {
1650     // If we're producing an iCalendar then we'll also need the repeat
1651     // information in order to construct the recurrence rule
1652     $sql .= ", T.rep_type, T.end_date, T.rep_opt, T.rep_interval, T.month_absolute, T.month_relative";
1653   }
1654   $sql .= " FROM " . _tbl('entry') . " E
1655        LEFT JOIN " . _tbl('room') . " R
1656               ON E.room_id = R.id
1657        LEFT JOIN " . _tbl('area') . " A
1658               ON R.area_id = A.id";
1659 
1660   if ($output_format == OUTPUT_ICAL)
1661   {
1662     // We do a LEFT JOIN because we still want the single entries, ie the ones
1663     // that won't have a match in the repeat table
1664     $sql .= " LEFT JOIN " . _tbl('repeat') . " T
1665                      ON E.repeat_id=T.id";
1666   }
1667 
1668   $sql .= " WHERE E.start_time < ? AND E.end_time > ?";
1669   $sql_params[] = $report_end;
1670   $sql_params[] = $report_start;
1671   if ($output_format == OUTPUT_ICAL)
1672   {
1673     // We can't export periods in an iCalendar yet
1674     $sql .= " AND A.enable_periods=0";
1675   }
1676 
1677   // Get the match conditions for the simple cases
1678   $match_columns = array('A.area_name'    => $areamatch,
1679                          'R.room_name'    => $roommatch,
1680                          'E.name'         => $namematch,
1681                          'E.description'  => $descrmatch,
1682                          'E.create_by'    => $creatormatch);
1683 
1684   foreach ($match_columns as $column => $match)
1685   {
1686     $sql .= get_match_condition($column, $match, $sql_params);
1687   }
1688 
1689   // Then do the special cases
1690   if (!empty($typematch))
1691   {
1692     $sql .= " AND ";
1693     $or_array = array();
1694     foreach ( $typematch as $type )
1695     {
1696       // syntax_casesensitive_equals() modifies our SQL params array for us
1697       $or_array[] = db()->syntax_casesensitive_equals('E.type', $type, $sql_params);
1698     }
1699     $sql .= "(". implode(" OR ", $or_array ) .")";
1700   }
1701 
1702   // (In the next three cases, you will get the empty string if that part
1703   // of the form was not displayed - which means that you need all bookings)
1704   // Note that although you can say eg "status&STATUS_PRIVATE" in MySQL, you get
1705   // an error in PostgreSQL as the expression is of the wrong type.
1706 
1707   // Match the privacy status
1708   if (($match_private != BOOLEAN_MATCH_BOTH) && ($match_private !== ''))
1709   {
1710     $sql .= " AND ";
1711     $sql .= "(E.status&" . STATUS_PRIVATE;
1712     $sql .= ($match_private) ? "!=0)" : "=0)";  // Note that private works the other way round to the next two
1713   }
1714 
1715   // Match the confirmation status
1716   if (($match_confirmed != BOOLEAN_MATCH_BOTH) && ($match_confirmed !== ''))
1717   {
1718     $sql .= " AND ";
1719     $sql .= "(E.status&" . STATUS_TENTATIVE;
1720     $sql .= ($match_confirmed) ? "=0)" : "!=0)";
1721   }
1722   // Match the approval status
1723   if (($match_approved != BOOLEAN_MATCH_BOTH) && ($match_approved !== ''))
1724   {
1725     $sql .= " AND ";
1726     $sql .= "(E.status&" . STATUS_AWAITING_APPROVAL;
1727     $sql .= ($match_approved) ? "=0)" : "!=0)";
1728   }
1729 
1730   // Then do the custom fields
1731   foreach ($custom_fields as $key => $value)
1732   {
1733     $var = "match_$key";
1734     $sql .= get_match_condition("E.$key", $$var, $sql_params);
1735   }
1736 
1737   // We only want the bookings for rooms that are visible
1738   $invisible_room_ids = get_invisible_room_ids();
1739   if (count($invisible_room_ids) > 0)
1740   {
1741     $sql .= " AND (E.room_id NOT IN (" . implode(',', $invisible_room_ids) . "))";
1742   }
1743 
1744   // If we're not an admin (they are allowed to see everything), then we need
1745   // to make sure we respect the privacy settings.  (We rely on the privacy fields
1746   // in the area table being not NULL.   If they are by some chance NULL, then no
1747   // entries will be found, which is at least safe from the privacy viewpoint)
1748   if (!$cli_mode && !is_book_admin())
1749   {
1750     if (isset($mrbs_user))
1751     {
1752       // if the user is logged in they can see:
1753       //   - all bookings, if private_override is set to 'public'
1754       //   - their own bookings, and others' public bookings if private_override is set to 'none'
1755       //   - just their own bookings, if private_override is set to 'private'
1756       $sql .= " AND ((A.private_override='public') OR
1757                      ((A.private_override='none') AND ((E.status&" . STATUS_PRIVATE . "=0) OR (E.create_by = ?))) OR
1758                      ((A.private_override='private') AND (E.create_by = ?)))";
1759       $sql_params[] = $mrbs_user->username;
1760       $sql_params[] = $mrbs_user->username;
1761     }
1762     else
1763     {
1764       // if the user is not logged in they can see:
1765       //   - all bookings, if private_override is set to 'public'
1766       //   - public bookings if private_override is set to 'none'
1767       $sql .= " AND ((A.private_override='public') OR
1768                      ((A.private_override='none') AND (E.status&" . STATUS_PRIVATE . "=0)))";
1769     }
1770   }
1771 
1772   // If we're allowing unauthenticated requests and this is one then check that the
1773   // room is in the list of open rooms or the area is in the list of open areas.
1774   if ($report_unauthenticated_get_enabled && is_get_request())
1775   {
1776     $sql .= " AND (";
1777     $sql .= db()->syntax_in_list('A.id', $report_open_areas, $sql_params) . " OR ";
1778     $sql .= db()->syntax_in_list('R.id', $report_open_rooms, $sql_params);
1779     $sql .= ")";
1780   }
1781 
1782   if ($output_format == OUTPUT_ICAL)
1783   {
1784     // If we're producing an iCalendar then we'll want the entries ordered by
1785     // repeat_id and then start_time
1786     // Note that by default NULLs are low in MySQL and high in PostgreSQL and as it's
1787     // important that the NULLs (ie non-series entries) are at the beginning then we
1788     // need to be explicit about the sort order of NULLS.
1789     $sql .= " ORDER BY repeat_id IS NULL DESC, repeat_id, start_time";
1790   }
1791   elseif ($sortby == "r")
1792   {
1793     // Order by Area, Room, Start date/time
1794     $sql .= " ORDER BY A.sort_key, R.sort_key, start_time";
1795   }
1796   else
1797   {
1798     // Order by Start date/time, Area, Room
1799     $sql .= " ORDER BY start_time, A.sort_key, R.sort_key";
1800   }
1801 
1802   // echo "<p>DEBUG: SQL: <tt> $sql </tt></p>\n";
1803 
1804   $res = db()->query($sql, $sql_params);
1805   $nmatch = $res->count();
1806 }
1807 
1808 $combination_not_supported = ($output == SUMMARY) && ($output_format == OUTPUT_ICAL);
1809 
1810 $output_form = (($output_format == OUTPUT_HTML) && !$is_ajax &&!$cli_mode) ||
1811                $combination_not_supported;
1812 
1813 
1814 // print the page header
1815 if ($is_ajax)
1816 {
1817   // don't do anything if this is an Ajax request:  we only want the data
1818 }
1819 elseif ($output_form)
1820 {
1821   $context = array(
1822       'view'      => $view,
1823       'view_all'  => $view_all,
1824       'year'      => $year,
1825       'month'     => $month,
1826       'day'       => $day,
1827       'area'      => $area,
1828       'room'      => $room ?? null
1829     );
1830 
1831   print_header($context);
1832 }
1833 else
1834 {
1835   $filename = ($output == REPORT) ? $report_filename : $summary_filename;
1836   switch ($output_format)
1837   {
1838     case OUTPUT_CSV:
1839       $filename .= '.csv';
1840       $content_type = "text/csv; charset=" . get_csv_charset();
1841       break;
1842     default:
1843       require_once "functions_ical.inc";
1844       $filename .= '.ics';
1845       $content_type = "application/ics; charset=" . get_charset() . "; name=\"$filename\"";
1846       break;
1847   }
1848   if (!$cli_mode)
1849   {
1850     http_headers(array("Content-Type: $content_type",
1851                        "Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=\"$filename\""));
1852   }
1853 
1854   if (($output_format == OUTPUT_CSV) && $csv_bom)
1855   {
1856     echo get_bom(get_csv_charset());
1857   }
1858 }
1859 
1860 
1861 // Upper part: The form.
1862 if ($output_form)
1863 {
1864   echo "<div class=\"screenonly\">\n";
1865 
1866   $form = new Form(Form::METHOD_POST);
1867 
1868   // Search variables
1869   $search_var_keys = array('from_date', 'to_date',
1870                            'areamatch', 'roommatch',
1871                            'typematch', 'namematch', 'descrmatch', 'creatormatch',
1872                            'match_private', 'match_confirmed', 'match_approved',
1873                            'custom_fields');
1874   $search_vars = array();
1875   foreach($search_var_keys as $var)
1876   {
1877     $search_vars[$var] = $$var;
1878   }
1879 
1880   // Presentation variables
1881   $presentation_var_keys = array('output', 'output_format',
1882                                  'sortby', 'sumby');
1883   $presentation_vars = array();
1884   foreach($presentation_var_keys as $var)
1885   {
1886     $presentation_vars[$var] = $$var;
1887   }
1888 
1889   $attributes = array('id'     => 'report_form',
1890                       'class'  => 'standard',
1891                       'action' => multisite(this_page()));
1892 
1893   $form->setAttributes($attributes)
1894        ->addHiddenInput('phase', '2');
1895 
1896   $outer_fieldset = new ElementFieldset();
1897   $outer_fieldset->addLegend(get_vocab('report_on'))
1898                  ->addElement(get_fieldset_search_criteria($search_vars))
1899                  ->addElement(get_fieldset_presentation_options($presentation_vars))
1900                  ->addElement(get_fieldset_submit_buttons());
1901 
1902   $form->addElement($outer_fieldset);
1903 
1904   $form->render();
1905 
1906   echo "</div>\n";
1907 }
1908 
1909 // PHASE 2:  Output the results, if called with parameters:
1910 if ($phase == 2)
1911 {
1912   if (($nmatch == 0) && !$cli_mode && ($output_format == OUTPUT_HTML))
1913   {
1914     if ($is_ajax)
1915     {
1916       http_headers(array("Content-Type: application/json"));
1917       echo json_encode($json_data);
1918     }
1919     else
1920     {
1921       echo "<p class=\"report_entries\">" . get_vocab("nothing_found") . "</p>\n";
1922     }
1923     unset($res);
1924   }
1925   elseif ($combination_not_supported)
1926   {
1927     echo "<p>" . get_vocab("combination_not_supported") . "</p>\n";
1928     unset($res);
1929   }
1930   else
1931   {
1932     if ($output_format == OUTPUT_ICAL)
1933     {
1934       // We set $keep_private to FALSE here because we excluded all private
1935       // events in the SQL query
1936       export_icalendar($res, FALSE, $report_end);
1937       exit;
1938     }
1939 
1940     if (($output_format == OUTPUT_HTML) && !$is_ajax)
1941     {
1942       echo "<p class=\"report_entries\"><span id=\"n_entries\">" . $nmatch . "</span> "
1943       . ($nmatch == 1 ? get_vocab("entry_found") : get_vocab("entries_found"))
1944       .  "</p>\n";
1945     }
1946 
1947     // Report
1948     if ($output == REPORT)
1949     {
1950       open_report();
1951       report_header();
1952       $body_rows = array();
1953       while (false !== ($row = $res->next_row_keyed()))
1954       {
1955         $row = clean_row($row);
1956         report_row($body_rows, $row);
1957       }
1958       output_body_rows($body_rows, $output_format);
1959       close_report();
1960     }
1961     // Summary
1962     else
1963     {
1964       open_summary();
1965       if ($nmatch > 0)
1966       {
1967         while (false !== ($row = $res->next_row_keyed()))
1968         {
1969           $row = clean_row($row);
1970           accumulate_summary($row, $count, $hours,
1971                              $report_start, $report_end,
1972                              $room_hash, $name_hash);
1973         }
1974         do_summary($count, $hours, $room_hash, $name_hash);
1975       }
1976       else
1977       {
1978         // Excel doesn't seem to like an empty file with just a BOM, so give
1979         // it an empty row as well to keep it happy
1980         $values = array();
1981         output_row($values, $output_format);
1982       }
1983       close_summary();
1984     }
1985   }
1986 }
1987 
1988 if ($cli_mode)
1989 {
1990   exit(0);
1991 }
1992 
1993 if ($output_form)
1994 {
1995   print_footer();
1996 }

/standard_vars.inc.php

   1 <?php
   2 declare(strict_types=1);
   3 namespace MRBS;
   4 
   5 // Gets the standard variables of $day, $month, $year, $area and $room
   6 // Checks that they are valid and assigns sensible defaults if not
   7 
   8 // Get the standard form variables
   9 use DateInterval;
  10 
  11 $page_date = get_form_var('page_date', 'string');
  12 $view = get_form_var('view', 'string', $default_view ?? 'day');
  13 $view_all = get_form_var('view_all', 'int', empty($default_view_all) ? 0 : 1);  // Whether to view all rooms
  14 $year = get_form_var('year', 'int');
  15 $month = get_form_var('month', 'int');
  16 $day = get_form_var('day', 'int');
  17 $area = get_form_var('area', 'int');
  18 $room = get_form_var('room', 'int');
  19 $kiosk = get_form_var('kiosk', 'string');
  20 
  21 if (empty($area))
  22 {
  23   $area = get_default_area();
  24 }
  25 
  26 if (empty($room))
  27 {
  28   $room = get_default_room($area);
  29 }
  30 
  31 // No point in showing all the rooms if there's only one of them.  Show
  32 // the normal view (with time slots) instead
  33 if (($view != 'day') && !$always_offer_view_all & count(get_rooms($area)) == 1)
  34 {
  35   $view_all = 0;
  36 }
  37 
  38 // Get the settings (resolution, etc.) for this area
  39 get_area_settings($area);
  40 
  41 if (isset($page_date) && ($page_date !== ''))
  42 {
  43   if (false === ($page_date_split = split_iso_date($page_date)))
  44   {
  45     if (is_ajax())
  46     {
  47       http_response_code(500);
  48       trigger_error("Ajax: invalid page_date '$page_date'", E_USER_NOTICE);
  49       exit;
  50     }
  51     trigger_error("Invalid page_date '$page_date'", E_USER_NOTICE);
  52   }
  53   else
  54   {
  55     list($year, $month, $day) = $page_date_split;
  56   }
  57 }
  58 
  59 $date = new DateTime();
  60 
  61 // If we're in kiosk mode and the current time is after the end of the last slot
  62 // then advance to tomorrow - unless we're in periods mode when we don't know
  63 // the actual time of the last slot.
  64 if (isset($kiosk))
  65 {
  66   if (!$enable_periods && ($date->getTimestamp() > get_end_last_slot($date->getMonth(), $date->getDay(), $date->getYear())))
  67   {
  68     $date->add(new DateInterval('P1D'));
  69   }
  70 }
  71 // If we are not in kiosk mode and have been given a date then use that
  72 elseif (!empty($day) && !empty($month) && !empty($year))
  73 {
  74   $date->setDate($year, $month, $day);
  75 }
  76 
  77 // Advance to the next non-hidden day
  78 if (!empty($hidden_days) &&     // Use !empty in case $hidden_days is not set
  79     (count($hidden_days) < 7))  // Avoid an infinite loop
  80 {
  81   while ($date->isHiddenDay())
  82   {
  83     $date->modify('+1 day');
  84   }
  85 }
  86 
  87 $day = $date->getDay();
  88 $month = $date->getMonth();
  89 $year = $date->getYear();

/style.inc

   1 <?php
   2 declare(strict_types=1);
   3 namespace MRBS;
   4 
   5 
   6 // Generates the HTML for a <link> element
   7 function link_html(string $href, bool $add_version=false, ?string $media=null) : string
   8 {
   9   $html = '<link rel="stylesheet" type="text/css" href="';
  10   $value = ($add_version) ? add_version($href) : $href;
  11   $html .= escape_html($value) . '"';
  12   if (isset($media))
  13   {
  14     $html .= " media=\"$media\"";
  15   }
  16   $html .= ">\n";
  17 
  18   return $html;
  19 }
  20 
  21 
  22 global $custom_css_url;
  23 global $debug;
  24 
  25 echo link_html(($debug) ? 'jquery/ui/css/jquery-ui.structure.css' : 'jquery/ui/css/jquery-ui.structure.min.css', true);
  26 echo link_html(($debug) ? 'jquery/ui/css/cupertino/jquery-ui.theme.css' : 'jquery/ui/css/cupertino/jquery-ui.theme.min.css', true);
  27 echo link_html(($debug) ? 'jquery/datatables/datatables.css' : 'jquery/datatables/datatables.min.css', true);
  28 echo link_html('js/flatpickr/css/flatpickr.min.css', true);
  29 echo link_html('jquery/select2/dist/css/select2.min.css', true);
  30 echo link_html(multisite('css/mrbs.css.php'), true);
  31 
  32 if (using_rtl_lang())
  33 {
  34   echo link_html(multisite('css/mrbs-rtl.css.php'), true);
  35 }
  36 
  37 echo link_html(multisite('css/mrbs-print.css.php'), true, 'print');
  38 
  39 echo "<!--[if IE]>\n";
  40 echo link_html('css/mrbs-ie.css', true);
  41 if (using_rtl_lang())
  42 {
  43   echo link_html('css/mrbs-ie-rtl.css', true);
  44 }
  45 echo "<![endif]-->\n";
  46 
  47 if (isset($custom_css_url))
  48 {
  49   echo link_html($custom_css_url, true);
  50 }

/systemdefaults.inc.php

   1 <?php
   2 declare(strict_types=1);
   3 namespace MRBS;
   4 
   5 use IntlDateFormatter;
   6 
   7 require_once 'lib/autoload.inc';
   8 
   9 /**************************************************************************
  10  *   MRBS system defaults file
  11  *
  12  * DO _NOT_ MODIFY THIS FILE YOURSELF. IT IS FOR _INTERNAL_ USE ONLY.
  13  *
  14  * TO CONFIGURE MRBS FOR YOUR SYSTEM ADD CONFIGURATION PARAMETERS FROM
  15  * THIS FILE INTO config.inc.php, DO _NOT_ EDIT THIS FILE.
  16  *
  17  **************************************************************************/
  18 
  19 /********
  20  * System
  21  ********/
  22 
  23 // Set $debug = true to force MRBS to output debugging information to the browser.
  24 // Caching of files is also disabled when $debug is set.
  25 // WARNING!  Do not use this for production systems, as not only will it generate
  26 // unnecessary output in the browser, but it could also expose sensitive security
  27 // information (eg database usernames and passwords).
  28 $debug = false;
  29 
  30 
  31 /*********
  32  * Logging
  33  *********/
  34 
  35 $logger_settings['channel_name'] = 'MRBS';
  36 
  37 // Whether to send log messages by email
  38 $logger_settings['mail']['enabled'] = false;
  39 
  40 // The From address - RFC 822 format
  41 $logger_settings['mail']['from'] = 'logging@your.org';
  42 
  43 // The To address - can be a comma separated list (RFC 822 format)
  44 $logger_settings['mail']['to'] = 'logging@your.org';
  45 
  46 // The level at which to start sending emails. See lib/Psr/Log/LogLevel.php.
  47 $logger_settings['mail']['level'] = \Psr\Log\LogLevel::ERROR;
  48 
  49 // Whether to send stream output to the browser
  50 $logger_settings['stream']['browser'] = true;
  51 
  52 // Whether to send stream output to the browser console
  53 $logger_settings['stream']['console'] = false;
  54 
  55 
  56 /**********
  57  * Timezone
  58  **********/
  59 
  60 // The timezone your meeting rooms run in. It is especially important
  61 // to set this if you're using PHP 5 on Linux. In this configuration
  62 // if you don't, meetings in a different DST than you are currently
  63 // in are offset by the DST offset incorrectly.
  64 //
  65 // Note that timezones can be set on a per-area basis, so strictly speaking this
  66 // setting should be in areadefaults.inc.php, but as it is so important to set
  67 // the right timezone it is included here.
  68 //
  69 // When upgrading an existing installation, this should be set to the
  70 // timezone the web server runs in.  See the INSTALL document for more information.
  71 //
  72 // A list of valid timezones can be found at http://php.net/manual/timezones.php
  73 // The following line must be uncommented by removing the '//' at the beginning
  74 //$timezone = "Europe/London";
  75 
  76 // If you are using iCalendar notifications of bookings (see the mail settings below)
  77 // then the iCalendar attachment includes a definition of your timezone in
  78 // VTIMEZONE format.   This defines the timezone, including the rules for Daylight
  79 // Saving Time transitions.    This information is included in the MRBS distribution.
  80 // However, as governments can change the rules periodically, MRBS will check from
  81 // time to time to see if there is a later version available on the web.   If your
  82 // site prevents external access to the web, this check will time out.  However
  83 // you can avoid the timeout and stop MRBS checking for up to date versions by
  84 // setting $zoneinfo_update = false;
  85 $zoneinfo_update = true;
  86 
  87 // The VTIMEZONE definitions exist in two forms - normal and Outlook compatible.
  88 // $zoneinfo_outlook_compatible determines which ones to use.
  89 $zoneinfo_outlook_compatible = true;
  90 
  91 // The VTIMEZONE definitions are cached in the database with an expiry time
  92 // of $zoneinfo_expiry seconds.   If your server does not have external internet
  93 // access set $zoneinfo_expiry to PHP_INT_MAX to prevent MRBS from trying to
  94 // update the VTIMEZONE definitions.
  95 $zoneinfo_expiry = 60*60*24*7;    // 7 days
  96 
  97 /*******************
  98  * Database settings
  99  ******************/
 100 // Which database system: "pgsql"=PostgreSQL, "mysql"=MySQL
 101 // ("mysqli" is also supported for historical reasons and is mapped to "mysql")
 102 $dbsys = "mysql";
 103 // Hostname of database server. For pgsql, can use "" instead of localhost
 104 // to use Unix Domain Sockets instead of TCP/IP. For mysql "localhost"
 105 // tells the system to use Unix Domain Sockets, and $db_port will be ignored;
 106 // if you want to force TCP connection you can use "127.0.0.1".
 107 $db_host = "localhost";
 108 // If you need to use a non-standard port for the database connection you
 109 // can uncomment the following line and specify the port number
 110 // $db_port = 1234;
 111 // Database name:
 112 $db_database = "mrbs";
 113 // Schema name.  This only applies to PostgreSQL and is only necessary if you have more
 114 // than one schema in your database, and you are also using the same MRBS table names in
 115 // multiple schemas.
 116 //$db_schema = "public";
 117 // Database login username:
 118 $db_login = "mrbs";
 119 // Database login password:
 120 $db_password = 'mrbs-password';
 121 // Prefix for table names.  This will allow multiple installations where only
 122 // one database is available
 123 $db_tbl_prefix = "mrbs_";
 124 // Set $db_persist to true to use PHP persistent (pooled) database connections.  Note
 125 // that persistent connections are not recommended unless your system suffers significant
 126 // performance problems without them.   They can cause problems with transactions and
 127 // locks (see http://php.net/manual/en/features.persistent-connections.php) and although
 128 // MRBS tries to avoid those problems, it is generally better not to use persistent
 129 // connections if you can.
 130 $db_persist = false;
 131 // The number of times to retry getting a database connection in the event that there are
 132 // too many connections.  [MySQL only at the moment]
 133 $db_retries = 2;
 134 // The number of milliseconds to wait before retrying.  [MySQL only at the moment]
 135 $db_delay = 750; // milliseconds
 136

 142 // following options. (You may need to use the 'nd_pdo_mysql' extension
 143 // instead of 'pdo_mysql'.)
 144 
 145 // The file path to the SSL certificate authority.
 146 $db_options['mysql']['ssl_ca'] = null;

 149 $db_options['mysql']['ssl_capath'] = null;

 156 $db_options['mysql']['ssl_cipher'] = null;
 157 
 158 // The file path to the SSL key.
 159 $db_options['mysql']['ssl_key'] = null;
 160 
 161 // Provides a way to disable verification of the server SSL certificate.
 162 $db_options['mysql']['ssl_verify_server_cert'] = null;  // boolean

 192  *********************************/
 193 
 194 // Set to true to enable multisite operation, in which case the settings below are for the
 195 // home site, identified by the empty string ''.   Other sites have their own supplementary
 196 // config fies in the sites/<sitename> directory.
 197 $multisite = false;
 198 $default_site = '';
 199 
 200 $mrbs_admin = "Your Administrator";
 201 $mrbs_admin_email = "admin_email@your.org";
 202 // NOTE:  there are more email addresses in $mail_settings below.    You can also give
 203 // email addresses in the format 'Full Name <address>', for example:
 204 // $mrbs_admin_email = 'Booking System <admin_email@your.org>';
 205 // if the name section has any "peculiar" characters in it, you will need
 206 // to put the name in double quotes, e.g.:
 207 // $mrbs_admin_email = '"Bloggs, Joe" <admin_email@your.org>';
 208 
 209 // The company name is mandatory.   It is used in the header and also for email notifications.
 210 // The company logo, additional information and URL are all optional.

 212 $mrbs_company = "Your Company";   // This line must always be uncommented ($mrbs_company is used in various places)
 213 
 214 // Uncomment this next line to use a logo instead of text for your organisation in the header
 215 //$mrbs_company_logo = "your_logo.gif";    // name of your logo file.   This example assumes it is in the MRBS directory
 216 
 217 // Uncomment this next line for supplementary information after your company name or logo.
 218 // This can contain HTML, for example if you want to include a link.
 219 //$mrbs_company_more_info = "You can put additional information here";  // e.g. "XYZ Department"
 220 
 221 // Uncomment this next line to have a link to your organisation in the header
 222 //$mrbs_company_url = "http://www.your_organisation.com/";
 223 
 224 // This is to fix URL problems when using a proxy in the environment.

 230 /*******************
 231  * Themes
 232  *******************/
 233 
 234 // Choose a theme for the MRBS.   The theme controls two aspects of the look and feel:
 235 //   (a) the styling:  the most commonly changed colours, dimensions and fonts have been
 236 //       extracted from the main CSS file and put into the styling.inc file in the appropriate
 237 //       directory in the Themes directory.   If you want to change the colour scheme, you should
 238 //       be able to do it by changing the values in the theme file.    More advanced styling changes
 239 //       can be made by changing the rules in the CSS file.
 240 //   (b) the header:  the header.inc file which contains the function used for producing the header.
 241 //       This enables organisations to plug in their own header functions quite easily, in cases where
 242 //       the desired corporate look and feel cannot be changed using the CSS alone and the mark-up
 243 //       itself needs to be changed.
 244 //
 245 //  MRBS will look for the files "styling.inc" and "header.inc" in the directory Themes/$theme and
 246 //  if it can't find them will use the files in Themes/default.    A theme directory can contain
 247 //  a replacement styling.inc file or a replacement header.inc file or both.
 248 
 249 // Available options are:
 250 
 251 // "default"        Default MRBS theme
 252 // "classic126"     Same colour scheme as MRBS 1.2.6
 253 
 254 $theme = "default";
 255 
 256 // Use the $custom_css_url to override the standard MRBS CSS.
 257 //$custom_css_url = 'css/custom.css';
 258 
 259 // Use the $custom_js_url to add your own JavaScript.
 260 //$custom_js_url = 'js/custom.js';
 261 
 262 
 263 /*******************
 264  * Calendar settings
 265  *******************/
 266 
 267 // MRBS has two different modes of operation: "times" and "periods".   "Times"
 268 // based bookings allow you to define regular consecutive booking slots, eg every
 269 // half an hour from 7.00 am to 7.00 pm.   "Periods" based bookings are useful
 270 // in, for example, schools where the booking slots are of different lengths
 271 // and are not consecutive because of change-over time or breaks.
 272 
 273 // It is not possible to swap between these two options once bookings have
 274 // been created and to have meaningful entries.  This is due to differences
 275 // in the way that the data is stored.
 276 
 277 // It is however possible to configure the system so that some areas operate in
 278 // "periods" mode and others in "times" mode.    Therefore the configuration variable
 279 // that determines the default setting for new areas appears together with other
 280 // variables that can be set on a per-area basis in the file areadefaults.inc.php.
 281 // This is done to draw attention to the fact that they are default settings for new
 282 // areas only and to avoid frustration when trying to change settings for existing
 283 // areas: this is done by editing the settings for an area using a web browser by
 284 // following the "Rooms" link in MRBS.
 285 
 286 
 287 // TIMES SETTINGS
 288 // --------------
 289 
 290 // The times settings can all be configured on a per-area basis, so these variables
 291 // appear in the areadefaults.inc.php file.
 292 
 293 
 294 // PERIODS SETTINGS
 295 // ----------------
 296 
 297 // The "Periods" settings are used only in areas where the mode has
 298 // been set to "Periods".
 299 
 300 
 301 /******************
 302  * Booking policies
 303  ******************/
 304 
 305 // Most booking policies can be configured on a per-area basis, so these variables
 306 // appear in the areadefaults.inc.php file.
 307 
 308 // The settings below are global policy settings
 309 
 310 // Set the maximum *number* of bookings that can be made by any one user, in an interval,
 311 // which can be a day, week, month or year, or else in the future.  (A week is defined
 312 // by the $weekstarts setting).   These are global settings, but you can additionally
 313 // configure per area settings.   This would allow you to set policies such as allowing
 314 // a maximum of 10 bookings per month in total with a maximum of 1 per day in Area A.
 315 $max_per_interval_global_enabled['day']    = false;
 316 $max_per_interval_global['day'] = 1;      // max 1 booking per day in total
 317 
 318 $max_per_interval_global_enabled['week']   = false;
 319 $max_per_interval_global['week'] = 5;     // max 5 bookings per week in total
 320 
 321 $max_per_interval_global_enabled['month']  = false;
 322 $max_per_interval_global['month'] = 10;   // max 10 bookings per month in total
 323 
 324 $max_per_interval_global_enabled['year']   = false;
 325 $max_per_interval_global['year'] = 50;    // max 50 bookings per year in total
 326 
 327 $max_per_interval_global_enabled['future'] = false;
 328 $max_per_interval_global['future'] = 100; // max 100 bookings in the future in total
 329 
 330 // Set the maximum total *length* of bookings that can be made by any one user, in an interval,
 331 // which can be a day, week, month or year, or else in the future.  (A week is defined
 332 // by the $weekstarts setting).   These are global settings, but you can additionally
 333 // configure per area settings.   This would allow you to set policies such as allowing a
 334 // maximum of 10 hours per week in total with a maximum of 1 hour per day in Area A.
 335 // These settings only apply to areas in "times" mode.
 336 
 337 $max_secs_per_interval_global_enabled['day']    = false;
 338 $max_secs_per_interval_global['day'] = 60*60*2;      // max 2 hours per day in total
 339 
 340 $max_secs_per_interval_global_enabled['week']   = false;
 341 $max_secs_per_interval_global['week'] = 60*60*10;    // max 10 hours per week in total
 342 
 343 $max_secs_per_interval_global_enabled['month']  = false;
 344 $max_secs_per_interval_global['month'] = 60*60*25;   // max 25 hours per month in total
 345 
 346 $max_secs_per_interval_global_enabled['year']   = false;
 347 $max_secs_per_interval_global['year'] = 60*60*100;   // max 100 hours per year in total
 348 
 349 $max_secs_per_interval_global_enabled['future'] = false;
 350 $max_secs_per_interval_global['future'] = 60*60*100; // max 100 hours in the future in total
 351 
 352 // Set the latest date for which you can make a booking.    This can be useful if you
 353 // want to set an absolute date, eg the end of term, beyond which bookings cannot be made.
 354 // If you want to set a relative date, eg no more than a week away, then this can be done
 355 // using the area settings.   Note that it is possible to have both a relative and absolute
 356 // date, eg "no more than a week away and in any case not past the end of term".
 357 // Note that bookings are allowed on the $max_booking_date, but not after it.
 358 $max_booking_date_enabled = false;
 359 $max_booking_date = "2012-07-23";  // Must be a string in the format "yyyy-mm-dd"
 360 
 361 // Set the earliest date for which you can make a booking.    This can be useful if you
 362 // want to set an absolute date, eg the beginning of term, before which bookings cannot be made.
 363 // If you want to set a relative date, eg no more than a week away, then this can be done
 364 // using the area settings.   Note that it is possible to have both a relative and absolute
 365 // date, eg "no earlier than a week away and in any case not before the beginning of term".
 366 // Note that bookings are allowed on the $min_booking_date, but not before it.
 367 $min_booking_date_enabled = false;
 368 $min_booking_date = "2012-04-23";  // Must be a string in the format "yyyy-mm-dd"
 369 
 370 // Set this to true if you want to prevent users editing or deleting approved bookings.
 371 // Note that this setting only applies if booking approval is in force for the area.
 372 // If it isn't in force you can prevent bookings being edited or deleted by using the
 373 // min and max delete ahead settings.
 374 $approved_bookings_cannot_be_changed = false;
 375 
 376 // Set this to true if you want to prevent users having a booking for multiple rooms
 377 // at the same time.
 378 $prevent_simultaneous_bookings = false;
 379 
 380 // The maximum number of simultaneous bookings allowed if $prevent_simultaneous_bookings is true.
 381 $max_simultaneous_bookings = 1;
 382 
 383 // Whether to count simultaneous bookings just in the area concerned (true), or globally (false).
 384 // NOTE: it only makes sense to count globally if all the enabled areas are in "times" mode; or
 385 // they are in "periods" mode and the periods in each area correspond to the same time; or there
 386 // is only one area.
 387 $simultaneous_ignore_other_areas = false;
 388 
 389 // Set this to true if you want to prevent bookings of a type that is invalid for a room or day of the week
 390 $prevent_invalid_types = true;
 391 
 392 // Provided $prevent_invalid_types is set to true, this can be used to specify a set of days of the
 393 // week (0 = Sunday) that are invalid for a certain type.  For example
 394 // $invalid_types_days['I'] = [1, 3] means that bookings of type 'I' cannot be made on Mondays or Wednesdays.
 395 $invalid_types_days = array();
 396 
 397 // The start of the booking day when using periods.  Because MRBS has
 398 // no notion of when periods actually occur they are assumed to start
 399 // at the time below when we are enforcing book ahead policies.
 400 // The setting defines the time of day when bookings open.
 401 // This should be a string in the format hh:mm using the 24-hour clock.
 402 $periods_booking_opens = '00:00';
 403 
 404 // When setting max_create_ahead and max_delete_ahead policies, the time interval is normally
 405 // measured to the end time of the booking.  This is to prevent users cheating the system by
 406 // booking a very long slot with the start time just inside the limit and then either not using
 407 // the early part of the booking, or else editing it down to what they actually need later.
 408 // However this is not very intuitive for users who might expect the measurement to be relative
 409 // to the start time, in which case this can be achieved by changing this setting to true.
 410 $measure_max_to_start_time = false;
 411 
 412 // By default, bookings cannot be made on days that are designated holidays (see $holidays).
 413 $prevent_booking_on_holidays = true;
 414 
 415 // Set this to true to prevent bookings being made on weekends (see $weekdays).
 416 $prevent_booking_on_weekends = false;
 417 
 418 
 419 /******************
 420  * Display settings
 421  ******************/
 422 
 423 // [These are all variables that control the appearance of pages and could in time
 424 //  become per-user settings]
 425 
 426 // The maximum number of slots per day in an area for the year view to be shown.
 427 // Because each slot takes a minimum of 1 pixel and there are 365/366 days in a
 428 // year, the year view can get very wide.  It is therefore only shown if there
 429 // are only a few slots per day in an area.  Set this to zero to disable the year
 430 // view completely.
 431 // Note: the year view button is not displayed on narrow screens.
 432 $max_slots_for_year_view = 4;
 433 
 434 // Start of the week: 0 for Sunday, 1 for Monday, etc.
 435 $weekstarts = 0;
 436 
 437 // Start of the year: 1 for January, 2 for February, etc.
 438 // 0 for the current month
 439 $year_start = 1;
 440 
 441 // Days of the week that are weekdays
 442 $weekdays = array(1, 2, 3, 4, 5);
 443 
 444 // Set this to true to add styling to weekend days
 445 $style_weekends = false;
 446 
 447 // A two-dimensional array of holidays in yyyy-mm-dd format, indexed first by year, for example
 448 // $holidays[2022] = array('2022-01-01', '2022-11-24');  // New Year's Day and US Thanksgiving 2022
 449 // Dates can include ranges in the form 'yyyy-mm-dd..yyyy-mm-dd', eg
 450 // $holidays[2022] = array('2022-01-01', '2022-07-01..2022-07-31');  // New Year's Day and all of July
 451 // By default, bookings cannot be made on days that are designated holidays (see $prevent_booking_on_holidays).
 452 // Holidays are styled differently in the main calendar views.
 453 $holidays = array();
 454 
 455 // Days of the week that should be hidden from display
 456 // 0 for Sunday, 1 for Monday, etc.
 457 // For example, if you want Saturdays and Sundays to be hidden set $hidden_days = array(0,6);
 458 //
 459 // By default the hidden days will be removed completely from the main table in the week and month
 460 // views.   You can alternatively arrange for them to be shown as narrow, greyed-out columns
 461 // by defining some custom CSS for the .hidden_day class.
 462 $hidden_days = array();
 463 
 464 // Whether to display the timezone
 465 $display_timezone = false;
 466 
 467 // Whether to scroll automatically so that the current time slot is in view
 468 $autoscroll = true;
 469 
 470 // Results per page for searching:
 471 $search["count"] = 20;
 472 
 473 // Page refresh time (in seconds). Set to 0 to disable.
 474 // (Note that if MRBS detects that a client is on a metered network
 475 // connection it will disable page refresh for that client.)
 476 $refresh_rate = 0;
 477 
 478 // Refresh rate (in seconds) for Ajax checking of valid bookings on the edit_entry page
 479 // Set to 0 to disable.
 480 $ajax_refresh_rate = 10;
 481 
 482 // Refresh rate for page pre-fetches in the calendar views.   MRBS tries to improve
 483 // performance of navigation between pages in the calendar view by pre-fetching some
 484 // pages.   This setting determines how often (in seconds) the pre-fetches should be
 485 // refreshed in order to keep them from getting out of date.  Set to 0 to disable.
 486 $prefetch_refresh_rate = 30;
 487 
 488 // Refresh rate (in seconds) when in kiosk mode
 489 $kiosk_refresh_rate = 300; // 5 minutes
 490 
 491 // Whether kiosk mode is enabled
 492 $kiosk_mode_enabled = false;
 493 
 494 // Default mode for kiosk mode.  Can be 'room' or 'area'.
 495 $kiosk_default_mode = 'room';
 496 
 497 // Whether to show a QR code in kiosk mode
 498 // Note that PHP 7.4 or greater and the mbstring extension are required for a QR code
 499 $kiosk_QR_code = true;
 500 
 501 // Timeout if the exit kiosk mode dialog is not acted upon
 502 $kiosk_exit_dialog_timeout = 10; // seconds
 503 
 504 // Timeout if there is no activity on the kiosk exit page
 505 $kiosk_exit_page_timeout = 10; // seconds
 506 
 507 // Entries in monthly view can be shown as start/end slot, brief description or
 508 // both. Set to "description" for brief description, "slot" for time slot and
 509 // "both" for both. Default is "both", but 6 entries per day are shown instead
 510 // of 12.
 511 $monthly_view_entries_details = "both";
 512 
 513 // To show week numbers in the main calendar, set this to true. The week
 514 // numbers are only displayed if you set $weekstarts to start on the first
 515 // day of the week in your locale and area's timezone.  (This assumes that
 516 // the PHP IntlCalendar class is available; if not, the week is assumed to
 517 // start on Mondays, ie the ISO stanard.)
 518 $view_week_number = false;
 519 
 520 // To display week numbers in the mini-calendars, set this to true. The week
 521 // numbers are only displayed if you set $weekstarts to the start of the week.
 522 // See the comment about when the week starts above.
 523 $mincals_week_numbers = false;
 524 
 525 // Whether or not the mini-calendars are displayed.  (Note that mini-calendars are only
 526 // displayed anyway if the window is wide enough.)
 527 $display_mincals = true;
 528 
 529 // If the window is too narrow the mini-calendars are normally not displayed.  However by
 530 // setting the following variable to true they will be displayed above the main calendar,
 531 // provided the window is high enough.
 532 $display_mincals_above = false;
 533 
 534 // To display the endtime in the slot description, eg '09:00-09:30' instead of '09:00', set
 535 // this to true.
 536 $show_slot_endtime = false;
 537 
 538 // To display the row labels (times, rooms or days) on the right hand side as well as the
 539 // left hand side in the day and week views, set to true;
 540 // (was called $times_right_side in earlier versions of MRBS)
 541 $row_labels_both_sides = false;
 542 
 543 // To display the column headers (times, rooms or days) on the bottom of the table as
 544 // well as the top in the day and week views, set to true;
 545 $column_labels_both_ends = false;
 546 
 547 // Show a line in the day and week views corresponding to the current time(
 548 $show_timeline = true;  // normal mode
 549 $show_timeline_kiosk = false;  // kiosk mode
 550 
 551 // For bookings that allow registration, show the number of people that have
 552 // registered and, if there is one, the registration limit.  This will typically
 553 // be appended to the description in the calendar view, eg "Lecture [12/40]".
 554 // The way the registration level is presented can be changed with a
 555 // $vocab_override config setting.
 556 $show_registration_level = true;
 557 
 558 // Define default starting view (month, week or day)
 559 // Default is day
 560 $default_view = "day";
 561 
 562 // The default setting for the week and month views: whether to view all the
 563 // rooms (true) or not (false).
 564 $default_view_all = true;
 565 
 566 // If there's only one room in an area, the view_all option will not normally
 567 // be offered.  This can be overridden by setting the variable below to true.
 568 $always_offer_view_all = false;

 570 // Define default room to start with (used by index.php)

 576 // Define clipping behaviour for the cells in the day and week views.
 577 // Set to true if you want the cells in the day and week views to be clipped.   This

 579 // Alternatively set to false if you want the cells to expand to fit the content.

 581 $clipped = true;
 582 
 583 // Define clipping behaviour for the cells in the month view.

 586 // each booking entry will be large enough to display all information.
 587 $clipped_month = true;
 588 
 589 // Set to true if you want the cells in the month view to scroll if there are too

 591 // accommodate the bookings.
 592 $month_cell_scrolling = true;
 593 
 594 // Define the maximum length of a string that can be displayed in an admin table cell
 595 // (eg the rooms and users lists) before it is truncated.  (This is necessary because
 596 // you don't want a cell to contain for example a 2 kbyte text string, which could happen
 597 // with user defined fields).
 598 $max_content_length = 20;  // characters
 599 
 600 // The maximum length of a database field for which a text input can be used on a form
 601 // (eg when editing a user or room).  If longer than this a text area will be used.
 602 $text_input_max = 70;  // characters
 603 
 604 // For inputs that have autocomplete options, eg the area and room match inputs on
 605 // the report page, we can define how many characters need to be input before the
 606 // options are displayed.  This enables us to prevent a huge long list of options
 607 // being presented.   We define the breakpoints in an array.   For example if we set
 608 // $autocomplete_length_breaks = array(25, 250, 2500); this means that if the number of options
 609 // is less than 25 then they will be displayed when 0 characters are input, ie the input

 612 // is empty then the options are displayed when 0 characters are input.

 661 /***********************
 662  * Date and time formats
 663  ***********************/
 664 
 665 // MRBS uses PHP's IntlDateFormatter and IntlDatePatternGenerator classes for formatting
 666 // dates and times in the user's locale.  On systems where the 'intl' extension is not
 667 // enabled, MRBS emulates those two classes and uses the strftime() function. However,
 668 // strftime() is deprecated from PHP 8.1 onwards, and you are recommended to ensure that
 669 // the 'intl' extension is enabled.
 670 //
 671 // The formats used by MRBS are specified using the $datetime_formats configuration
 672 // settings below. Each setting is an associative array, indexed by four possible keys:
 673 //
 674 //    'date_type'   one of the IntlDateFormatter constants (ie FULL, LONG, MEDIUM, SHORT
 675 //                  or NONE; default FULL).  Note that the RELATIVE_ constants are not
 676 //                  supported by the emulation.
 677 //    'time_type'   one of the IntlDateFormatter constants (ie FULL, LONG, MEDIUM, SHORT
 678 //                  or NONE; default FULL).
 679 //    'skeleton'    a "skeleton".  See
 680 //                  https://unicode-org.github.io/icu/userguide/format_parse/datetime/#datetimepatterngenerator.
 681 //                  Note that not all skeletons are emulated.
 682 //    'pattern'     a "pattern".  See https://unicode-org.github.io/icu/userguide/format_parse/datetime/
 683 //
 684 //    If a 'skeleton' is specified and a pattern can be generated from the skeleton, that
 685 //    will be used; otherwise the 'pattern' is used.  If no skeleton or pattern are specified
 686 //    then the appropriate date and time representations for 'date_type' and 'time_type' will
 687 //    be used.
 688 //
 689 //    Note that IntlDateFormatter automatically determines whether a 12 or 24-hour clock should
 690 //    be used based on the locale. If you need to override this and force a 12 or 24-hour clock
 691 //    then you will need to override the settings below in your config file with formats using
 692 //    patterns instead of date_type and time_type.  For example, the en-AU locale will use a 12-
 693 //    hour clock by default.  To force a 24-hour clock for time set
 694 //
 695 //    $datetime_formats['time'] = array(
 696 //      'pattern' => 'HH:mm'
 697 //    );
 698 //
 699 //    and similarly for the other formats involving time.  The files in intl/types are useful for
 700 //    seeing what the default pattern is for a locale.
 701 
 702 // The format used for dates
 703 $datetime_formats['date'] = array(
 704   'date_type' => IntlDateFormatter::FULL,
 705   'time_type' => IntlDateFormatter::NONE
 706 );
 707 
 708 // By default the datepickers use a date format appropriate to the locale.  If you want to
 709 // override this, set 'pattern' as required, eg to 'y-MM-dd' for ISO8601 format.  Note: only
 710 // the 'pattern' key is recognised.
 711 $datetime_formats['datepicker'] = array(
 712   'pattern' => null
 713 );
 714 
 715 // The format used for dates with times
 716 $datetime_formats['date_and_time'] = array(
 717   'date_type' => IntlDateFormatter::FULL,
 718   'time_type' => IntlDateFormatter::SHORT
 719 );
 720 
 721 // The format used for dates with times on the Help page
 722 $datetime_formats['date_and_time_help'] = array(
 723   'date_type' => IntlDateFormatter::FULL,
 724   'time_type' => IntlDateFormatter::LONG
 725 );
 726 
 727 // The format used for dates with times on the Report
 728 $datetime_formats['date_and_time_report'] = array(
 729   'date_type' => IntlDateFormatter::FULL,
 730   'time_type' => IntlDateFormatter::SHORT
 731 );
 732 
 733 // Used in policy violation reports for holidays and weekends
 734 $datetime_formats['date_holiday'] = array(
 735   'date_type' => IntlDateFormatter::SHORT,
 736   'time_type' => IntlDateFormatter::NONE
 737 );
 738 
 739 // Used on the Search page
 740 $datetime_formats['date_search'] = array(
 741   'date_type' => IntlDateFormatter::SHORT,
 742   'time_type' => IntlDateFormatter::NONE
 743 );
 744 
 745 // The default format for day names
 746 $datetime_formats['day_name'] = array(
 747   'pattern' => 'cccc'
 748 );
 749 
 750 // The format used for the weekly repeat day name on edit_entry.php
 751 $datetime_formats['day_name_edit'] = array(
 752   'pattern' => 'ccc'
 753 );
 754 
 755 // The format used for the month name in the year view
 756 $datetime_formats['month_name_year_view'] = array(
 757   'pattern' => 'LLL'
 758 );
 759 
 760 // The format for ranges with both dates and times
 761 // Note: this setting only accepts 'date_type' and 'time_type' keys
 762 // and ignores 'pattern' and 'skeleton' keys.
 763 $datetime_formats['range_datetime'] = array(
 764   'date_type' => IntlDateFormatter::MEDIUM,
 765   'time_type' => IntlDateFormatter::SHORT
 766 );
 767 
 768 // The format used for times
 769 $datetime_formats['time'] = array(
 770   'date_type' => IntlDateFormatter::NONE,
 771   'time_type' => IntlDateFormatter::SHORT
 772 );
 773 
 774 // The format used for timezones
 775 $datetime_formats['timezone'] = array(
 776   'pattern' => 'z'
 777 );
 778 
 779 // The title of the day view calendar
 780 $datetime_formats['view_day'] = array(
 781   'date_type' => IntlDateFormatter::FULL,
 782   'time_type' => IntlDateFormatter::NONE
 783 );
 784 
 785 // The title of the month view calendar
 786 $datetime_formats['view_month'] = array(
 787   'skeleton' => 'MMMMy',
 788   'pattern' => 'MMMM y'
 789 );
 790 
 791 // The day and month as used in the header row of the week view
 792 $datetime_formats['view_week_day_month'] = array(
 793   'skeleton' => 'dMMM',
 794   'pattern' => 'MMM d'
 795 );
 796 
 797 // The day and month as used in the header column of the week view
 798 $datetime_formats['view_week_day_date_month'] = array(
 799   'skeleton' => 'dEMMM',
 800   'pattern' => 'EEE, MMM d'
 801 );
 802 
 803 // The title of the week view calendar
 804 // Note: this setting only accepts 'date_type' and 'time_type' keys
 805 // and ignores 'pattern' and 'skeleton' keys.
 806 $datetime_formats['view_week'] = array(
 807   'date_type' => IntlDateFormatter::LONG,
 808   'time_type' => IntlDateFormatter::NONE
 809 );
 810 
 811 // Week number
 812 $datetime_formats['week_number'] = array(
 813   'pattern' => 'w'
 814 );
 815 
 816 // Sometimes if the server's ICU library is out of date and cannot easily be updated
 817 // it can be better to use the IntlDateFormatter emulation and strftime(), even if the
 818 // 'intl' extension is installed.  To do this set the variable below to true.
 819 $force_srtftime = false;
 820

 822 /***************
 823  * ICU overrides
 824  * *************/
 825 
 826 // Sometimes we may want to override the standard ICU library settings,
 827 // for example if the ICU library on the server is out of date and can't
 828 // be updated.  This can be done by setting:
 829 //
 830 // $icu_override[<locale>]['first_day_of_week'] and/or
 831 // $icu_override[<locale>]['minimal_days_in_first_week']
 832 //
 833 // where <locale> is a valid locale in BCP 47 format and both settings take
 834 // integer values in the range 1..7 (IntlCalendar days start with Sunday = 1).
 835 
 836 // For example:
 837 //
 838 // $icu_override['en-AU']['first_day_of_week'] = 2; // Monday
 839 // $icu_override['en-AU']['minimal_days_in_first_week'] = 1;

 925  $select_options  = array();
 926 // It is possible to constrain some form values to be selected from a drop-
 927 // down select box, rather than allowing free form input.   This is done by
 928 // putting the permitted options in an array as part of the $select_options
 929 // two-dimensional array.   The first index specifies the form field in the
 930 // format tablename.columnname.    For example to restrict the name of a booking
 931 // to 'Physics', 'Chemistry' or 'Biology' uncomment the line below.
 932 
 933 //$select_options['entry.name'] = array('Physics', 'Chemistry', 'Biology');
 934 
 935 // At the moment $select_options is only supported as follows:
 936 //     - Entry table: name, description and custom fields
 937 //     - Users table: custom fields
 938 
 939 // For custom fields only (will be extended later) it is also possible to use
 940 // an associative array for $select_options, for example
 941 
 942 //$select_options['entry.catering'] = array('c' => 'Coffee',
 943 //                                          's' => 'Sandwiches',
 944 //                                          'h' => 'Hot Lunch');
 945 
 946 // In this case the key (eg 'c') is stored in the database, but the value
 947 // (eg 'Coffee') is displayed and can be searched for using Search and Report.
 948 // This allows you to alter the displayed values, for example changing 'Coffee'
 949 // to 'Coffee, Tea and Biscuits', without having to alter the database.   It can also
 950 // be useful if the database table is being shared with another application.
 951 // MRBS will auto-detect whether the array is associative.
 952 //
 953 // Note that an array such as
 954 //
 955 // $select_options['entry.catering'] = array('2' => 'Coffee',
 956 //                                           '4' => 'Sandwiches',
 957 //                                           '5' => 'Hot Lunch');
 958 //
 959 // will be treated as a simple indexed array rather than as an associative array.
 960 // That's because (a) strictly speaking PHP does not distinguish between indexed
 961 // and associative arrays and (b) PHP will cast any string key that looks like a
 962 // valid integer into an integer.
 963 //
 964 // If you want to make the select field a mandatory field (see below) then include
 965 // an empty string as one of the values, eg
 966 //
 967 //$select_options['entry.catering'] = array(''  => 'Please select one option',
 968 //                                          'c' => 'Coffee',
 969 //                                          's' => 'Sandwiches',
 970 //                                          'h' => 'Hot Lunch');
 971 
 972 
 973 $datalist_options = array();
 974 // Instead of restricting the user to a fixed set of options using $select_options,
 975 // you can provide a list of options which will be used as suggestions, but the
 976 // user will also be able to type in their own input.   (MRBS presents these using
 977 // an HTML5 <datalist> element in browsers that support it, falling back to a
 978 // JavaScript emulation in browsers that don't - except for IE6 and below where
 979 // an ordinary text input field is presented).
 980 //
 981 // As with $select_options, the array can be either a simple indexed array or an
 982 // associative array, eg array('AL' => 'Alabama', 'AK' => 'Alaska', etc.).   However
 983 // some users might find an associative array confusing as the key is entered in the input
 984 // field when the corresponding value is selected.
 985 //
 986 // At the moment $datalist_options is only supported for the same fields as
 987 // $select_options (see above for details)
 988

1075 /***********************************************
1076  * Authentication settings - read AUTHENTICATION
1077  ***********************************************/
1078 
1079 // NOTE: if you are using the 'joomla', 'saml' or 'wordpress' authentication type,
1080 // then you must use the corresponding session scheme.
1081 
1082 $auth["type"] = "db"; // How to validate the user/password. One of
1083                       // "auth_basic", "cas", "config", "crypt", "db", "db_ext", "idcheck",
1084                       // "imap", "imap_php", "joomla", "ldap", "none", "nw", "pop3",
1085                       // "saml", "wix" or "wordpress".
1086 
1087 $auth["session"] = "php"; // How to get and keep the user ID. One of
1088                           // "cas", "cookie", "host", "http", "ip", "joomla", "nt",
1089                           // "omni", "php", "remote_user", "saml" or "wordpress".
1090 
1091 // Configuration parameters for 'cookie' session scheme
1092 
1093 // The encryption secret key for the session tokens. You are strongly
1094 // advised to change this if you use this session scheme
1095 $auth["session_cookie"]["secret"] = "This isn't a very good secret!";
1096 // The expiry time of a session, in seconds. Set to 0 to use session cookies
1097 $auth["session_cookie"]["session_expire_time"] = (60*60*24*30); // 30 days
1098 // Whether to include the user's IP address in their session cookie.
1099 // Increases security, but could cause problems with proxies/dynamic IP
1100 // machines
1101 $auth["session_cookie"]["include_ip"] = true;
1102 // The hash algorithm to use, must be supported by your version of PHP,
1103 // see http://php.net/manual/en/function.hash-algos.php
1104 $auth["session_cookie"]["hash_algorithm"] = 'sha512';
1105 
1106 $csrf_cookie["hash_algorithm"] = 'sha512';
1107 $csrf_cookie["secret"] = "This still isn't a very good secret!";
1108 
1109 // Configuration parameters for 'php' session scheme
1110 
1111 // The session name
1112 // Unset this in your config file if you want to use the default session name
1113 $auth["session_php"]["session_name"] = 'MRBS_SESSID';
1114 
1115 // The expiry time of a session cookie, in seconds.  Set it to 0 for the
1116 // session to expire when the browser is closed.
1117 // Note:
1118 // (1) The expiration timestamp is set relative to the server time, which
1119 //     is not necessarily the same as the time in the client's browser.
1120 // (2) If session.gc_maxlifetime is less than the expiry time, MRBS will
1121 //     set it to the expiry time.
1122 $auth["session_php"]["session_expire_time"] = (60*60*24*30); // 30 days
1123 
1124 // Set this to the expiry time for a session after a period of inactivity
1125 // in seconds.   Setting to zero means that the session will not expire after
1126 // a period of activity - but note that it will expire if the session cookie
1127 // happens to expire (see above).  Note that if you have $refresh_rate set and
1128 // your system is not capable of doing Ajax refreshes but instead uses a <meta>
1129 // tag to do the refresh, then these refreshes will count as activity - this
1130 // be the case if you have JavaScript disabled on the client.
1131 $auth["session_php"]["inactivity_expire_time"] = 0; // seconds
1132 
1133 // Normally, provided the server is running PHP 7.3 or above,  the session cookies
1134 // are issued with SameSite attribute of "Strict", unless the session type requires
1135 // "Lax", eg for CAS and Saml. However, this can be inconvenient for users who might
1136 // access MRBS from more than one site and expect their login status to be retained.
1137 // By setting the variable below to true, the attribute can be relaxed to "Lax",
1138 // although this does trade off some security.
1139 $cookie_samesite_lax = false;
1140 
1141 // Cookie path override. If this value is set it will be used by the
1142 // 'php' and 'cookie' session schemes to override the default behaviour
1143 // of automatically determining the cookie path to use
1144 //$cookie_path_override = '/mrbs/';
1145 
1146 // The list of administrators (can modify other peoples settings).
1147 //

1631 // details will be shown as private if you set this to true.
1632 $auth['force_private_for_guests'] = false;

1634 // Set to true if you want admins to be able to perform bulk deletions

1636 $auth['show_bulk_delete'] = false;

1638 // Allow admins to insert custom HTML on the area and room pages.  This can be useful for
1639 // displaying information about an area or room, eg with a picture or a map.   But it
1640 // also presents a security risk as the HTML is output as is, and could therefore contain

1644 // Set to true if you want to allow MRBS to be run from the command line, for example

1656 /**********************************************
1657  * Email settings
1658  **********************************************/
1659 
1660 // BASIC SETTINGS
1661 // --------------
1662 
1663 // Set the email address of the From field. Default is 'admin_email@your.org'
1664 $mail_settings['from'] = 'admin_email@your.org';
1665 
1666 // By default MRBS will send some emails (eg booking approval emails) as though they have come from
1667 // the user, rather than the From address above.   However some email servers will not allow this in
1668 // order to prevent email spoofing.   If this is the case then set this to true in order that the
1669 // From address above is used for all emails.
1670 $mail_settings['use_from_for_all_mail'] = false;
1671 
1672 // By default MRBS will set a Reply-To address and use current user's email address.  Set this to
1673 // false in order not to set a Reply-To address.
1674 $mail_settings['use_reply_to'] = true;
1675 
1676 // The address to be used for the ORGANIZER in an iCalendar event.  The address should
1677 // be an RFC822-style address of the form "display name <address>" or just "address".
1678 // Do not make this email address the same as the admin email address or the recipients
1679 // email address because on some mail systems, eg IBM Domino, the iCalendar email
1680 // notification is silently discarded if the organizer's email address is the same
1681 // as the recipient's.  On other systems you may get a "Meeting not found" message.
1682 $mail_settings['organizer'] = 'mrbs@your.org';
1683 
1684 // Set the recipient email. Default is 'admin_email@your.org'. You can define
1685 // more than one recipient like this "john@doe.com,scott@tiger.com"

1687 
1688 // Set email address of the Carbon Copy field. Default is ''. You can define
1689 // more than one recipient (see 'recipients')
1690 $mail_settings['cc'] = '';
1691 
1692 // Set to true if you want the cc addresses to be appended to the to line.
1693 // (Some email servers are configured not to send emails if the cc or bcc
1694 // fields are set)
1695 $mail_settings['treat_cc_as_to'] = false;
1696 
1697 
1698 
1699 // WHO TO EMAIL
1700 // ------------
1701 // The following settings determine who should be emailed when a booking is made,
1702 // edited or deleted (though the latter two events depend on the "When" settings below).
1703 // Set to true or false as required
1704 // (Note:  the email addresses for the area and room administrators are set from the
1705 // edit_area.php and edit_room.php pages in MRBS)
1706 $mail_settings['admin_on_bookings']      = false;  // the addresses defined by $mail_settings['recipients'] below
1707 $mail_settings['area_admin_on_bookings'] = false;  // the area administrator
1708 $mail_settings['room_admin_on_bookings'] = false;  // the room administrator
1709 $mail_settings['booker']                 = false;  // the person making the booking
1710 $mail_settings['book_admin_on_approval'] = false;  // the booking administrator when booking approval is enabled
1711                                                    // (which is the MRBS admin, but this setting allows MRBS
1712                                                    // to be extended to have separate booking approvers)
1713 
1714 // WHEN TO EMAIL
1715 // -------------
1716 // These settings determine when an email should be sent.
1717 // Set to true or false as required
1718 //
1719 // (Note:  (a) the variables $mail_settings['admin_on_delete'] and
1720 // $mail_settings['admin_all'], which were used in MRBS versions 1.4.5 and
1721 // before are now deprecated.   They are still supported for reasons of backward
1722 // compatibility, but they may be withdrawn in the future.  (b)  the default
1723 // value of $mail_settings['on_new'] is true for compatibility with MRBS 1.4.5
1724 // and before, where there was no explicit config setting, but mails were always sent
1725 // for new bookings if there was somebody to send them to)
1726 
1727 $mail_settings['on_new']    = true;   // when an entry is created
1728 $mail_settings['on_change'] = false;  // when an entry is changed
1729 $mail_settings['on_delete'] = false;  // when an entry is deleted
1730 
1731 // It is also possible to allow all users or just admins to choose not to send an
1732 // email when creating or editing a booking.  This can be useful if an inconsequential
1733 // change is being made, or many bookings are being made at the beginning of a term or season.
1734 $mail_settings['allow_no_mail']        = false;
1735 $mail_settings['allow_admins_no_mail'] = false;  // Ignored if 'allow_no_mail' is true
1736 $mail_settings['no_mail_default'] = false; // Default value for the 'no mail' checkbox.
1737                                            // true for checked (ie don't send mail),
1738                                            // false for unchecked (ie do send mail)
1739 
1740 
1741 // WHAT TO EMAIL
1742 // -------------

1746                                      // otherwise you just get a link to the entry
1747 $mail_settings['html']      = false; // Set to true if you want HTML mail
1748 $mail_settings['icalendar'] = false; // Set to true to include iCalendar details
1749                                      // which can be imported into a calendar.  (Note:
1750                                      // iCalendar details will not be sent for areas
1751                                      // that use periods as there isn't a mapping between
1752                                      // periods and time of day, so the calendar would not
1753                                      // be able to import the booking)

1758 // Set the language used for emails.  This should be in the form of a BCP 47
1759 // language tag, eg 'en-GB'.  MRBS will use the language tag to set the locale
1760 // for date and time formats, and find the best match in the lang.* files for
1761 // translations.  For example, setting the admin_lang to 'en' will give English
1762 // text and am/pm style times; setting it to 'en-GB' will give English text with

1766 
1767 // HOW TO EMAIL - ADDRESSES
1768 // ------------------------

1770 // the room and area administrators are set though the edit_area.php and edit_room.php
1771 // pages in MRBS.  But if you have set $mail_settings['booker'] above to true, MRBS will
1772 // need the email addresses of ordinary users.   If you are using the "db"
1773 // authentication method then MRBS will be able to get them from the users table.  But
1774 // if you are using any other authentication scheme then the following settings allow
1775 // you to specify a domain name that will be appended to the username to produce a
1776 // valid email address (eg "@domain.com").  MRBS will add the '@' character for you.
1777 $mail_settings['domain'] = '';
1778 // If you use $mail_settings['domain'] above and the username returned by mrbs contains extra
